title: Wild hogweed infused cream
intro: It all comes down to the gentleness of the heat: a cream that boils is a cream that curdles.
titane: The covered pan replaces the oven. Its mass diffuses a low, even heat to the center of the dish, and its bare, uncoated surface can withstand twenty minutes of very low heat without flinching. A light dusting of clarified butter on the bottom is all it takes to release the cream when serving.
steps: Pour the cream and milk into the pan. Add the hogweed. Heat gently until it just begins to simmer, without ever letting it boil.
Remove from heat, cover with a lid or an inverted plate. Let it steep for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs and sugar together in a bowl until the mixture lightens in color and thickens slightly.
Strain the still-warm infusion through a fine sieve. Press the leaves to extract the aroma, then discard them.
Gradually whisk the warm liquid into the egg and sugar mixture. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface; it will create bubbles during baking.
Wipe the pan, grease it with clarified butter, pour in the mixture.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 20 to 25 minutes. The surface should be set, the center still wobbly.
Let it cool off the heat in the pan, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: White butter sauce with wild thyme and vegetable broth
intro: A beurre blanc lightened with stock, where wild thyme provides the lemony note that holds the whole sauce together.

ing.note: including 20g for sweating and 100g very cold
for the zest if you replace the thyme with

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly: the shallots sweat in five minutes and the vinegar reduces almost completely without anything browning. Its large surface then serves as a work surface for assembly; the whisk moves freely and the butter blends without sticking.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. A drop of water should sizzle immediately.
Melt the 20g of butter, then sweat (cook without browning, covered or uncovered) the shallots with the thyme for 5 minutes. They become translucent and the lemony aroma is released.
Pour in the vinegar, add the pepper mill.
Reduce over medium heat until almost evaporated: only a damp base should remain around the shallots.
Moisten with vegetable broth.
Add the liquid cream.
Bring to a boil over high heat, until the liquid thickens slightly.
Add salt lightly. Taste it: the broth already provides salt.
Reduce the heat to low. Whisk in the cold butter cube by cube until the sauce is thick and glossy, about 3 minutes. The sauce should not boil.
Spoon the sauce over the fish or meat when serving.

title: Pear crumble with honey, cinnamon and caraway
intro: It's all about the contrast: very ripe pears reduced to a compote right in the pan, and a buckwheat shortbread that stays dry because it's finished cooking uncovered.

ing.note: plus a knob of clarified butter for the

titane: The hot pan sears the bottoms of the pears and concentrates their juices while the lid does the work of the oven. The lid is removed for the last five minutes: the steam escapes, the crumble dries and browns. A single utensil is used for everything from the compote to the crust, and it's served in the same pan.
steps: Peel the pears without crushing them, remove the core and seeds. Keep the cores aside (see below).
Mash the flesh roughly with a fork: there should still be some chunks.
Add the honey, cinnamon, and caraway seeds. Mix and taste. If the pears are very ripe, reduce the amount of honey.

Rub the dough together (flour and butter between your fingers until you obtain a coarse, crumbly mixture): buckwheat flour, cold butter, brown sugar. Work quickly with your fingertips, without warming the butter. Stop when the texture is sandy and uneven, with a few pea-sized lumps. Refrigerate.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter: it should simmer without smoking.
Spread the compote evenly over the entire surface. Let it sit for 1 minute without touching it.
Spread the shortbread on top by hand, without pressing down.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Allow 20 minutes: the pears will release their juices, and the bottom will caramelize slightly.
Remove the lid, return to medium heat and continue for 3 to 5 minutes, until the top dries and takes on color.
Let it cool for 10 minutes off the heat. Serve in the pan, or unmold onto a plate with a decisive movement.

title: Reblochon cheese in a crust with Good King Henry
intro: A whole cheese under its rind, placed on wild leaves: everything depends on the diameter of the pan, which must match that of the Reblochon so that the heat rises everywhere at the same time.

ing.note: plus a pinch for the bleaching water

titane: The pan performs three functions: it blanchs the sheets in a little water, it receives the filling, and then it goes in the oven. The bare metal, preheated empty, retains its heat and sears the bottom of the dough while the top browns — no soft bottom, no transferring.
steps: Sort the lamb's quarters leaves, remove the toughest stems, wash them thoroughly and drain.
Bring 400 ml of salted water to a boil directly in the pan. Blanch the leaves for 2 minutes over high heat (blanch: briefly plunge into boiling water to soften and set the color).
Drain the leaves, squeeze them between your hands to remove the water, spread them on a cloth and let them cool outside the pan.
Preheat the oven to 210°C. Wipe the pan thoroughly, then heat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, until a drop of water dances in it.
Remove from heat and arrange the cooled leaves in an even layer at the bottom of the pan. Place the Reblochon cheese in the center, rind intact.
Unroll the pastry, cover the cheese and leaves, then press the edges against the side of the pan, sealing them with your fingertips. Make a small vent at the top.
Beat the egg yolk with a few drops of water, brush the crust with a pastry brush, and add a little salt.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 15 minutes, until the crust is puffed and golden brown. Wait 5 minutes before cutting: the cheese holds its shape better.

title: Potato mille-feuille with wild garlic
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the slices: if cut too thin, the potatoes release their starch into the milk instead of binding the layers together.

ing.note: It can withstand high temperatures without

titane: The titanium pan doubles as a gratin dish. Preheated empty, greased, and then placed directly in the oven, it cooks and browns the mille-feuille in the same pan. Direct contact with the heated base starts the first layers cooking as soon as they are assembled, and the top browns without anything sticking.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Heat the milk over medium heat in a saucepan, without letting it boil.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the clarified butter and spread it evenly: it should simmer gently, never smoke.
Peel the potatoes and slice them into 3-4 mm pieces. Do not rinse them; the surface starch will bind the ingredients.
Remove from heat and spread the wild garlic at the bottom of the pan, still frozen if it comes straight from the freezer.
Layer the slices tightly, overlapping them flat. Press down with your fingertips at each layer: compact layers require less milk and hold together when cut.
Pour the hot milk over the mixture. It should just cover the last layer without drowning it.
Place the pan in the oven as is for at least 20 minutes. A knife tip should pierce it easily and the top should turn golden brown.

Remove the pan from the heat, dot with small pieces of butter, and season with salt. The salt is added at the end of cooking: it brings out the flavor of the wild garlic instead of causing it to release its juices during cooking. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Béchamel sauce with cassava starch, and its two derivatives
intro: Without butter or flour, the binding relies on the starch alone: everything depends on the cold dilution and a whisk that never stops.
titane: The pan offers a much larger, flat surface than a saucepan: the milk heats up quickly, evaporates rapidly, and thickens sooner. However, the heat is intense, and the bottom sticks at the slightest pause. Whisk continuously from the first simmer, sweeping across the entire surface, including the edges.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes over medium heat. The base must be thoroughly hot before adding any liquid.
Take 5 cl of cold milk and set it aside. Pour the rest into the hot pan and let it heat up over medium heat.
Dissolve the cassava starch in the reserved cold milk. Whisk until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture, with no lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Pour this mixture into the hot milk in a thin stream, whisk in hand, while continuing to stir.
Season with salt and nutmeg.
Bring to a boil, whisking continuously, for 4 to 5 minutes. The sauce thickens suddenly at the first boil: this is the time to watch the edges, which set before the center.

Judge the consistency by the coating (the sauce should cling to the back of a spoon). If it remains runny, dissolve an extra teaspoon of cornstarch in a little cold milk and stir it in, then bring back to a boil.
For the gratin sauce, reduce the heat to low and stir in the grated cheese by handfuls, whisking until completely melted. If it's over high heat, it will stick to the bottom.
For the Savoyard version, proceed in the same way with the Beaufort cheese, grated at the last moment so that it melts without stretching.
For the Mornay sauce, remove the pan from the heat, wait a minute, then whisk in the egg yolks one at a time. Do not let it boil: the yolks will curdle and the sauce will become grainy.

title: Beef fajita wraps and tomato rice
intro: Twenty wraps in advance in the freezer, provided that the meat and vegetables are seared in batches: it is the colouring, not the sauce, that makes the taste.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any fat. Then work in small batches: an overloaded pan releases water and the meat boils instead of browning. Don't touch anything while the pieces are sticking. When they release on their own, the crust has formed and you can stir.
steps: Cut the peppers and onions into strips. Mince the garlic. Combine the spices in a bowl: you will add them all at once.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil.

Sear the vegetables in two or three batches. Leave them to stand still until they begin to separate and show browning spots. Remove them from the pan (transfer them to a separate dish) as they are done.
Turn up the heat to high. Brown the ground beef in the same pan, in two batches, breaking it up gradually. Wait until it breaks up easily before stirring. It should no longer be pink.
Return the vegetables and garlic to the meat. Add the spices, salt, and pepper. Stir for 1 minute to warm them through.
Pour in the fajita sauce and tomato paste. Mix until completely coated.
Reduce the heat to low-medium and simmer for 10 minutes, covered if the mixture dries out too quickly. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.

In a wiped pan, toast the rice for 1 minute in a little oil (the grains will become translucent around the edges). Crumble in the stock cube, pour in 450 ml of water, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, until the water is completely absorbed.
Let the rice and filling cool separately at room temperature. A warm filled wrap will release water in the freezer.
Top each tortilla with a spoonful of rice, a spoonful of filling and grated cheese, leaving a 3 cm margin on the edges.
Fold in the sides, then roll tightly. Wrap individually and freeze: 3 months.

To serve, defrost in the refrigerator the day before. Reheat for 3 to 4 minutes per side in a titanium pan over medium heat, or place the pan directly in the oven at 180°C for 10 minutes for a drier crust.

title: French toast with brioche
intro: It all comes down to two things: a brioche dense enough to absorb the mixture without falling apart, and a pan that's really hot before the fat gets into it.

ing.note: fresh fruit, honey, hazelnut pieces, sugar

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the fat. The heat, rising quickly and evenly, caramelizes the sugar in the soaked brioche into a crisp crust. Do not touch the slices while they are still warm: once the crust has formed, they will detach easily.
steps: Whisk the eggs, cream, sugar and cinnamon in a bowl until you have a smooth mixture, with no white streaks of egg.
Dip the brioche slices in the mixture for 10 to 15 seconds per side. They should be soaked through but hold their shape without bending.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.

Pour the clarified butter or oil over the pan, then arrange the slices loosely. Leave them in place: they will release on their own once the top is set, after 2 to 3 minutes. Turn them over and brown the other side.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process, place on a plate, add the topping and serve immediately.

title: Chicken and merguez couscous (freezable)
intro: Twenty portions from a single simmer: everything depends on the color of the onions and meat before adding the water, because it is the water that will give its flavor to the broth that will come out of the freezer.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the oil. The temperature rises quickly: the onions form a crisp crust instead of sweating (releasing their water without browning), and the meat sears immediately upon contact. The simmering time is under 45 minutes, and the added water remains under 500 ml, so a covered pan is sufficient from start to finish.
steps: Finely chop the onions. Cut the carrots, celery and courgettes into even bite-sized pieces.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in a drizzle of olive oil.
Drop the onions into the hot oil. Don't move them while they're still sticking: they'll detach on their own when one side is browned. Then stir once.
Add the carrots, celery, peeled tomatoes and tomato paste. Stir to coat.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat, until the vegetables begin to give way under the tip of a knife.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken fillets into large cubes and the merguez sausages into 3 cm pieces.
Add the chicken, merguez sausages, and chickpeas. Season with salt, pepper, couscous spices, and ras el hanout. Mix to distribute the spices.
Pour in less than 500 ml of water, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes over low heat. Monitor the evaporation: the bottom should remain moist without the contents becoming waterlogged.
Pour the semolina into a large bowl, cover it with hot water to a height plus one centimeter, cover and let it swell for 10 minutes.
Fluff the semolina with a fork, then stir in a few ladles of broth taken from the pan.
Add the courgettes to the pan and continue simmering, covered, over low heat for 25 minutes. Adjust the seasoning at the end of cooking.
Remove from heat and divide into individual bags or molds: one portion of semolina, one portion of meat and vegetables per serving.
Allow to cool completely to room temperature before sealing, then freeze. Portions will keep for 3 months.
To serve, reheat the portion in the microwave on a plate, or fry the portion of meat and vegetables in a titanium pan over medium heat: the base regains its bite and the spices awaken.

title: Peanut and dark chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the dough: firm enough to hold its shape when cut, flexible enough to spread without cracking.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its rapid and even heat-up melts chocolate over very low heat in two or three minutes, provided you stir continuously. You keep a close eye on the mixture, feel when it becomes smooth, and turn off the heat before it gets too hot. One less pan to wash, one less utensil to get out.
steps: Combine the peanut butter, almond flour, agave syrup, and vanilla in a bowl. Mix with a spatula until you have a perfectly smooth paste, without any streaks or lumps.
Line a baking dish with baking paper. Pour in the batter and spread it evenly to a thickness of about 1.5 cm, pressing it down with the back of a spoon. Push the batter firmly into the corners.

Chop the chocolate with a knife: the smaller the pieces, the more evenly it will melt. Place them in the titanium pan over very low heat, away from any direct flame. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula. In three minutes, the mixture will become smooth and glossy. Remove from the heat at this point.
Coat the pastry (cover it with an even layer) by pouring the chocolate in the center and then spreading it towards the edges. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Refrigerate for 2 hours, or freeze for 30 minutes if you're in a hurry. Unmold using the paper, then cut into six bars with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each cut.

title: Three summer spreads on crusty bread
intro: It all comes down to the colouring of the vegetables: the more intense the searing, the more flavourful the spread will be once blended.

ing.note: a net (or the one from the jar of tomatoes)

ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: No oven needed here. The titanium pan, preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding a single drop of oil, rises high enough to sear the eggplant and pepper on the surface while the lid finishes softening them. You get the caramelization that an oven can't provide, and you only dirty one pan.
steps: Cut the eggplants and peppers into similarly sized pieces so they cook together. Separate the garlic cloves from the head without peeling them.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should roll around in it without evaporating immediately.
Pour in the olive oil, then the vegetables and garlic cloves. Let them brown uncovered, stirring little: it is the prolonged contact with the bottom that marks them.
Cover, reduce heat to low and continue cooking for up to 20 minutes in total. The pieces will be tender and the garlic will easily pull away from the bottom of the pan.

Squeeze the garlic pulp out of its skin and combine it with the vegetables in a blender. Blend with a drizzle of oil, salt, and pepper until smooth. Transfer to a cold container and let cool slightly.

In a food processor, combine sundried tomatoes, garlic cloves, basil, tomato paste, cream cheese, and oil. Pulse until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs; the spread should remain slightly chunky. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Drain the chickpeas, keeping their liquid aside.

Blend them with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and two tablespoons of the reserved juice. Add the ice cube while blending: it cools the purée and makes it whiten. Continue blending until you obtain a perfectly smooth hummus, then drizzle with olive oil.
Spread the mixture on the bread slices at the last minute. On those topped with tomato, crumble the feta cheese by hand.

title: Peanut butter and dark chocolate cups
intro: It all comes down to how the chocolate melts: too hot, it becomes grainy and loses its shine; just hot enough, it coats in a thin layer and breaks cleanly under the tooth.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat is distributed quickly and evenly, without hot spots, allowing you to melt chocolate over very low heat in three minutes, without water or steam. You keep your eyes on the chocolate and your hand on the spatula, giving you complete control over the texture. Remove from the heat as soon as the last chocolate chip disappears: the pan continues to heat for a few seconds.
steps: Mix the peanut butter and almond flour in a bowl. Work with a spatula until you obtain a smooth, cohesive dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Divide the batter among the paper muffin cups. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon to create a flat surface: this will give you a regular chocolate line.
Break the chocolate into even pieces in the titanium pan placed over very low heat. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula for about 3 minutes, until it is shiny and runny.
Remove from the heat source by pouring directly from the pan onto each cup. Coat to the edges.
Add the pinch of fleur de sel while the chocolate is still liquid, otherwise it will not adhere.
Place in the refrigerator until completely set: the chocolate should be firm and matte on the surface.
Remove from the mold and store in an airtight bag in the freezer for up to three months. Take them out 5 minutes before serving.

title: Shredded chicken wraps, barbecue sauce and cream cheese
intro: It all comes down to the searing: chicken that is coloured on the surface shreds better and retains its juices once mixed with the sauce.
titane: The empty pan retains its heat when the chicken cubes are added: they sear instead of boiling, and release easily once a crust has formed. The peppers are then added to the same pan, without being washed, to soak up the juices left by the poultry.
steps: Remove the seeds from the peppers and cut them into short strips. Cut the chicken breasts into even cubes of about 4 cm: they will cook quickly and shred more easily.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It is ready when a drop of water immediately sizzles in it.

Pour the grapeseed oil over the chicken, then add the chicken seasoned with salt, pepper, and herbs. Let it sit for 10 minutes, turning the cubes only once: they will separate on their own as soon as the crust sets.
Push the meat to one side, add a drizzle of oil and fry the peppers for 5 minutes, until tender and charred in places.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside on a cutting board. Shred it with a fork, pulling in the direction of the fibers.
In a large bowl, combine the shredded chicken, barbecue sauce, and cream cheese. Mix until each strand is coated.
Stir in the still-warm peppers and grated mozzarella. Adjust the seasoning.
Spread a generous amount of the mixture onto each tortilla, leaving a 3cm border. Fold in the sides, then roll tightly.
Store the wraps in the refrigerator for a maximum of 3 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months, individually wrapped.

title: Chocolate-covered, glazed raspberries
intro: It all comes down to the melting temperature: chocolate melted too quickly will grain, and the shell will lose its crispness when unmolded.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its even heat distribution, without hot spots, allows you to melt chocolate over very low heat, keeping a close eye on it. Turn off the heat as soon as the first pieces begin to soften and finish melting off the heat, using the residual heat: the chocolate will remain smooth and glossy. Rinse and dry the pan between melting the two batches of chocolate.
steps: Roughly chop the milk chocolate. Preheat the titanium pan over very low heat, pour in the chocolate, and stir. Remove from the heat as soon as it begins to melt and continue stirring off the heat until you obtain a smooth and glossy mass. Transfer to a bowl.
Clean and dry the pan, then repeat the process with the white chocolate.
Place a frozen raspberry in each cavity of an ice cube tray. If the cavities are large, use two raspberries.
Fill half the trays with melted chocolate, half with milk chocolate, half with white chocolate. Tap the tray on the work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Place in the freezer until completely frozen, at least 2 hours.
Unmold by gently twisting the tray. Store the bites in the freezer in a tightly sealed bag.
Take them out 15 minutes before serving: the raspberry needs to regain its juice without softening the shell.

title: Frozen fruit, skyr and chocolate bites
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the chocolate: too hot, it solidifies into a brittle sheet when it comes into contact with the cold skyr; just melted, it retains a fine crunch.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its even heat distribution allows you to melt chocolate over very low heat in three minutes, without it sticking. Stir continuously and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture becomes smooth and glossy—the residual heat finishes the job.
steps: Cut the still-frozen fruit into even pieces, about the size of an ice cube tray compartment. Work quickly, they shouldn't sweat.
Melt the chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat for about 3 minutes, stirring continuously. Stop as soon as it is smooth and glossy. Transfer it to a bowl to stop the cooking process.
Distribute the fruit pieces into the ice cube trays. Cover halfway with skyr, then top with melted chocolate.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel while the chocolate is still soft, otherwise the crystals will not stick.
Place the containers in the freezer until completely frozen, at least 4 hours.
Remove the bites from the molds and transfer them to freezer bags. They will keep for 3 months.

title: Cottage cheese pancakes
intro: It all comes down to the fluidity of the batter and patience: a pancake that is not touched during its first side is a pancake that falls apart on its own.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the first ladleful. The heat rises quickly and remains even: the browning is perfect from the very first batch, without sacrificing a test batch. Once the crust has formed, the pancake releases itself, eliminating the need to add more oil or butter. Between batches, wipe the pan with paper towels before adding a thin layer of oil or butter: this prevents the oil from accumulating and browning too quickly.
steps: Mix the cottage cheese with the eggs, vanilla, maple syrup, baking powder and flour until you get a perfectly smooth, grain-free batter.
Incorporate the chocolate chips with a spatula, in just a few turns.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the clarified butter or oil. Wait until it simmers gently, without smoking.
Pour small ladles of batter, spacing them apart. Let it cook for 2 minutes without moving: bubbles will appear on the surface and the pancake will detach easily.

Flip with a flick of the wrist and continue cooking for 2 minutes, until golden brown and firm to the touch. Repeat with the remaining batter, wiping the pan and adding a little more oil between batches.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto a wire rack and let cool completely: the steam escapes instead of softening the crust.
Freeze the pancakes flat, separated by baking paper, to keep them for several weeks.
In the morning, put a still-frozen pancake directly in the toaster.

title: Peanut-chocolate cottage cheese bites
intro: What matters here is the firmness of the dough before shaping: if it's too soft, the balls collapse and the coating slips.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the bain-marie. Its thinness conducts heat quickly and evenly: chocolate and coconut oil melt in three minutes over low heat, without sticking to the bottom, and the same pan then serves as a coating bath off the heat.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese with the peanut butter, maple syrup and vanilla until you get a perfectly smooth, grain-free cream.
Pour the mixture into a bowl. Add the salt and almond flour, then work with a spatula until the dough comes away from the sides and holds together.

Scoop out even portions, about a heaping teaspoon, and roll them between your palms. Transfer the balls to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Refrigerate for 20 minutes: they will coat more neatly.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in the titanium pan over low heat, stirring continuously. Cook for 3 minutes; stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Remove the pan from the heat. Place the balls one by one in the chocolate and roll them with a fork, then drain them against the edge before placing them back on the baking paper.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel immediately, while the chocolate is still moist.
Let it set in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week.

title: Cubed pancakes, ready for the freezer
intro: A large batch cooked all at once, cooled, portioned: mornings are then settled in two minutes in the pan.
titane: The pan heats up quickly and retains its heat from one pancake to the next, ensuring even browning throughout. Wait until the pancake releases itself; it will then flip cleanly. When reheating, the warm surface is enough to revive frozen pancakes without them sticking and without the need for added fat.
steps: Combine the flour, both sugars, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Mix together the dry ingredients.
Pour the melted butter over this mixture and work it in with a spatula.
Gradually incorporate the milk and eggs, whisking between each addition. The batter should remain smooth, without lumps.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then add a drizzle of clarified butter or grapeseed oil.

Pour a small ladleful of batter onto the pan. Sprinkle with chocolate chips if using. Leave it alone: when the pancake releases easily from the pan, flip it over and continue cooking until golden brown on both sides.
Let them cool completely on a wire rack. Then place one pancake per compartment of an ice cube tray, or store them flat in freezer bags.
Place in the freezer. They will keep for three months.
When ready to serve, place them, still frozen, in the already hot pan over medium heat. Turn them over once, until they are hot throughout and lightly browned.

title: Pan-fried protein banana bread
intro: A dense, protein-rich banana cake, cooked all at once in the pan: what matters is the ripeness of the bananas and a barely sketched marbling.
titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe. You melt the chocolate in it, pour in the batter, and bake in the same pan. No transferring required, and the cake releases easily once it's lukewarm.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Melt the dark chocolate in the titanium pan over low heat, stirring constantly. Transfer it to a bowl and set aside.
Wipe the pan, then grease it with grapeseed oil or butter, bottom and sides.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl until you get a slightly uneven puree.
Add the eggs and skyr. Mix until the mixture is smooth.
Incorporate the oat flour and whey protein. Mix well.
Add the vanilla extract, agave syrup, wheat flour, and yeast. Mix again, without overworking the dough.
Pour the mixture into the pan in an even layer.

Drizzle a little melted chocolate over the batter and marble it (make a few sweeping motions with the tip of a knife to blend the two mixtures without combining them). Stop soon: the veins should remain distinct.
Cover the pan and bake for 30 minutes. The cake is cooked when a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow to cool slightly before unmolding. The cake will detach from the titanium without forcing.

title: Banana, peanut and dark chocolate bars
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas: when they are very speckled, they sweeten the dough and bind it without any addition.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan, without a double boiler. Preheat it empty for one minute over low heat, turn off the heat, pour in the chopped chocolate, and stir: the residual heat of the titanium is enough to liquefy it without ever burning it. With no coating, there's no sticking, and the pan pours just like a saucepan.
steps: Mash the 4 ripe bananas with a fork until you obtain a smooth puree.
Add the peanut butter, maple syrup, salt and cinnamon. Mix.
Incorporate the oat flour, almond flour and protein powder. Work until a smooth, pliable dough forms, pulling away from the sides of the bowl.
Cut the 4 firm bananas into even half-centimeter slices.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over low heat. Turn off the heat, pour in the chopped chocolate and stir constantly for 2 to 3 minutes, until smooth and glossy.

Line a baking dish with parchment paper. Spread half the dough evenly, pressing it down with your hands. Arrange the banana slices on top, pour over the melted chocolate, then cover with the remaining dough, gently flattening it.
Refrigerate for 10 minutes: the chocolate must solidify on the surface, otherwise it will migrate when cut.
Wrap the dish in film and place it in the freezer overnight, until the base is firm to the touch.
The next day, unmold and cut into bars with a chef's knife, the blade having been rinsed under hot water and wiped between each cut.
Store the bars in the bag, separated by squares of baking paper. Three months in the freezer, three days in the refrigerator.

title: Peanut, caramel and crunchy chocolate popsicles
intro: It all depends on the order of the layers and the temperature of the chocolate: if it's too hot, it melts the ice cream when dipping.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, the chocolate and coconut oil melt without sticking or burning, and the pan then becomes the soaking bath. One container, from start to finish.
steps: Whisk the mascarpone with the sugar and cold cream until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture (basic mixture) that is supple but already holds its shape.
Fill the popsicle molds only two-thirds full, using a piping bag or a spoon. The remaining third will hold the delicious layers.
Spread a layer of salted caramel, then a layer of peanut butter. Press down lightly to remove any air bubbles.
Insert the sticks and place in the freezer for at least one hour, until the mixture is completely frozen.
Place the chocolate and coconut oil in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula. Remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy, in about three minutes.
Let the chocolate cool off the heat, then unmold the ice pops and dip them directly into the pan to coat them completely.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts while the chocolate is still melting.
Return to the freezer until serving, until the coating sets and crackles when you bite into it.

title: Skyr bread with chocolate chips
intro: A dough without resting or kneading, whose success depends entirely on the gentle heat under the lid.
titane: Preheated empty and then covered with its lid, the titanium pan creates a miniature convection heat: the balls puff up and cook through without forming a crust too quickly. They are then transferred to the oven in the same pan, without transferring them, to brown only the tops.
steps: Combine the skyr, flour, baking powder, vanilla sugar, and chocolate chips in a bowl. Work the mixture by hand until you have a soft dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl. It should be slightly damp to the touch and not sticky.
Divide the dough into three equal parts. Roll each part into a ball between your palms, gently pressing the surface to keep it smooth.

Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Place the clarified butter (butter with the whey removed, which can withstand high temperatures without burning) in the pan and spread it into a thin film.
Place the three balls, well spaced apart, on the hot surface. Do not flatten them: they should spread out on their own as they cook.
Beat the egg yolk with a fork and a few drops of water and brush the top of each loaf with a pastry brush.

Cover and cook for 25 minutes over medium-low heat. Resist the urge to lift the lid before the 20-minute mark. Uncover, then place the pan as is in the oven at 185°C (365°F) for 10 minutes. The loaves are ready when the bottom easily pulls away from the pan and the base sounds hollow when lightly pressed.

title: Pan-fried chocolate and sweet potato fondant
intro: Sweet potato replaces some of the butter and sugar: it is what gives the texture, provided it is cooked until it is really tender.
titane: Covered pan, low heat: the heat circulates under the lid and cooks the cake like an oven, from below and with steam. The bare titanium releases the fondant on its own, without paper or mold—just wait for the edges to shrink.
steps: Peel the sweet potato, cut it into large cubes, and cook it for 20 minutes in simmering water or steam it. A knife should pierce it easily. Drain and let it cool slightly.
Mash the flesh with a fork until you obtain a smooth puree. Incorporate the eggs one by one, then the agave syrup and vanilla.
Add the sifted flour, cocoa, and baking powder. Mix gently, just until the batter is smooth. Finish by adding the chocolate chips.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes: a drop of water should slide off the surface in beads. Brush with a thin layer of fat.
Pour the mixture into the pan and spread it evenly with a spatula.
Cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid: each time you open it, the heat will drop. If the surface starts to simmer rapidly, reduce the heat further.
Check the center with the tip of a knife; it should come out clean. The thickness varies depending on the diameter of the pan, so rely on the tip rather than a timer.
Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes. The edges will loosen easily. Invert the pan onto a plate.

title: Pan-fried salmon and vegetables, finished with a lid
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the pan when the salmon touches the metal: if it's too warm, the skin sticks and tears.

ing.note: (or just one and the rest cold the next day)

titane: Preheat the empty skillet over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It's ready when a drop of water in it rolls into a ball instead of evaporating completely. The hot titanium will sear the vegetables and then the skin of the salmon on the surface; the lid then takes over, replacing the oven. One single skillet, from the first slice to the plate.
steps: Cut the peppers and courgette into even pieces, about 3 cm. Evenness matters more than shape: it ensures even cooking.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, medium-high heat, 2 to 3 minutes, until the water droplet test.
Pour in a drizzle of oil, add the vegetables. Fry them for 6 minutes, stirring regularly, until the edges are browned.
Push the vegetables to the edge of the pan. Place the steaks in the center, skin-side down. Season with spices, salt, pepper, and a final drizzle of oil.
Let it cook for 4 minutes without touching it. The salmon will release itself under the spatula when the skin is set: that's the only signal to wait for.
Cover, reduce heat to low-medium and continue for 10 minutes. The flesh should flake easily with a fork, while remaining amber in the center.
Remove from the pan immediately, otherwise the residual cooking will dry out the fish.

title: Chocolate chip cookies, shaped and frozen dough
intro: A dough worked in one go, portioned and then chilled: the cookie baked without defrosting retains a soft center and clean edges.
ing: Brown sugar, or very fine brown sugar

ing.note: softened at room temperature, creamy texture

ing: Crushed or chipped dark baking chocolate
titane: Place the titanium pan in the oven, with the dough balls directly inside. Its rapid heat conduction caramelizes the base while the top remains soft. Let them cool for two minutes before removing the cookies: they will come off easily.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, fleur de sel and both sugars in a bowl. Mix dry to distribute the salt and yeast.
Add the softened butter and the egg. Work until the mixture is homogeneous, without overworking it (without kneading it too much, to keep a soft crumb).
Taste the dough. Adjust the salt or brown sugar according to the bitterness of your chocolate.
Stir in the chopped chocolate. Mix briefly, just to distribute it.
Shape into regular balls of 35 to 40 g. Squeeze them tightly in your hand so that they do not collapse in the cold.
Arrange them on a baking sheet, without touching, and place in the freezer. Once firm, transfer them to a bag or box. They will keep for three months.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Bake the frozen balls, spaced 5 cm (2 inches) apart: 10 minutes for a gooey center, 13 to 15 minutes for a classic texture. Let them cool on the baking sheet before transferring them to a wire rack.

title: Pan-fried bagels with skyr
intro: A dough without rising or kneading, where everything depends on patience during baking: the lid does the work of the oven.
titane: Preheating the pan empty and then covering it traps the heat around the bagel, cooking it by coating it, not just by contact. Don't touch the dough while it's still sticking: once the crust has formed, it will detach itself from the bottom. Forcing it too early will leave half the crust in the pan.
steps: Mix the skyr, flour, yeast, and salt in a bowl. Knead with a dough scraper or by hand until you obtain a smooth, pliable dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl. If it's too sticky, add a handful of flour, but no more.
Divide into five equal-sized pieces of dough. Roll each into a ball on a lightly floured surface.
Pierce the center of each ball with your finger, then widen the hole to about two centimeters. It will partially close during baking.
Brush the top with beaten egg, then sprinkle with seeds. Press lightly so they stick.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter or oil, and spread it with a wrist movement.
Place the bagels seed-side up, spacing them apart. Cover and reduce the heat to low-medium. Cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid more than once.

Check: the bottom should be golden brown and easily release from the pan. Gently turn over, cover, and bake for another 10 minutes. The bagels should have puffed up and been browned on both sides, and should feel firm to the touch.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack and let cool completely. On a wire rack, the steam escapes from underneath and the crust remains crisp.

To store: place them in a box or freezer bag for up to 3 months. Take them out the day before and place them in the refrigerator, then reheat them for 5 minutes in a covered pan over low heat before serving.

title: Parmesan cottage bites
intro: A soft dough, very little fat, and everything depends on the patience of the low heat: it is the parmesan crust that gives the crispness, not the oil.
titane: The covered pan works like a miniature oven. The heat rises, reflects under the lid, and cooks the tops of the pastries while the bases brown. There's no need to preheat a full oven for two trays of small pastries. Wait until each pastry releases itself from the bottom before turning it over: as long as it's sticking, the crust hasn't formed.
steps: Pour the cottage cheese into a bowl. Add the egg whites and whisk until smooth, with no visible lumps of cottage cheese.

Incorporate the flour all at once, then the 30g of Parmesan cheese, salt, dried onion, paprika and pepper. Work with a spatula until you obtain a smooth and supple dough that falls back from the ribbon when folded slowly.
Fill a piping bag with the dough. Let it rest for 5 minutes: the flour hydrates and the dough holds its shape better when piping.
Lightly oil the cold titanium pan, wiping it with absorbent paper to leave only a film. Spoon in 4 cm diameter bites, spacing them two fingers apart.
Sprinkle the top of each bite with the remaining Parmesan cheese.
Cover and place over low-medium heat. Cook for approximately 12 minutes. The pastries are ready to turn when they easily detach from the spatula; as long as they resist, leave them.
Turn them over, cover, and continue cooking for 5 to 6 minutes, until the Parmesan side is golden brown. Transfer them to a wire rack to allow steam to escape and the crust to dry.
For storage: allow to cool completely, then spread in freezer bags in a single layer. Up to 3 months.
When ready to serve, place the frozen bites directly into the titanium pan, over medium heat and covered, for 6 minutes, turning them over halfway through.

title: Freezable lasagna wraps
intro: It all comes down to the color of the meat: a well-seared Bolognese sauce can withstand freezing without losing its flavor.

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

ing: a mixture of grated mozzarella and cheddar cheese
titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the 800g of meat is added: it sears instead of boiling. Onions, meat, sauce reduction: everything is done in the same pan, and the juices (caramelized deposits at the bottom of the pan) remain in the sauce.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes: a drop of water should bead on it.
Pour in the grapeseed oil, add the sliced onions. Sweat them (cook without browning) for 5 minutes, until they become translucent.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the ground meat. Spread it out, then leave it alone: it will release from the metal once a crust has formed. Cook for 8 minutes, turning once.

Season with salt and pepper, then pour in the tomato sauce. Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the pan and let cool slightly.
On each tortilla, spread a spoonful of béchamel sauce, a spoonful of Bolognese sauce, and a handful of grated cheese. Roll tightly, folding in the sides.
Lay the wraps flat, without overlapping them, and freeze them. They will keep for 3 months.
The day before serving, transfer the wraps to the refrigerator for slow thawing.
Heat them in the oven or microwave until hot throughout.

Cover with a little béchamel sauce, top with grated cheese and bake until golden brown: under the oven grill, or in a covered titanium pan over high heat for a few minutes, until the cheese is golden and bubbly.

title: French fries topped with seared beef and caramelized onions
intro: It's all about the contrast: crispy fries under seared meat, baked in a crust before being topped.
titane: One pan for two cooking sessions. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil (high smoke point, it won't burn at high heat). The onions will caramelize first, then the meat will develop its crust. In between, a quick wipe with a paper towel is all it takes: the remaining juices will do the work for you.
steps: Cut the potatoes into even sticks. Soak them for 10 minutes in a large volume of cold water to remove the surface starch, then dry them thoroughly with a tea towel. A wet fry won't be crispy.
Mix the sticks with the oil, salt, paprika and rosemary.
Bake at 200°C, or use an air fryer, for 30 minutes. Stir three or four times during cooking, until golden brown and crispy.
Meanwhile, heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of oil.
Add the sliced onion. Let it brown without stirring; it will detach from the pan on its own when it's ready to be stirred. Cook for about ten minutes until it turns amber.
Deglaze (dissolve the browned bits stuck to the bottom with a liquid) with the balsamic cream. Scrape the bottom with a spatula, then transfer the onions to a serving plate.
Quickly wipe the pan, then put it back on high heat for 1 to 2 minutes without any food.

Mix the beef with the diced onion, paprika, and garlic powder. Spread it in a thick layer in the hot pan and leave it alone. It will release itself once a crust forms: that's the signal to turn it over and roughly break it up.
While the pan is cooking, whisk together the cream cheese, mustard, ketchup, sriracha, garlic powder, and salt. Stir in the chopped pickles last.
To assemble: place the fries at the bottom, top with the mozzarella so that it melts in the heat, then add the onions, the meat, and the sauce in thin strips.

title: Marinated chicken with peppers, parmesan potatoes
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's spice crust: dry marinade, very hot pan, and above all, no movement during searing.

ing.note: deseeded and cut into wide strips

ing: High smoke point olive oil, or clarified butter
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil or butter. The temperature rises quickly and evenly: the marinated chicken seals immediately, and the spices caramelize instead of sticking. Wait until the pieces release easily from the bottom of the pan before turning them. The same pan, simply wiped clean, will then be used to make the Parmesan sauce.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the potatoes into equal-sized cubes: this is essential for even cooking.
In a bowl, coat them with olive oil, then add the rosemary, garlic semolina, paprika, and salt. Finish with 30g of Parmesan cheese and mix by hand.
Spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer, without overlapping. Bake for 35 minutes, until golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out easily.

Meanwhile, combine the chicken cubes, bell pepper strips, and crushed garlic in a shallow dish. Add the paprika, curry powder, oregano, garlic powder, salt, cayenne pepper, and lemon juice. Stir until the meat is evenly coated with the spices. Let it rest while the other ingredients cook.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the fat. It should ripple without smoking.

Place the chicken and peppers in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Leave them undisturbed for 3 minutes: the pieces will separate on their own. Then turn them over to brown the other sides; cook for a total of 6 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, add the 20g of cream cheese and stir: it will coat the meat with a creamy veil without drowning it. Check that it is cooked through.
Remove the chicken (transfer it to a dish), then wipe the pan with absorbent paper, keeping the most colored juices.

Over low heat, pour in the milk, add the remaining 30g of Parmesan cheese and the 50g of cream cheese. Season with pepper and add the oregano. Let it reduce for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until you have a sauce that coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the potatoes from the oven and pour them into the pan. Mix to coat them, and serve with the chicken.

title: Roquefort smashed tacos
intro: The entire recipe lies in one side: that of the beef pressed against the hot metal, which must form its crust before being touched.
ing: teaspoon of brine taken from the jar of pickles
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, until a wisp of smoke rises. The titanium surface sears the smashed meat in one piece, without sticking, and then retains enough heat to melt the Roquefort cheese under the lid, with the heat off. One skillet, one pass.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes, until the first wisp of smoke appears.

Spread a tortilla on the work surface. Place one-third of the ground beef on top and press it down with your hand or the back of a spoon to cover the entire tortilla with an even layer, right to the edge.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika on the meat side.
Pour a drizzle of grapeseed oil into the pan. Place the meat taco against the metal and turn up the heat to high. Don't move it for 5 minutes: it will release itself once the crust is set.
Turn off the heat. Flip the taco over, crumble 30g of Roquefort cheese over the meat, and cover. Two minutes of residual heat will be enough to soften it.
Meanwhile, whisk together the fromage blanc, mustard, garlic powder, and pickle brine. Add the chopped mint, season with salt, and chill.

Remove from the pan and place on a plate. Chop the gherkins, thinly slice the red onion, and cut the cucumber into thin strips. Arrange these on top of the cheese along with the lettuce leaf, and drizzle with the sauce.
Fold in half and eat immediately, while the crust is still crisp. Repeat for the other two.

title: Pasta with chicken and mushrooms, cooked in one pan
intro: Everything hinges on the first minute: if the chicken really browns before the liquid arrives, the pasta will cook in a sauce that already has flavor.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains the heat when the chicken cubes are added: a crust forms instead of evaporating. Place the pieces in the skillet and leave them alone. They will stick, then release on their own once browned. This is the signal, not the stopwatch. If the skillet is full, work in two batches: a crowded surface cools down and the chicken releases its juices.
steps: Thinly slice the onion and mushrooms. Mince the garlic. Cut the pepper and chicken into even cubes, around 2 cm.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should ripple slightly.
Place the chicken in a single layer, without stirring it. Wait until it falls apart on its own, about 4 minutes, then add the onion, garlic, pepper and mushrooms.
Add the pasta, tomato puree and stock. Season with salt and pepper.
Mix, cover and simmer over medium heat for the cooking time indicated for your pasta, approximately 14 minutes. Stir halfway through and add a splash of hot water if the sauce thickens too quickly.
Remove from heat, stir in the cream cheese, then grate the Parmesan cheese over the top. Serve immediately.

title: Apple crumble, pan and oven
intro: It all comes down to the caramelization of the apples before the crumble: it's this that gives depth, not the sugar on top.
titane: The titanium pan goes from high heat to oven seamlessly. You caramelize the apples in it, cover them with the crumble topping, and bake the same pan. No transferring, no dishes to wash.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel the apples and cut them into small, even pieces, about one and a half centimeters in size.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the clarified butter: it should simmer without smoking or browning.

Add the apples, half the brown sugar, and the cinnamon. Reduce the heat to medium and let it cook for 10 minutes. Don't stir right away: the pieces will pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own once they've turned a caramel color. That's when it's time to turn them over.
Remove from heat and leave the apples in the pan.
In a bowl, mix the flour, the remaining brown sugar and the almond flour.
Add the softened butter and rub it in with your fingertips until you get irregular lumps, about the size of a hazelnut. Stop before the dough clumps together.
Spread the sand over the apples in an even layer, without packing it down.
Bake the pan as is for 35 minutes, until the crumble is golden brown and the juices are bubbling around the edges.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving: the filling holds its shape better.

title: Butternut squash gnocchi shaped like a pumpkin
intro: It all comes down to the moisture content of the puree: well-dried meat requires little flour, and the gnocchi remain light.

ing.note: piece, or approximately 700g of flesh once
/2 teaspoons for the dough, a pinch

titane: The titanium pan is used twice without being washed in between. First, it's preheated dry for one minute to evaporate the water from the butternut squash purée without it sticking. Then, it's used to thicken the cream sauce and sauté the poached gnocchi. One single utensil, from purée to plate.
steps: Cut the butternut squash into large cubes and steam them until a knife tip pierces them easily. Weigh out approximately 700g of flesh.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute. Mash the meat in it over low heat, without any oil. Stir for 5 minutes to dry it out (evaporate the water from the purée). The purée is ready when it no longer sticks and pulls away from the bottom of the pan in one piece. Transfer to another container and let it cool completely.

In the cold puree, mix the egg, salt, and half a teaspoon of nutmeg. Gradually add the flour, stopping as soon as the dough comes together and no longer sticks to your fingers. Depending on the water content of your squash, you may need a little more or less flour.
Take portions of approximately 30g and roll them into balls. Make vertical grooves all around with the back of a knife, then plant a pumpkin seed at the top.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Poach the gnocchi in small batches. As soon as they rise to the surface, count another 20 seconds, then remove them with a slotted spoon and drain them without stacking them.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes. Melt the clarified butter with the olive oil in it, reduce the heat to low and add the garlic. Let it infuse the fat with its aroma without browning.
Pour in the cream, add the cheese, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg. Let it reduce for 5 minutes over low heat, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Slide the gnocchi into the pan. Coat them with a flick of the wrist rather than a spoon, so as not to flatten the ridges. Serve immediately.

title: Chicken with mushrooms, butternut squash and potatoes
intro: It's all about patience: potatoes and chicken only turn over when they come apart on their own.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and intensely. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the first fat: a clean crust forms, the food releases itself, and the same pan can be used for searing and then simmering, without transferring or scraping.
steps: Peel the butternut squash and cut it into small cubes. Cut the potatoes into even wedges. Slice the mushrooms and onion, and mince the garlic.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil and add the clarified butter (butter with the milk solids removed, it can withstand high temperatures).
Place the potatoes in a single layer. Let them brown for 8 minutes without moving them: they will detach on their own when a crust has formed. Turn them over.
Add the butternut squash, stir, reduce the heat to medium. Pour in a splash of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until a knife inserted into the squash meets no resistance.
Remove the vegetables (take them out of the pan and set them aside in a dish).
Return the pan to high heat with a drizzle of grapeseed oil. Sear the chicken without touching it for about 8 minutes, until it falls off the bone. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside.
In the same pan, over medium-high heat, sauté the onion and mushrooms for 4 minutes, until the vegetable water has evaporated.
Add the garlic and thyme, mix for 1 minute over medium heat.

Return the chicken and vegetables to the pot. Pour in the stock, soy cream, and mustard. Cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, or until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Adjust the seasoning.

title: Butter chicken for the week
intro: A butter chicken base held over a single heat, where everything hinges on searing and toasting the spices before the liquid is added.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and withstands intense heat without flinching: preheat it empty for two to three minutes, then add the clarified butter. The chicken sears beautifully, the spices burst in the hot fat, and this aromatic base infuses the entire sauce. When it's time to serve again, the same pan can withstand the direct transfer from cold to hot without any sticking.
steps: Cut the chicken fillets into bite-sized pieces. Season lightly with salt. Mince the garlic.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the clarified butter.
Sauté the garlic for one minute over medium heat, until it turns golden and infuses the fat with its aroma. Do not let it brown any further.
Add the chicken and all the spices at once. Spread the pieces in a single layer.

Turn up the heat to high and let it sear for 5 minutes without touching it. The spices will toast (they heat dry in the fat and release their oils). Turn only when the meat easily lifts from the bottom of the pan.
Pour in the tomato coulis, then the fromage blanc. Mix, scraping the bottom to get the juices.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Add the honey at the end of cooking, taste, and adjust the salt.
Divide into freezer-safe containers or molds, dividing into portions of two to four servings. Allow to cool completely before sealing.
Freeze. The preparation will keep for 3 months.
To serve, defrost and then reheat over medium heat in the pan, or in the microwave, until the sauce is simmering again.

title: Three pasta sauces, to be frozen in portions
intro: Three bases that are prepared in the same pan one after the other, freeze flat and reheat in five minutes: the whole challenge lies in the fractionation of the liquids, never more than one liter at a time.

ing.note: to be poured in 1 L batches

titane: The titanium pan handles all three cooking methods without needing to be changed: a quick sear for the chicken, gentle and even heat for the roux, and then an uncovered reduction for the tomato sauce. Always preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any fat. Between sauces, wipe the pan with paper towels and reheat: the surface will be clean again, with no flavor transfer. The only caveat: a maximum of one liter of liquid per batch, otherwise the heat will drop and the béchamel sauce will simmer.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should ripple without smoking.

Increase the heat to medium-high and sear the chicken in a single layer, without moving it. It will release easily once a crust has formed; cook for a total of 8 minutes, turning it once. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Wipe the pan clean, reduce the heat to medium-low and melt the butter. Add the flour all at once and whisk for 2 to 3 minutes: the roux should remain light golden and smooth.
Gradually add the warm milk, a little at a time, whisking between each addition, without exceeding 1 liter per batch. Cook for 10 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take 1.5 L of this plain béchamel sauce and reserve it for the pesto.
Off the heat, whisk the parmesan into the remaining béchamel sauce, add the garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Return the chicken and its juices to the sauce, stir over low heat for one minute. The Alfredo is ready.
Wipe the pan, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, pour in the olive oil.
Sauté the minced garlic for 2 minutes over medium heat, until it becomes translucent and fragrant. Do not let it brown.
Add the cherry tomatoes, tomato paste and cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Let it reduce uncovered for 15 minutes over low-medium heat, crushing the tomatoes with a spatula. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon and the skins should have broken down.
In a blender, combine basil, cashews, olive oil, parmesan, salt and pepper. Blend in short bursts until you obtain a smooth but still textured paste.
Wipe the pan, preheat it, then gently reheat the reserved béchamel sauce in small quantities, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir the pesto into the hot béchamel sauce. Mix well: the basil will stop cooking at this point, and the color will remain green.

Allow all three sauces to cool completely, then divide them into flat freezer bags, one portion per bag. The arrabbiata and pesto béchamel sauces will keep for three months, and the chicken Alfredo sauce for two months.

To serve: defrost, gently reheat in a preheated pan, then add the drained pasta (cooked separately in plenty of water). Finish with a little Parmesan cheese or a spoonful of cream to restore the creaminess lost in the cold.

title: Mini brioches with skyr and chocolate chips
intro: A dough without rising or kneading, where skyr replaces both butter and rising time: everything depends on the texture of the mixture, which must remain supple without sticking.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop

titane: The titanium pan acts as a baking sheet. The dough is shaped inside while cold and placed directly into the oven: the bare metal conducts heat from below, browning the bases while the oven works on the tops. Once the crust has formed, the brioches release themselves—this is the most reliable sign that they are cooked.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Combine the skyr, flour, and yeast in a large bowl. Mix until you have a smooth, pliable dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl. If it sticks to your fingers, add the flour a little at a time.
Stir in the chocolate chips and mix briefly, just to distribute them.
Lightly flour the work surface. Shape into regular balls the size of a large walnut, rolling the dough between your palms.
Place the balls in the cold titanium pan, spacing them two centimeters apart. Cook them in batches rather than crowding them.
Beat the eggs with a fork. Brush the balls with beaten egg (this is what gives them their color and shine when they come out of the oven).
Place the pan in the oven for 20 minutes at 180°C. The brioches are cooked when the surface is golden and they easily detach from the metal.
Remove (transfer from the cooking container) to a wire rack and allow to cool completely before packaging.

title: Hot tuna and two-cheese sandwich
intro: It all comes down to the low heat and the lid: the cheese must melt before the bread gets too brown.

ing.note: (It can withstand higher heat without blackening)

titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, until hot but not smoking. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat: combined with clarified butter, it sears the bread without sticking. Then, reduce the heat to low and cover: the enveloping warmth melts the cheese while the top surface browns slowly.
steps: Mash the tuna with a fork in a bowl. Add the shallot, spring onion, parsley, gherkins and their juice.
Stir in the mayonnaise, sriracha, honey, chili oil, and lemon juice. Mix until you have a smooth but still slightly textured topping. Taste and adjust the salt if necessary.
Spread the filling on a slice of bread, pushing it to the edges.
Spread the mozzarella and then the cheddar on top. Close with the second slice and press lightly with the palm of your hand.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It should be hot, but not smoking.
Butter the outside of the sandwich with clarified butter, then place it against the pan. Reduce heat to low and cover.
Let it brown for about 4 minutes, without touching the sandwich. It's ready to be flipped when it releases easily and the other side is evenly browned.
Butter the still pale face, turn over with a quick movement, cover again.
Continue cooking for 4 minutes over low heat, until fully browned and the cheese is melting around the edges.
Remove from the pan and place on a board, let rest for 1 minute, then cut in half diagonally. Serve hot.

title: Mini brioches with Comté cheese
intro: A dough without leavening or rising, where everything depends on the moisture of the skyr and the direct contact with the hot metal.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop
the whitewash that gives color during baking

titane: The titanium pan goes straight from the countertop to the oven, handle and all. Its metal mass heats up more slowly than the oven floor, then radiates heat through the base: the bottom of the brioches develops a crisp crust while the crumb finishes setting. You'll know they're done when they release easily from the bottom, without any resistance.
steps: Combine the flour and baking powder in a large bowl. Add the skyr and mix until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl. It should remain soft, slightly sticky, and not spread out.
Incorporate the grated Comté cheese and work briefly, just to distribute it.
Flour your work surface. Shape the dough into about forty even balls, the size of an apricot. Roll them in your palm to smooth the surface.
Place the balls directly into the cold titanium pan, in a single layer and slightly spaced apart. Cook in batches if they don't all fit.
Beat the eggs and brush each ball with the egg wash, without letting it drip onto the bottom of the pan.

Place the pan in the oven at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes. The brioches are ready when they are golden brown and easily release from the bottom of the pan. Remove them from the oven (transfer them to a wire rack) to prevent condensation from forming underneath.

title: Roasted chickpeas with paprika and cheese
intro: Everything hinges on the cheese rind: it must adhere to the metal without being touched, otherwise it crumbles and the chickpeas remain soft.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. This allows the cheese to melt, then dry and crisp directly on the metal, whereas an oven would take twenty-five minutes. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then do not stir until the golden layer starts to detach on its own.
steps: Drain the chickpeas and rinse them in cold water. Spread them out on a clean cloth and dry them thoroughly: a damp seed will splatter during cooking and won't crisp up.
Combine the chickpeas, grated cheese, paprika and fleur de sel in a large bowl. Mix by hand so that each grain is coated.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and tilt the pan to distribute it.
Spread the mixture in a single layer. If the pan is too full, work in two batches: the chickpeas should touch the bottom, not pile up.
Sprinkle with pepper on top.

Let it roast undisturbed. The cheese will melt, then dry, and form a golden crust that easily detaches from the metal: that's the signal. Stir, reduce the heat to medium, and continue for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally for even browning.
Remove from the pan and place on a plate. Let cool to room temperature. The crispiness will set as it cools.
Divide into portions in bags and place in the freezer.
To serve, defrost, then reheat for 5 minutes in the hot titanium pan over medium-high heat, until crispy again.

title: Banana, petit suisse and chocolate ice cream bites
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the banana slices: too thin, they disappear under the topping; too thick, they remain hard when taken out of the freezer.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without a double boiler. The thin base distributes the heat evenly, preventing hot spots: the pieces melt smoothly, without any burnt bits sticking to the center. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture becomes smooth and flowing; the residual heat will finish the job.
steps: Cut the bananas into slices about 1.5 cm thick. Arrange them flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, without them touching.
In a bowl, work the petits suisses with the agave syrup until you obtain a smooth cream, without lumps.
Place a spoonful of this cream on each slice. Smooth it with the back of the spoon.
Add a dollop of peanut butter on top. Place the baking sheet in the freezer while you prepare the chocolate: the topping will adhere better to the glaze.

Break the chocolate into pieces in the cold titanium pan. Place over very low heat and stir continuously with a flexible spatula for about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat as soon as the chocolate is smooth and flowing.
Take out the baking sheet and drizzle (cover with an even layer) each bite with melted chocolate.
Return to the freezer for 45 minutes, until the bites are completely frozen and detach cleanly from the paper.
For storage, place sheets of parchment paper between the layers, put in an airtight bag and keep in the freezer for up to 3 months. Take them out 2 minutes before serving.

title: Three pasta sauces, in frozen portions
intro: Three bases that are prepared in the same pan, freeze in cubes and transform a packet of pasta into a real dinner: it all comes down to the crust of the meat, the warmth of the fire for the cheeses, and the cold for the pesto.
titane: Preheating the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes gives the ground beef a rich brown crust, impossible to achieve on a warm non-stick surface. This browning is the very essence of Bolognese sauce. And since the surface also tolerates long cooking times over very low heat, the cheese sauce and then the reheating of the cubes can be done in the same pan, without anything ever sticking.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should roll into a ball before evaporating.

Pour in the olive oil, then sauté the diced onion and carrot. Wait until they detach from the bottom of the pan on their own before stirring them: this is a sign that they are seared and not sweating.
Add the chopped garlic, mix for 30 seconds, then push everything to one side of the pan.

Increase the heat to medium-high and spread the ground beef evenly over the surface. Don't touch it. The meat will stick at first, then release itself once a crust has formed. Only then should you break it up with a spoon.
Add the tomato paste and let it cook for 1 minute (cook in contact with the metal until it darkens and loses its acidity).
Pour in the tomato sauce, half a glass of water, season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes over low heat, stirring two or three times.
Remove the Bolognese sauce from the pan and let it cool slightly. Rinse and dry the pan.

While simmering, blend the basil with the pine nuts, garlic, and salt. With the motor running, slowly drizzle in the oil, then stir in the Parmesan at the very last second to prevent it from overheating under the blades.

In a clean pan over low heat, warm the cream with the Comté, Gorgonzola, and Parmesan cheeses. Stir regularly until the cheeses have melted and the sauce is smooth. Season with nutmeg, white pepper, and salt at the end of cooking. Never let it boil: the cream will curdle.
Allow all three sauces to cool completely, then pour them into individual portion molds. One mold is equivalent to one serving for a plate of pasta.
Freeze. Once frozen, unmold and store in labeled bags.

When ready to serve, defrost preferably in the refrigerator the day before, then melt the cube in a pan over very low heat. Creamy sauces require the lowest possible heat and a little pasta cooking water to thicken.

title: Skyr bagels, baked in a pan
intro: Without baker's yeast or rising time: it is the skyr that gives the structure and the softness, provided that the dough is worked just enough so that it stops sticking.
titane: The pan goes directly from the countertop to the oven without any transfer. You place the bagels in the cold pan and put the whole thing in the oven. The metal mass absorbs the heat and radiates it through the bottom: the base browns as much as the top, and the crust, once formed, releases itself. No parchment paper, no baking sheet.
steps: Combine the skyr, flour, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Mix first with a spatula, then finish by hand.
Work the dough for two minutes on a lightly floured surface. It should become smooth and no longer stick to your fingers. Do not knead it any longer: it will become tough when baked.

Divide into five equal portions. Roll each into a log, seal the ends, then pierce the center with your index finger and widen the hole to about three centimeters. It will always close up a little in the oven.
Beat the egg yolk with a teaspoon of water. Brush the bagels with the mixture, then sprinkle with seeds, pressing them in lightly to make them stick.
Place the bagels directly into the cold titanium pan, spacing them about two fingers apart. Bake, pan and all, at 180°C (350°F) for 30 minutes. The pan is oven-safe.
Remove from the pan when the crust is thoroughly golden. Let it rest for three minutes: the bagels will then release cleanly, without sticking.

title: Spicy beef burritos with seared peppers
intro: It all comes down to the searing: colorful peppers and meat that browns instead of boiling in its own juices, otherwise the filling makes the wrap soggy.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when you place a cold object on top: this is what allows you to sear 1.5 kg of beef in a tight layer without the temperature dropping. Work in two batches if your pan is less than 28 cm in diameter.
steps: Dice the peppers into even pieces, slice the onions, and mince the garlic. Combine all the spice powders in a bowl: they will dissolve all at once.
Place the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the peppers in the pan, spread them out, then leave them undisturbed for 4 minutes. They will detach from the bottom on their own once they have browned.
Add onions and garlic, stir for 3 minutes until the onion becomes translucent.

Push the vegetables to one side. Increase the heat to high, add the beef in a tightly packed layer, and let it brown for 5 minutes without stirring. Then, crumble it with a spoon and continue cooking for 3 minutes, stirring the vegetables into the meat.
Reduce heat to medium. Pour in the bowl of spices, season with salt and pepper, and stir for 1 minute to activate them in the fat.

Stir in the tomato paste and honey. Cook over low heat for 5 minutes: the mixture should thicken and coat the back of a spoon, with no liquid remaining at the bottom. Transfer to a wide dish and let cool slightly.
Place a strip of warm meat on the bottom third of each tortilla. Sprinkle with grated cheese if using.
Fold the sides inwards, then roll tightly starting from the trimmed edge.
Store for 3 days in the refrigerator, or 3 months in the freezer, individually wrapped. Defrost overnight in the refrigerator, then reheat in a pan for 3 minutes per side to restore crispness.

title: Burger in lettuce leaves, seared steak and skyr sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the steak: a nice hot pan, no moving, and the salad stays crisp under the hot topping.

ing.note: minced, plus 1 teaspoon of its juice

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat. Preheat it empty, then oil it: the minced steak sears raw without sticking and forms a crisp crust while the onions finish caramelizing on the side, in the same cooking process.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. Holding your hand a few centimeters away should feel a dry, steady heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil; it should coat the surface while remaining fluid.
Sweat the sliced onion for 5 minutes over medium heat (soften it without letting it brown). It should become translucent, barely golden at the edges.
Push the onions to one side of the pan. Increase the heat to medium-high, add the steaks, and leave them undisturbed. They are ready to be flipped when they release easily from the bottom of the pan.
Turn them over, place a slice of cheddar on each one and continue for 3 minutes, until the cheese melts and the onions finish caramelizing.
Meanwhile, mix together in a bowl the skyr, mustard, ketchup, chopped pickle, its juice, and pepper. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, neither too runny nor too firm.
Lay the salad leaves flat on the plate, veins outwards, overlapping them.
Layer a steak, onions, tomato slices, a spoonful of sauce, then the second steak and the rest of the sauce.
