Fold the leaves around the filling, hold for a few seconds until the salad takes the shape, and serve immediately.

title: Skyr bagels
intro: A dough without rising or proofing: everything depends on drying the surface before baking, otherwise the crust remains pale and soft.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, grease it with a thin layer of clarified butter (melted butter with the whey and casein removed), then place the bagels in it. Cover: the trapped steam will cause the crumb to rise while the bottom browns. Since the pan can be used in the oven, finish baking the bagels in the same pan, without handling the still-fragile dough.
steps: Mix the skyr, flour, baking powder, and salt. Knead by hand until you obtain a smooth, homogeneous dough, free of dry flour lumps. It should pull away from the bowl without sticking to your fingers: add 10g of flour at a time if necessary.
Divide into 6 equal portions. Roll each into a log of approximately 20 cm, seal the ends into a ring and widen the central hole with your finger: it will close during cooking.
Brush the top and sides with beaten egg. Sprinkle with seeds. Let it rest for 10 minutes at room temperature, until the egg wash dries.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Heat a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, grease it, and place the bagels in it without crowding them. Cover and cook for 4 minutes: the bottoms should be amber-colored.
Remove the lid, place the pan in the oven, and continue baking for approximately 20 minutes. The bagels are cooked when the crust is evenly golden brown and they sound hollow when tapped.
Meanwhile, mix the cream cheese with the shallot, garlic powder, and chives. Season with salt and pepper, and refrigerate.
Let the bagels cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes, slice them in half and fill them.

title: Cereal bars with almonds and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to tamping: a tightly packed preparation by hand produces bars that break cleanly instead of crumbling.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. It heats up quickly and distributes heat evenly without hot spots: peanut butter melts without burning, and chocolate stays smooth instead of grainy. Wipe it dry between uses, and you'll only have one pan to wash.
steps: Combine the almonds, peanuts, oat flakes, puffed rice and chia seeds in a large bowl. Mix by hand to distribute the seeds.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Keep it within easy reach: the rest will happen quickly.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the peanut butter, honey, coconut oil, and vanilla extract. Stir for about 3 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy, without lumps.
Pour this hot mixture over the dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly: each flake must be coated.
Transfer to the baking sheet. Spread out, then press down firmly with the back of a spoon or with a second piece of baking paper, to an even thickness.
Wipe the pan with paper towels. Return it to low heat with the dark chocolate broken into pieces and the coconut oil. Stir until completely melted and glossy, about 3 minutes.
Coat (cover with an even layer) the mixture with melted chocolate. Smooth with a spatula.
Place in the refrigerator for 1 hour, until the chocolate has set and the mass is firm.
Remove from the mold, then cut into bars of approximately 20 cm using a large knife. Wipe the blade between cuts.
Store in the freezer for up to 3 months. Remove the bars from the freezer 10 minutes before eating.

title: Dark and milk chocolate fondant cooked in a pan
intro: It all comes down to heat: low enough for the chocolate to melt without graining, constant enough under lid so that the edges set while the center remains soft.
ing: The same quantity of milk baking chocolate
titane: The pan acts as both a mold and an oven. Place it over very low heat without preheating it empty: here, the food melts, it doesn't sear. Titanium conducts heat quickly, the crust forms sooner than in an oven, and the center retains its runny texture. Lift the lid halfway through cooking to check; the temperature rises faster than in a mold.
steps: Combine the two chocolates and the butter in a pan over very low heat. Stir with a silicone spatula until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture, free of any lumps. This should take 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs with the sugar in a bowl, just enough to make the mixture smooth and pale.

Remove the pan from the heat. Pour the cooled chocolate over the eggs in two additions, mixing slowly with a spatula: do not incorporate air, as this will cause the cake to rise and then collapse. Add the sifted flour and fleur de sel, and mix again until all traces of flour have disappeared.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, pour in the batter, and cover. Cook over very low heat for 25 minutes. Check around the 15-minute mark: the edges should be set, but the center should still be slightly wobbly when you shake the pan.
Let it cool slightly off the heat, in the pan. Carefully unmold onto a wire rack, then dust with unsweetened cocoa powder through a small sieve.

title: 'Three things prepared in advance: peanut cups, frozen banana bites, pancakes'
intro: Three formats for the same thirty-minute session: two that set in the cold while the third cooks in the pan, and the whole success lies in not rushing the setting of the chocolate or the turning of the pancakes.
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, before adding any oil or butter. Then add a drizzle of clarified butter (melted butter with the milk solids removed, as it can withstand higher heat) or grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, never smoke. The batter will set immediately upon contact, and the pancake will release easily when it's ready. Do not push it with a spatula before this signal.
steps: Work the peanut butter and almond flour together in a bowl until you get a soft dough that holds its shape on a spoon.
Distribute it into the paper molds, pressing down with the back of a spoon for a flat surface.
Melt the dark chocolate in a double boiler, then coat each mold to the top. Add a pinch of salt to the center if desired.
Refrigerate for 20 minutes, until the chocolate is set and matte on the surface.
Slice the bananas into thick rounds or in half lengthwise, depending on the desired bite size.
Mix the fromage frais and agave syrup until you obtain a smooth cream.
Arrange the bananas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover them with fromage frais cream, then place a dollop of peanut butter on each one.
Drizzle with melted dark chocolate.
Place the tray in the freezer until completely frozen, about 2 hours. Then transfer the bites to an airtight container.
Mix the cottage cheese, eggs, vanilla, maple syrup, yeast and flour until you have a perfectly smooth, grain-free batter.
Gently fold in the chocolate chips with a spatula, without remixing.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the fat. Wait until it simmers.

Pour small ladles of batter into the pan. Let it cook without touching it: when the edges are set and the pancake releases easily from the pan, flip it with a flick of the wrist and brown the other side. Wipe the pan clean between batches if any residue sticks.

title: Oat, banana and pecan bars
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas: when they are very spotted, they sweeten and bind the mixture without adding anything.
titane: The titanium pan is used here only for chocolate. Preheat it empty for 2 minutes over low heat, turn off the heat, and pour in the chocolate pieces. As soon as the first pieces melt, remove the pan from the heat and stir: the residual heat finishes the job. The chocolate remains smooth and shiny, without the need for a double boiler and without the risk of graining (solidifying into dry lumps).
steps: Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl until you obtain a smooth puree.
Add the rolled oats, milk, peanut butter, pecans, chia seeds, agave syrup, and 30g of chopped chocolate. Mix for 5 minutes, until the oats are evenly moistened.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Pour the mixture onto the paper and spread it to a thickness of 1.5 cm, pressing it down firmly with the back of a spoon. A compact mass will cut cleanly.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 minutes over low heat. Turn off the heat, pour in the 80g of chocolate, remove the pan as soon as it starts to melt and stir off the heat until smooth.
Coat (cover with a thin and even layer) the preparation with melted chocolate, smoothing with an offset spatula.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, until firm to the touch.
Lift the baking paper to unmold, then cut into even bars with a large knife, wiping the blade between each cut.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Chicken drumstick tagine with carrots and potatoes
intro: It all comes down to two things: proper colouring at the start, then very little water so that the vegetables cook in steam and not in broth.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a substitute for an earthenware dish. It heats up quickly, giving the onions and chicken the sear that a classic tagine achieves slowly. Then, the tightly fitting lid traps the moisture, and you switch to steaming mode (cooking covered in the steam released by the food). Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or fat: this prevents the chicken from sticking.
steps: Mix the drumsticks with the turmeric, cumin, sweet paprika, salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Massage the mixture into the meat to distribute the spices. Set aside while you prepare the vegetables.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then pour in the remaining olive oil.
Add the sliced onions, spread them evenly over the bottom and let them brown over medium heat. Stir sparingly: you're looking for color, not a compote.
Place the drumsticks on the bed of onions in a single layer. Do not move them while they are still attached. They will detach on their own once seared, after 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Scrape the remaining marinade over the chicken, pour in the water, cover and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Arrange the potatoes and carrots around the chicken, then place the tomato slices on top. Keep it in a single layer: the heat from the titanium circulates better this way.
Cover again and continue cooking over low heat for 30 minutes, until a knife inserted into the carrots meets no resistance. If the sauce remains too thin, remove the lid for the last 5 minutes.

title: Chicken, pepper and curry tacos
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the pan: hot enough to brown the chicken without drying it out, stable enough to brown the folded patties right after.

ing.note: it holds up better than olive oil in this respect

ing: portions of Laughing Cow-type processed cheese
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. This allows you to cook vegetables, sear chicken, and grill tacos all in the same pan, without any sticking or the need for a panini press. Always preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter: this ensures the food releases naturally.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, never smoke.
Sauté the onion for 4 minutes over medium-high heat, stirring constantly. It should become translucent and brown around the edges.

Add the bell peppers, water, salt, pepper, curry powder, and garlic. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 5 minutes, stirring two or three times. The water will deglaze (dissolving the browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan), and the bell peppers will remain tender with a touch of crunch.

Push the vegetables to one side of the pan. Return the pan to medium-high heat and sear the chicken pieces for 6 minutes, turning them once. Do not move them while they are still firm; they will release easily once a crust has formed. Check that there are no pink spots remaining in the center, then slice them into strips and mix them with the vegetables.
Remove the filling (transfer it to a dish). Cut each galette in half, fill each half with stuffing and a portion of cheese, then fold into a turnover.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, then return it to the pan and reheat over medium-high heat. Sear the folded tacos for 1 to 2 minutes per side, pressing down with the back of a spatula. The tortilla should be golden brown and crisp, with the cheese melted.

title: Pan-fried doughnuts with sugar
intro: A leavened dough rich in butter, cooked in a thin film of oil rather than in a bath: what matters is the regular temperature of the pan and the patience before turning.
ing: Finely grated zest of an untreated lemon
Neutral oil with a high smoke point
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in a thin stream of oil. The surface heats up evenly and sears the dough on contact: a crust forms without the doughnut absorbing the oil. The result is a golden shell and a soft, moist center, using ten times less oil than deep-frying.
steps: Crumble the fresh yeast into the lukewarm milk and let it dissolve for a minute. The milk should be barely lukewarm to the touch: if it's too hot, it will kill the yeast.
Break the eggs into this mixture and whisk to combine.
Incorporate the caster sugar, vanilla sugar, a pinch of salt and the lemon zest. Mix well.
Add the flour and baking powder. Knead for 8 minutes, until you obtain a smooth dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Add the softened butter in small pieces and knead for another 5 minutes, until it disappears completely into the dough.
Cover with plastic wrap, then with a cloth and let rise (the fermentation that makes the dough expand) for 1 hour 30 minutes at room temperature. The dough should double in size.
Roll out on a floured surface to a thickness of 1.5 cm. Cut out the shapes of your choice: triangles, squares, circles, strips.
Cover with a cloth and let it rest for 20 minutes: the pieces should inflate slightly.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the oil. It will barely simmer when it's ready.

Place the doughnuts loosely in the pan, three or four at a time. Let them brown without touching them: they will release on their own when the crust is ready. Turn them over and cook for another 3 minutes.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto absorbent paper, then roll them in sugar while they are still warm: it sticks better.
If you are filling them, pierce the side and inject melted chocolate, compote or coulis with a pipette.

title: Pan-fried pizza, homemade leavened dough
intro: Everything hinges on the direct contact of the dough with the hot metal: this is what gives the crispy base that a domestic oven struggles to produce.

ing.note: or 250g of T55 flour and 250g of bread flour
plus a fillet for the pan
Drained mozzarella, grilled vegetables, white of

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty, then oil it just before adding the dough: the disc will be seared the second it touches the bottom. The lid then takes over, melting the filling from above, like an oven dome.
steps: Combine flour, water, crumbled yeast, salt, and olive oil in a bowl. Mix, then knead until you obtain a smooth dough that no longer sticks to your fingers. Shape into a ball.
Cover with film then with a cloth. Let rise for 1 hour 30 minutes at room temperature, until the volume has doubled.
Deflate the dough (press it down with the palm of your hand to release the fermentation gases). Take a ball of dough the size of the bottom of your pan. Cover the rest and set it aside.

Flour your work surface. Flatten the dough ball by hand, from the center outwards, pushing the air towards the edge. Do not use a rolling pin: it will flatten the texture. Aim for a disc slightly smaller than the diameter of your pan.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It's ready when a drop of water sizzles immediately. Drizzle in some olive oil and slide the pastry disc into the pan.
Cover. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes: the bottom should be golden brown and the pastry should easily detach when you lift it with a spatula.
Turn the pastry over. Spread the tomato sauce on the already cooked side, distribute the filling, sprinkle with oregano.

Cover again, reduce the heat to medium-low, and continue cooking for 4 to 5 minutes, until the cheese melts and the bottom sounds hollow when pierced with a spatula. If you want to brown the top, finish under the oven broiler for 2 to 3 minutes.

title: Swiss brioche buns with pastry cream and chocolate chips
intro: It all comes down to two things: dough kneaded long enough to develop the gluten network, and pastry cream cooled completely before shaping.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan and baking dish. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat before pouring in the milk: the heat is distributed evenly, and the cream thickens without sticking to the bottom. Once the Swiss pastries are shaped, return them to the same pan to go in the oven, where the coating ensures even browning underneath.
steps: Crumble the yeast into the lukewarm milk and let it dissolve for 10 minutes.
Pour the flour, sugar, salt, eggs and yeast milk into the bowl of the food processor. Keep the butter aside.
Knead for 5 minutes at slow speed, until the dough comes together.
Add the softened butter in small pieces and knead for another 20 minutes. The dough should pull away from the sides of the bowl and form a thin film when you stretch it between your fingers.
Cover with a cloth and let rise for 1 hour 30 minutes at room temperature, until doubled in volume.
Meanwhile, preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat.
Split the vanilla pods lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Pour the milk, seeds, and pods into the hot pan. Heat for 2 minutes, being careful not to let it boil.
Remove from heat, transfer to a bowl and let steep for 10 minutes. Remove the pods.
Whisk the egg yolks briefly with the sugar, just to loosen them, then stir in the cornflour.
Pour half of the hot vanilla milk over this mixture while whisking: this tempers the yolks and prevents them from coagulating.
Pour the mixture back into the pan with the remaining milk. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the butter.
Remove (transfer from the cooking utensil) to a dish, cover with film — film placed directly on the cream to prevent a skin from forming — and let cool completely.
Degas the dough (release the fermentation gas by punching it down) on a floured surface.
Roll it out to a thickness of 6 mm, then cut it into strips 6 cm wide.
Smooth the cold cream with a whisk, spread it lengthwise on one half of each strip, and sprinkle with chocolate chips.
Fold the bare dough over the filling, lightly seal the edges, then cut into rectangles of approximately 8 cm.
Arrange them in the titanium pan without packing them tightly, cover with a cloth and let rise for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mix the egg yolk and milk, then brush the mixture over the egg wash.
Bake for 13 minutes, until the top is evenly golden brown. Let it cool slightly before removing from the pan.

title: Banana, chocolate and coconut cake
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: spotted skin, almost candied flesh, it is this that provides the sugar and the structure, since there is no flour.

ing.note: It can withstand high temperatures without

titane: The titanium pan serves as a mold. Preheated empty and greased with clarified butter, it receives the batter and goes straight into the oven. Once the cake is unmolded and the pan wiped dry, it becomes a saucepan again for melting the chocolate. A single utensil, from start to finish.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 140°C.
Remove from heat and brush the bottom and sides of the pan with clarified butter. Set aside.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until the mixture lightens in color and becomes airy: the volume should triple. This should take 4 to 5 minutes with a mixer.
Add the vanilla and cornflour, whisk for just a few seconds.
Blend the bananas with an immersion blender. Aim for a thick puree: if it's too runny, it will loosen the mixture and the cake will collapse.
Incorporate the puree into the egg-sugar mixture using a spatula, lifting the mass to retain air.

Pour into the pan, smooth the surface, and bake for 50 minutes at 140°C (275°F). The surface should be set and golden brown, with the center still slightly soft to the touch. Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes before turning it out onto a wire rack.
Wipe the pan clean. Over very low heat, melt the chopped chocolate with the cream, stirring constantly until you have a smooth ganache. Remove from the heat as soon as the last piece disappears.
Spread the glaze over the cooled cake and sprinkle with shredded coconut. Serve warm or cold.

title: Chebakia Cheesecake
intro: The chebakia, blended into a shortbread base, provides the honey and sesame that the fresh cheese mixture deliberately keeps discreet.
ing: vanilla extract or orange blossom water
titane: The oven-safe titanium pan replaces the springform pan: you press the base into it, pour in the batter, bake it, and serve it. Its metallic mass withstands the initial 180°C and then evenly releases the remaining 90°C, preventing dry edges and the central crack that often occurs when cheesecakes are baked in a thin pan.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Blend the 300g of chebakia until you obtain a coarse powder, similar to crumbled biscuits. The honey is enough to bind it; do not add butter.
Spread this powder evenly in the bottom of the cold titanium pan. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon, pushing it up slightly by about a centimeter.
Beat the cream cheese for just a few seconds, just long enough to loosen it (soften it without aerating it).
Pour in the cream, beat briefly. Add the sugar, mix.
Incorporate the eggs one at a time, mixing just enough between each addition to incorporate them. Too much air at this stage will cause the cake to rise and then collapse.
Add vanilla or orange blossom fragrance.
Sift the cornflour over the mixture and stir. Pour in the milk and smooth until you obtain a homogeneous and fluid cream.
Pour the mixture onto the base, into the pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 180°C, until the surface is colored.
Lower the oven to 90°C and continue baking for 60 minutes. The center should still jiggle slightly when you move the pan.
Turn off the oven and leave the pan inside, door closed, for another hour. The cooking process will finish on its own.
Let it cool to room temperature, then place the pan in the refrigerator overnight. The texture is only just right at that point.
When ready to serve, sprinkle with chebakia crumbs and sesame seeds. Serve directly from the pan.

title: Pan-fried peach and mozzarella toasts
intro: It all comes down to the bread: golden on the surface, still soft in the center, and topped off the heat so that the mozzarella melts without cooking.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat. Preheated empty, it browns the bread on the surface before the inside dries out. Once removed from the heat, the remaining warmth is enough to soften the mozzarella: no need to return it to the flame.
steps: Cut the peaches into even slices of half a centimeter. Set them aside on a plate.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. A drop of water dropped into the pan should sizzle and retract.
Add the clarified butter and a drizzle of olive oil. Place the bread slices flat.
Let it brown for 3 minutes without touching it. The bread will release itself from the surface when the side is ready: that's the signal to flip it. Cook for another minute on the second side.
Remove the pan from the heat. Arrange the peach slices on the warm bread, then add the torn mozzarella directly to the pan.
Sprinkle with mint, season with fleur de sel, and pepper. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve immediately.

title: Bruschetta with cherry tomatoes and burrata
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the bread: toasted in garlic butter in the pan, it must remain firm enough to support the burrata without collapsing.
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before placing the buttered bread inside. The buttered side will sear on contact and form an even crust in just a few minutes, without sticking or the pale patches that occur when toasted. Do not press or move the bread: it will release easily when it's ready.
steps: Work the softened butter with the chopped garlic until you obtain a smooth paste.
Spread one side of each slice of bread generously with this garlic butter.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Place the slices buttered-side down in the pan. Let them brown for 3 to 4 minutes without pressing or moving them. Garlic butter browns quickly: rely on the color rather than the time.
Meanwhile, cut the cherry tomatoes in half, or into quarters for the larger ones. Salt them lightly and set aside.
When the bread comes away easily and has an amber side, remove it (take it out of the pan to stop the cooking) onto a board, toasted side up.
Tear the burrata by hand and distribute it over the still-warm slices. Add the tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil, add a twist of pepper, adjust the salt and sprinkle with basil.

title: Crab, avocado and lime toasts
intro: It's all about the contrast: only one side of the bread is toasted, the other remains soft to hold the filling without cracking.
ing: Crab meat, brown crab or spider crab

ing.note: piece, green, deseeded then finely chopped

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. The bread browns instantly, on one clean side, without sticking and without the inside having time to dry out.
steps: Mash the avocado flesh with a fork in a bowl. Add the chopped jalapeño, lime juice, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Keep it chunky; don't aim for a smooth puree.
In a second bowl, loosen the crabmeat with the chopped coriander, 2 tablespoons of olive oil and a few drops of lemon juice. Mix with a fork, without crushing the fibers.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It is ready when a drop of water sizzles and evaporates immediately.
Pour in the grapeseed oil, place the bread slices flat in the pan and leave them untouched for 5 minutes. The bread will release itself from the pan when the top is golden brown and crispy.
Remove (from pan and set aside) the slices onto a rack, grilled side up, and salt this still-warm side.
Spread the avocado on the soft side, then arrange the crab on top. Zest the lemon (using a fine grater) over the toasts and place a wedge on the side. Serve immediately.

title: Ratte potato gnocchi, almond pesto and parmesan
intro: It all comes down to the dryness of the pulp: a baked potato accepts very little flour, and that's where the gnocchi become light.
ing: Ratte potato pulp cooked in the oven and then passed through a vegetable mill
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two to three minutes when empty. The poached gnocchi, still moist, are tossed in all at once: they stick, form a crust, then release easily. Don't move them before this point. The pesto is then stirred in off the heat, in the same pan, so it stays green and doesn't cook.
steps: Pour the still-warm potato pulp into a bowl. Let it dry for a few moments in the open air; the steam should escape.
Add the grated parmesan, egg yolks, flour and salt. Knead by hand until you obtain a smooth dough, without overworking it.
Spread the mixture onto a baking sheet and sprinkle with potato starch. Chill for a few minutes until the dough firms up.
Divide the dough into balls of approximately 8g each. Roll them over the back of a fork to create ridges, then place them on a plate dusted with cornflour. Refrigerate.
Blend the almond flour, garlic, parmesan and basil in a blender.
Pour in the olive oil and lemon juice, blend again. Season with salt and pepper, and give it one last pulse in the blender.
Bring a pot of salted water to a simmer—just enough to cover the gnocchi, no more. Drop them in and remove them as soon as they rise to the surface.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Add the olive oil: it should shimmer slightly.

Drain the gnocchi using a slotted spoon (a large, perforated one) and transfer them all at once to the pan. Let them brown without touching them. They will release from the pan on their own once golden.
Turn off the heat. Add the pesto and mix gently to coat.
Arrange on a plate, grate lemon zest over the top, add the parmesan shavings and basil.

title: Poached pears, saffron custard and gianduja sauce
intro: It all comes down to temperature: a custard made too quickly curdles, a chocolate sauce emulsified too quickly remains dull.

ing.note: (syrup: 400 g of sugar per 1 liter of water)

titane: The titanium pan is used twice, first for the cream and then for the sauce. Its conductivity is excellent: keep the heat medium-low and move the spatula all over the surface, including the edges, otherwise the cream will curdle around the edges before it coats the center. Between the two preparations, rinse the pan with hot water and dry it.
steps: Zest the oranges. Reserve a third of the zest for garnish. Pour the milk into the pan with the remaining zest and heat over medium heat for 5 minutes. Keep an eye on it: the large surface area accelerates evaporation.
In a bowl, whisk the yolks with the vanilla sugar and saffron until pale (the mixture will lighten and thicken).
Pour the hot milk over it in a thin stream, whisking for only a few seconds.

Pour the mixture back into the pan. Cook for 4 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring with a spatula, without ever letting it simmer, until the cream coats the back of a spoon (it sticks to the spatula and a finger line remains clear).
Remove from heat immediately (transfer to a cold container) to stop the cooking process. Let cool slightly, then refrigerate.
Rinse and dry the pan. Bring the remaining milk and cream to a boil over medium heat.
Combine the chocolate and gianduja in a mixing bowl.
Pour the boiling liquid over the chocolate in three stages, mixing vigorously from the center outwards with each addition. The emulsion should become smooth and glossy.
Spoon a few dollops of custard into the bottom of each soup plate.
Place a drained pear in the center.
Scatter the reserved orange zest over the top.
Drizzle with warm gianduja sauce and serve immediately.

title: Caramelized apple mille-feuille with salted caramel sauce
intro: It all comes down to two dry cooking processes: puff pastry crushed and vitrified in the oven, apples left alone until they take on color.

ing.note: peeled and then cut into balls with a spoon

titane: Use just one pan for both the apples and the caramel. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the butter: the heat is already evenly distributed, and the apple balls will color instantly instead of releasing their juices. A quick wipe with a paper towel between the two cooking stages is all that's needed. The bare pan allows the sugar to melt without creating hot spots, and the caramel will easily detach with a spatula.
steps: Unroll the puff pastry on the work surface. Cover it generously with granulated sugar, covering the entire surface.
Roll the dough into a tight sausage shape, then cut into one-centimeter pieces.
Place each piece flat and roll it out into a thin oval: these are the arlettes (caramelized puff pastries baked flat). You will need twelve.
Arrange them on a baking sheet between two sheets of parchment paper, place a second baking sheet on top to prevent them from puffing up. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Take them out, remove the baking sheet and the paper on top, and dust them with icing sugar.
Cover again, return to the oven at 200°C for 10 minutes, until the sugar vitrifies. Let cool under the baking sheet.
Whip the very cold cream until it forms stiff peaks. Refrigerate.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then melt the 50g of butter in it.

Add the apple balls and vanilla sugar, and increase the heat to medium-high. Do not stir: the apples are ready to be turned when they easily release from the bottom of the pan and have a golden-brown side. Continue cooking until they are soft.
Remove them (transfer them out of the pan) onto a plate. Wipe the pan with paper towels.
Pour the caster sugar into the dry pan over medium heat. Let it melt without stirring, tilting the pan if necessary, until it reaches a dark golden color.
Remove from heat, add the cubes of semi-salted butter and mix with a spatula.
Add the cream in a thin stream, stirring constantly. If any sugar lumps remain, return the sauce to low heat for a few seconds. Set the sauce aside.
In each plate: a spoonful of whipped cream as a base, an arlette placed on top, more cream, a few apple balls all around, a second arlette.
Repeat once, then top with a third arlette.
Drizzle a line of salted caramel around the plate. Serve immediately, as the puff pastry becomes soggy quickly.

title: Lamb chops, salsa verde and orange parsnips
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the parsnip takes on its color and orange glaze, then the lamb arrives on a wiped and once again burning hot surface.

ing.note: zest removed and reserved for the salsa
a quarter of a bunch, leaves only

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before each cooking stage. The temperature rises quickly: the parsnip caramelizes without falling apart, and the cutlets form a crisp crust while the center remains pink. In between, a simple wipe with a paper towel is all it takes; no need to change utensils.
steps: Blend the three herbs and garlic together in short bursts until you obtain a still coarse mixture.

Pour in the olive oil, lemon juice, orange zest, cumin, and Tabasco sauce. Blend briefly. The salsa should remain runny and slightly grainy. Adjust the seasoning with salt and set aside at room temperature.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then melt the clarified butter in it.
Pour the diced parsnips into an even layer. Let them brown without touching them: they will detach on their own when the browned side is set. Then turn them over.
Deglaze the pan with the orange juice. Reduce the liquid until it coats the cubes. Season with salt and pepper, then transfer to a covered dish and keep warm.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper. Place it back on high heat empty for 2 to 3 minutes.
Season the chops on both sides with salt. Add olive oil and a knob of butter to the pan, place the chops in it without crowding them, in two batches if necessary.
Don't move them while they're still sticking. When they release on their own, turn them over and spoon the foaming fat over them for 1 to 2 minutes. Let them rest for 3 minutes on a wire rack.
Draw a line of salsa verde on each plate. Place three chops on top, add the parsnips and their reduced orange juice on the side, and sprinkle with buckwheat.

title: Chocolate-peanut skillet brownie
intro: Everything hinges on the sabayon (egg-sugar mixture whipped until it triples in volume): it is what gives the cake its soft texture, and the spatula (flexible spatula) preserves it.
ing: clarified butter or oil with a high smoke point
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before pouring in the batter, then place it directly in the oven with the lid on. The immediate heat will set the edges and create a thin, caramelized crust, while the center remains soft and moist. The edges will shrink on their own at the end of baking: it will release easily, without needing a mold or parchment paper.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then remove it from the heat and set it aside while preparing the batter.
Melt the chopped chocolate and butter together in a double boiler over a gentle simmer. Stir until smooth and glossy, then remove from the heat.
In the bowl of a mixer, combine the eggs and sugar. Whisk until the mixture has doubled in volume, lightened in color, and become smooth.
Chop the peanuts with a knife, keeping some irregular pieces for textural contrast.
Sift the flour and then the cocoa over the sabayon. Incorporate them with a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom to the top, without whisking.
Add the peanuts and the still-warm chocolate-butter mixture. Incorporate in the same way, until the batter is smooth and no more.

Brush the bottom and sides of the hot pan with clarified butter. Pour in the batter: aim for a thickness of 3 to 4 cm. If it's thinner, the brownie will dry out; if it's thicker, the center will remain raw.
Cover and bake for 22 minutes at 200°C. The center should remain slightly wobbly and the edges should pull away from the pan on their own.
Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan, unmold onto a wire rack, sprinkle with icing sugar and serve warm.

title: Chocolate mousse
intro: Everything depends on the temperature of the chocolate when it meets the yolks: too hot it cooks them, too cold it solidifies and the mousse becomes grainy.

ing.note: 30g for the yolks and 30g for tightening

titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, it distributes heat evenly enough to melt chocolate and butter without them sticking, and then serves as a mixing bowl for the whisked egg yolks. Only one surface to wash before moving on to the egg whites.
steps: Place the pan over very low heat. Add the chopped chocolate and butter. Stir regularly until smooth and glossy, with no hard spots. This should take 4 to 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and continue stirring for a few seconds to combine. Let it cool slightly while you prepare the rest.
Separate the eggs: the whites in a dry mixing bowl, the yolks in a separate bowl.

Pour 30g of sugar over the egg yolks and whisk immediately until pale (whisk until the mixture lightens in color and thickens). Sugar left in contact with the yolks without being stirred will burn them and form grains.

Whisk the egg whites with an electric mixer. As soon as they begin to foam, add the remaining 30g of sugar, then increase the speed to stiffen them (firm them at the end of the whisking process). They should be firm, glossy, and hold their shape when whisked.
Check the chocolate: it should be lukewarm, still fluid, and pliable enough to touch. Pour in the whisked egg yolks and mix in the pan until you have a smooth and homogeneous mixture.
Whisk in a quarter of the egg whites, quite frankly, to loosen the mixture.

Add the remaining egg whites in two batches, using a flexible spatula. Cut the mixture in half, then fold it back over the egg whites, rotating the bowl a quarter turn. Stop as soon as the color is uniform.
Fill a piping bag and pipe into individual jars, bringing the bag up to the center to avoid bubbles.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight: the mousse firms up and the chocolate flavor settles.

title: Creamy rice pudding with orange zest
intro: Everything hinges on the starch in the rice and the binding with the yolks: slow cooking, spatula often in hand, thorough cooling.

ing.note: rinsed briefly under cold water (we keep

ing: The zest of an untreated orange
titane: The pan heats up quickly and without any hot spots: the milk simmers without sticking, even over a prolonged medium heat. And because it goes directly from the stovetop to the ice bath without any transition, the egg yolk binding stops at the precise moment it's ready, without needing to transfer the mixture.
steps: Rinse the rice for ten seconds in cold water, no longer. Drain. The remaining starch film will form the cream.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Add the rice and milk. Bring to a simmer: the surface should tremble, not boil.
Add the orange zest.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently with a spatula and scraping the bottom well. Allow about thirty minutes: the rice should be tender and the milk should have thickened around the grains.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar in a bowl until the mixture lightens in color and thickens slightly.
Temper: take two spoonfuls of hot rice pudding, pour them over the yolks while whisking, then pour everything back into the pan.
Return to medium heat and stir constantly until thickened. The cream should coat the back of a spatula. Do not let it boil.
Place the pan on an ice bath. Stir for one minute to stop the cooking process completely, then let it cool thoroughly.
Whip the very cold cream in a chilled bowl. Stop at a soft, not stiff, texture.
Gently fold it into the cold rice pudding in three stages, using a spatula and lifting the mixture. Chill for one hour before serving.

title: Potato tortilla
intro: It all comes down to the colouring of the potatoes: they must stick, form a crust, then detach on their own before being touched.
titane: The pan goes straight from the hot pan to the oven. You sear the onion and potatoes over high heat, pour the eggs over them, bake, flip, and finish. All done with one utensil. When you flip it, the tortilla will release itself as soon as the crust has formed; if it resists, it's not ready.
steps: Peel the potatoes and place them one by one in a bowl of cold water while you process them all: they will not turn black.
Cut them into even 2 cm pieces. Place them in a saucepan of lightly salted cold water. Starting with cold water ensures even cooking all the way through.
Bring to a boil over high heat. As soon as the water is boiling vigorously, the potatoes should be tender on the surface and still firm in the center.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion.
Drain the potatoes immediately. Let them air dry for a few minutes.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the olive oil; it should ripple immediately.
Throw the onion into the hot pan. Let it become translucent, then take on the first colours.

Add the drained potatoes, reduce the heat to medium-high, and let them brown in the fat, without adding any liquid. Do not stir while they are still sticking; they will detach from the bottom of the pan on their own once a crust has formed. This should take about ten minutes, turning them two or three times.
Add half the herbs if you are using them, then remove the pan from the heat.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Crack the eggs one by one into an intermediate bowl before combining them: a questionable egg will not ruin the whole thing.
Season with salt and pepper, whisk gently until well combined. Stir in the remaining herbs.
Return the pan to high heat with a drizzle of oil. Pour the eggs over the potatoes and onion, spreading them with a flick of the wrist.
Reduce heat to medium. Let the edges set and the bottom cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Place the pan in the oven as is, for 10 minutes at 180°C, until the center no longer jiggles.
Run a spatula all around to loosen the edges. Place a plate on the pan and flip it over in one swift motion.
Slide the reversed tortilla into the still-hot pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes to brown the second side. Let it rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

title: Soft-boiled eggs with spinach and Mornay sauce
intro: It all comes down to two short cooking times: six minutes for the egg, thirty seconds for the spinach.
titane: One pan from start to finish. It heats the sauce, sears the spinach with garlic, then goes straight into the oven for the gratin. The intense heat of the titanium pan wilts the spinach before it releases its water, and the direct pass under the oven's heating element saves you an extra gratin dish to wash. Always preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any fat.
steps: Bring a small saucepan of water to a boil, just enough to cover the eggs. Prepare a bowl of very cold water alongside it.
Separate two eggs (whites from yolks). Set aside the yolks, keep the whites for another use.
Sort and wash the spinach, remove the stems from the large leaves, and drain them thoroughly.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the béchamel sauce. Heat it until it just begins to simmer.
Place the eggs in simmering water and cook for exactly 6 minutes over medium heat. Immediately transfer them to cold water.
Lower the heat under the béchamel sauce. Once it's not boiling vigorously, whisk in the egg yolks one by one: they should bind the sauce, not coagulate.
Add 80g of grated cheese and stir until the sauce is smooth. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Transfer to a bowl.
Carefully peel the cooled eggs under running water, without piercing the yolk. Set them aside.
Wipe the pan clean, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the clarified butter and crushed garlic. The butter should sizzle without smoking.
Add the spinach in two batches to avoid overloading the pan. Drop it in for 30 seconds: it will detach itself from the metal with the movement of the pan and remain firm.
Pour half of the mornay sauce over the spinach, mix and turn off the heat.
Level the bed of spinach in the pan. Place the eggs on top, and cover with the remaining sauce.
Scatter the remaining 40g of cheese over the top. Bake the pan as is for 5 minutes at 220°C, until golden brown. Serve immediately.

title: Caesar salad with garlic croutons
intro: It all comes down to two things: croutons that stay dry in the center and a sauce that's thick enough to stick to the sheet.

ing.note: plus a whole piece for the finishing touch

ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the bread is added. As a result, a crust forms before the crumb has time to absorb the oil. Place the cubes in the pan, then leave them alone. As long as they stick, the other side isn't ready. They'll release on their own once golden brown. The bare, uncoated surface also allows the crushed garlic to caramelize in direct contact with the bread.
steps: Cut the bread into cubes of about two centimeters. Keep them regular: this is what gives an even colouring.
Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water thrown onto it should sizzle and evaporate immediately.

Pour the olive oil into the pan, add the bread cubes in a single layer, and the crushed garlic clove. Let them brown for 5 minutes without stirring, turning them only when they begin to separate from the pan on their own. Transfer them to a plate and let them cool.
In a bowl, mash the anchovies with a fork and the grated parmesan until you get a coarse paste.
Add the mustard, soy sauce, lemon juice and egg yolk. Whisk until smooth.

Whisk in the oil in a thin stream, whisking constantly, as you would for mayonnaise. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon. Season with pepper. Taste before adding salt: the anchovies and Parmesan already contribute a lot.
Separate the romaine leaves, wash them, and dry them thoroughly. A damp leaf will not absorb the sauce.
Pour the sauce over the leaves and mix by hand, lifting from underneath. Fingers distribute better than cutlery and don't damage the ribs.
Add the cooled croutons, grate the parmesan over the top at the last moment and serve.

title: Gluten-free raspberry and almond cake
intro: A cake whose bottom caramelizes in a pan before ending up in the oven: it is this direct contact with the hot metal that makes all the difference in texture.

ing.note: g, or 70 g of vegetable oil

titane: Preheat the empty skillet over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then brush it with a thin layer of oil or butter. The batter poured onto this hot base sets immediately: a golden crust forms while the center remains soft. The skillet then goes directly into the oven as is, without transferring the batter, thus ensuring the cooking process continues uninterrupted.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until the mixture turns white and doubles in volume.
Pour in the melted butter, then the yogurt. Mix gently.
Combine the oat flour, cornflour, almond flour, baking powder, and fleur de sel. Stop mixing as soon as the dough is smooth.
Heat the empty pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Brush it with clarified butter or grapeseed oil: the fat should ripple slightly, without smoking.
Pour half the batter into the hot pan. Spread a layer of raspberries, cover with the remaining batter, then arrange the remaining raspberries on top.
Cover and cook over low heat until the top begins to set.
Place the removed covered pan in the oven for approximately 40 minutes of total cooking time. The cake is ready when the surface is golden brown and the edges have pulled away from the sides.
Let it cool slightly in the pan. Only remove from the pan when the cake comes away easily, without using a spatula.

title: Chocolate rolled log, cooked in a pan
intro: It all comes down to two things: a meringue that is stiff enough to support the biscuit, and rolling done while still hot, as soon as it comes out of the pan.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the pan

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then lightly grease it with a thin film. This pan serves as both the ganache pan and the sponge cake mold: pour in the batter, spread it into a thin, even layer, and cover. The lid traps the steam and replicates the enveloping heat of an oven, while the bare titanium diffuses heat without creating hot spots. The sponge is ready when it shrinks back on its own from the edges and the surface is no longer sticky to the touch.
steps: Heat the cream in the pan over medium heat until it just begins to simmer, about 5 minutes.
Pour it in three stages over the chopped chocolate, mixing from the center outwards with each addition. The ganache should become smooth and glossy.
Add the butter in small pieces and whisk to smooth.
Cover with cling film (the film placed directly on the ganache, without air) and refrigerate. Wash and dry the pan.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks.
Whisk the yolks with the 50g of sugar for 5 minutes: the mixture will turn white and thicken.
Whisk the egg whites with the 70g of sugar for 8 minutes, until you have a smooth and stiff meringue.
Incorporate the egg yolks into the meringue with a spatula, lifting the mixture rather than stirring.
Sift the flour and baking powder over the mixture and incorporate them in the same way.
In a bowl, vigorously mix the milk, oil and a ladleful of batter until you obtain a smooth liquid.
Pour this mixture back into the main appliance and incorporate it gently.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, lightly oil it, pour in the batter and spread it in a thin and even layer.
Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes. Open as little as possible: the biscuit is cooked when it pulls away from the sides and the surface is dry.
Turn out immediately onto a sheet of baking paper, roll up the biscuit with the paper and let it cool rolled up. This step sets the shape.
Unroll gently, spread the ganache to within 2 cm of the edges, then roll up again tightly.
Trim both ends for clean edges, decorate, and chill for 1 hour before slicing.

title: Rustic apricot tart
intro: A barely assembled dough, ripe fruit and nothing to hide: everything hinges on the cooking of the base, which must be crispy and not soggy under the juice of the apricots.
titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe with no temperature restrictions: it becomes the baking pan. The bare metal, in direct contact with the batter, conducts heat faster than a dish or baking sheet lined with parchment paper. The bottom cooks from the very first minute, and the base remains dry. The downside: the color fades more quickly. Check the 35-minute mark.
steps: Combine the flour, sugar, and fleur de sel in a bowl. Add the butter and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse sand. Stop rubbing until you still have visible pieces of butter; these will give the pastry its characteristic layers.
Pour in the cold water. Gather by hand, without kneading. The dough should hold together, not be smooth.
Flatten into a disc, wrap in cling film, refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Pit the apricots and cut them into quarters. Mix them with the vanilla sugar and honey. Let it sit while the dough rests.
Spread the dough directly in the cold, lightly buttered pan. Bring it up two or three centimeters against the sides.
Spread the almond flour over the base: it will absorb the juices released during cooking. Arrange the wedges in a rosette pattern on top, rounded side up.
Fold the excess dough over the fruit, forming irregular folds.
Brush these folds with beaten egg, then sprinkle them with brown sugar.
Bake the pan at 180°C for 45 minutes. The tart is ready when the edges are thoroughly brown and the pastry easily pulls away from the base.
Let it cool in the pan, then slide the pie onto a wire rack or serving dish.

title: Thin pancakes
intro: It all comes down to two things: a lump-free batter and a pan that's really hot before the first ladleful.

ing.note: (therefore with a high smoke point) or oil

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, then lightly grease it, never a dab. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the crepe cooks evenly across its entire surface, releases easily from the edges, and flips with a quick flick of the wrist, without sticking.
steps: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl. Add the vanilla sugar if using. Make a well in the center.
Pour the eggs and the cooled melted butter into the well. The butter should never be hot, otherwise it will cook the eggs. Whisk vigorously in the center of the well.
Add the milk gradually, whisking between each addition and progressively incorporating the flour from the sides of the bowl towards the center. You should obtain a smooth, fluid batter without lumps.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Then brush it with a very thin film of clarified butter or grapeseed oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter and immediately tilt the pan while rotating to spread the batter over the entire surface.

Let it cook for about 2 minutes without touching it. When the pancake detaches itself from the edges and slides freely, turn it over with a flick of the wrist and continue for 2 minutes on the other side.
Repeat until all the batter is used up, adding another layer of fat when the pan starts to dry out.

title: Chocolate, coconut and oat fondant squares
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the coconut milk: hot enough to dissolve the chocolate off the heat, but never boiling, otherwise the mixture will become grainy.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even after being removed from the heat. You heat the coconut milk, turn off the heat, and add the chocolate: the metal's thermal inertia is enough to melt it without a double boiler or a second container. A single pan is all you need, from start to set and chilling.
steps: Pour the coconut milk and sugar into the still-cold pan. Heat over medium heat, stirring, for about 3 minutes, until the crystals have completely disappeared and the liquid is slightly steaming.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the chocolate pieces, wait a minute without touching it, then mix with a spatula until you obtain a shiny and homogeneous mass.
Stir in the oat flakes and shredded coconut. Mix until the liquid is completely absorbed by the flakes: the mixture should hold its shape on a spoon.
Transfer the mixture from the baking utensil to silicone molds or a frame lined with baking paper. Press down with a spoon to remove any air pockets.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours. Unmold when cold, cut into squares with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry.

title: Raw courgette tagliatelle with feta cheese and pine nuts
intro: It all comes down to the fineness of the cut and the timing of the seasoning: raw courgettes release water as soon as they come into contact with salt and lemon.
titane: Pine nuts are toasted dry in a preheated, empty pan. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: the toasting is consistent and nothing sticks, without a drop of oil. Shake the pan rather than stirring with a spoon; the pine nuts will brown on all sides.
steps: Using a mandoline, spiralizer, or vegetable peeler, slice the courgettes into long tagliatelle-like strips, working around the vegetable until you reach the seedy core. Set aside in a salad bowl.
Preheat the titanium pan empty over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It is ready when a few drops of water sizzle immediately upon contact.

Pour the pine nuts into the dry pan and reduce the heat to medium. Shake regularly for 2 minutes: they will detach from the bottom and turn golden brown. Remove them immediately (transfer them out of the pan) to stop the browning.
Finely slice the red onion. Chop the mint at the last minute, using a very sharp blade, to prevent it from turning black.
Combine the courgettes, onion, warmed pine nuts, olives and mint in the salad bowl.
Zest the lemon over the salad bowl, squeeze in the juice, add the olive oil, fleur de sel, and pepper. Gently mix by hand, being careful not to break the ribbons.
Sprinkle with crumbled feta cheese just before serving. Serve immediately.

title: Crispy sardine chips
intro: Two cans of sardines become a thin and brittle pancake, provided you roll it out really thin and don't touch it during cooking.
titane: The covered pan acts as an oven: the lid traps the heat above the pancake and dries it from the top while the bottom browns. You only need to watch for one thing: when it starts to lift. As long as the pancake sticks, it's not ready; as soon as it slides easily under the spatula, flip it over.
steps: Drain the sardines thoroughly, press them for a few seconds in a colander to remove residual water, then mash them with a fork without aiming for a perfectly smooth puree.
Stir in the spices and pepper. Taste before adding salt: canned sardines already contain salt.
Place the mixture between two sheets of baking paper. Roll it out to a uniform thickness of 2 to 3 mm. The thinner the layer, the crispier the chip will be.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly: it should simmer gently, without smoking.
Remove the top sheet, flip the pancake in the pan, then peel off the second sheet. Cover and reduce the heat to low-medium.
Cook for 12 minutes without stirring. The galette is ready to be flipped when it easily detaches from the bottom. Flip it in two or three pieces if it resists; it won't affect the result.
Continue cooking uncovered for 5 to 6 minutes, until the second side is dry and golden brown. Transfer to a wire rack: residual steam would make a plate soggy.
Mix the Greek yogurt with the herbs, a turn of the pepper and a pinch of salt.
Break the galette into irregular pieces. Serve immediately, with a generous amount of sauce — the chip is dry by design, it's the sauce that balances it.

title: Flounder meunière, crushed potatoes and crisp salad
intro: It's all about contrast: hot, crispy potatoes under a pearly fish, with a cold, raw salad placed on top at the last moment.
titane: The preheated titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly: it replaces the oven, just like an air fryer, for potatoes as well as fish. The rule is the same in both cases: don't touch anything until the food sticks. Once a crust has formed, it will release on its own. Forcing it with a spatula will leave the skin of the sole or the golden-brown side of the potatoes stuck to the pan.
steps: Cook the new potatoes for 20 minutes in boiling salted water in a saucepan. They are ready when the tip of a knife pierces them without resistance.
Drain and let cool slightly, then completely. A cold potato holds its shape better when mashed and is crispier.
Crush each small potato with the bottom of a glass, to a thickness of about 1.5 cm. The flesh should open without falling apart.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple on the surface.
Place the crushed potatoes flat, without overlapping them. Sprinkle with fleur de sel. Leave for 12 minutes without touching them: they will detach on their own, with a golden crust.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist and count 6 minutes for the second side.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a covered plate, keep warm.
Dice the apple, fennel, celery, radishes and red onion. Keep the size consistent, around 5 mm.
Mix the yogurt with the lemon juice and zest, chopped dill, salt and pepper.
Bind the salad with some of this dressing, reserving the rest for garnish. Add a drizzle of raw olive oil.
Return the pan to high heat for 1 to 2 minutes without any oil, then melt the clarified butter. It should foam slightly without browning.

Place the fillets skin-side down. Leave for 4 minutes without moving, turn over, and cook for 2 minutes on the flesh side. The flesh will become opaque and pearly (translucent, turning to a pearly white).
Cut the fillets into large pieces by hand or with a spatula.
To serve: place the hot potatoes at the bottom, the fish on top, the cold salad on top and a spoonful of yogurt sauce.

title: Lemon madeleines with a chocolate shell
intro: It all comes down to thermal shock: very cold dough in a very hot oven is what gives the hump.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheat it empty for 2 minutes over low heat, turn off the heat, then add the chocolate chips: the residual heat is enough to melt them without sticking or burning. Stir continuously; the base stays hot for a long time.
steps: Zest the lemon over the sugar. Rub the zest and sugar together between your fingers until the mixture becomes moist and fragrant.
Pour the flour and yeast on top. Make a well (a crater in the center of the powders).
Crack the eggs into the well. Mix with a wooden spoon in the center only, without touching the sides.
Add the milk. Continue mixing towards the center, incorporating the flour in small amounts.
Incorporate the melted butter, lemon juice and vanilla. Work vigorously until you have a smooth and shiny dough.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Overnight gives better results.
Fill the mold cavities three-quarters full. Preheat the oven to 230°C, conventional setting.
Place the filled mold in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Bake and immediately reduce the temperature to 200°C. Allow 12 minutes: the madeleines should be thoroughly golden brown around the edges.
Remove from the mold and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes over low heat. Turn off the heat, pour in the pistoles, and stir constantly until completely melted.
Remove from heat and dip the rounded side of each madeleine into the chocolate that has collected at the bottom of the pan. Work quickly, it sets fast.
Place them shell-side up and refrigerate for 30 minutes to allow the chocolate to harden.

title: Cat tongues
intro: It's all about finesse: a supple dough, short strips, and a fairly high heat to brown the edges before the center dries out.
titane: The pan becomes the mold. You pipe the batter directly into the cold metal, then bake the pan as is. The rapid heat conduction of titanium results in a thin crust and even browning, without the need for butter or parchment paper: on a clean, dry surface, the cookies release easily.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C, fan-assisted.
Work the softened butter with the icing sugar and vanilla until you obtain a smooth, pale mixture. Do not overmix: a dough that is too airy will not spread well.
Incorporate the sifted flour, then the egg whites in two batches. Mix just enough so that the batter becomes smooth and glossy again.

Fill a piping bag fitted with a 6mm plain nozzle. Pipe 4cm sticks into the cold titanium pan, spacing them well apart: they will double in width when cooked. Keep them small, as larger ones will overflow and stick together.
Place the pan in the oven for 10 minutes. The biscuits are ready when the edges are amber, the center still pale, and the edges easily detach from the metal.
Let them cool for 1 minute in the pan, then transfer them to a wire rack. They will harden as they cool.

title: French toast cooked in a pan
intro: It all comes down to two things: bread that is dry enough to absorb the mixture without collapsing, and a pan that is already hot when the slice arrives.
ing: case of clarified butter or grapeseed oil
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two or three minutes and retains that temperature when cold bread touches it. This stability is what creates the caramelized crust. Never check the time: wait until the slice lifts itself from the bottom; that's the signal that the surface is cooked.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the milk, vanilla, cinnamon and sweetener in a bowl until you obtain a smooth mixture.
Dip the slices one by one, 10 to 15 seconds per side. The bread should be soaked through but still hold its shape. Drain them briefly over the bowl.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the fat and let it spread.
Place the slices without overlapping them. Do not touch anything for about 4 minutes: they will detach themselves once the crust has formed.
Flip with a flick of the wrist. Cook for another 4 minutes, until evenly golden brown on the second side. Serve immediately.

title: Skillet Apple Cake
intro: A madeleine batter loaded with diced apples, cooked under a lid: everything depends on the gentleness of the heat, which allows the center to rise while the bottom caramelizes.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat before coating it with clarified butter. Titanium heats up slowly and retains its temperature: once covered, it behaves like an oven, with the added benefit of direct contact that browns the bottom. Keep the heat on low throughout, and do not uncover before the 30th minute.
steps: Peel the apples, remove the core, and cut them into 1 cm cubes.
Zest the lemon over the diced meat, squeeze it over, and mix. The flesh will remain pale.
Sweeten the apples with a tablespoon taken from the 100g, set aside.
In a bowl, combine the remaining sugar, honey, and vanilla.
Add the softened butter, work until you obtain a smooth cream, then incorporate the eggs one by one.
Add the flour, yeast and salt. Mix just enough so that there are no lumps.
Add the apples and their juice, and stir with a spatula. The batter should remain thick.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then brush the clarified butter onto the bottom and sides.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface, and cover. Cook over low heat for 40 minutes. Check after 30 minutes: a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Turn off the heat and let the cake cool slightly in the pan before turning it out onto a plate. Slice once cooled; the crumb will remain soft.

title: Apricot clafouflan
intro: Between a clafoutis and a flan: a dense and creamy batter placed on top of already caramelized apricots, which changes everything when it is cut.

ing.note: Alternatively, replace this duo with 80g of flour

titane: The apricots caramelize over high heat in the titanium pan, cut-side down, without being touched. They release themselves when the sugar has turned color: that's the signal. The pan then goes directly into the oven as is, pastry and all. No mold, no transferring, a crisp, caramelized crust across the entire base.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, before adding any fat.
Add the clarified butter and vanilla sugar. Place the apricots cut-side down in a single layer.
Let them caramelize for 10 minutes without moving them. They will detach from the bottom on their own when they are ready: do not force them before then.
Meanwhile, beat the eggs with the caster sugar and vanilla extract.
Pour in the cream, then sift the flour and cornflour over it (sift them to avoid lumps). Mix until you obtain a thick batter, similar to pancake batter.
Thin with milk, then stir in the grated coconut if you are using it.
Remove the pan from the heat. Spread the apricots evenly over the entire surface, pour the mixture over them and smooth it out.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 40 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the center is set.
Let it cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before unmolding. Serve chilled. When warm, the texture is more runny but the cut is less clean.

title: Soft muffins with a molten chocolate center
intro: It all comes down to the two-stage cooking process: a base seared over low heat, a top that rises in the oven, and a center filled only once the dough is cold.
ing: A little butter for the pan
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from stovetop to oven without any special precautions. Start over low heat, covered, to begin forming a thin crust on the muffins. Then place the pan directly in the oven: the tops will puff up and brown, while the centers finish setting. No need to transfer or use muffin liners.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until white (the mixture pales, thickens and forms a ribbon when the whisk lifts).
Combine the flour, almond flour, baking powder and salt. Mix gently.
Pour in the melted butter, milk, and vanilla. Mix until you have a smooth dough. The almond flour will leave a slight graininess: this is normal.
Add the chocolate chips, with a final fold of a spatula.
Lightly butter the pan. Place well-spaced mounds of batter in it, or arrange buttered metal rings and fill them two-thirds full.
Cover and cook over low to medium heat until the bottom is browned and the edges begin to set.
Place the pan in the oven, still at 180°C, for approximately 20 minutes total cooking time. The muffins will be puffed up and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove (take the muffins out of the pan and place them on a wire rack) and let them cool completely.
Hollow out the center of each muffin using a small spoon or an apple corer, to a depth of two-thirds of its height.
Spread generously with chocolate spread. Replace the small cake top to close it.

title: Fluffy pancakes with whipped egg whites
intro: It all comes down to two things: whipped egg whites incorporated without breaking them, and a hot pan before adding the fat.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the oil or butter. The heat rises quickly and is evenly distributed, causing the air bubbles to freeze on contact: the crumb puffs up and holds its shape instead of collapsing. The pancake will release itself once the crust is set, without tearing.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, both sugars and salt in a bowl. Whisk to distribute the yeast.
Break the eggs, separating the whites and yolks. Reserve the whites in a perfectly dry bowl.
Whisk the egg yolks with the milk, then pour this mixture over the dry ingredients. Mix just enough to obtain a smooth batter, no more.
Let it rest for 20 minutes at room temperature. The flour will hydrate, the dough will thicken.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form (whisk them until they form a soft peak at the end of the whisk, without becoming grainy).
Incorporate them into the batter in three stages, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom up. Stop as soon as there are no more white streaks.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Add a drizzle of clarified butter (melted butter with the whey removed, it can withstand higher heat) and spread it with absorbent paper in a thin film.
Pour a small ladleful of batter and let it cook for about 2 minutes without touching it. Bubbles will break through the surface, and the edges will become matte.
Flip the pancake when it slides easily in the pan. Cook for another 1 minute 30 seconds, until it is evenly browned.
Stack them up as you go under a cloth and drizzle with maple syrup when serving.

title: Apple and cinnamon cake
intro: This cake relies on two things: pieces of apple large enough to remain soft, and a base seared in a pan before baking, which gives a caramelized base instead of a soft one.
ing: Whole cane sugar or coconut sugar
titane: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then grease it. The batter sets immediately on contact, and the bottom begins to caramelize even before baking. The pan then serves as a mold: no transferring, no parchment paper.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Peel the apples. Cut them into quarters, then cut each quarter into generous chunks: if they're too small, they'll disappear during cooking. Set aside one apple, which you'll slice thinly for the top.
Sprinkle the pieces with vanilla sugar and mix to coat them. Set them aside while you prepare the dough.
Beat the eggs with the brown sugar until the mixture lightens slightly.
Pour the oil (or melted butter) in a thin stream, whisking continuously. Add the milk.
Incorporate the sifted flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Mix just enough to obtain a smooth dough, no more: if overworked, it will harden when baked.
Add the sweetened apple pieces and spread them out with a spatula.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with clarified butter or oil.
Pour the batter mixture into the hot pan. Smooth the surface, then arrange the reserved strips on top.
Sprinkle with the remaining vanilla sugar and dot with a few knobs of butter.
Let it sear for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat: the edges should begin to set. Then place the entire pan in the oven for 40 to 45 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before unmolding, to allow the crust underneath to firm up.

title: Apple-cinnamon latte
intro: It all comes down to reducing the apple juice: a syrup that is too runny will dilute in the milk, a syrup that is too concentrated will solidify at the bottom of the glass.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan. Its large surface area exposes more liquid to the air, evaporation is faster, and the syrup concentrates in about ten minutes. Guide it by texture, not by time: the juice should become thick enough to coat the back of a spoon (it should leave a clear trail when you run your finger along it).
steps: Pour the apple juice into the titanium pan along with the cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, uncovered.
Let it reduce for about ten minutes, stirring occasionally. Stop when about 4 tablespoons of syrupy liquid remain. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Pour half of this syrup into the bottom of a glass. Keep the rest chilled for subsequent cups.
Heat the milk and froth it using the frother or the machine's nozzle.
Pour the frothy milk over the syrup, slowly, to preserve the two layers.
Pull the coffee and pour it into the center.
Sprinkle with a pinch of cinnamon. Place the apple chip on the mousse at the last moment, otherwise it will soften.

title: Thin peach and burrata tart
intro: It all comes down to how the peaches are handled: if they are quickly and firmly seared, they keep their flesh firm instead of releasing their water onto the puff pastry.

ing.note: (It can withstand high temperatures) or oil

titane: Titanium heats up in minutes and retains its temperature. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the oil or butter: the peach wedges will brown on the surface without ever simmering in their own juices. The same pan, preheated a second time empty, will toast the pistachios immediately. No need to change utensils.
steps: Cut the peaches into quarters, preferably into four pieces: the flesh separates more easily from the pit.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.

Pour the clarified butter or oil over the cheese, then place the wedges flesh-side down. Don't touch them. They will stick at first, then separate on their own: that's the signal. Stir regularly until they are soft and glossy.
Add the honey and let it caramelize for 5 minutes, rolling the wedges in the syrup.
Remove the peaches with their juice from the pan and set aside: they will absorb it as they cool.
Unroll the puff pastry into the tart tin and prick the base with a fork.
Cover with a sheet of baking paper, fill with baking beans and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, until the base is golden brown.
Meanwhile, preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes.
Add the pistachios and toast them for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring constantly. They should become fragrant without browning.
Chop them finely with a knife, or give them a few pulses in a blender.
Once out of the oven, spread the burrata on the still warm base: it melts slightly and binds to the pastry.
Let it cool for about ten minutes.
Arrange the peaches on top, without aligning them. A rustic look is better than a carefully arranged presentation.
Scatter the chopped pistachios over the top and scatter the basil leaves.
Only add the balsamic vinegar pearls at the very last moment. If added too early, they will sink.

title: Stewed beets, feta, walnuts and capers
intro: It all comes down to how the beets are cooked: whole, with their skin on, under a lid, so that they retain their juice and color.

ing.note: or grapeseed oil, for the base of

titane: A covered pan is a great alternative to an oven. It heats up quickly, retains steam, and gently cooks (covered in a small amount of liquid, without browning) whole beets without drying them out. It takes about ten minutes less than oven cooking.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter: it should simmer gently without smoking.

Place the whole beets in the pot, pour in the water, and cover. Reduce the heat to low-medium and simmer for 50 minutes. Turn them over once or twice during cooking so they are heated evenly on all sides.
Check by the tip of the knife rather than by the watch: the blade should slide in without resistance. Depending on their caliber, allow 10 minutes more or less.
Let them cool slightly, then peel the beets. The skin will come off easily with your fingers.
Cut them into thick strips, about half a centimeter.
Arrange the scallop-like strips in a shallow dish, slightly overlapping.
Distribute the red onion, capers, crumbled feta, walnut kernels and spring onions.
Drizzle with walnut oil and balsamic vinegar. Season with pepper. Add salt sparingly: the feta and capers already provide salt.

title: Marbled cheesecake brownie
intro: It all comes down to undercooking: the center must remain soft when the surface is already set.

ing.note: g, plus a hazelnut for the pan

titane: The pan serves as a mold. Melt the chocolate and butter in it over low heat, pour the batter into the same pan, swirl it around, and bake. There's no transfer, so there's no risk of smudging the design when moving the batter. The titanium's heat conduction quickly creates a thin, cracked crust on the surface while the center remains soft and gooey. Butter the inside before pouring: the surface is bare, without any coating.
