steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Butter the inside of the pan, including the sides.

In a pan over very low heat, melt the chopped chocolate and butter together. Stir until smooth and free of lumps. This should take about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for two or three minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the sugar, then the eggs one at a time. Add the flour, cocoa, and salt. Mix just until the dough is smooth; overmixing will make it lose its fluffiness.
In a bowl, smooth the mascarpone with the sugar, vanilla, and cornstarch. Add the egg white and whisk until you obtain a smooth, flowing cream that holds its shape on a spoon.
Spread the chocolate paste in an even layer at the bottom of the pan. Spoon the cream over the surface, spacing it evenly.
To marble: dip the tip of a knife into the glaze and draw three or four slow figure-eights. Stop soon. Over-marbling will turn the glaze a uniform brown.
Bake for 25 minutes. The surface should be matte and slightly cracked, the center still wobbly under the tip of a finger.
Remove from the oven and let cool in the pan for at least an hour before cutting. The brownie will firm up as it cools; if cut while still hot, it will crumble.

title: Cream puffs with pearl sugar
intro: It all comes down to drying out the dough and the exact weight of the eggs: the rest is just patience.
titane: The titanium pan serves as a saucepan, poaching mat, and baking tray. Its wide base maximizes the surface area: the dough dries in three minutes instead of five, and because it goes directly from the stovetop to the oven without transfer, the dough experiences no temperature drop. No parchment paper is needed; a simple dusting of clarified butter is all that's required.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C, fan-assisted.

Combine the water, butter, sugar, and salt in the titanium pan. Heat over medium heat. The butter should be completely melted when the first simmers appear: if the water boils before, it will evaporate and the ratio will be off.
Remove from heat and add all the flour at once. Mix with a spatula until you obtain a smooth, lump-free mixture.

Return to medium heat and dry out the dough (evaporate the excess water) by pressing it against the wide base, then gathering it up. This should take 3 minutes. It's ready when it easily pulls away from the metal and forms a soft ball.
Remove from the cooking container and let cool for 10 minutes. Dough that is too hot will cook the eggs.
Incorporate the beaten eggs in 3 or 4 additions, vigorously rubbing the dough between each addition. Stop when it is smooth, shiny, and falls back into a thick ribbon.

Wipe the pan clean and grease it with a thin layer of clarified butter. Fill a piping bag fitted with a choux pastry nozzle and pipe small mounds the size of a walnut, leaving plenty of space between them.
Sprinkle generously with pearl sugar. Turn the pan upside down over the sink with a quick flick to remove the excess.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 30 minutes, without opening the door for the first 20 minutes. The choux pastries should be a deep golden brown, not pale.
Place them immediately on a wire rack. The moisture escapes from underneath: crispy exterior, soft interior.

title: Skillet Apple Cake
intro: Without egg or butter, the softness comes entirely from the compote and the oil powder: do not try to lighten the dough further, it is calibrated.
ing: Firm apples, a variety that holds up well to cooking
Apple compote, with no added sugar
Plant-based cream, hazelnut, almond or soy
titane: The titanium pan becomes the baking pan. You mix, you pour, you bake in the same pan. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat before greasing it: the oil film will spread on an already hot surface, and the cake will release itself from the sides at the end of baking. Choose an oil with a high smoke point, preferably grapeseed oil.
steps: Combine the applesauce and plant-based cream in a bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Pour in the sunflower oil, sugar and vanilla sugar. Mix until everything is perfectly combined.
Incorporate the flour, yeast, hazelnut powder and fleur de sel. Work briefly, just enough to obtain a homogeneous dough.
Slice the apples into thin strips. Slide half of them into the dough, lifting with a spatula so as not to break them.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Add the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly over the bottom with a paper towel.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and smooth the surface.
Arrange the remaining apple slices on top. Sprinkle with brown sugar: this is what will give the caramelized crust.

Bake the pan at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes, until the cake is cooked through (a knife inserted into the center should come out clean) and easily pulls away from the sides of the pan. If you don't have an oven, cover and continue baking over low heat for the same amount of time.

title: Yellow tomato salmorejo
intro: It all comes down to the quality of the stale bread: it is the bread that gives salmorejo its dense and silky texture, not the cream.
ing: Stale bread for the creamy soup
titane: The garlic-rubbed bread is placed in a scorching hot, preheated pan. The heat rises quickly and remains even across the entire surface: the crumb toasts instead of absorbing the oil. In five minutes, you get dry croutons, golden brown all the way through. The only rule of thumb: don't touch anything while the slices are sticking. They will release on their own once the crust has formed.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into rough wedges. Keep the skin on: it will be blended and adds colour.
Peel the garlic, cut it in half and remove the germ. Reserve one half for the bread.
Blend the tomato wedges with the remaining half clove of garlic until you obtain a smooth juice.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Then pour in a drizzle of olive oil: it should ripple on the surface.

Rub the two slices of bread with the reserved half vanilla bean, then place them in the pan. Let them brown undisturbed for about 5 minutes, until they release easily from the pan and are evenly golden. Transfer them to a wire rack to cool.
Break the stale bread intended for the soup into pieces and throw them into the blender with the tomato juice. Let it soak for 5 minutes.
Add salt, pepper, chili pepper and vinegar.

Blend thoroughly while slowly drizzling in the olive oil until the mixture thickens (emulsifies and lightens in color) and becomes perfectly smooth. Adjust the seasoning, then chill for at least one hour.
Divide among chilled bowls. Top with diced tomato and pepper, hand-broken croutons, parmesan shavings, pine nuts, and basil. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Egg-free banana and dark chocolate cookies
intro: An overripe banana replaces the egg: it binds the dough and keeps the center moist, provided that the cookies are taken off the heat while they still seem raw.
ing: Very ripe banana, with a well-spotted peel

ing.note: g, crushed with a knife into irregular pieces

titane: Preheat the empty skillet over medium-low heat for two to three minutes, then place the lid on once the mounds of dough are in place. The air trapped under the lid acts like an oven dome: the heat envelops the cookies from above while the titanium base slowly browns them. When the base is set, it will release itself from the surface without needing a spatula.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a bowl, until you get a coarse puree with some pieces still remaining.
Pour in the melted butter, both sugars and the vanilla. Mix by hand until smooth.
Add the baking soda, cinnamon, salt, then the flour. Work briefly: the dough should be bound, not smoothed.
Stir in the chocolate chips. Do not chill the dough; it will go straight into the oven.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Then brush it with a light coating of clarified butter: the surface should shine without smoking.
Place spaced mounds of dough in the warm pan, leaving room for spreading.
Press a few reserved pieces of chocolate onto the top of each mound.
Cover and cook for 14 minutes over low heat. The indicators: slightly cracked top, still very soft center, golden base that pulls away easily.
Remove from heat, lid off. Let the cookies firm up for a few minutes in the pan, then transfer them to a wire rack.

title: Melt-in-your-mouth Greek yogurt brookie
intro: Two pastas, one pan: it all comes down to the cooking, which must be stopped when the center is still wobbly.

ing.note: butter worked until it has the texture of a cream

titane: The pan serves three successive purposes. Over low heat, it melts chocolate and butter without a double boiler. Off the heat, it becomes the mixing bowl for the brownie batter. Finally, it goes in the oven as a baking pan. The titanium's conductivity heats the base without burning it while the cookie top browns. No transferring, no washing up in between.
steps: Place the broken chocolate and butter in the cold pan. Place over low heat and stir continuously for about 5 minutes, until the mixture becomes smooth and glossy.
Remove from heat. Let cool for two minutes, then stir in the Greek yogurt. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Pour in the sugar, then the sifted flour and salt. Mix until the lumps disappear, but don't overmix: the dough should remain soft.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl (remove the preparation from its cooking container). Wipe the pan, lightly butter the bottom, then pour in the brownie batter and smooth it with a spatula.
In a second bowl, work the softened butter with the almond puree and the light brown sugar until you obtain a smooth cream.
Add the egg, then the flour mixed with the yeast. Mix gently without overworking the dough.
Stir in the chocolate chips with a quick motion.
Take the cookie dough in large, irregular pieces and place them on the raw brownie. Leave spaces between them: the dough will spread during baking.
Place the pan in the oven at 180°C, uncovered, for 30 to 35 minutes. The surface should crack and the center should remain soft when pressed with a finger.
Remove the pan and let it cool completely inside. Cut into nine squares using a thin-bladed knife while still cold.

title: Courgette flan with feta
intro: It all comes down to the courgette: seared rather than blanched, it doesn't release its water into the mixture and the flan holds its shape when cut.
titane: The preheated pan, empty, concentrates the zucchini's sugars instead of drowning them. It then serves as a mold: low heat, covered, to set the base, then bake uncovered. A single container, no transfer, no leaks.
steps: Cut the courgettes into even cubes of about 1 cm. Preheat the empty titanium pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour the oil over the cubes, spread them in a single layer, and leave them alone. They will stick at first, then detach on their own as they brown: allow 6 minutes. Transfer to a dish and let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, flour, curry, salt and pepper until smooth.
Stir in the warm courgettes, crumbled feta and, if desired, grated cheese.
Wipe the pan clean, pour in the mixture. Cover and let it cook for 10 minutes over low heat: the base will sear without browning.
Remove the lid, place the pan in the oven for 25 minutes at 180°C. The surface should be set and lightly browned, the center barely wobbly.
Allow to cool completely in the pan. Half a day in the refrigerator before unmolding will give clean slices.

title: Cinnamon apple fritters
intro: A lightened pastry with whipped egg whites, apple slices thin enough to cook at the same time as the coating: it all comes down to the thickness of the slice.

ing.note: sachet, or 1 tsp of vanilla extract
melted butter with the whey removed

titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes, then add the fat. The heat will then be high enough to sear the coating on contact and form a golden crust while the apple softens. Don't touch it: the fritter will release itself when it's ready to turn. If you force it, the batter will tear and leave the slice bare.
steps: Separate the eggs: the yolks in a large bowl, the whites in a second, perfectly dry container.
Whisk the egg whites (until they hold their shape on the whisk) adding half the caster sugar as soon as they become frothy. They should form a soft peak.
Whisk the egg yolks with the remaining sugar, vanilla sugar and salt until the mixture turns pale.
Pour the milk in a thin stream, whisk to combine.
Add the flour and baking powder all at once. Mix just enough so that there are no lumps left: the batter should be thicker than pancake batter, it coats the spoon.
Incorporate the egg whites in three stages, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the center outwards. Stop as soon as the batter is homogeneous.
Dip the apple slices one by one, letting the excess drain for a few seconds.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the clarified butter or oil.
Place the coated slices loosely, four or five at most. Let them brown for 4 to 5 minutes without moving them.
Turn them over with a quick, firm motion as soon as they detach on their own, and continue for 4 to 5 minutes until the color is even.
Mix the sugar and finishing cinnamon, sprinkle over the doughnuts as they come out of the pan, while they are still hot.

title: Focaccia with grapes, rosemary and stracciatella
intro: A focaccia cooked in a covered pan: the base becomes crispy like on an oven floor, the crumb remains soft, and the grapes release their sweet juice into the oiled indentations.
titane: The titanium pan acts as both a griddle and an oven. Preheated empty and then oiled, it produces an evenly browned base without the dough sticking. The lid traps the steam: it is used first for the second rise off the heat, then for baking, heating the surface from above while the base browns.
steps: In a bowl, combine the flour, yeast, and lukewarm water. Mix roughly until no dry flour remains.
Cover and let rest for 5 minutes: the flour will hydrate itself, kneading will be shorter.
Add the honey, salt and 2 tablespoons of olive oil.
Knead for about ten minutes, until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. It should pull away from the sides of the bowl while remaining soft to the touch.
Shape into a ball, cover with a cloth and let it rise (first rise) for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the volume has doubled.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in a drizzle of olive oil and spread it evenly over the bottom.
Place the dough in the warm pan and spread it with your fingertips to the edges. Make clean indentations, pressing down to the bottom without piercing.
Drizzle with olive oil, distribute the grapes, pressing them in slightly, sprinkle with rosemary needles and a pinch of fleur de sel.
Cover the pan and let it rise a second time, off the heat, for 30 minutes. The dough should expand again around the grains.

Place over medium-low heat, with the lid securely in place, and cook for approximately 22 minutes. The focaccia is done when the bottom easily pulls away from the sides and sounds hollow when lifted with a spatula. If the top appears too pale, place it under the broiler for 2 minutes, uncovered.
Work the stracciatella with a fork, adding a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of fleur de sel. Spoon it onto the still-warm focaccia, then serve.

title: Brownie with chocolate spread, cooked in a pan
intro: Three ingredients, no oven: everything depends on the gentleness of the fire and the lid, which transforms the pan into a small enclosed space.
titane: The lid acts as the oven. Over very low heat, the titanium pan concentrates the heat around the batter while the metal forms a thin crust on direct contact. Don't rely on the timer, but on the edge: when it shrinks and detaches itself from the pan, the center is still soft and gooey. That's the signal.
steps: Heat the empty pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove it from the heat and coat it (cover the bottom and sides with a thin layer of fat) with clarified butter, using a brush or absorbent paper.
Remove from heat and pour the spread into the still-warm pan. Stir with a spatula for 2 minutes: the residual heat is enough to soften it. It should become smooth and homogeneous.
With the mixture still off the heat, crack the eggs into the pan and add the flour all at once. Whisk vigorously for 3 minutes, until you have a smooth, lump-free batter.
Smooth the surface with a spatula to obtain a consistent thickness across the entire base.
Cover and return to very low heat. Allow 20 to 22 minutes without lifting the lid: each glance will lower the temperature inside.
Discover it. The surface is cracked, the edges firm and detached from the pan, the center still soft to the touch. Remove from the heat and let it cool for 10 minutes in the pan before cutting.

title: Pan-fried goat cheese and honey pizza
intro: Dough that has risen overnight, cooked covered in a very hot pan: the crust forms in a few minutes, the crumb remains soft, and the oven is unnecessary.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: this is what gives it that crispy, seared base in just five minutes. Preheat it empty for two to three minutes before oiling. Then, leave the pastry alone. It will release on its own when the bottom is set—that's your signal to flip. The lid traps the steam and cooks the center without drying out the top.
steps: Pour the flour into a large bowl and make a well in the center.
Add the yeast, then the lukewarm water. Let it rest for 5 minutes, to allow the yeast to activate.
Add the salt and olive oil. Mix with a fork until a rough ball forms.
Flour your work surface and knead for 10 minutes, pushing the dough with your palm and folding it over itself. It should become smooth and supple to the touch.
Lightly oil a bowl, place the dough in it, and cover with a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm place overnight: it should at least double in size.
Degas the dough (expel the gas by pressing with the flat of your hand), divide it in two, briefly rework each piece of dough and then roll them out to the desired thickness.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Drizzle with grapeseed oil, place a pastry disc on top, and cover. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat without touching it: the bottom will detach on its own and have a golden crust.
Flip it over with a flick of the wrist, cover it, and continue for 5 minutes. The base should crack under finger pressure.
Remove from heat, sprinkle with crumbled goat cheese and let it melt in the residual heat. Drizzle with honey at the last minute, just before serving.

title: Pan-roasted chestnuts
intro: Everything hinges on two points: sorting in cold water, which eliminates hollow or inhabited fruits, and incising the shell, without which the chestnut bursts.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Titanium heats up faster than cast iron and distributes heat just as evenly, while being much lighter: you can easily shake it by the handle every two minutes, which rotates the chestnuts and prevents them from burning. Keep the lid on and listen for the sound: when the shells begin to open, they're almost done.
steps: Place the chestnuts in the bowl of cold water. Let them sit for a minute.
Remove and discard any that float to the surface: they are dried out, damaged, or infested with a worm. Keep those that remain at the bottom.
Drain and dry the reserved chestnuts.

Place each chestnut on its flat side. Make a horizontal cut through the rounded side, slicing only through the shell, without cutting into the flesh. Without this opening, the steam will cause the chestnut to burst during cooking.
Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour the chestnuts in a single layer, cut side up. No fat: they cook dry.
Cover and grill for 25 minutes over medium heat. Shake the pan by the handle every 2 to 3 minutes, without lifting the lid each time.
The chestnuts are ready when the shells gape open along the incision and the fruits detach easily from the bottom. If some resist, cook for another 5 minutes.
Remove the chestnuts from the pan and place them in a tea towel. Cover the tea towel and leave for 5 minutes. The trapped steam will loosen the shell and the second skin.
Peel while still hot: the brown skin comes off with the shell. Serve immediately.

title: Apple and cinnamon cake
intro: A family cake where everything hinges on the base: cooked in direct contact with the metal, it takes on a caramelized base that a mold will never give.
ing: Whole cane sugar or coconut sugar

ing.note: g, or 100 g of melted butter

ing: Clarified butter or neutral oil for lining
titane: Preheat the empty pan over low heat for two minutes, then coat it (spread a thin film of fat over the surface) with clarified butter. The bare metal is perfectly safe from high heat and oven use: the batter is cooked on a surface that is already hot and oily, the base caramelizes within minutes, and you can put the pan in the oven as is.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel the apples and cut them into even wedges. Roll them with a spoonful of sugar (taken from the weighing) and a pinch of cinnamon. Set aside.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining sugar until the mixture lightens in color. Slowly pour in the oil or melted butter, whisking continuously.
Add the flour, yeast, salt and the remaining cinnamon all at once. Mix with a spatula until the dough is smooth, but no more.
Loosen with the milk: the batter should fall from the whisk in a thick ribbon.
Place the pan over low heat, empty, for two minutes. Off the heat, brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter.
Pour the batter into the hot pan. Press half of the apple wedges into the batter, arrange the others in a rosette pattern on top.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Place the pan directly in the oven for 40 minutes. The top should be thoroughly golden brown and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let it cool for ten minutes in the pan before unmolding: the caramelized base will come off in one piece once relaxed.

title: Old-fashioned tart with caramelized onions
intro: It all comes down to the onions: they must melt without ever sticking, until they become translucent and barely blond.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
Fleur de sel for the device
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, before adding any oil or butter. It heats up quickly and evenly: the onions will soften without any hot spots. Then, everything stays in the skillet—you line the pan with pastry, add the filling, and bake. All in one container from start to finish.
steps: Combine the flour, herbs, and fleur de sel in a bowl. Add the cold butter, then the ice water. Gently rub the mixture together with your fingertips, being careful not to overwork it: small pieces of butter should remain visible, as this will create the flaky texture. Allow 10 minutes.
Form into a ball, flatten it slightly and let it rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be hot, never smoking.

Pour in the fat, then the sliced onions. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring regularly. They will detach from the bottom of the pan and become translucent, with a hint of color. Remove from the pan (transfer to another container) and let cool slightly. Wipe the pan clean.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roll out the dough on a floured surface and press it directly into the pan, bringing the edges up by a good two centimeters.
Spread the base with old-fashioned mustard, then distribute the onions in a generous and even layer.
Beat the cream with the egg, fleur de sel and pepper.
Pour this mixture over the onions, tilting the pan so that it seeps everywhere.
Place the pan in the oven as is, handle included, and cook for 40 minutes at 180°C. The surface should be thoroughly golden brown and the cream set.

title: Forest-style tagliatelle with crispy smoked tofu
intro: It's all about the color: tofu left alone until the crust forms, golden mushrooms that aren't sweaty.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. Place the tofu on top, then leave it alone. A crust will form, the tofu will release on its own, and only then should you intervene. The same principle applies to mushrooms: a quick sear rather than constant stirring, and the Maillard reaction (browning that creates the toasted flavor) will do the work for you.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cut the smoked tofu into thin strips. Pat them dry with a cloth or paper towel: the residual moisture prevents any crust from forming.
Dust the matchsticks with cornstarch and mix with your fingertips for a light, almost invisible coating.

Pour a drizzle of oil into the hot pan, spread the tofu in a single layer. Let it brown for 5 minutes without stirring. The tofu sticks will separate easily when they are ready: turn them over, brown the other side, then remove from the pan and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium, add a drizzle of oil and sweat the minced shallots for 2 minutes.
Turn up the heat, add the sliced mushrooms, the sprig of thyme, and the crushed garlic clove. Let them brown for 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 or 3 minutes. Add salt only at the end of cooking.
Plunge the tagliatelle into boiling water and cook them al dente, about 10 minutes. Remove a ladleful of cooking water before draining.
Pour the vegetable mixture over the mushrooms, scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan and simmer for 2 minutes. Remove the thyme. Season generously with pepper.
Add the drained pasta to the pan and stir off the heat. Thin with a little pasta water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Divide among the plates, top with crispy tofu, chopped flat-leaf parsley and crushed hazelnuts.

title: Rustic yellow nectarine tart
intro: A tart without a mold or ring, where everything depends on the consistency of the pastry and the juice of the fruit, which must be captured before it soaks the base.
titane: The pan becomes the mold. You spread the dough directly in the cold pan, add the filling, fold it over, and then bake the whole thing, handle and all. No parchment paper needed: titanium doesn't stick, the base cooks flat and releases easily once it's lukewarm.
steps: Combine the flour, light brown sugar, and fleur de sel in a bowl. Add the cold butter and work it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse sand. Stop soon: some visible pieces of butter should remain, as these are what give the pastry its characteristic flakiness during baking.
Gradually pour in the cold water, just enough to bring the dough together. Form a ball without kneading, then flatten it into a disc.
Let it rest in the refrigerator while you prepare the fruit.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Remove the pits from the nectarines and cut them into even wedges.
In a bowl, combine the wedges with the brown sugar and vanilla sugar. Mix by hand so as not to damage them.
Sprinkle in the cornflour and mix again: it will bind the juices released during cooking.
Roll out the dough on a floured work surface to a thickness of 3 to 4 mm, forming a disc larger than the pan. Place it in the cold titanium pan, letting the edges fall over.
Crush the speculoos cookies with a rolling pin and spread the powder over the pastry base. It will absorb the fruit juices and keep the bottom dry.
Arrange the nectarine wedges in a rosette pattern on the biscuit crumbs.
Fold the edges of the pastry over the fruit, in successive folds, leaving the center open.
Bake the pan as is for 40 minutes at 180°C. The tart is ready when the pastry is golden brown and the fruit is caramelized around the edges.
Allow to cool slightly in the pan before sliding the pie onto a wire rack.

title: Pasta with cherry tomatoes and melted feta cheese
intro: It all comes down to the feta: cooked whole in the middle of the tomatoes, it releases its fat and becomes the sauce itself, without cream or reduction.
titane: The pan starts on the stovetop to sear the tomatoes and garlic, goes straight into the oven, then returns to low heat to coat the pasta. A single pan is used from start to finish, and the sauce settles directly at the bottom without transferring anything.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C, conventional heat.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil, or grapeseed oil if you want a higher smoke point. The oil should be simmering gently.
Place the whole cherry tomatoes in the pan. Do not cut them: they will soften and then burst on their own in the oven.
Crush the garlic cloves with the palm of your hand, using the flat side of the blade, and scatter them over the tomatoes. Add a few basil leaves. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the block of feta in the center, and arrange the tomatoes around it. Drizzle with a little olive oil.
Bake the pan for 30 minutes. The feta should be melted and creamy, the tomatoes softened. Nothing should be sticking to the bottom.
Meanwhile, cook the penne al dente in a large pot of salted water. Reserve a ladleful of the cooking water before draining.
Once out of the oven, mash the feta and tomatoes with a fork directly in the pan until you obtain a smooth, creamy texture.
Add the pasta to the pan, return to low heat and stir for 2 minutes to coat it well. Thin with a little pasta water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Add a few fresh basil leaves and serve in the pan.

title: Crispy wrap cups, avocado cream and ribbed tomatoes
intro: It all comes down to the shell: a crumpled, dry-brown wrap that must remain firm under the fresh filling until the moment it is broken.

ing.note: a tablespoon, plus a drizzle for the

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains heat: the wraps brown dry, without a drop of oil. Press each crumpled wrap against the bottom with the back of a small ladle for the first few seconds to set the indentation, then let it set. When the wrap loosens on its own, it's ready to be flipped.
steps: Heat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes, without oil.
Crumple a wrap between your hands to dig an irregular nest. Repeat with the other five.
Place the ramekins in the hot, dry pan. Hold them in place for a few seconds with the back of a spoon or a small ladle, until they set. Cover.
Cook for 6 minutes over medium heat, turning once halfway through. The shell is cooked when it easily detaches from the bottom and sounds hollow.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack. The cups will harden as they cool.
Blend the avocado flesh with olive oil, lime juice, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper until smooth.
Rinse the tomatoes, remove the stem, and cut them into small, even cubes.
Mix the diced meat with the red onion, chopped coriander, a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper. Taste.
Fill the bottom of each bowl with avocado cream, then top with seasoned tomatoes.
Serve immediately. Break the shell to mix it with the filling; it's the contrast that makes the bite special.

title: Lemon skillet cake
intro: A cake without an oven, whose moistness comes entirely from the firmness of the egg whites and the gentleness of the fire.

ing.note: to clarify (separate the egg whites from the yolks)

titane: A covered pan works like an oven: the heat rises slowly, spreads through the bottom, and remains trapped under the lid. Preheat the pan empty for two minutes over low heat, then butter it generously, including the sides—this film of butter ensures clean release in an uncoated pan. The bottom will brown a little more than in the oven: this is normal, and it's delicious.
steps: Separate the eggs. Reserve the whites in a perfectly dry bowl.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture lightens and thickens slightly.
Roll the lemons under your palm on the work surface, then squeeze them. Strain the juice to remove the seeds.
Pour the lemon juice and cooled butter over the egg yolk and sugar mixture. Whisk to combine.
Add the flour in three batches along with the fleur de sel. Mix just enough: overworked dough loses its softness.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form (whisk them until they trap air and hold their shape). Check by the inverted bowl test: they should not slide off.
Incorporate two spoonfuls of egg whites briskly to loosen the batter, then fold in the rest with a spatula, lifting from the bottom up.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 minutes over low heat. It should be warm to the touch. Generously butter the base and sides.

Pour the batter into the pan, cover, and cook over very low heat for 28 minutes, without lifting the lid for the first 20 minutes. The cake is ready when the surface springs back when lightly touched and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let it cool for 5 minutes off the heat, with the lid removed. The cake will easily pull away from the sides. Turn the pan upside down onto a wire rack or plate.
Sprinkle with icing sugar when serving.

title: Puff pastry tarts with caramelized apples
intro: It all comes down to the base: a base seared in a pan before the oven will never get soggy.

ing.note: Boskoop or Queen of Reinettes type

ing: brown sugar for the pastry base
titane: One pan, three uses. It heats the butter-brown sugar syrup, it sears the apple side of the tarts to set the caramel, then it goes straight into the oven thanks to its compatible handle. No transferring, no baking dish to grease, and the heat accumulated in the base continues to cook the pastry while the surface browns.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. The butter should sizzle as soon as it touches the pan: this is the only reliable indicator.
Melt the butter for about 1 minute, without letting it brown.
Add the 30g of brown sugar and the cinnamon. Stir for 2 minutes until you obtain a glossy, smooth, slightly amber syrup. Transfer it from the pan to a bowl. Keep the pan on the heat.
Cut the apples in half, remove the core, then slice each half thinly, keeping the shape together.
Cut out four circles from the puff pastry using a cookie cutter, slightly larger than the apple halves.
Sprinkle each circle with the remaining 2 tablespoons of brown sugar. This dry layer absorbs the juice and ensures crispness.
Place half a sliced apple in the center of each circle, then lightly fold the edges of the pastry over the fruit.
Place the tarts in the hot pan, apple side down. Cook over medium-high heat and do not move them: they will release on their own once caramelized, after about 2 minutes.
Drizzle with the reserved cinnamon syrup.
Bake the pan as is for 20 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown and the apples are browned around the edges. Let it cool for 5 minutes before loosening with a spatula.

title: Crushed quinoa, spinach and edamame with sardines
intro: An introduction to chunky foods: everything cooks in the same pan, and it's the fork, not the blender, that decides the final texture.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding water. The base heats up evenly: the grain expands without sticking, and you can alternate vegetables and then fish without ever changing the pan.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be hot to the touch when held ten centimeters away, without smoking.
Pour in the broth, add the rinsed quinoa. Cover and cook for about ten minutes over medium heat: the liquid should have completely evaporated and the grains should open in small spirals.

Push the grain to one side of the pan. Place the edamame and spinach leaves in the empty space, add two tablespoons of water, and cover again. Cook for 4 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the beans are tender.
Turn off the heat. Crumble the sardines over the top, after removing the central bone if it's in the way. Pour over the rapeseed oil, which should never be heated.
Mash with a fork, directly in the pan. Stop early: you should still see fragments of bean and strands of cereal.
Add lemon juice if desired, then transfer (out of the pan) to a plate and check the temperature before serving.

title: Thick pancakes
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the batter: thick, almost lazy to spoon, it's what gives you tall and fluffy pancakes.

ing.note: It can withstand higher temperatures without

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Titanium heats up quickly and without a cold spot: the first side will brown evenly as soon as it starts to cook. Then, leave it alone. The pancake will release on its own when it's ready—that's the only reliable sign to flip it.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, vanilla sugar and sugar in a bowl.
Form a well (a hollow in the center of the powders, like for pancake batter).
Beat the eggs and pour them into the well. Add the milk in a thin stream, whisking from the center outwards to gradually incorporate the flour.
Whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free batter that is significantly thicker than pancake batter. Do not add milk to thin it out: it is this density that makes the pancakes rise.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a knob of clarified butter and spread it in a thin film.

Reduce the heat to low. Pour 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake, without sticking them together. Let them cook for about 2 minutes without moving them: the surface will be covered with small bubbles and the edges will become matte.
When the pancake releases easily from the pan, flip it over with a quick, firm movement using a spatula. Continue cooking for 2 minutes on the other side, until the center is set.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a plate. Add a knob of clarified butter between each batch.

title: Avocado Vinaigrette
intro: Mashed avocado replaces mustard: it binds the sauce and gives it body, without revealing its texture.
titane: The pan stays cool. It serves as your single container: you mash the avocado in the bottom, mix it in, and rinse it immediately. Its smooth surface doesn't retain the acidity of the vinegar or lemon juice, so there's no need to get out a bowl.
steps: Cut the avocado in half, remove the pit, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and place it in the cold titanium pan.
Mash with a fork, pressing against the bottom, until you obtain a creamy puree without any lumps.
Pour in the balsamic vinegar, soy sauce, honey and lime juice.
Add salt, pepper or chili, and a pinch of cumin.
Whisk vigorously with a fork to emulsify (incorporate the fat and liquid until they no longer separate). The vinaigrette should be smooth, glossy, and coat the back of the fork.

title: Carrot, squash, potato and turnip soup
intro: It all comes down to the onion: coloured brightly before the water, it gives the soup a depth that vegetables alone cannot provide.

ing.note: at the level of the vegetables, without exceeding 500 ml

titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes over medium heat before adding any oil. The onion placed on top will stick, brown, and then release easily: that's the signal. The titanium handles this searing and then supports the immersion blender, eliminating the need to transfer the contents. A single piece of equipment, from start to finish.
steps: Wash, peel and cut carrots, squash, potatoes and turnip into 1.5 cm cubes. Aim for uniformity: this determines the evenness of the cooking.
Finely chop the half onion.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the oil, then the onion. Do not stir it while it remains at the bottom. Allow 5 minutes: it will detach on its own and become translucent at the edges, browned underneath.
Add the vegetables, salt, pepper, cumin and the bouillon cube crumbled between your fingers — crumbled, it dissolves before the water boils.
Pour in enough water to cover, without drowning. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes over medium-low heat, until a knife tip pierces a cube of carrot without resistance.
Remove from heat. Blend directly in the pan with an immersion blender, starting with short bursts and then continuing until smooth. Adjust the salt seasoning.

title: Chocolate cream and coconut milk
intro: Two ingredients, no eggs: it's all about the gentleness of the heat and the regularity of the mixture.
titane: The pan offers a large surface area: the heat diffuses evenly without hot spots, and the chocolate melts without sticking to the bottom. The mixture becomes smooth faster than in a narrow saucepan, where the mixture accumulates and heats in layers. Since the liquid is poured in from the start, there's no need for preheating or adding fat.
steps: Break the chocolate into even pieces. Place them in the cold pan with the coconut milk.
Place over low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula, scraping the bottom and sides, for about 5 minutes. The mixture should become smooth and glossy, without lumps or sediment at the bottom.
Remove from heat as soon as it is homogeneous. There's no need to continue: overheated chocolate loses its shine.
Ladle the mixture into four ramekins.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, preferably overnight, until completely set.

title: Creamy scrambled eggs with butter
intro: It all comes down to the slowness of the heat and the regularity of the movement: successful scrambled eggs behave like a custard, not like an omelet.
titane: Preheat the empty pan over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes before adding the butter. Titanium distributes heat evenly without creating hot spots: the eggs won't coagulate any faster around the edges than in the center. You can still whisk continuously, but there's more room for error than with a saucepan. Also, keep in mind that the metal retains heat even off the heat: the cooking process continues in the pan.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add salt and pepper, then whisk until the whites and yolks are perfectly smooth, without incorporating air.
Toast the bread and keep it within easy reach. The scrambled eggs don't wait, the bread does.
Preheat the titanium pan empty over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the butter and let it melt over very low heat, without letting it foam or color.
Pour in the beaten eggs. Whisk immediately and continuously, over very low heat. Allow approximately 5 minutes.

Scrape the edges and then continuously bring the mixture back towards the center: these are the areas where coagulation starts first. You will see a light foam form, then the mixture thicken suddenly.
Remove from the heat while the eggs are still noticeably runny. The residual heat of the pan will finish the job in seconds while you plate.
Remove from the heat source and serve immediately.

title: Vanilla and orange blossom doughnuts
intro: It all comes down to the double rise: it's what gives the crumb its stringy texture and thin crust, not the amount of oil.

ing.note: for 1.5 cm height in the pan

titane: Forget deep-frying. Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in just 1.5 cm of oil. The heat rises quickly and remains even across the entire surface: the doughnuts brown perfectly on top and bottom, without becoming soggy. The smooth surface prevents the batter from sticking, and the doughnuts release easily once the first side is cooked.
steps: Split the vanilla pod and scrape the seeds into the milk. Bring to a boil in a small saucepan, then let it cool to 30°C.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm vanilla milk. Let it rest for 10 minutes, until a foam forms on the surface.
In the bowl of a food processor, combine the flour, sugar, salt and orange blossom water. Add the egg, then the risen milk.
Knead for 3 minutes at medium speed.
Incorporate the softened butter and knead for another 8 minutes. The dough should pull away from the sides of the bowl and remain pliable.
Shape into a ball, cover with a cloth and let rise for 1 hour 30 minutes at room temperature.
Deflate the dough (press it to release the fermentation gas) on a floured surface. Roll it out to 0.5 cm thick and cut into even rectangles.
Cover again and let rise for 1 hour. The rectangles should puff up and feel light to the touch.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in 1.5 cm of oil and wait for it to simmer.
Place the doughnuts in the pan without overcrowding it. Do not touch them: they will release on their own once golden brown, about 3 minutes. Turn them over and brown the other side.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on absorbent paper.
Sprinkle with icing sugar at the last moment and finish with a drizzle of honey.

title: Eggplant, mozzarella and rocket rolls
intro: It all depends on the thickness of the strips: too thick, they break when rolled; too thin, they become supple and golden in a few minutes.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold slices are placed inside. The eggplant browns before it has time to dry out, unlike in the oven which dries it from the outside. The lid then takes over: the steam softens the flesh and melts the cheese, which acts as glue for the slice when rolling.
steps: Slice the eggplants lengthwise into very thin strips, using a knife or mandoline. Aim for 3 to 4 mm: below this thickness they will tear, above this thickness they will refuse to bend.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a drizzle of oil. It should ripple on the surface.
Place the strips flat, without overlapping them. Let them brown for 4 minutes without touching them: they will detach themselves from the bottom when the underside is golden.
Turn them over, sprinkle with herbes de Provence and grated cheese. Cover for 3 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Continue cooking, covered, over medium heat until the strips are soft and browned on both sides, about 10 minutes total. Work in small batches: an overcrowded pan will steam and won't brown.
Transfer to a plate (remove from the pan to stop the cooking) and let cool slightly.
Spread a little pesto on each slice. Add a slice of tomato, a piece of mozzarella, a few rocket and basil leaves, then a drizzle of balsamic cream.
Roll each strip loosely, starting from the widest end.
Slice the rolls into pieces and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Thin zucchini and fresh goat cheese tart
intro: It all depends on the thickness of the strips: if they are too thick, they release water and make the puff pastry soggy.
ing: Fresh goat cheese flavored with garlic and herbs
Dried herb blend from the South of France
titane: The titanium pan goes straight from the countertop to the oven. You blind bake the pastry (bake the pastry alone, weighted down, before adding the filling), then add the filling, and return it to the oven. No transferring, so no broken pastry base.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. In a bowl, combine the olive oil, crushed garlic, dried herbs, honey, pepper, and a pinch of fleur de sel. Whisk to create a smooth marinade.
Unroll the puff pastry and cut out a disc the same diameter as the bottom of the pan. Brush it with a third of the marinade.

Place the disc in the bottom of the cold pan. Cover with a sheet of parchment paper, then with a light weight or a small baking sheet: the dough should remain flat. Bake for 25 minutes, until golden brown and dry to the touch.
Meanwhile, slice the courgettes with a mandoline into 1-2 mm strips, lengthwise or into rounds according to the desired design.
Pour the remaining marinade over the strips. Mix gently by hand to coat them all.
Take out the pan, remove the weight and the paper. Spread the cream cheese over the still warm pastry, leaving a 1 cm border.
Arrange the strips in a tight rosette, slightly overlapping them.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Return to the oven for 15 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and lightly browned. Season with pepper, add chopped fresh herbs, and serve warm, sliced in the pan.

title: Chocolate cake, ganache and soaking syrup
intro: Everything depends on the order of operations: the ganache is prepared the day before, the biscuit is completely cooled before being sliced, and the syrup is applied lukewarm to a cold crumb.
ing: Crushed dark chocolate or chocolate chips
titane: One pan for three uses. It heats the ganache cream, goes in the oven as a cake pan, and then cooks the chocolate syrup. Uncoated, it's oven-safe at any temperature and releases the cake cleanly once it's cooled. Grease it before pouring in the batter.
steps: Pour the cream into the pan and heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer. It heats up quickly on titanium: stay close by.

Place the chopped chocolate in a bowl. Pour in the hot cream in three stages, mixing from the center outwards with each addition to emulsify (bind the fat and liquid into a smooth mass). Incorporate the butter in the final stage.
Refrigerate the ganache for 3 hours, or overnight at room temperature. It should reach the consistency of a spreadable paste.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Wipe the pan and lightly grease it with clarified butter, including the sides.
Melt the chocolate and butter from the biscuit together, either in a double boiler or in short bursts in the microwave. Let it cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 10 minutes, until tripled in volume. The ribbon should remain on the surface for a few seconds.
Add the sifted flour and yeast, folding the mixture in with a spatula.
Gently incorporate the cooled chocolate-butter mixture, without trying to go fast.
Pour the batter into the greased pan and smooth the surface.
Bake for 25 minutes at 180°C. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from the oven and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Wipe the pan clean. Combine the water, caster sugar and cocoa, mix, bring to a boil over medium heat and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Allow the syrup to return to room temperature.
Slice the cold biscuit horizontally. Soak each side with syrup (moisten with a brush until lightly saturated), generously spread ganache between the layers, then cover the entire cake.

title: Seared ribeye steak, drizzled with butter
intro: It's all about patience: a piece that you don't touch while it's coloring, and that you let rest before slicing it.

ing.note: 2 kg, beautiful whole piece with its bone

titane: The titanium pan heats up in two minutes when empty and maintains that temperature beneath the cold mass of the meat. You sear, you crisp the fat, you prepare the basting sauce: a single pan from start to finish. Wait until the rib easily lifts from the bottom; that's the signal that the crust has formed—the same one you want on hot coals.
steps: Remove the rib from the refrigerator 45 minutes beforehand. Salt generously on all sides, including the cut edge. The salt draws out surface moisture and helps form a crust.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the rib upright, fat side down. Hold it in place with your hand or prop it against the edge of the pan. Let the fat render and brown over medium heat.
Lay the piece flat. Do not move it, do not press on it. It will detach on its own once the coloring is complete.
Turn over once, when the first side has a uniform, dark crust. Repeat the same instructions for the second side.
Check by touch and with a skewer rather than a stopwatch: the flesh should remain supple, around 40°C at the core for a rare steak. Allow a few degrees more for medium-rare.
Turn the heat up to high for thirty seconds, with the piece upright on its fat side, to make it thoroughly crispy. Remove from the pan to stop the cooking.
To debone: run the tip of the knife along the bone; it will serve as your guide. Separate the sirloin from the ribeye and remove the tough tendon that separates them.
Let it rest for 5 minutes on a rack or board, away from the stovetop. The juices will redistribute, and the meat will stop cooking.
Return the pan to medium heat with the rendered fat and butter. Let it melt until the mixture is golden brown and smells nutty.
Slice the meat, season with pepper, then generously drizzle with the hot fat. Serve immediately.

title: Almond tart with chestnuts, mascarpone and raspberries
intro: A dense and lightly sweetened almond dessert, where chestnut cream replaces the sugar in the mixture: it dictates the dosage, don't add any more.
ing: Finely grated zest of half a lemon
titane: The titanium pan serves as a mold: generously buttered, it goes directly from the work surface to the oven without transferring. Its even heat conduction cooks the pastry base at the same rate as the filling, something a ring placed on a baking sheet rarely does. Let it cool in the pan before unmolding; the pastry will firm up and release cleanly.
steps: Rub the flour, butter, salt, and sugar together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse sand. Gradually add the ice water, mixing gently without kneading. Form a flattened ball.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes. The butter should become firm again.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs with a fork in a mixing bowl. Add the mascarpone, chestnut cream, almond flour, zest, vanilla, and salt. Mix until smooth, being careful not to overmix.
Generously butter the titanium pan, right up to the edges. Spread out the dough, place it in the pan, bring it up two centimeters on the sides and prick the bottom with a fork.
Pour the mixture into the pan and smooth it with a spatula.
Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes, uncovered. The surface should be golden brown and the filling set: it should no longer be wobbly in the center.
Allow to cool completely in the pan, then unmold by sliding a flexible spatula under the bottom.
Whip the cream with the vanilla sugar until stiff peaks form. Spread a thin layer over the cooled tart.
Arrange the raspberries tightly across the entire surface, point upwards.
Dust with icing sugar and sprinkle with borage flowers at the last moment.

title: Pan-fried apple yogurt cake
intro: Everything hinges on the gentleness of the fire: a flame that is too intense will burn the base before the heart catches.

ing.note: The empty pot serves as a measuring tool for what follows.

titane: When covered, the titanium pan becomes a miniature oven: the heat rises from the bottom, the moisture is trapped under the lid, and the crumb retains its softness. Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes, then oil generously—on an uncoated surface, this film of oil ensures easy release. Lift the lid halfway through cooking to check the browning, but don't overcook.
steps: Empty the yogurt into a bowl. Rinse and dry the container: it will serve as your measuring cup.
Add the sugar, flour, oil, yeast and eggs all at once. Whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free batter, about 3 minutes.
Incorporate the vanilla sugar and the apple cubes. Mix with a spatula to distribute them without working the dough.
Heat the 20cm pan empty, over low-medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil and swirl it around: it should coat the bottom and sides without smoking.
Pour the batter, smooth the surface with a spatula.

Cover and cook over low heat for 28 minutes. The surface should be set and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean. If the top remains moist, continue cooking for another 3 to 5 minutes, still covered.
Let it rest for 5 minutes off the heat. The cake will shrink and pull away from the sides of the pan on its own. Invert the pan onto a wire rack, then turn the cake out onto a plate.
Sprinkle with icing sugar through a sieve just before serving.

title: Crispy fish sando with avocado and raw vegetables
intro: It all comes down to the breading: it must come out of the pan dry and squeaking, otherwise the bread will soften it in two minutes.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold fish is placed on it. This allows the breading to set over medium-high heat instead of drying it out in the oven. One rule: don't touch the fillets while they're still coated. Once the coating has set, it will detach on its own. If you force it with a spatula beforehand, you'll leave the breading in the pan.
steps: Mix together the mayonnaise, lemon juice, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Whisk with a fork until the sauce is smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.

Place the fillets breaded-side down. Do not move for 4 minutes. When the fish easily flakes under the spatula, turn it over and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, never place on paper towels: the steam will soften the bottom.
While it's cooking, grate the carrot, finely slice both cabbages and the red onion. Season lightly with salt and mix.

Spread the sauce generously on all four slices. Roughly mash the avocado on two of them, then top with microgreens. Place the still-warm fish on top, followed by the hand-packed raw vegetables. Close the sandwich, press down for 10 seconds, and slice in half cleanly with a smooth-bladed knife.

title: Chocolate and zucchini fondant
intro: Raw courgette, blended with eggs, replaces flour and butter here: it is what gives the fondant its moist consistency and almost mousse-like texture after resting.
ing: whole cane sugar or coconut sugar
titane: The titanium pan serves as a mold. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, grease it with clarified butter, pour in the batter, and bake directly: no transferring, no parchment paper. The cake bakes and cools in the same pan, and unmolds cleanly as soon as it pulls away from the sides on its own.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Wash the courgette, remove the ends, cut it into large chunks without peeling it.
Blend the zucchini and eggs in a blender until perfectly smooth. No lumps should remain, otherwise they will release water during cooking.
Add the sugar and cocoa. Mix again briefly, until you have a thick and smooth chocolate paste.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Add the clarified butter and spread it evenly over the bottom and sides. It should simmer gently without smoking.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan and smooth the surface.
Place the pan in the oven as is, handle included, and cook for 40 minutes at 180°C. A matte and slightly cracked surface indicates that it is done.
Let it cool completely in the pan, then refrigerate for a few hours. Unmold when the cake easily pulls away from the sides, and cut.

title: Skillet Blueberry Cake
intro: It all comes down to two things: floury blueberries that remain suspended in the batter, and a pan that is already hot when the batter arrives.
ing: clarified butter or 1 tablespoon of neutral oil
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing it, then transfer it directly from the stovetop to the oven without transferring the batter. The batter sets immediately on the hot base: the base browns beautifully where the blueberry juices have simmered, and it releases easily from the pan.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Whisk together the eggs, oil, and sugar until the mixture lightens in color and thickens slightly. Add the vanilla sugar.
Add the flour and yeast, mix until you obtain a smooth dough. Stop as soon as the flour has been absorbed.

Roll the blueberries in the spoonful of flour, shaking off the excess. Gently fold them in with a spatula, lifting the batter from the bottom to the top (a mixing motion that blends without crushing). The berries should remain whole and evenly distributed.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter or oil: the fat should simmer without smoking.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and smooth the surface.
Place the pan in the oven as is, handle included, for 30 minutes at 180°C. The top is golden brown, the blueberries have softened at the bottom, and a knife blade comes out clean.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before unmolding onto a wire rack, or serve directly from the pan.

title: Buttery spritz cookies coated in chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the mixture: too firm, it won't fit through the piping bag; too soft, the flutes will disappear during baking.
titane: The pan goes in the oven, covered, instead of the baking sheet: the direct contact creates a crispier base. After being wiped dry, it's used to melt the chocolate coating. A single utensil is used from start to finish.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Using a spatula, mash the softened butter with the icing sugar, vanilla, and salt. Work until the mixture is perfectly smooth and grain-free.
Add the egg white. Whisk a few times to combine.

Incorporate the flour, then take the spatula and press the mixture against the side of the bowl. You're looking for a dense but pliable mass, with the consistency of vanilla ice cream straight from the freezer.

Lightly grease the bottom of the pan with clarified butter. Fill a piping bag fitted with a star nozzle and pipe small spiral roses directly into the pan, well spaced apart: they will spread out during cooking.
Cover and bake for 15 minutes. The spritz cookies are cooked when the edges are golden brown and the cookies easily pull away from the base.
Remove the pan using oven mitts. Transfer the spritz cookies to a wire rack and let them cool completely.

Wipe the pan dry. Heat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over very low heat, remove it from the heat, then melt the chocolate in it, stirring with a spatula. The residual heat is sufficient: return it to the heat for just a few seconds if it stops melting.
Dip each spritz halfway into the chocolate, shake off the excess, and place it back on the rack.
Allow to set at room temperature, or 10 minutes in the refrigerator if you are in a hurry.

title: Pan-fried apricot crumble
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the apricots: if they are too firm, they will remain acidic under an already golden paste.
titane: The titanium pan, cooked over low heat, allows the fruit to simmer from below while the crust browns above, without drying out the edges like a gratin dish. Cover to cook the fruit, then uncover and place in the oven or under the broiler for a few minutes, using the same pan, to finish the crispness. Use only one container from start to serve.
steps: Cut the apricots in half and remove the pits. Keep them in half-halves; they will hold up better during cooking.
Drizzle them with lemon juice, sprinkle with brown sugar and vanilla seeds. Mix, then let them rest while you prepare the dough: the juice should start to bead.
In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, brown sugar and almond flour.

Add the cold butter and rub it in with your fingertips (crush the butter with the dry ingredients, without warming it, until you get a coarse, sandy texture). Stop when there are still lumps the size of a hazelnut: these are what will give it its crunch.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. It should be hot on top, but not smoking.
Place the apricots with the rounded side down, along with all their juice, then spread the sand mixture over them without packing it down.

Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 30 minutes, until the fruit has softened slightly and the crust has set. For a deeper browning, place the pan uncovered in a 180°C (350°F) oven for the last 10 minutes.
Let it cool in the pan before serving: the crumble firms up as it cools and does not collapse when scooped with a spoon.

title: Rustic tart with heirloom tomatoes and burrata
intro: It all comes down to the moisture of the tomatoes: a flavorful breadcrumb slipped under the filling absorbs the juice and keeps the pastry clean.
ing: fleur de sel for the finishing touch
Fine salt for the dough and filling
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from stovetop to oven without any transfer. You press the pastry base onto the baking sheet to set the crust, then place the pan directly into the oven. The tart arrives at the table in its baking container, with the burrata on top.
steps: Rub the flour and cold butter together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add the fine salt, herbes de Provence, and then the cold water all at once. Gather the dough together without overworking it, flatten it into a disc, wrap it in plastic wrap, and let it rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Chop the basil and mince the garlic. Mix them with the breadcrumbs. Set aside.
Cut the tomatoes into even 4mm slices. Even slices ensure even cooking. Place them on paper towels, lightly salt them, and let them drain while the oven preheats.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the clarified butter: it should spread out on its own in a fluid coating.

Roll out the dough to the diameter of the pan, plus a 5 cm overhang. Place it in the hot pan. Spread the aromatic breadcrumbs in the center, then arrange the tomato slices in a rosette pattern, alternating the colors. Season with salt and pepper.
Fold the edges of the pastry over the filling, pleating them. The center remains uncovered.
Cook over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. The dough will brown and pull away from the bottom of the pan on its own: that's the signal. Bake the pan for 27 minutes.

Remove from the oven. Place the whole burrata in the center, still warm from rinsing under hot water if you took it out of the refrigerator. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with fleur de sel, season with pepper, and add a few basil leaves. Serve in the pan.

title: Apple tart in a rosette pattern, rose water and pistachios
intro: It all comes down to the thinness of the slices and a base of pastry protected from the water released by the fruit.
ing: Almond flour, or failing that, fine breadcrumbs
Gala, Reine des Reinettes or Golden Delicious apples
Clarified butter or neutral oil with a high smoke point, for coating
titane: The pan serves as a mold: the dough is pressed into it, the rosette is piped on top, and then it goes into the oven as is, handle included. The direct contact with the bare metal causes the bottom of the dough to brown within the first few minutes, and the conductivity of the titanium pushes the caramelization of the apples further than with a traditional mold.
steps: Rub the flour, light brown sugar, salt and cold butter together with your fingertips, bring the dough together without working it, then let it rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. It should be hot enough to touch with the back of your hand, a few centimeters away. Remove from the heat.
Brush the inside with a thin layer of clarified butter. Let it cool down for a few moments: the dough should not melt on contact.
Roll out the dough and line the pan (cover the base and push the dough up the sides), pressing firmly in the corner. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Spread the almond flour over the base: it will absorb the juice from the apples during baking.

Slice the apples very thinly using a mandoline. Arrange them in a tight rosette, starting from the edge and working towards the center, with each slice overlapping the previous one. Brush with melted butter, then dust with brown sugar.
Bake the pan for 40 minutes at 180°C, until the pastry is golden brown and the apple tips are marked with caramel.
Warm the apricot jam with rose water, brush the apples with it as soon as they come out of the oven, then sprinkle with crushed pistachios.
Let it cool for 10 minutes before sliding the tart onto a rack: the base will detach on its own once the pan has relaxed.

title: Chocolate madeleines with brown butter
intro: It all comes down to two things: butter cooked until it's nutty brown, and a really cold dough when you put it in the oven.
titane: Brown butter is made in a titanium pan, not a saucepan. The temperature rises quickly and evenly across the entire surface: the milk proteins color without burning, and the light background allows you to judge the shade by eye. As soon as it reaches amber, remove it from the pan (immediately transfer it to a cold container) — the pan retains enough heat to cause the browning to become too intense.
steps: Melt the 70g of butter in the titanium pan over medium heat. Stir. Allow approximately 5 minutes: rely on the amber color and the nutty aroma, not the timer.
Transfer immediately to a bowl and let cool for 20 minutes off the heat.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar in a bowl. Add the milk and almond extract, mix.
Incorporate the flour and yeast, stopping as soon as the dough is homogeneous.
Pour in the lukewarm brown butter and work until completely absorbed.
Add the chocolate chips and mix briefly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Overnight will give a more pronounced hump.
Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Butter the mold cavities and fill them three-quarters full.
Bake for 2 minutes at 220°C, then reduce to 180°C and continue for 8 minutes, until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly in the mold before unmolding.

title: Baked oats, cocoa and peanuts
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: when they are very speckled, they alone sweeten the dough and give it its melt-in-your-mouth texture.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the gratin dish and goes directly from the worktop to the oven without transfer. Preheated empty and then greased with a film of high-smoke fat (which withstands high temperatures without browning), it releases the edges in one piece when serving.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Check that the pan handle is removable or oven-safe.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a bowl until you have a smooth puree without large pieces.
Add the oat flakes, cocoa, baking powder, peanut butter, maple syrup, plant-based milk, and vanilla. Mix until you have a smooth, thick batter.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Remove from heat and grease it with a thin film of clarified butter or grapeseed oil, including the edges.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface and bake for 30 minutes. The center should come away cleanly under the tip of a knife and the edges should pull away easily.
Take out the pan. Sprinkle the broken chocolate pieces over the hot surface, wait 2 minutes, then spread it into a smooth layer with a spatula.
Let it cool for 10 minutes in the pan before cutting into portions.

title: Burmese chickpea tofu
intro: A soy-free tofu that holds together solely through the gelling of chickpea flour: it all comes down to continuous whisking until the paste leaves the sides.

ing.note: that is, 160 ml for the tempera and 320 ml for the

titane: The wide surface of the pan allows steam to evaporate faster than in a narrow saucepan: the batter becomes creamy in just a few minutes. No need to preheat the pan; we're working with a liquid, not a mixture. Whisk continuously, and stop when the mixture pulls cleanly away from the sides of the pan.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the chickpea flour, turmeric, and salt with 160 ml of cold water. Mix until you obtain a perfectly smooth, lump-free batter.
Pour the remaining 320 ml of water into the titanium pan. Bring to a boil over high heat.

Reduce the heat to medium. Pour the dough in a thin stream into the simmering water, whisking constantly. Cook for about 5 minutes: the dough will thicken, become creamy, and then pull away cleanly from the sides of the pan.
Remove from heat and immediately transfer to a lightly oiled rectangular mold. Smooth the surface with a spatula.
Allow to set at room temperature for approximately 1 hour, or 30 minutes in the refrigerator. The surface should be firm to the touch, without leaving a mark.
Remove from the mold in one smooth motion onto a board. Cut into cubes or sticks as needed.

title: Gluten-free potato flade
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the dough: mash the potatoes while they are still hot, but only work them once they are lukewarm, otherwise the gluten-free flour will get soggy and the discs will stick.

ing.note: peeled and cut into large cubes
plus a little bit for the worktop

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. The pastry disc develops a golden crust in two to three minutes per side, without sticking, while the crumb remains soft. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the oil.
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the potatoes for 18 to 20 minutes, until a knife tip pierces them easily.
Drain thoroughly, then let them dry for 2 minutes in the pan off the heat. Residual moisture is the enemy of the dough.
Mash with a potato masher until smooth, without lumps. Let cool slightly.
Add the flour, yeast, salt, nutmeg, olive oil and spring onions.
Knead by hand for a few minutes, until you have a smooth dough that holds its shape in a ball. Lightly dampen your palms: it will stop sticking.
Divide into eight equal portions. Roll them into balls.
Roll out each portion (spread it out with a rolling pin) into a disc of 3 to 4 mm on a floured surface.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in a drizzle of high-smoke oil.
Place a disc in the pan. Do not touch it: it will detach itself from the pan once the first side is cooked, after 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and brown the other side.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack or a clean cloth to keep them moist. Repeat with the remaining discs, adding a drizzle of oil to the pan every two batches.

title: Pan-fried flax and psyllium bread
intro: It all comes down to hydration: the psyllium must swell enough to hold the crumb together, otherwise the bread remains dense and moist in the center.

ing.note: (which absorb water and structure the crumb)

titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe and replaces the baking pan. Shape the dough directly in it, starting with a cold pan on low heat, covered, to prime the base, then bake the pan uncovered. The base develops a dry, even crust, impossible to achieve with a baking pan.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C, fan-assisted.
Grind the flax seeds in a coffee grinder or blender until you obtain a fine flour. A few remaining pieces are fine; they add texture.
Mix the flaxseed flour, psyllium, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Work the mixture dry to distribute the yeast.

Pour the hot water in all at once and mix with a spatula. The mixture will thicken in about thirty seconds. Let it rest for 5 minutes: the psyllium will finish absorbing the water and the paste will become workable.

Lightly oil the titanium pan. Place the dough inside and shape it into a flattened ball, slightly smaller than the diameter of the pan, smoothing the surface with a wet hand. Make a 1 cm cut in the top with a blade.
Sprinkle with whole flax seeds, press lightly to make them adhere.
Place the cold pan over low heat, cover and leave for 5 minutes. The base will begin to set without browning.
Remove the lid and bake the pan for 40 minutes. The bread will rise, the crust will brown, and it will sound hollow when tapped. The center should be firm, not elastic.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. The crumb will stick to the knife when still warm.

title: Beetroot and red bean burgers
intro: A vegetable patty holds together or crumbles depending on the crust you give it in the first thirty seconds: it all depends on a pan that is already hot and a patty that you don't touch again.

ing.note: soaked for 10 minutes in 6 tablespoons of water

titane: Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil. The heat must be even and consistent across the entire surface: upon contact, the galette seals immediately and forms a firm crust that encases the bean and beet puree. A lukewarm pan, on the other hand, allows moisture to escape, and the galette falls apart at the first turn.
steps: Pulse the sunflower seeds, oat flakes, and smoked spices in a food processor until coarsely ground. Some grain should remain: this is what absorbs the water from the vegetables.

Add the onion, garlic, kidney beans, tamarind, tomato paste, grated beetroot, and chia seeds with their soaking water. Season with salt and pepper. Blend until you have a smooth paste that holds its shape when you press it in your hand.

Shape 4 to 6 even patties, with slightly damp hands, about 2 cm thick. Let them rest for 10 minutes in the refrigerator: the oats will finish absorbing the moisture and their texture will improve significantly.
Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be hot but not smoking.

Drizzle a little grapeseed oil into the pan, then add two or three patties without overcrowding it. Sear them (cooking over high heat will form a crust on contact) for 4 minutes without moving them. They are ready to turn when they easily release from the bottom of the pan.
Turn over, brown for 4 minutes on the other side, then transfer (remove from the pan and set aside) to a wire rack, not paper towels: the crust will stay crispy. Repeat with the remaining patties.
Briefly toast the bread in the still-hot pan. Assemble with the lettuce, fresh vegetables, and sauce.

title: Cherry tomato crumble with Comté cheese
intro: It all comes down to the water in the tomatoes: you have to boil them over high heat before putting them in the oven, otherwise the crust will soften.

ing.note: plus a few extra bits for finishing

titane: The pan never leaves the cooking area. It starts the tomatoes on high heat, then goes into the oven as a gratin dish. No transferring, so no juices are lost, and the heat rises from the bottom to brown the crumble evenly. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil: the titanium heats up quickly, and the tomatoes sear instead of mushy.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (conventional setting). Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut the cherry tomatoes in half. Mince the garlic. Combine them in a salad bowl with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, half the salt, and the thyme leaves. Mix well.
Pour the remaining oil into the hot pan. Increase the heat to high and sauté the tomatoes for 3 to 4 minutes, until they begin to release their juices.
Place the pan in the oven at the middle height for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese.

In a bowl, rub together the softened butter, flour, flaked almonds, three-quarters of the cheese, the remaining salt, and pepper with your fingertips. Stop as soon as you get a coarse, sandy texture: large, irregular lumps give more crunch than a smooth dough.

Remove the pan with an oven mitt—the handle is hot and stays that way for a long time. Sprinkle the tomatoes with the remaining cheese, then spread the crumble topping evenly without pressing it down.
Return to the oven at the middle rack for 30 minutes, until the crust is golden and crispy.
Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan. Add a few sprigs of fresh thyme and serve directly from the dish.

title: Dark chocolate and speculoos cookies
intro: A dough rich in brown sugar and almond flour, cooked directly in the pan: the bottom caramelizes while the center remains soft.
titane: The titanium pan goes in the oven, replacing the baking sheet and parchment paper.
