The dough rests directly on the surface: the heat penetrates the bottom unimpeded, allowing the bases to brown beautifully and develop a thin crust. After a few minutes of cooling, the cookies release cleanly with a spatula.
steps: Preheat the oven to 165°C, conventional heat.

Cream the softened butter (work it until it has a spreadable consistency) with the speculoos spread, brown sugar, and white sugar using an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until the mixture is smooth and homogeneous.
Incorporate the flour, almond flour, baking powder, and vanilla with a spatula. Stop as soon as the flour has been absorbed: overworking the dough will result in dry cookies.
Chop the chocolate with a knife into irregular, fairly large pieces. Roughly break the speculoos by hand.
Mix chocolate and speculoos into the dough, still using a spatula, in a few movements.
Form 11 to 12 balls using an ice cream scoop or your hands, directly in the cold titanium pan. Space them out: the dough will spread during cooking.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven and cook uncovered for 14 minutes. The edges should be golden brown and the center still soft to the touch; it will finish setting outside the oven.
Remove the pan from the heat and sprinkle with fleur de sel. Let the cookies cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then loosen them with a spatula.

title: Eggplant rolls with ricotta and tomato sauce
intro: It all comes down to how you handle the slices: coloured enough to have flavour, flexible enough to roll without breaking.
ing: tablespoons of olive oil or grapeseed oil
fleur de sel or coarse salt
tablespoons of fresh or dried thyme
titane: The preheated pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: the eggplant slices brown in minutes instead of drying out in the oven for twenty minutes. The gratin is then cooked under a lid; the retained heat is enough to melt the cheese. No oven or grill required.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the eggplant lengthwise into thin slices using a mandoline. Even slices ensure even cooking.
Pour the oil into the hot pan, turn up the heat to high and spread it with a flick of the wrist.

Arrange the slices in a single layer, without overlapping. Season with salt. Leave them undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes; they will release easily when golden brown. Turn them over and cook the other side. Cook for approximately 10 minutes in total, in batches.
Remove the cooked slices from the pan and set aside on a plate as you go, and repeat until all the slices are used up.
Grate the cheese. Peel and finely chop the garlic.
In a bowl, work the ricotta with the garlic, thyme, half of the grated cheese and pepper.
Wipe the pan with paper towels. Pour in the tomato sauce and spread it evenly over the bottom.
Let the eggplant slices cool for a few minutes: when hot, they tear easily.
Place a teaspoon of filling at the base of each slice, then roll towards the tip.
Arrange the rolls upright or lying down on the coulis, tightly packed together.
Sprinkle with the remaining grated cheese.
Cover and cook for 12 minutes over low heat, until the cheese is melted and the sauce is simmering.
Remove the lid, return to high heat for 3 minutes to brown the surface. Watch carefully: the cheese can quickly go from golden to burnt.
Add the chopped basil at the last second and serve in the pan.

title: Warm salad of roasted chickpeas, yellow zucchini and fresh goat cheese
intro: It's all about the contrast: really golden chickpeas, still warm, placed on cold raw vegetables and a tangy vinaigrette.

ing.note: in slices about a centimeter thick

titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter. The heat accumulated in the bottom will sear the chickpeas on contact, causing them to develop a crust instead of steaming. The lid does the rest of the work, like an oven: it retains the moisture from the zucchini while the base caramelizes. Use only one layer, without overlapping, otherwise the vegetables will release their water and boil.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the chickpeas and dry them thoroughly with a cloth. A dry surface will color, a damp surface will smoke.
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan. Immediately add the chickpeas and courgette slices, sprinkle with smoked paprika and thyme, then spread in a single layer.

Cover and roast for 15 minutes over the same heat, stirring as little as possible. The vegetables are ready when they easily pull away from the bottom of the pan, are golden brown, and the zucchini yields to the tip of a knife.
Take advantage of the cooking time to halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber and slice the olives.
Finely chop the mint and dill.
In a bowl, whisk together the mustard and vinegar, then gradually whisk in the olive oil. Add the honey and lemon juice, and whisk again.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the vegetables cool for 5 minutes: if they were piping hot, they would wilt the rocket.
Divide the sprouts among the plates, add the warm stir-fry, then the raw vegetables and olives. Crumble the goat cheese, sprinkle with pistachios and herbs.
Drizzle with vinaigrette, season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately.

title: Homemade pita bread, sliced peas and broad beans
intro: Everything happens in the pan: first the loaves, well risen and stained brown, then the slices in the same fragrant fat.
ing: Packet of spiced vegetable mince (peas and broad beans)
titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and retains its heat: the bread develops golden blisters without sticking, and the sliced meat can be added to the still-hot pan for a rich color in 5 minutes. In both cases, the same rule applies: don't touch anything until it releases easily.
steps: In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, salt, olive oil, honey, and water. Mix until you have a smooth ball that no longer sticks to your fingers. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.

Cut the cucumbers into large chunks and the cherry tomatoes into quarters. Season with olive oil, lemon juice, honey, and chili salt. Set aside: the tomatoes will release some juice, which is intentional.
Mix the yogurt with the juice and zest of half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper. Chill.
Divide the dough in half and roll out each piece into a 20-22 cm disc, regular and thin.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat.

Drizzle a little grapeseed oil over the pan, then place the first disc on top. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side over high heat, then reduce to medium so the center cooks through without burning the surface. Don't try to remove it; it will release easily when it's ready.
Remove from the pan and set aside under a damp cloth, then cook the second loaf in the same way.
In the still-hot, unwashed pan, add a drizzle of oil and toss in the sliced meat. Let it brown for 2 minutes without touching it, then stir and continue cooking for up to 5 minutes in total.
To serve: warm bread, a drizzle of yogurt sauce, vegetables and their juices, piping hot sliced meat, and generously chopped mint. Adjust the salt and finish with a squeeze of lemon.

title: Cornflake-crusted chicken burgers
intro: It all comes down to the breading: roughly crushed corn flakes, a really hot pan, and you don't touch anything for four minutes.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, until a drop of water sizzles and rolls in the pan. The oil you pour in will be at the perfect temperature immediately: the breading will seal on contact instead of absorbing the fat. You'll know the crust is set when the patty easily lifts off the bottom. Before this happens, any attempt to lift it will tear the cornflakes.
steps: Combine the ground chicken, garlic salt, pepper, smoked paprika, onion powder, cayenne pepper, and mustard in a bowl. Mix by hand until the spices are evenly distributed, without overworking the meat, as this will make it rubbery.
Lightly oil your palms. Weigh out 115g balls, then flatten them into even patties of about 1.5cm. You will get ten.

Prepare three containers: flour, egg whites, and cornflakes. Coat each patty in flour, tap off the excess, dip it in the egg whites, then press it firmly into the cornflakes so the coating adheres. Set aside on a baking sheet.
Preheat the oven to 190°C. Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the water droplet test.
Pour the grapeseed oil over the pan, then place the pancakes loosely on top—two or three per batch. Cook for 4 minutes without touching them, until they release from the pan on their own.

Flip with a flick of the wrist, sear for 3 minutes on the second side. If the patties are thick, transfer them from the pan to a baking sheet and bake for 5 to 8 minutes to finish cooking through without drying out the crust.
Assemble each burger: bun base, light mayonnaise, patty, shredded lettuce, top. Serve immediately; the breading won't benefit from waiting.

title: Cherry tomato and vegetarian merguez risotto
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the rice first, then the merguez sausages, and the juices from the searing return to the risotto.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in seconds. As soon as the risotto is removed (transferred to a dish to free up the pan), it's ready to sear the vegetarian merguez sausages over high heat. No rinsing is needed between cooking: the juices from the rice and tomatoes contribute to the crust.
steps: Press the garlic, finely chop the onion, and halve the cherry tomatoes. Keep the stock simmering in a small saucepan alongside: it should never boil.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Pour a drizzle of olive oil, then sauté the garlic and onion for 2 to 3 minutes, without letting them brown.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to make it translucent (the grains become translucent at the edges, opaque in the center).

Add enough hot stock to just cover the rice. Add the thyme and cherry tomatoes. Simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring regularly and adding more stock as soon as it is almost absorbed. Stop cooking when the rice is al dente and the mixture is still slightly runny.
Transfer the risotto to a shallow dish, cover, and keep warm.

Return the pan to high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Place the merguez sausages in the pan and leave them untouched: they will release their skins once a crust has formed. Reduce the heat to medium-high and continue cooking for approximately 6 minutes in total, turning them occasionally.
Take out the merguez sausages and cut them into thick slices.
Deglaze the pan (dissolve the browned bits stuck to the bottom) with two tablespoons of hot stock, then return the risotto to the pan. Grate the Parmesan cheese over the top and stir until melted.
Add the merguez pieces, mix one last time. Adjust the salt.
Arrange in bowls, season with pepper, and distribute the hand-chopped basil.

title: Small sweet potato buns stuffed with chicken and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to how well the dough holds up: a sweet potato that is well dry after cooking, otherwise the loaves stick and collapse in the pan.

ing.note: half a dose, or about 5 g
average, plus its greens if you have them

ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and intensely. Preheat it empty, then grease it: the chicken will develop a crust in seconds and the bread will brown without sticking. In both cases, don't flip anything until it releases easily. When it releases on its own, it's ready.
steps: Cut the sweet potato into large cubes and steam it, or bake it in the oven at 200°C (390°F). It's ready when a knife blade pierces it easily. Let it cool uncovered until slightly cool: the residual steam needs to escape.
Cut the chicken into approximately 2 cm cubes, finely chop the onion. Season with herbs, spices and salt.
Place the empty pan over high heat and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the fat, followed by the chicken and onion in a single layer.
Don't touch anything. The pieces will stick at first, then release on their own once a crust has formed. Turn it over at that point and finish cooking.

Deglaze the pan (dissolve the caramelized bits from the bottom with liquid) with two tablespoons of water, scraping with a spatula. Reduce the heat to medium, add soy sauce, ketchup, and maple syrup. Let it simmer for one minute.
Remove from the heat and stir in the roughly torn mozzarella. Remove two spoonfuls of sauce and set aside for serving. Transfer the filling to a cold dish to stop the cooking process.
Mash the sweet potato with a fork, season lightly with salt, and add flour and baking powder. Work the dough until it is smooth and no longer sticks to your fingers. Add flour if necessary.
Divide into 6 equal parts. Flatten each into a disc about 10 cm in diameter, place a spoonful of filling in the center, bring up the edges and seal them. Gently flatten with the palm of your hand.

Wipe the pan clean, brush it with oil, and return it to medium-high heat. Toast the buns for about 1 minute per side, seam-side down first. Don't press them down; they will release easily once golden brown.
Serve immediately with the reserved sauce and the chopped green onions.

title: Crispy pan-fried pasta
intro: Leftover pasta from the day before becomes a crunchy snack, provided you leave it alone in the pan until it comes away from you on its own.
ing: Pasta that has already been cooked and cooled
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: it does the work of an oven, without the wait. Preheat it empty, spread the pasta in a single layer, then leave it alone. When a crust has formed, the pasta will easily lift from the bottom—that's the signal to flip it.
steps: In a bowl, combine the oil, paprika, herbs, salt and pepper. Whisk with a fork to obtain a smooth marinade.
Pour the cold pasta into a bowl. Coat them with the marinade and mix gently by hand until each piece of pasta is coated.
Place the empty titanium pan over high heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes: a drop of water should dance on it before evaporating.
Spread the pasta in a single layer. Work in two batches rather than overloading the pan: if piled up, they will steam instead of browning.
Reduce the heat to medium-high and let it sear for 5 minutes without stirring. The pasta is ready to be turned when it easily releases from the bottom and has a golden-brown side.
Flip with a flick of the wrist, or give it a good stir, and continue cooking for 5 minutes until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.

title: Lentil curry with coconut milk
intro: It all comes down to the balance between the acidity of the tomato and the fat of the coconut milk: it is the reduction, not the cooking time, that determines when the dish is ready.
titane: Heat the pan empty for 1 to 2 minutes before adding anything. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the sauce starts reducing as soon as it touches the pan, without that lull where liquids cool down. On the other hand, the bottom can stick if you forget to do this. Stir every two or three minutes, scraping the bottom with a flexible spatula.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat. Let it heat for 1 to 2 minutes: a drop of water should sizzle immediately.
Add the lentils, tomato sauce, coconut milk, frozen spinach, curry, and salt. Mix to coat.

Cover and simmer for 10 minutes over medium heat. Stir three or four times, scraping the bottom of the pan. The spinach will break up and blend into the sauce, which will thicken slightly and coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from heat. Add the lemon juice, stir, then add the roughly chopped coriander. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve in the pan, with rice or warm flatbread.

title: Buffalo chicken turnovers
intro: A yogurt-based dough without resting, a well-drained filling: everything depends on the moisture, otherwise the pastry will get soggy underneath.
titane: The pan goes through the whole process. It sears the chicken dry, then oiled, it goes in the oven with the turnovers inside, and it restores crispness straight from the freezer. Always preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding a high-smoke-point fat (like grapeseed oil). Don't touch anything until the pastry releases itself: that's the sign of a good crust.
steps: Mix the flour, garlic salt, and Italian herbs. Add the yogurt all at once. Knead by hand until a smooth ball forms, about two minutes. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Drizzle in a little grapeseed oil, place the chicken breasts in the pan, and leave them in place. Turn them over when they release easily, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side depending on the thickness. Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and let cool slightly.

Shred the chicken (separate the meat into strands with a fork) or roughly chop it. Mix with the garlic salt, smoked paprika, ranch, pepper, salsa, onions, buffalo sauce, mozzarella, and chives. The filling should be a good binder, not runny; if it releases liquid, drain it in a colander.
Divide the dough into ten pieces. Roll each out into an oval about 3 mm thick. Place the filling on one half, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold over, seal with a fork, and make a small slit in the top.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Preheat an empty skillet for 2 minutes, place two or three turnovers in it, then put the skillet directly into the oven. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden brown and the base releases easily. Repeat in batches.
Blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, buffalo sauce, milk, garlic salt, pepper, and onion powder until smooth. Add a tablespoon of milk if the sauce is too thick.
For storage: allow to cool completely, wrap individually in aluminum foil or freezer bag, for up to one month.

To reheat: wrap a frozen pastry in a damp paper towel and microwave for 3 to 4 minutes on a plate. Finish for 2 to 3 minutes in a preheated titanium pan over high heat, without touching it, until a crust forms and the pastry releases easily.

title: Pan-fried breaded chicken nuggets
intro: Here, everything hinges on the crust: it forms on contact with hot metal, not in the soft heat of a furnace.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil. On titanium, the breadcrumbs adhere immediately and brown through direct contact. Once the nuggets are in the pan, do not touch them: they will release on their own when the crust is formed. If you force them, you will leave the breading in the pan.
steps: Mix the chicken pieces with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, Worcestershire sauce, and salt. Let it marinate for 20 minutes in the refrigerator, allowing the spices to penetrate the meat.

Coat using the English method (dip in beaten egg then in breadcrumbs). Use one hand for the egg and the other for the breadcrumbs: this keeps your fingers clean and the coating even. Press the breadcrumbs lightly so they adhere.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it out: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the nuggets in a single layer, without crowding them. Let them brown for 4 minutes without touching them. The piece will detach easily when the crust is set.

Turn them over with a flick of the wrist, reduce the heat to medium and continue for 6 minutes. Cover for the last two minutes if the pieces are thick: the steam finishes cooking them through without drying out the meat.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack, never on paper towels, to keep the bottom crispy.

title: Rustic apple, onion and Comté cheese tart
intro: It all comes down to the pan: apples and onions that are nicely browned and have lost their water before going into the oven, otherwise the dough will absorb it and collapse.

ing.note: large, or 4 if they are small

titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil: the temperature rises quickly, and the fruit sears on contact instead of simmering in its own juices. Once the slices are in place, don't touch them. They will stick, then release on their own when one side is set. That's when you flip them over, in one smooth motion.
steps: Combine flour, butter, egg, water and fleur de sel in a bowl. Knead until the dough forms a smooth ball, with no traces of dry flour.
Cover and refrigerate while preparing the filling.
Peel the apples and slice them into even pieces. Finely slice the onions (thin and even slices).
Place the titanium pan over high heat, empty. Wait 2 to 3 minutes: a light wisp of smoke indicates it's ready. Pour in the oil.

Add the apples and onions. Let them brown without stirring, then reduce the heat to medium-high. When the pieces start to pull away from the sides of the pan, turn them over. Cook for 10 minutes in total, until the flesh is soft and golden. If it starts to stick, a spoonful of water will loosen the browned bits.
Grate the Comté cheese.
Preheat the oven to 195°C, conventional heat.
Roll out the dough directly onto a sheet of baking paper, into a disc of about 30 cm.
Slide everything onto a baking sheet and prick the surface with the tip of a knife.
Spread the mustard in the centre, leaving a 2-3 cm margin all around.
Spread two-thirds of the Comté cheese, cover with the pan-fried topping, and finish with the remaining cheese.
Fold the pastry edge over the filling, forming irregular folds.
Place in the bottom of the oven for 35 minutes. Move the tray to the top of the oven for the last 3 minutes: the crust takes on a rich color and the cheese sizzles.
Scatter the thyme leaves over the tart as soon as it comes out of the oven. Serve warm.

title: Oat and banana pie crust
intro: Two ingredients, no oven: it all comes down to the pressure exerted at the bottom of the pan, which decides whether the dough will hold up when cut.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the batter. Covered, it works like an oven: the steam cooks the top while direct contact with the metal dries and browns the base. The bottom will tell you when it's ready, by shrinking from the edges.
steps: Mash the bananas with a fork until you have a smooth puree, without any lumps. The more discolored the peel, the more sugar it contains and the better the dough will bind.
Pour the oat flakes over the puree. Mix until all the flakes are coated and the mixture holds together in a ball when you hand it.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Coat it (cover the entire surface) with a thin layer of clarified butter using a brush.
Place the dough in the hot pan. Spread it out and press it firmly with the back of a spoon, in an even layer, right to the edges. A poorly pressed dough will fall apart when you try to unmold it.
Cover. Reduce heat to low and cook for 18 to 20 minutes without stirring or lifting the dough. It is ready when it pulls away from the sides of the pan on its own and sounds firm when touched.
Remove from heat, let cool for 10 minutes with the lid open, then unmold by turning the pan upside down onto a rack.

title: Red lentil patties
intro: It all depends on the moisture of the puree: too loose, the patties collapse; well bound, they take on a clean crust in four minutes.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two to three minutes when empty, replacing a thirty-minute oven cycle. Place the patties in the pan, then leave them alone. They will stick at first, which is normal: a crust is forming. Once set, the patty will release easily under the spatula. This is the only reliable indicator for flipping.
steps: Combine the lentils, potato, carrot and onion in a saucepan. Pour in the water: it should just cover the vegetables.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30 minutes. The lentils should be very tender and the potato should yield easily to the tip of a knife.
Mash everything with a potato masher, directly in the saucepan. Aim for a lumpy texture rather than a smooth, velvety consistency: the pieces provide structure.
Transfer (out of the pan) into a large bowl and let cool for five minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch, then the smoked paprika. Add the soy sauce, herbs, salt, and pepper. Mix with a spatula until you have a smooth dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Shape into patties about 7 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick, with slightly damp hands to prevent the dough from sticking.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the patties in the pan, leaving space between each one. Cook in two batches rather than overloading the pan. Let them cook for 4 minutes without stirring.
Flip the pancake over with a flick of the wrist as soon as it's free. Cook for another 4 minutes, until it's evenly golden brown. Place it on a wire rack, not paper towels, to keep it crisp.

title: Pan-fried pizza with a mozzarella-stuffed crust
intro: A dough without rising, two ingredients, and a pan hot enough to brown the bottom while the cheese melts under the lid.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the dough: this dry, hot contact replaces the pizza stone. The oil should be added afterward, never before, otherwise it will smoke and burn. The crust is ready when it easily lifts from the bottom without needing to be lifted with a spatula. If the top isn't brown enough, place the pan directly under the broiler.
steps: Combine the flour, yogurt, garlic salt and herbs in a bowl. Mix by hand until you get a crumbly mixture, without aiming for homogeneity at this stage.
Knead for 3 minutes on a lightly floured surface, until the dough becomes smooth and no longer sticks to your fingers.
Roll it out to the diameter of your pan, leaving a 3cm margin all around. Place the mozzarella sticks in a ring around the edge, fold the dough over and seal by pinching.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then brush it with a film of grapeseed oil.
Place the crust in the hot pan, sealed edge down.
Top directly in the pan: tomato sauce spread on the back of a spoon, grated mozzarella, slices of turkey pepperoni.
Cover and cook for 12 minutes over low-medium heat. The cheese should be melted and the bottom golden: lift an edge with a spatula, the pastry should detach easily.
To brown the top, slide the pan under the oven grill for 3 minutes, keeping a close eye on it.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before cutting. The mozzarella in the crust needs this time to stop oozing.

title: Bowls of Korean beef, broth rice and sriracha mayo
intro: Ten portions at once, and it all comes down to one thing: letting the beef brown before mixing it with the sauce.

ing.note: or other high smoke point oil

titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then oil it. Spread the beef in a thin layer and leave it undisturbed. The titanium coating quickly heats up, creating a brown crust in just a few minutes: this crust, not the sauce, is what gives the meat its color and charred flavor. The meat will tell you when it's ready; it will easily pull away from the bottom of the pan. The rice, however, should remain in the pot: nearly a liter of broth is more than a skillet can handle.
steps: Whisk together soy sauce, honey, gochujang, brown sugar, rice vinegar and sesame oil. Set aside.
Rinse the rice, then cook it in a saucepan with the chicken stock and garlic salt, covered, for about 15 minutes over medium heat. Let it rest off the heat, with the lid on.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the grapeseed oil: it should ripple on the surface without smoking.
Add the onion and garlic to the hot pan. Wait before stirring. The onion will detach from the bottom on its own when it becomes translucent.
Add the beef, spread it in a thin layer, and push the herbs to the edges. Let it sear undisturbed until the meat is tender and golden brown. Then, gradually crumble it with a spatula.
When the meat is almost cooked, reduce the heat to medium. Pour in the sauce, add the green onion and chili pepper. Stir and let it reduce for 3 minutes: the sauce should coat the meat and be glossy.
Remove from the pan (transfer to stop the cooking process) and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Mix mayonnaise, sriracha, lemon juice and garlic salt. Transfer to a squeeze bottle and keep chilled.
Divide the rice and beef into 10 equal portions in the containers. Allow to cool completely before sealing.
In the freezer, the bowls will keep for 3 to 6 months. To reheat: cover with a damp paper towel, microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through.
When ready to serve, add a dash of sriracha mayo and a little fresh green onion.

title: Beef Crunchwraps with Chipotle Sauce
intro: It all comes down to two contacts with the pan: a proper browning of the beef, then a golden and watertight tortilla seal.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the grapeseed oil (high smoke point) just before the meat, and leave it alone. The beef will release itself once a crust has formed. The same principle applies to toasting: place the seam side down against the cast iron, let it set, and it will detach on its own.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Drizzle in a little grapeseed oil, then add the ground beef and taco seasoning.

Let it sear without stirring. After 3 to 4 minutes, the meat will begin to break up easily and brown: then break it up with a spatula and continue cooking for 4 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Whisk together the Greek yogurt, chipotle paste, garlic salt, and lime juice. Taste and adjust the acidity with lime juice.

Spread the nacho cheese in the center of a large tortilla, on a disc the size of a small tortilla. Distribute the meat, add a tostada, then the Greek yogurt, tomatoes, and lettuce. Top with a small tortilla.
Fold the edges of the large tortilla towards the center in overlapping folds to enclose the filling. Press down. Repeat for all 10 pieces.

Wipe the pan with paper towels and return it to medium-high heat. Place the crunchwrap seam-side down. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes; it will release easily when the seam is set and golden brown. Flip and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately, or wrap in foil for freezing — removing the tostada, which does not withstand reheating.

title: Creamy crozets with pumpkin and Reblochon cheese
intro: The crozets are seared dry before the broth: it is this passage over high heat that gives the dish its grilled base, the rest is just patience.

ing.note: peeled and cut into small cubes

titane: The titanium pan heats up in two minutes, allowing the garlic and crozets to brown quickly and easily. However, it evaporates the broth faster than a heavy-bottomed pan: as soon as the liquid returns to a simmer, reduce the heat and add the remaining broth in small ladles, never all at once.
steps: Mince the garlic. Peel the pumpkin and cut it into one-centimeter cubes. Cut the Reblochon cheese into pieces and chop the hazelnuts: everything must be ready before lighting the fire.
Preheat the pan empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should roll into a ball before evaporating.
Pour in the oil, add the garlic, then the crozets. Leave them undisturbed for about 1 minute: they will detach themselves from the bottom when they are seared.
Add the butternut squash and stock in small amounts, just enough to cover, without exceeding 450 ml in total. Season with salt. Reduce the heat to medium-high.

As soon as it starts to simmer again (the surface will tremble, but not boil vigorously), reduce the heat to medium and cook for 20 minutes. Stir occasionally and add a ladleful of broth if it starts to stick.
At the end of cooking, stir more vigorously to crush the pumpkin cubes: they break down and bind the sauce around the crozets.
Turn off the heat, or reduce it to the lowest setting. Add the Reblochon cheese and stir until it melts and coats the crozets.
Adjust the salt and pepper. Serve in bowls, topped with hazelnuts and chives.

title: Quesadillas with shredded chicken, honey and chipotle
intro: It all comes down to two pan stages: cooking with the lid on to tenderize the chicken, then a quick and firm contact that seals the tortilla.
titane: The pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: place the quesadilla on top and leave it alone. The crust will form on its own and release itself when it's ready—if the tortilla resists, it needs another thirty seconds. The same pan is used to cook the chicken covered, then to brown it: a single piece of equipment from start to finish.
steps: Place the chicken breasts in the cold pan with the garlic salt, pepper, chipotles, lime juice and honey. Pour in a little water, about 1 cm deep.
Cover and cook over low heat for 40 minutes. The chicken is ready when a fork easily separates it.
Meanwhile, blend all the sauce ingredients together until smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Refrigerate.
Remove the chicken from the pan and place it on a plate. Drain it, reserving two or three tablespoons of the cooking juices.
Shred the flesh using two forks, pulling in the direction of the fibers.
Mix the shredded chicken with half the sauce, the mozzarella, the chives and the reserved juices. Taste and adjust the salt.
Fill one half of each tortilla, fold over the other half and press lightly with the palm of your hand.
Wipe the pan clean. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the clarified butter: it should ripple without smoking.

Place one or two quesadillas on the grill, reduce the heat to medium, and leave them undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes. When the quesadilla releases easily from the grill, flip it over and cook for another 2 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Cut in half and serve with the remaining chipotle sauce.

title: Honey Cajun Chicken Burritos
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: if seared thoroughly, it retains character even after being shredded and smothered in sauce.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature even when you add 1.7 kg of cold chicken. Preheat it empty, then leave the meat alone: it will stick, brown, and release itself once a crust has formed. The same pan can be used to brown the burritos when serving, without needing to wash it in between.
steps: Mix the chicken with the garlic salt, Cajun seasoning, Italian herbs, garlic, tomato paste, and honey. Massage to coat each piece. Let it rest while you prepare the rest.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the oil: it should ripple on the surface without smoking.
Place the chicken in a single layer, without overlapping. Repeat this process if necessary. Leave it undisturbed for 6 to 7 minutes: the meat will release easily once the crust has set.
Turn over, continue cooking for 5 to 6 minutes until fully cooked. Remove from the oven (transfer to a separate dish) and set aside.
In the same still-hot pan, sauté the onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes over medium heat. They should remain firm and release their juices from the bottom of the pan. Set aside with the chicken.
Blend all the sauce ingredients until you get a perfectly smooth texture, with no cottage cheese grains.
Shred the chicken using two forks, pulling in the direction of the fibers.
Remove from heat and combine the shredded chicken, vegetables, sauce, mozzarella, and chives in the pan. Mix well: the residual heat will melt the cheese.
Spread 60g of rice on each tortilla, then add a ladleful of filling, leaving a 3cm border. Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly.
To store: wrap each burrito in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag. Up to 3 months in the freezer.
To reheat: wrap the frozen burrito in a damp paper towel, place it on a plate, microwave for 5 to 6 minutes.
Finally: cook it for 2 to 3 minutes per side in the hot titanium pan, without oil, until the tortilla is golden and crispy.

title: Seared chicken and creamy cottage pasta
intro: The entire success of this dish comes from two things: a sauce thick enough to coat without being soggy, and a chicken of even thickness that takes on its crust all at once.
titane: The titanium pan heats up faster than a regular non-stick pan. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding the oil: the chicken will stick at first, then release easily once a crust has formed. This is the signal to flip it, not the clock. And since the sauce won't burn on the bottom, you can toss the pasta in the same pan.
steps: Combine the cottage cheese, Parmesan, garlic, milk, garlic salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. If it seems too runny, don't add more milk; it should coat the cheese, not be swimming in it. Set aside.
Place the breasts between two sheets of cling film. Flatten them with a rolling pin or in the bottom of a pan to an even thickness of about 1.5 cm. Uniformity is more important than thinness.
Mix the garlic salt, Italian seasoning, onion powder, smoked paprika, and pepper. Coat the chicken on both sides: the surface should be completely colored by the spices.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil. It should ripple slightly, without smoking.

Place the chicken in the pan without overcrowding it, working in two or three batches. Don't touch it: the chicken will stick at first, then release on its own once the crust has formed, after 4 to 5 minutes. Turn it over and cook for another 4 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F). Remove from the pan and keep covered.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water for one minute less than the package instructions. Drain, reserving a ladleful of the cooking water.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the pasta and sauce to the still-hot pan. Stir until completely coated. Thin with a little pasta water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Slice the chicken against the grain. Divide the pasta among 10 containers, place the chicken on top, and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Let cool uncovered before sealing, then refrigerate or freeze.

title: Pan-grilled turkey burrito
intro: It's all about patience: let the turkey and vegetables brown without moving them, then grill the patty long enough so that it gets a crust instead of getting soggy.

ing.note: 1 fillet for cooking, 1 fillet for grilling

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil or butter. Then, sear the vegetables, cook the meat, and grill the burrito all in the same pan: the caramelized juices that stick to the bottom will remain in the pan, and the burrito will brown evenly.
steps: Thinly slice the red onion and bell pepper. Cut the turkey fillet into even strips.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil. It should simmer gently, without smoking.
Add the vegetables to the hot pan and leave them alone. They will release their fat on their own once they are browned: that's when you need to stir them. Cook for 4 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan. Sear the turkey in the freed-up cooking juices, without turning it until it has browned and releases easily from the pan. Cook for about 4 more minutes.
Combine the meat and vegetables, mix, and remove from the heat. Place the filling in the center of the galette, spread the grated mozzarella on top, fold over the two sides, and then roll tightly.
Whisk together the fromage blanc, mustard, ketchup, stevia and salt. Chill until ready to serve.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, add a drizzle of oil over medium heat. Place the burrito seam-side down and leave it alone: it will release on its own once a crust has formed. Flip it over and brown the second side. Cook for a total of 5 minutes, then slice diagonally and serve with the sauce.

title: Creamy pasta with chicken and mushrooms
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the chicken releases its juices, the mushrooms absorb them, and the pasta finishes absorbing them.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat: the chicken sticks just enough to create juices that will then flavor the mushrooms and the sauce. No need to change utensils, nothing is wasted.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.

Increase the heat to high and place the chicken pieces in a single layer. Do not touch them. They will separate easily when browned, about 3 minutes. Turn them over, cook for another 3 minutes, season with salt and pepper, and remove from the pan and set aside, covered.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the pan, stir for 2 minutes, then add the mushrooms and garlic. Let them release their liquid and begin to brown, about 3 minutes.
Deglaze (dissolve the juices stuck to the bottom with a liquid) with a little chicken stock, scraping the bottom with a spatula.

Add the uncooked pasta and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring regularly, for 12 to 15 minutes depending on the type of pasta. Add more water a little at a time if the surface dries out too quickly. The liquid should be almost completely absorbed and coat the pasta.
Turn off the heat. Return the chicken and its juices to the pan, then stir in the cream cheese, Parmesan, and parsley. Mix until you have a smooth sauce.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover and let it melt for 3 to 5 minutes off the heat, using the residual heat. Serve immediately.

title: Bowl of sautéed potatoes, minced beef and pickle sauce
intro: It all comes down to two crusts: the potato crust and the beef crust, obtained dry in a very hot pan and left to do its work.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven tray. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, until a light wisp of smoke rises, then oil it and arrange the diced potatoes in a single layer. Ten minutes of direct contact, without stirring, is enough to form a crust. The same principle applies to the beef: it will release itself when it's ready. If you have to force it, it's too soon.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even cubes, around 2 cm.
Plunge them into a saucepan of boiling salted water. Count 5 minutes: the surface should yield under the tip of a knife, the center should remain firm.
Drain thoroughly and allow the steam to evaporate for 2 minutes. Season with garlic salt, smoked paprika, onion powder, and grapeseed oil. Toss to coat.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. When it is lightly smoking, pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil.
Arrange the cubes in a single layer. Don't touch them for 10 minutes. They will separate on their own once golden brown. Work in two batches rather than overcrowding the pan.
Remove the potatoes from the pan and set aside, then cover to keep warm.
In the same pan, over medium heat, sauté the onions for 5 minutes until golden brown. Remove from heat.
Turn up the heat. Spread the ground beef in a thick layer in the hot pan and let it cook for 6 minutes without stirring, until a brown crust forms and it releases easily.
Chop the meat with a spatula, remove from the heat, then stir in the garlic salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cheddar cheese, mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard. The residual heat will melt the cheese.
Mix together in a bowl the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, chopped pickles, pickle juice and pepper.
Transfer the sauce into a flexible bottle: the stream will be more even than with a spoon.
Divide the potatoes among the bowls, cover with beef and browned onions, then drizzle with sauce.

title: Crispy polenta fries
intro: It all comes down to cooling: a firm polenta cuts cleanly and holds its shape without collapsing.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when cold polenta sticks are added. Preheat it empty, then oil it: a crust forms in minutes, whereas an air fryer requires a full cycle. Don't touch anything while the polenta is sticking. When it releases easily, the side is cooked.
steps: Salt the water and bring it to a simmer in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Gradually pour in the polenta while whisking constantly.
Continue cooking, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Remove from heat, stir in the parmesan and mix until fully absorbed.
Transfer the mixture from the pan to a dish and spread it evenly into a layer about 1.5 cm thick. Let it cool for 1 to 2 hours, until the surface is firm to the touch.
Remove the block from the mold onto a board and cut into even sticks, the size of a large French fry.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. It is ready when a drop of water rolls into a ball.
Pour the fat over the pan, arrange the sticks in a single layer without packing them too tightly. Let them cook for 4 minutes without intervening: they will detach themselves once a crust has formed.
Turn them over one by one, reduce the heat to medium-high, and cook for another 4 minutes. The outside should be crisp, the inside soft and melting. Serve immediately with a pinch of salt.

title: Seared cod bowls, corn-tomato salsa and avocado crema
intro: The fish goes straight from the freezer into the hot pan: it's the only way to get a clean crust without the flesh falling apart.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then place the oiled fillets in it and leave them undisturbed. The titanium dioxide heats up quickly and intensely: a crust forms in just a few minutes, and the fish will release easily once it's set. If you try to force it with a spatula, you'll leave the crust stuck to the bottom.
steps: Mix the tomatoes, corn, red onion, jalapeño, coriander, garlic salt and lime juice in a salad bowl.
Let the salsa rest in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. The onion will soften and the juices will bind together.
Blend the yogurt, avocado, garlic, lime juice, garlic salt and pepper until smooth. Chill.
Cook the rice in water, separately in a saucepan. The frying pan is reserved for the fish.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Brush the still-frozen steaks with grapeseed oil or clarified butter, then sprinkle generously with taco seasoning.

Place the fish in the hot pan, without overcrowding it: allow two or three batches. Do not move it. Wait until it releases easily, about 6 to 7 minutes, then turn it over and brown the second side for 5 minutes.
Remove (transfer from the pan to stop cooking) to a plate and break into large pieces with a fork.
Assemble the bowls: rice at the bottom, fish, salsa, then a spoonful of crema.
For meal prep, divide into 10 airtight containers. They can be kept in the freezer for 3 months.
When reheating, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water to the frozen container, cover with a damp paper towel and microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through.

title: Shredded chicken burrito with chipotle sauce
intro: It all comes down to two things: a colored chicken before being shredded, and a roll tight enough so that the patty toasts without opening.
ing: with 2 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the chicken. The rapid heat ensures even browning, and the meat will release easily. Between steps, a quick wipe with a paper towel is all it takes: titanium doesn't retain residue like a non-stick coating, and this same pan, without any added fat, will brown the burrito.
steps: Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. The surface should be very hot, but not smoking.
Pour in the oil. Sear the chicken breasts over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, turning them halfway through. They will release easily from the pan when browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove the chicken from the pan and place it on a board, let it rest for 5 minutes, then shred it with a fork, that is, separate the meat into strands.
In a bowl, mix the yogurt, chipotle, lime juice, and garlic powder. Season with salt and pepper. Taste and adjust the chili pepper.
Wipe the still-warm pan with paper towels. Over low heat, warm each patty for 30 seconds per side, just to soften it.
Arrange in the center, in a strip: chicken, cheddar cheese, nacho sauce, chipotle sauce.
Add the pico de gallo, the lettuce, then the crushed chips last so that they remain crunchy.

Fold in the sides and roll tightly. Return the pan to medium heat, without any oil, and place the burrito seam-side down. Toast for 2 minutes: it will release easily once a crust has formed. Brown the other side for 1 minute.

title: Large savory pancake with cherry tomatoes and Gruyère cheese
intro: It's all about the contrast: a crispy, clean base, a soft center, and a golden-brown top.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold batter is added: the bottom sears immediately instead of absorbing the butter. Then, the same pan can do it all—sear, gently cook covered, or broil. Just make sure the handle is oven-safe.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the clarified butter; it should coat the bottom without smoking.
Meanwhile, cut the cherry tomatoes in half.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs vigorously with the flour, milk, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. The batter should be smooth and lump-free.
Incorporate the grated Gruyère cheese and give it one last whisk.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan, arrange the cherry tomatoes cut-side up. Leave it alone: let it cook until the edges pull away from the sides.
Reduce heat to low, cover and cook for 15 minutes. The center should be set without the bottom browning further.
Preheat the oven grill to 225°C and place the pan in the oven for 5 minutes, until the surface is golden brown.
Remove (slide out of the pan) onto a board and cut into portions.

title: Gado gado, sautéed vegetables and tempeh with peanut sauce
intro: It all comes down to the tempeh: seared dry or almost dry, it crisps up without going through the deep fryer, and the sauce is then made in the same pan.

ing.note: cut into small cubes (2 cm maximum)

ing: The juice of half a lime
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat. Place the tempeh cubes in it and don't touch them: they'll stick at first, then release on their own once a crust has formed. That's the signal, not the timer. The vegetables, the stir-fry, and the sauce all go in the same pan, without rinsing between steps—the juices left by the tempeh enrich the peanut sauce.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It is ready when a drop of water forms a bead in it before evaporating.
Pour in a tablespoon of oil. Add the potatoes and carrots, stir to coat them, and let them brown for 3 minutes.

Add the snow peas, then 3 tablespoons of water. Cover for 1 minute, uncover, and let the water evaporate, stirring occasionally. Repeat once or twice depending on the size of the cubes. Cook for a total of 10 minutes: the vegetables should be tender when pierced with a knife but still firm to the bite.
Remove (take out of the pan and set aside in a bowl) all the vegetables.

Return the pan to high heat and add the remaining oil. Place the tempeh cubes in the pan, leaving space between them, without moving them. Wait until they release their fat on their own, about 2 minutes, then turn them over. Cook for a total of 6 minutes. Season with salt.
Remove the tempeh from the pan along with the vegetables.

Reduce the heat to low. In the still-warm pan, combine the peanut butter, soy sauce, curry paste, sambal oelek, lime juice, coconut milk, and 60 ml of water. Stir with a whisk or spatula to loosen any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Heat for 5 minutes without boiling, until the sauce is smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Taste and adjust the salt.
Return the vegetables and tempeh to the pan, add the raw cucumber, mix off the heat and serve immediately, either in the pan or in deep plates.

title: Crispy chocolate, hazelnut and fleur de sel tablet
intro: It all comes down to melting the chocolate: very gently, stirred continuously, to keep it shiny and crisp when cut.
titane: The pan replaces the double boiler. Placed over very low heat, it melts chocolate and coconut oil in just a few minutes, without water or a suspended bowl. Stir constantly to distribute the heat, and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth: the residual heat of the titanium finishes the job.
steps: Roughly crush the rice cakes by hand in a bowl. Keep some uneven pieces: this is what gives them texture when you bite into them.
Add the hazelnut puree, peanuts, and maple syrup. Mix until each piece is coated.
Spread the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, to a thickness of approximately 1 cm. Press down firmly with the palm of your hand to seal the mixture.

Place the broken chocolate and coconut oil in the cold titanium pan. Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly with a flexible spatula, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy. Remove from the heat as soon as it is homogeneous.
Pour the chocolate over the spread mixture and smooth with a spatula, pushing well to the edges.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel while the chocolate is still liquid, so that it adheres.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, until completely set. Cut into irregular pieces by breaking the slab by hand.

title: Thin tart with tomatoes, courgette and parmesan
intro: It all comes down to the base: a dough that's been seared in a pan before going in the oven will never release the water from the vegetables.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a mold. Preheat it empty, oil it, press the dough into the bottom (spreading it to fit the shape), then sear the base for two minutes over high heat before placing the pan in the oven as is. No transferring or handling of the filled dough: the base cooks from the bottom from the very first minute.
steps: Combine flour, olive oil, egg, grated Parmesan cheese, and salt in a bowl. Work the mixture until you have a smooth ball of dough, free of dry flour lumps. If the dough is crumbly, add a tablespoon of water; if it's sticky, add a little flour.
Wrap the ball in plastic wrap and keep it chilled while you prepare the filling.
Cut the tomatoes and courgette into even slices, about 4 mm thick.
Arrange the tomato slices on a plate, salt them and let them sit for 8 minutes to draw out the excess moisture. Then pat them dry with paper towels.
Preheat the oven to 190°C using conventional heat.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then brush the bottom with a drizzle of olive oil.
Roll out the dough into a disc slightly smaller than the diameter of the pan. Place it in the oiled base and push it up to the edges with your fingertips.
Prick the dough with a fork. Spread the ricotta, leaving a 2-3 cm border.
Arrange the tomato and courgette slices alternately, in a tight spiral from the edge towards the center.
Fold the pastry edge over the filling. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese and thyme.
Return the pan to high heat for 2 minutes: the base should firm up and begin to pull away from the sides on its own. Slide the entire pan into the bottom of the oven.

Bake for 28 minutes on the bottom rack of the oven, then move the pan to the top rack for 5 minutes, until the topping is golden brown and the Parmesan has formed a crust. Let it cool for 5 minutes before sprinkling with basil and slicing.

title: Pan-fried oatmeal wraps
intro: Two ingredients, a very smooth blended batter: everything depends on the temperature of the pan, which must set the pancake as soon as it touches the pan.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the first ladleful. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without any cold spots: the oat paste sets instantly on contact, the wrap remains thin, flexible, and releases easily when you flip it.
steps: Blend the oats with the water for 2 minutes, until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous paste, without any perceptible grains. Let it rest while the pan heats up: the paste will thicken slightly.
Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush with a drizzle of grapeseed oil or clarified butter: the fat should ripple, not smoke.

Pour a ladleful of batter and spread it with a circular motion of the wrist. Let it cook for 3 minutes without touching it, over medium heat. The surface will set, the edges will shrink and detach on their own.
Flip the wrap over with a quick, sharp movement and continue for 2 minutes on the other side, until it reaches a blonde color.
Remove the wraps from the pan and place them on a plate, stacking them as you go: the trapped steam keeps them soft. Lightly grease the pan between each stack.
Fill as desired, sweet or savory, and roll while the wrap is still warm.

title: Sliced pea protein with almond cream
intro: It all comes down to two things: well-plumped pea proteins, drained without restraint, and a sauce reduced uncovered until it coats the back of a spoon.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. On titanium, the onion will release easily when it's ready: don't force it with a spatula, just wait. Then, the cream will reduce quickly and without sticking, provided you keep the liquid level below 500 ml and stir regularly.
steps: Pour boiling water over the pea protein in a bowl, covering it completely. Let it soak for 10 minutes, until it feels soft to the touch. Drain and squeeze out the excess water.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion.
Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A few drops of water thrown onto it should dance before evaporating.
Pour in the grapeseed oil, add the onion. Let it color for 5 minutes without stirring it right away: it will detach itself from the surface when it is translucent and golden in places.
Add the herbs of Provence, mix for 30 seconds to awaken them with the heat.

Reduce the heat to low. Pour in the cream and plant-based milk, add the nutritional yeast and soy sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the grated vegan cheese off the heat, stirring for 2 minutes until the sauce becomes smooth again.
Add the drained pea protein. Stir for 2 minutes to coat and heat through. Adjust the salt.
For meal prep: divide into containers, let cool uncovered before sealing. Four to five days in the refrigerator, two months in the freezer.

title: Chicken oyakodon with runny egg and miso mayonnaise
intro: Here, the chicken is seared thoroughly before being coated with egg: it is this contrast between color and tenderness that separates this oyakodon from a simple stew.
ing: Japanese short-grain rice, weighed before cooking
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the meat is added. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, oil it, then place the chicken inside without moving it. It will stick, brown, and then release on its own: that's the signal. If you overload the pan, the temperature will drop and the meat will steam.
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Mix them with the soy sauce and rice vinegar. Let it marinate while you prepare the rice, about 10 minutes.

Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs almost clear: the surface starch will be rinsed away. Cook it covered in a saucepan over medium heat with its usual amount of water for about 15 minutes, until the grains are tender. Remove from heat and set aside, covered.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.

Place the drained chicken and onion in a single layer. Leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes. When the pieces begin to separate on their own, stir and continue cooking for 4 to 5 minutes, until the meat is cooked through and the onion is translucent.
Reduce the heat to low. Beat the eggs with a fork, without making them frothy, and pour them in a steady stream over the entire surface.
Cover and poach for 3 to 4 minutes. Stop when the egg is set around the edges and still creamy in the center.
Divide the rice between two bowls. Slide the chicken and egg mixture on top in one piece. Finish with a drizzle of miso mayonnaise and the sliced scallions.

title: Golden potatoes, spicy tofu and lime crema
intro: It all comes down to the size of the wedges: if they are thin, they cook in a pan in twenty minutes and brown instead of sweating.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains heat. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before each use: the potatoes, and then the tofu, will stick at first, then release easily once a crust has formed. No oven, no air fryer, just one pan from start to finish.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin wedges. Mix them in a bowl with a drizzle of grapeseed oil, salt, cumin and paprika, until each side is coated.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Drizzle with oil, arrange the wedges in a single layer without overlapping. Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 18 minutes, turning every 4 to 5 minutes. They are ready when golden brown, tender in the center, and easily release from the pan.
Remove them from the pan and keep them warm. Wipe the pan with a paper towel.

Add a drizzle of oil to the pan over high heat. Add the crumbled tofu and chopped onion. Leave it alone for 2 minutes; wait until the tofu breaks up on its own before stirring. Cook for a total of 6 minutes, until it's nicely browned.
Add the soy sauce, tomato paste, cumin, maple syrup, and salt. Stir-fry for 3 minutes over high heat, until the paste loses its raw taste and coats the tofu.
Add the cherry tomatoes, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 2 minutes. They should warm through and release some juice, not fall apart.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, mix together the plant-based yogurt, cream cheese, sriracha, and a squeeze of lime juice. The crema should coat the back of a spoon.
To serve: place the potatoes at the bottom, top with the tofu and tomatoes, then the shredded lettuce, and finally drizzle with the crema. Serve immediately.

title: Soft apple and lupin flour cake
intro: It all comes down to the apples: softened in a pan before being added to the batter, they release their water at the right time and the cake remains moist without excess fat.
titane: Heat the empty pan for two to three minutes before greasing. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and distributes heat evenly: the apple cubes barely color, soften under the lid, and release easily from the surface. This slight caramelization gives the pastry its texture.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter or grapeseed oil, and spread it in a thin layer.

Cut the apples into even cubes about 1.5 cm in size. Add them to the hot pan, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Stir once or twice, no more: the cubes should soften and rise to the surface on their own.
Remove the apples from the pan to stop the cooking process and let them cool slightly.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the yogurt, plant-based drink and peanut butter until smooth.
Add the two flours, ground peanuts, whey protein, and yeast. Mix just enough to combine, without overmixing.
Gently fold in the cooled apples with a spatula, lifting the batter as you do so.
Pour into a 20-22cm cake tin and bake at 180°C for 33 minutes. Insert a knife into the center: the blade should come out clean.
Let it cool in the mold, unmold, then cut into 10 pieces.

title: Dark chocolate mousse and silken tofu
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the chocolate at the time of mixing: too hot, it makes the tofu grainy; too cold, it solidifies into grains.
titane: Forget the bain-marie. The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan, over very low heat: the heat is distributed without hot spots, nothing sticks, and you only have one utensil to wash before transferring to the blender.
steps: Remove the silken tofu from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature while you prepare the chocolate. Frozen tofu will cause the chocolate to harden on contact.
Break the chocolate into even pieces. Place them in the cold titanium pan, then turn on over very low heat.

Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the edges towards the center. This should take 3 minutes. The chocolate is ready when it is completely smooth and glossy, with no lumps at the bottom. Remove from heat immediately.
Pour the silken tofu into the blender bowl, add the agave syrup, then the still-warm melted chocolate.
Blend at full speed for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides halfway through. The mixture should be perfectly smooth, a deep brown and glossy.
Taste it. Adjust the sugar according to the bitterness of your chocolate, and blend for 10 more seconds if you add syrup.
Divide into four ramekins. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours. The mousse sets as it cools: this time is essential.

title: Pear-chocolate fudge
intro: Two ingredients, no cream: the entire structure of the fudge comes from the pectin in the pear and the cocoa butter, so the pear must stew until it loses its water.
titane: One pan for both cooking methods. The pears simmer, covered, in a little water, without a pot of boiling water. Then you wipe the pan, reduce the heat to very low, and melt the chocolate in it, without a double boiler. The titanium pan's mass cools down slowly: it's the mass that prevents the chocolate from burning, not the water.
steps: Peel the pears, remove the core and seeds, cut the flesh into 2 cm pieces.
Preheat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It must be thoroughly hot before adding any fat.
Pour in the grapeseed oil, add the pears and water. Cover, reduce the heat to medium and simmer (cook gently until the fruit breaks down) for 10 minutes, stirring two or three times.
Discover the consistency. If there is still liquid, continue cooking uncovered for a minute or two: the compote should be thick, not wet. Transfer (off the heat) to the blender bowl.

Wipe the pan with paper towels and return it to very low heat. Add the chocolate and stir constantly until melted and glossy, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat as soon as the last pieces disappear.
Pour the melted chocolate over the still-warm pears. Blend until smooth and homogeneous, without any lumps.
Pour into a baking paper-lined mold, to a thickness of 2 cm. Smooth with a spatula.
Refrigerate overnight. Unmold and cut into squares with a blade that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Cajun chicken pasta with creamy cottage cheese sauce
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: a really hot pan, a still contact, and juices (golden deposits left at the bottom) that the sauce will collect.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding the chicken. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the meat arrives cold: this is what makes the difference between a gray piece and a golden one. Then, do not wash the skillet. The sauce is heated directly in it and dissolves the juices. Only the pasta goes in a saucepan: the necessary amount of water doesn't belong in a skillet.
steps: Coat the chicken breasts with grapeseed oil, then massage them with the 35g of Cajun seasoning. Let them come to room temperature while the pan heats up.
Preheat the pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should bead on it without evaporating immediately.
Place the chicken in the pan and leave it alone. It will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. Only then should you turn it over and finish cooking it thoroughly.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside on a cutting board. Wipe the pan clean if the spices have darkened, without rubbing off the clear juices.
Blend the cottage cheese, milk, tomato paste, garlic and 25g of Cajun seasoning with the Parmesan cheese until smooth and grain-free.
Cook the pasta in plenty of salted water in a saucepan, according to the time indicated on the package. Reserve a ladleful of the cooking water.
Pour the sauce into the pan over medium-low heat. Scrape the bottom with a spatula to loosen any browned bits. Let it simmer gently without boiling; the sauce will curdle if it gets too hot.
Add the drained pasta and mix until completely coated. Thin with cooking water if the sauce thickens.
Slice the chicken into thick pieces and arrange them on top of the pasta.
Finish with chopped chives and chili flakes.

For meal prep: divide into 10 airtight containers, for up to 3 months in the freezer. To reheat, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through.

title: Vegan pan-fried chilaquiles
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the tortillas: they must be crispy before meeting the salsa, otherwise the dish turns into lukewarm mush.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and intensely. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil: the tortilla triangles will sear on contact, develop a crust, and release easily once it's formed. As long as they're sticking, they're not ready. A single pan is then all you need for the onion and assembly.
steps: Cut the tortilla into six triangles. Coat them with a little oil using your fingertips, and season lightly with salt.
Finely chop the onion. Crumble the tofu by hand. Slice the avocado, and chop the coriander.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Drizzle with a little grapeseed oil.

Place the triangles in a single layer, without overlapping them. Let them brown for 3 minutes without touching them: they will detach on their own when the crust is set. Turn them over and bake for another 3 minutes.
Remove the tortillas from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. In the same pan, sauté the onion with a drizzle of oil for 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add the red salsa and let it heat for 30 seconds. Return the tortillas to the pan and coat them quickly, for 1 to 2 minutes: they should remain crispy under the sauce.
Serve directly from the pan. Distribute the avocado, crumbled tofu, coriander, and squeeze the lime over at the last moment.

title: Crispy pan-fried chickpeas
intro: It all comes down to two things: perfectly dry chickpeas and a pan that's already hot when they get in.
ing: 1/2 tsp of spices of your choice
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two or three minutes when empty. You can sear the chickpeas immediately, without waiting for an oven to preheat, and the crust forms on direct contact with the metal.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should dance on it without evaporating immediately.
Drain the chickpeas, rinse them, then dry them thoroughly in a clean cloth or between two sheets of absorbent paper. Every remaining drop delays the crispness.
Pour them into a bowl. Add the oil, smoked paprika, spices, salt, pepper and cornflour.
Mix until each chickpea is coated with a thin matte film, with no lumps of starch at the bottom of the bowl.

Pour them into the hot pan and spread them out in a single layer. If they overlap, cook them in two batches. Let them cook for 8 minutes without touching them: they will detach from the bottom on their own once a crust has formed.

Shake the pan in short bursts for 4 minutes to brown the other sides. Taste one: it should crackle when you bite into it. Remove from the pan immediately and transfer to a wide dish, never to a covered container.

title: Red lentil and carrot patties
intro: It all comes down to the hydration of the dough and patience in the pan: a galette that is moved too soon will tear.
titane: Heat the empty pan for two to three minutes before adding oil: the rapid and even heat of the titanium coating sets the crust as soon as it touches the pan. Then, leave it alone. The pancake will release on its own when one side is set, and that's the only reliable sign to flip it.
steps: Place the lentils in a small saucepan, cover with 400 ml of cold water and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium heat for 13 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, peel the carrots and grate them finely.
Finely chop the onion and garlic. Chop the parsley and chives.
Drain the lentils and let them cool for a few minutes in the colander, so that they release their excess water.
Combine the lentils, carrots, onion, garlic, herbs, flour, curry, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add water and mix until you obtain a smooth, pliable dough that holds its shape on a spoon.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and tilt the pan to coat it (spread the oil in an even film over the entire surface).

Place portions of dough and flatten them slightly into patties. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for about 7 minutes without touching them: the patty should release easily and have a golden brown side.
Turn over and continue cooking on the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. Cook in two batches rather than overcrowding the pan.
Remove from the pan and place on absorbent paper towels to remove excess oil. Serve immediately, while still crispy.

title: Linguine with prawns, lemon and parmesan
intro: It all comes down to two things: a clean sear of the prawns so that they remain pearly (translucent and melting in the center, never rubbery), and a sauce made in the same pan, on the juices.

ing.note: plus a little extra to serve

ing: salt for the sauce and the shrimp
titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the shrimp. The titanium coating will quickly create an instant golden crust, and the shrimp will release themselves when they're ready: that's your only signal to turn them over. Then, prepare the sauce in the same pan, without washing it, to incorporate all the flavors left at the bottom during searing.
steps: Press or finely mince the garlic. Chop the parsley, reserving a few whole leaves for garnish. Zest the lemon, and squeeze half of it.
Season the shrimp with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the linguine according to the package directions. The volume of water dictates the pot size; a frying pan will suffice afterward.
Meanwhile, heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Drizzle with grapeseed oil, arrange the shrimp in a single layer, and let them sear for about 3 minutes without touching them. Turn them over only when they release easily, cook for another minute, then remove them to a separate plate.
Add another drizzle of oil to the still-hot pan, reduce the heat to medium, add the garlic and chili. Fry for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in the cream. It will loosen the juices from the bottom: scrape them with a spatula.
Add the Parmesan in two or three batches, mixing between each, until the sauce thickens and becomes smooth.
Thin with a ladleful of pasta cooking water.
Drain the linguine, keeping about two ladles of the cooking water.
Pour the pasta into the pan with the juice of half a lemon. Mix vigorously to coat.
Add the shrimp, chopped parsley, and half the zest. Mix again and adjust with cooking water if the sauce is too thick.
Arrange on warm plates. Finish with the remaining zest, the reserved parsley leaves, a turn of the pepper mill and a little Parmesan cheese.

title: Raspberry protein pancake cookie
intro: A soft cake baked without an oven, where everything depends on the gentleness of the fire and patience: it is the lid that makes the center rise while the base takes on its color.
titane: Heat the pan empty over low heat for two to three minutes before greasing it: titanium heats up slowly but retains its heat very evenly, preventing a brown crust in the center and a pale edge. Once the batter is poured in, don't touch it. The cake will tell you it's ready when it pulls away from the sides on its own. If you need to use a spatula to loosen it, it needs two more minutes.
steps: Melt the butter, let it cool slightly.
Combine the following powders in a bowl: flour, peanuts, whey, yeast, and salt. Whisk together to break up any lumps of protein, which are often compact.
Add the egg, milk, stevia, and melted butter. Mix just until the dough is smooth. Overmixing will cause the gluten to develop and the dough will lose its soft texture.
Gently fold in the still-frozen raspberries with a spatula, using a few simple movements. They should remain whole.
Preheat the pan empty, over low heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush it with clarified butter: the fat should simmer but never smoke.
Pour the batter, smooth the surface with the back of a spoon, cover.
Cook for 11 minutes covered, over low to medium heat. The bottom will brown, the top will remain pale and cook slowly. Only lift the lid once, halfway through cooking, to check the color.
The edges will shrink and pull away on their own: the cake is cooked. Slide it onto a wire rack and let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting. It will tear if it's hot.

title: Flourless white bean bread
intro: A bread without flour either holds together or it doesn't: everything depends on the psyllium, which structures the dough, and on the crust being seared in a pan before baking.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before pouring in the batter. Contact with the hot metal immediately forms a golden crust on the bottom, impossible to achieve on a sheet of parchment paper. The uncoated pan then goes directly into the oven: the batter finishes cooking in the same container, without having to handle the still-soft batter.
steps: Blend the drained white beans with the eggs and salt until you obtain a smooth paste, without any skin lumps.
Add the bicarbonate and psyllium. Mix again for a few seconds, then let it rest for 2 minutes: the paste thickens considerably and becomes moldable with a spatula.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with clarified butter or grapeseed oil.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and spread it into a thick loaf about 4 cm thick, rounding the edges with a spatula.
Scatter the seeds on top and press lightly to make them stick.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes over low heat. The bottom should be thoroughly browned and the bread should easily release from the pan when you shake it.
Bake the pan at 180°C for 25 minutes, uncovered. The bread should be firm to the touch and golden brown on top.
Remove from the pan onto a wire rack and let cool for 15 minutes before slicing: the crumb finishes structuring itself as it cools.

title: Pan-fried seed crackers
intro: It all comes down to flax and chia: they absorb the water, bind the other seeds together, and hold the pancake together without flour or egg.
ing: teaspoon of vegetable and herb salt
