ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: The pan replaces the oven. Covered and over very low heat, the heat rises steadily from the bottom, dehydrating the galette instead of browning it. No parchment paper: the batter will stick slightly at first, then shrink as it dries and detach itself from the edges. This is your signal that it's done.
steps: Combine all the seeds in a bowl with the 2 tsp of herb salt. Mix dry to distribute the ground flax, which tends to settle at the bottom.

Pour the boiling water all at once. Mix with a spatula for a good minute: the mixture should become homogeneous and distinctly sticky. Let it rest for 5 minutes, allowing the chia to swell (the seeds will be surrounded by a gel that binds them together).
Transfer to the cold titanium pan. Spread in a thin, even layer with the back of a damp spoon, right to the edges. An uneven thickness will result in soft patches.
Lightly salt the surface.
Cover and place over very low heat. Let it dehydrate for 30 minutes. The surface should be matte and firm to the touch.
Flip the pancake over in one swift motion, using a large spatula or a plate. Cover and continue cooking for 30 minutes.
The galette is ready when it's crispy all over and easily pulls away from the edges. Transfer it to a wire rack and let it cool completely: the crispiness will set as it cools.
Break into irregular pieces by hand.

title: Oat tiramisu with plant-based skyr
intro: It all comes down to soaking: a still-warm oatcake would absorb too much coffee and collapse, wait until it's cold.
titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe with no temperature restrictions. It becomes the mold, then the assembly dish, and finally the container for chilling. Pour the batter into the cold pan, cover, and bake: no unmolding required, so no broken cake. Cover the pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Blend the oat flakes, chia seeds, banana and plant-based milk until you obtain a smooth paste, with no visible pieces of banana.
Pour the batter into the cold titanium pan. Smooth the surface with a spatula. Cover with an oven-safe lid.
Bake for 25 minutes. The cake is cooked when the surface is set, lightly golden, and the center no longer sticks to the touch.
Meanwhile, mix the plant-based skyr and light brown sugar until the sugar is dissolved. Set aside in the refrigerator.
Remove the pan and let the cake cool completely inside. Allow at least one hour.
Soak the surface of the cold coffee in a steady stream, covering the entire cake. Let it soak in for two minutes.
Cover with the skyr cream, in an even layer, directly in the pan. Remove any remaining cream (transfer it to another container).
Cover the pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight. The breadcrumbs will finish absorbing the coffee and the cream will set.
The next day, sift the cocoa over the top just before serving. It would lose its flavor if left to sit.

title: Minced chicken burger with sundried tomatoes and basil
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the homemade minced steak, the courgettes, then the pressed and golden bread — no need to get out a panini press.

ing.note: fillet (high smoke point, suitable for searing)

titane: The titanium pan heats up in two to three minutes when empty and retains that heat when cold food is added. The steak sears without sticking, the zucchini browns instead of releasing its water, and the same surface is then used to toast the assembled burger. One pan, three cooking methods.
steps: Cut the chicken into large pieces. Combine them on the board with 20g of sundried tomatoes and half the basil. Chop with a knife until you obtain a homogeneous mixture, then squeeze it between your hands to form a compact patty, slightly wider than the bread: it will shrink during cooking.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Drizzle in the oil. It should ripple on the surface without smoking.

Slice the zucchini lengthwise and score the slices with the tip of a knife (these shallow cuts speed up cooking and help brown the meat). Place the steak and zucchini slices in the pan. Don't touch anything: the food will release on its own once a crust has formed. Flip halfway through; cook for a total of 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop the remaining sun-dried tomatoes with the remaining basil. Mix with the Parmesan, mayonnaise, and cream cheese until smooth.
Open the bread, spread generously with sauce on both sides. Place the steak, the courgettes, then the grated mozzarella. Close.

Return the burger to the still-hot pan. Press down with a wide spatula or the back of a lid for 2 minutes per side. The bun should be golden brown and crispy, and the mozzarella should start to melt around the edges. Remove from the pan and let rest for 1 minute before slicing.

title: Roasted nectarines, cherries and mozzarella, garlic croutons
intro: It's all about contrast: caramelized fruit that's still warm, cold mozzarella, and croutons that stay crispy until the last bite.

ing.note: or 2 to 3 slices of day-old bread

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: croutons brown and nectarines caramelize in the same pan, without needing an oven. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Once the fruit wedges are in the pan, don't touch them: they'll stick at first, then release easily once the surface is set. That's the signal.
steps: Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut the bread into irregular cubes of about 2 cm. Press the garlic.

Pour the olive oil into the hot pan, add the bread and garlic. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook for 6 minutes, stirring regularly, until golden brown. The croutons should sound hollow when tapped and have turned a uniform amber color. Work in two batches if the pan is full.
Remove the croutons (take them out of the pan and leave them to air dry, never under a lid).
Remove the pits from the nectarines and cut them into quarters.

Add another drizzle of oil to the pan, place the wedges flesh-side down, and add the honey. Let them sear for 5 to 6 minutes over medium-high heat without touching them, until they easily separate from the skin and the edges are tender.
Meanwhile, cut the cherries in half and remove the pits.
Mix the olive oil and lemon juice, add salt.
Divide the warm nectarines, cherries, hand-torn mozzarella, and croutons between two plates.
Add the basil, season with salt and pepper, pour over the vinaigrette at the last moment and serve.

title: Crispy potato pancakes
intro: It's all about patience: a galette that isn't touched will detach itself and come out with a clean crust.

ing.note: to be adjusted according to the consistency of the device

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. As a result, a crust forms in just a few minutes with only three tablespoons of oil, where deep-frying would normally be required. Preheat the pan empty, then add the oil. Wait until the pancake releases itself: this indicates that the crust has set and that it will flip cleanly.
steps: Peel the potatoes and grate them raw using a medium grating disc. Squeeze them between your hands to remove excess moisture: the less moisture remains, the drier the crust will be.

Mix the grated potatoes with the cornstarch, smoked paprika, herbes de Provence, salt, and pepper. Work the mixture until it forms a smooth mass that holds its shape when pressed. Add more cornstarch, spoonful by spoonful, if the mixture is too loose.
Form flat, even patties, about 1 cm thick. Press the edges down firmly.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. A drop of water should sizzle and run to the surface.
Pour the oil in a thin layer, place the patties in the pan without overcrowding it. Let them cook for 5 minutes without touching them: the patties should detach themselves from the bottom.

Flip it over quickly. Continue cooking for 5 minutes on the second side, until golden brown and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack, never to paper towels: the steam will soften the bottom. Cook in batches.

title: Pan-fried sweet potato wrap
intro: It's all about patience: a sweet potato pancake should only be flipped when it has finished forming its crust, never before.
ing: in the case of cornstarch or potato starch
case of grapeseed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan here takes on the role of an oven. Direct contact with the scorching hot base sears the sweet potato strands and builds a crust in minutes, whereas the diffused heat of an oven would take three times as long. Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for three minutes: a few drops of water sprinkled on the surface should bead up and run off in a single piece. Then leave it alone. When the pancake easily pulls away from the sides and bottom, it's ready to be flipped with a quick, firm movement.
steps: Grate the sweet potatoes using the fine grating disc. Squeeze the grated potatoes between your hands over the sink to remove the water: this is what prevents a crust from forming.
In a bowl, mix the grated potato with the cornstarch, oil, paprika, salt, and pepper. Work by hand until the cornstarch coats each strand.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 3 minutes. Test with water: the drops should slide off without evaporating immediately.
Pour in the fat. It should simmer gently, without smoking.
Spread the mixture in a thin, even layer over the entire surface. Press down gently with the back of a spatula.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes without moving the pan. The pancake will release itself from the bottom when the underside is golden brown.
Turn over sharply, using a spatula or by tossing. Continue for 5 minutes uncovered: the second side should be colored and firm to the touch.
Remove from the pan and place on a board. Let it cool for 3 minutes to allow the steam to escape, then roll it up.

title: Bowls of seared beef, golden potatoes and chipotle sauce
intro: It's all about patience: neither the potatoes nor the meat should be stirred before they separate on their own.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the first drop of oil. The rapid heat of the titanium will caramelize the potatoes like an oven, with a dry crust and a meltingly tender center. Then, add the beef to the same unwashed pan: the juices left by the potatoes will infuse the garlic butter.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even cubes. Place them in a saucepan of salted water and cook for 6 minutes from the time the water boils: the tip of a knife should slide in easily, but the cubes should still hold their shape.
Drain thoroughly and allow to air dry for a few minutes. Residual moisture is the enemy of the crust.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour in the grapeseed oil. Add the potatoes mixed with the smoked paprika, onion powder, and half the garlic salt. Spread in a single layer, reduce the heat to medium-high, and cook for 15 minutes: don't stir until the cubes are sticking together. They will separate on their own once golden brown.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a dish, cover and keep warm.
Season the beef cubes with the remaining garlic salt and black pepper.

Return the unwashed skillet to high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer, without stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until a crust forms and the pieces release easily. Work in two batches if the skillet is full.
Add the chopped garlic, light butter, and parsley. Mix for 3 minutes, until the butter coats the meat and absorbs the juices.
Whisk together the mayonnaise, chipotle paste, lime juice, and garlic salt until smooth. Blend with an immersion blender for a thicker texture.
Divide the potatoes and beef into 10 portions in airtight containers.
Sprinkle with chives, add the chipotle sauce on the side or drizzled over it. Store in the refrigerator for 3 days, or in the freezer for 2 months.

title: Gluten-free carrot and date cake
intro: No added sugar, no flour: everything relies on the date, which sweetens and binds, and on the carrot, which keeps the crumb moist.
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from the stove to the oven without transferring. You start covered over very low heat to cook the base in direct contact with the metal, which gives a caramelized bottom crust that a mold will never produce, then you put the pan in the oven as is to finish cooking and brown the top.
steps: Cover the dates with hot water and let them soak for 5 minutes. Drain them.
Blend the carrots and dates until you have a smooth, lump-free puree. No need to grate: the blender does both in one go.
Add the eggs, almond flour, baking powder, and baking soda. Mix until the mixture (the base mixture) is smooth and pourable.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Add the clarified butter and spread it evenly over the bottom and sides.
Pour in the mixture, cover, and cook over very low heat until the surface begins to set and is no longer liquid in the center, about 15 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake the pan for 40 to 45 minutes. The cake is ready when it has risen, is golden brown, and pulls away easily from the sides of the pan.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before unmolding: the caramelized base comes off more easily once relaxed.

title: Soft chocolate-hazelnut skillet cake
intro: Everything depends on the fluidity of the dough and the gentleness of the heat: if it is too thick or too hot, it dries out before it has risen.
titane: Preheat the pan empty over low heat, then place the lid on as soon as the batter is poured in. The trapped steam cooks the top while the direct contact with the bare metal browns the bottom. This dual action creates a soft center and a golden base, without the need for an oven or microwave.
steps: Crack the egg into a bowl. Add the oat flour, honey, protein powder, and peanut butter. Whisk until smooth and lump-free.
Pour the almond milk in small amounts, whisking after each addition. Stop when the batter coats the back of the spoon and falls back in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the pan empty, over low heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Place the clarified butter in the pan and spread it in a thin layer over the entire bottom.
Pour the batter into the center and let it spread on its own. Cover immediately and cook over low heat for 5 minutes. Do not lift the lid before the end.
Check if it's cooked: the top should be firm to the touch and the cake should easily pull away from the bottom. If the center remains moist, bake for another minute, still covered.
Slide the cake into a bowl or onto a plate. Drizzle with melted white chocolate-hazelnut and serve warm.

title: Quesarito burritos (to freeze)
intro: Ten burritos prepared at once, rolled in a double tortilla, and whose crispiness is achieved entirely in the last minute in the pan.
titane: Two methods of searing in the same pan, two approaches. For the beef: preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add a drizzle of oil, then leave it alone. The meat will release easily when a crust is formed—that's the signal. For the reheated burrito: use a bare, very hot pan with no oil. The tortilla will stick at first, then release itself with a golden crust. Flip it only once.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. A drop of water should sizzle in it.

Pour in the grapeseed oil. Add the ground beef and taco seasoning. Let it sear (cook over high heat to form a crust) without stirring: the meat will fall off the bone and begin to brown. Cook for 8 minutes, until almost fully cooked.
Reduce heat to low. Add the sliced red onion, enchilada sauce, and cheddar cheese. Stir for 3 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the sauce coats the meat.
Remove the filling (transfer it to a dish to free up the pan). Wipe the pan clean, return it to low heat, and reheat the rice for 3 minutes with the lime juice and chopped coriander.
Layer a small tortilla on top of a large one. Spread a tablespoon of nacho sauce and a tablespoon of Greek yogurt, then top with meat and rice. Roll up tightly into a burrito. Repeat ten times.
Wrap each burrito in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag.
Freeze. Shelf life: 3 months.
To serve, wrap the still-frozen burrito in a damp paper towel, place it on a plate and microwave it for 5 to 6 minutes.

Preheat a dry skillet over high heat. Place the warmed burrito in the skillet without adding any oil or butter. Flip it once, when it releases easily and has a golden crust. Cook for a total of 3 minutes.

title: Beef burritos for the week
intro: It all comes down to the meat: brightly colored, not boiled, otherwise the burrito will release water when defrosting.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature when cold meat is added: the beef sears instead of sweating. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the oil or fat, then the beef. Don't touch anything for the first minute. The same principle applies to finishing: over high heat, the burrito, placed seam-side down, will release itself once the crust has formed. No need for an air fryer.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently without smoking.
Add the ground beef and taco seasoning. Spread it out in one motion, then let it brown without stirring. The meat will pull away from the bottom of the pan on its own when it's seared.
Crumble with a spatula and continue cooking for about 8 minutes, until no pink remains.

Add the green chilies and enchilada sauce. Cook for 2 minutes over medium heat, until the liquid has almost completely evaporated. Transfer to a cold dish and let cool slightly: a hot topping will make the tortilla soggy.
Warm the tortillas briefly to soften them. Fill each one, on the bottom third: refried beans, meat, mozzarella, nacho sauce, sour cream, tomatoes. Add lettuce only if you are eating immediately.
Fold both sides inwards, then roll tightly upwards, seam underneath.
Wrap each burrito in aluminum foil, or store them in a sealed freezer bag. They will keep in the freezer for up to 3 months.
To reheat: unwrap, wrap the frozen burrito in a damp paper towel, place it on a plate and microwave for 5 to 6 minutes.

Finish in a preheated titanium pan over high heat for 2 minutes with a drizzle of high-smoke oil. Place the burrito seam-side down and cook for 2 minutes on each side without touching it. It will release easily once crispy.

title: Night oats with red berries and peanut butter
intro: Everything depends on the temperature of the compote: if poured too hot, it soaks the layer of oats and makes the contrast between the creamy and the fruit disappear.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for stewing frozen red berries. The heat rises evenly across the entire surface, without any hot spots: the berries release their juices without sticking, and without any added fat.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the oats, peanut butter, protein powder, salt, and cinnamon. Pour in the plant-based milk and mix until the peanut butter is fully incorporated and smooth. Set aside.

Place the frozen berries in a cold titanium pan and add the flax seeds. Increase the heat to medium and stir occasionally. Cook for 5 minutes: the berries will soften and release their juices, then the mixture will thicken slightly and coat the spatula.
Remove the compote from the pan and place it in a bowl. Let it cool for a few minutes. It should be barely warm to the touch before assembling.
Divide the oat mixture and the compote into alternating layers in five jars. Finish with a drizzle of melted chocolate.
Seal and refrigerate. The oats will rehydrate overnight and the jars will keep for five days.

title: Crispy pan-fried potato balls
intro: No oil bath here: it's all about the compactness of the balls and a really hot pan before adding the fat.
ing: mixture of dried herbs from the south
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour in the fat: a crust forms on contact in a few seconds, and the balls brown all around without frying.
steps: Cut the potatoes into large, even pieces. Put them in a saucepan with just enough salted water to cover them. Bring to a boil and cook until a knife inserted into them meets no resistance.
Drain thoroughly, then let the steam evaporate for 2 minutes in the pan off the heat. Mash with a potato masher until smooth, without lumps.
Add the cornstarch, smoked paprika, herbs, salt, and pepper. Mix with a spatula until you have a smooth, homogeneous dough. Let it cool slightly.
Shape into balls the size of a walnut by squeezing firmly between your palms: a compact ball will not crumble when picked up.
Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It is ready when a wisp of smoke rises above the surface.

Pour the oil or clarified butter into the pan, then place the balls in it, spacing them apart. Do not overcrowd the pan: the temperature will drop. Let them brown for 3 minutes without touching them. They will release easily once a crust has formed.

Turn them over quickly, then roll them regularly for 6 minutes to brown all sides. Remove from the pan and set aside on paper towels and serve immediately. Cook in batches if necessary, allowing the pan to reheat between each batch.

title: Roasted cod, melted cherry tomatoes
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the fish: a really hot pan, a very dry flesh, and you don't touch anything else.

ing.note: half a teaspoon, and a pinch for the

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains the temperature. Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding the fat: the cod loin takes on its color in two to three minutes per side without sticking, and the same pan is then used for the sauce, which collects all the juices.
steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Mix together the paprika, garlic powder, thyme, chili pepper, fine salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels on all sides. Moist flesh will steam instead of browning. Then coat it with the spice mixture on both sides.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Pour the oil into the pan, place the fish in it, and leave it for 2 to 3 minutes. It will release easily when a crust has formed: that's the signal to turn it over. Cook for the same amount of time on the other side, then remove it from the pan and set it aside on a plate.
In the pan, sauté the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the tomatoes, a pinch of salt, and the juice of half a lemon. Let it simmer for 7 to 8 minutes over medium-high heat. If the pan dries out, add a little water or chicken stock.

Return the cod to the sauce, reduce the heat to low-medium and let it finish for 4 to 5 minutes. Adjust the cooking time according to the thickness of the fillet: the flesh should flake easily under the tip of a knife.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve with rice or another grain, cooked separately.

title: Rigatoni with seared eggplant and cherry tomatoes
intro: It all comes down to the eggplant: cut small and seared on an already hot pan, it takes on a golden crust and keeps a melting center, without an oven.

ing.note: plus the water from the pasta

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains heat: the eggplant cubes behave like a piece of meat, releasing themselves when one side is seared. Don't move them before this signal. Then, everything stays in the same pan—sauce, then pasta—with the searing juices adding a final touch of flavor.
steps: Cut the eggplant into even 1.5 cm cubes. Finely chop the garlic, quarter the cherry tomatoes. Grate the Parmesan cheese.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in 2 tablespoons of olive oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Add the diced eggplant, season with salt, and spread in a single layer. Let it cook without touching it. It will separate on its own after 4 to 5 minutes.
Turn them over and continue browning on the other sides, 10 minutes in total. They should be golden brown on the outside and soft in the center. Remove them from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and start cooking the pasta according to the time indicated on the package.
In the pan, without washing it, pour the remaining oil and add the garlic. Fry it for 1 minute over medium-high heat, without letting it brown.
Add the cherry tomatoes and tomato paste, and season with salt. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes have softened and the sauce has thickened.
Add the eggplant back in, mix and let it sit together for 3 minutes.

Drain the pasta, reserving a ladleful of the cooking water. Add it to the pan and stir off the heat. If the mixture starts to stick or seems dry, add the reserved cooking water in small amounts; its starch will thicken the sauce.
Add two-thirds of the parmesan, mix to coat it, then add the hand-chopped basil.
Arrange on a plate, season with pepper, finish with the remaining parmesan and a few whole leaves.

title: Cheesecake and jam
intro: A cake without flour or oven, whose success depends entirely on the gentleness of the fire: too hot, the bottom browns before the center sets.
titane: The pan replaces the oven. The titanium base diffuses a low, even heat that forms a thin crust under the jam, while the lid traps steam and cooks the center without drying it out. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before pouring: the mixture sets immediately on contact and will release easily when unmolded.
steps: Whisk the cottage cheese and eggs in a bowl until the mixture is smooth.
Add the cornflour and sugar. Mix again to obtain a smooth, lump-free batter.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over low-medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush it with a thin layer of clarified butter.
Pour the mixture into the container and smooth the surface with a spatula.
Spread the jam in small dollops on top. Do not spread it: it will spread during baking.
Cover and cook for 30 minutes over low heat. The cake is ready when it pulls away easily from the sides and the center remains soft to the touch, without sticking.
Remove from heat, let cool slightly covered, then turn the cake out onto a plate. Cut it once cooled.

title: Chili, soybeans and red beans
intro: Everything happens before the liquids: the well-sweated onion and the spices roasted in fat give the chili its depth, the rest is just patience.
ing: Cooked and drained red kidney beans
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding any oil or butter. The surface heats up quickly and retains its heat: the onion sweats without releasing water, the tomato paste caramelizes, and the spices release their oils instead of remaining powdery. Then, the titanium's thermal inertia allows for a gentle reduction, uncovered, without the sauce sticking to the bottom. Add the 800 ml of liquid in two stages, never more than 500 ml at a time.
steps: Cover the soy protein with very hot water in a bowl. Let it soak while you continue, then squeeze it between your hands to remove the excess water.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat. Count three minutes: a drop of water should roll into a ball before evaporating.
Pour in the oil, reduce the heat to medium, and add the chopped onion. Let it sweat uncovered for five minutes. It should become translucent and pull away from the bottom of the pan on its own.
Add the tomato paste, curry, smoked paprika, herbs and chili. Stir constantly for one minute: the spices should heat up in the fat and become fragrant, not brown.
Deglaze (dissolve the browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan with liquid) with the hot stock. Scrape the bottom with a spatula. Let it reduce for five minutes over medium heat, uncovered.
Pour in the tomato sauce, then stir in the pressed soybeans, red beans and corn.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for ten minutes, stirring occasionally. The chili is ready when it coats the back of a spoon and a groove drawn in the bottom of the pan slowly closes.
Season with salt and pepper, taste. Serve from the pan over long-grain rice.

title: Chia, peanut and dark chocolate pot
intro: It all comes down to the night in the cool: it's what makes the chia swell and the chocolate shell harden, so that the spoon passes through three textures at once.
titane: The chocolate melts in the titanium pan over very low heat. The thin metal heats up almost instantly and distributes the heat evenly without hot spots: no lumps, no burnt residue at the bottom. Stir continuously, and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture becomes glossy and smooth. The pan then acts as a spout; pour the chocolate directly into the jar.
steps: Mix the plant-based yogurt, chia seeds, and agave syrup. Mix for thirty seconds so that the seeds disperse instead of clumping at the bottom.
Pour into a jar or glass container. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Spread the peanut butter in an even layer, then sprinkle with peanuts. Roughly chop them if you want a more pronounced texture.

In a titanium pan over very low heat, melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil. Stir continuously for about 3 minutes, until you obtain a glossy and smooth mixture. Turn off the heat at this point.
Pour the melted chocolate directly from the pan over the peanuts, covering the entire surface.
Refrigerate overnight, or for 8 hours. The chia will have set, and the chocolate will form a thin layer that cracks when you spoon it on.

title: Eggplant stew with gochujang
intro: Everything hinges on the first cooking: the eggplant, seared dry without a drop of oil, loses its water and takes on a vibrant color before encountering the spices.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: the eggplant browns in a dry pan in just a few minutes, without sticking or becoming mushy. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the pieces and leave them undisturbed. They will release easily once golden brown. The same pan is then used for sautéing the spices and simmering, covered, without transferring the eggplant.
steps: Preheat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle on contact.
Place the eggplant pieces in a single layer without adding any fat. Let them brown for 5 minutes without moving them: they will detach on their own once golden.

Pour the oil over the eggplant, add the cumin, smoked paprika, tomato paste, and gochujang. Stir-fry for 5 minutes, tossing the pan occasionally, until the spices are fragrant and the tomato paste is lightly browned.

Add the textured soy sauce, tomato sauce, water, salt, soy sauce, lemon juice, and sugar. Mix, cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 10 minutes: the sauce will thicken, and the eggplant will become tender.
Adjust the salt, then transfer (out of the pan) to containers. Refrigerate for up to four days or freeze in portions.

title: Gluten-free banana, poppy seed and cinnamon cake
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas and on a low enough heat so that the center catches before the bottom darkens.

ing.note: (it can withstand higher heat) or oil

titane: When covered, the titanium pan becomes a compact oven: the heat rises from the bottom and circulates under the lid, cooking a thick batter evenly without sticking. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat, grease it, then reduce the heat to very low as soon as the batter is poured in. The cake will release easily from the sides when it's cooked: that's your signal to unmold.
steps: Mash the bananas with a fork in a bowl until you obtain a puree without large pieces.
Add the eggs, Greek yogurt and agave syrup. Mix until smooth.
Incorporate the gluten-free flour, baking soda, and salt. Mix just enough so that no dry flour remains.
Add the poppy seeds and cinnamon. Mix one last time; the dough should be smooth and thick.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter or grapeseed oil.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and smooth the surface with a spatula for an even thickness.

Cover and reduce the heat to very low. Cook for 30 minutes: a knife inserted into the center should come out dry and the edges should curl back on their own. If the bottom browns quickly, place a heat diffuser under the pan.
Let it cool for 5 minutes uncovered, then turn the cake out onto a wire rack. It will come away easily.

title: Chicken and spiced rice, oven-baked
intro: The key is the liquid: enough for the rice to cook, but not too much, otherwise the bottom will never caramelize.

ing.note: pieces (or 4, if they are very large)

ing: Olive oil for the bottom of the pan

ing.note: cinnamon, coriander, cloves, chili pepper, nutmeg

titane: The titanium pan goes directly from the stovetop to the oven without any special precautions, eliminating the need to transfer the contents. Start by layering the tomato and onion mixture on the baking sheet, then place the whole thing in the oven, covered. The rice underneath browns on the bare metal instead of sticking: this thin crust, which you scrape off with a spoon when serving, is what makes the difference compared to cooking on a regular stovetop.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the olive oil and tilt to coat the entire surface. It should ripple without smoking.
Arrange the tomato slices and chopped onion directly on the hot base. Let them cook for a minute, without stirring.
Spread the rice evenly on top. Do not mix: the two layers should remain separate.
Place the chicken thighs on the rice, skin side up, side by side and without overlapping. Salt them.
In a bowl, combine the tomato paste, oil, date syrup, paprika, spice mix, pepper, and a pinch of salt. Mix with a fork until you obtain a smooth paste.
Dilute this paste with boiling water, pouring in small amounts at first to avoid lumps.
Pour this liquid over the chicken and rice. It should just cover the rice without drowning the thighs: keep a little aside if your pan is too small, the rice shouldn't be swimming in liquid.

Cover (make sure the lid is oven-safe up to 200°C) and bake for 60 minutes. The dish requires no further attention. When it's done, the liquid will be absorbed, the rice tender, and the chicken golden brown.
Remove the pan with oven mitts, let it rest covered for 5 minutes, then serve directly from the pan, scraping the bottom.

title: Creamy vegetable curry with pea protein
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the sautéing of the herbs perfumes the bottom, and the sauce then simmers on top to capture it.
ing: a thumb-sized piece of fresh ginger

ing.note: or a neutral oil if you are looking for a seizure
replaceable by the same dose of curry powder

titane: Heat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding any fat. The temperature rises quickly: the aromatics sear instead of simmering, and you proceed directly to simmering and then blending without ever transferring the mixture.
steps: Pour the hot broth over the pea protein in a bowl. Let it swell while the pan heats up.
Heat the empty pan over medium heat for two to three minutes. A drop of water should roll into a ball on the surface.

Add the margarine, then the onion, garlic and ginger. Sweat (cook gently without browning to release the water from the vegetables) for five minutes: the onions will pull away from the bottom on their own when they are ready.

Stir in the tomato paste and curry powder, and cook for thirty seconds to toast them. Add the tomato sauce, then the coconut milk in two or three additions. Stir in the cashews, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover, reduce heat to low and simmer for ten minutes. The sauce should simmer, not boil.
Remove from heat and blend with an immersion blender directly in the pan until smooth. The cashews provide the fat and binder.
Return to low heat. Drain the pea protein, stir it into the sauce and reheat for three minutes while stirring.
Serve as is with rice, or use it to fill wheat tortillas rolled into burritos.

title: Crispy rice paper dumplings
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the rice paper and patience in the pan: two overlapping sheets, a film of oil, and the shell becomes glassy then crispy.
ing: peanut sauce or tahini diluted with water
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the rice paper stretches and browns without deep-frying. A thin film of oil is all that's needed. Never force it apart; each side will release on its own once a crust has formed.
steps: Crumble the tofu with a fork into a bowl. Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar, five-spice powder, salt, and spring onion. Mix and taste: the seasoning should be pronounced, as cooking will mellow it.
Fill a shallow dish with cold water. Dip a sheet of rice paper in the water for two seconds, lay it flat, then dip a second sheet and place it on top. Wait until they become pliable but not sticky.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center. Fold over the bottom, then the sides, and roll to close. Place the seam underneath. Repeat to make five dumplings.
Preheat the titanium pan empty (without oil) over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle and run across the surface.
Pour the grapeseed oil over the dumplings and spread it with a flick of the wrist. Place the dumplings seam-side down, leaving space between them. Let them cook for 3 minutes without touching them.
Turn them over when each piece detaches easily and the surface is golden. Continue for 5 minutes, tilting them onto their sides to brown all sides.
Remove from the pan immediately and place on a wire rack, not paper towels: the steam will soften the shell. Serve with peanut sauce or tahini.

title: Cornflake-crusted chicken tenders with honey-buffalo sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust: firmly pressed corn flakes, a really hot pan, and above all the patience of not touching the tender before it detaches on its own.
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The cornflake coating will then set instantly on contact, without an oven or air fryer. Place the tenders in the pan and don't move them: until the crust forms, it will stick to the metal and tear if you try to force it. Once it's set, the tender will slide off easily when you shake the pan. That's the signal, not a timer.
steps: Cut the breasts into regular strips of about 85g. A consistent thickness is better than a pretty shape: it's the thickness that determines the cooking time.
Mix the flour, garlic salt, onion powder and pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk the egg whites with the pickle juice and hot sauce in a second bowl.
Crush the cornflakes by hand in a third container. Aim for irregular pieces, the size of a grain of rice: if they are too fine, they will no longer be crunchy.
Coat each strip in the seasoned flour, covering the entire surface. Tap to remove any excess.
Then dip it in the egg mixture, let the excess drip off for a few seconds.

Press it firmly into the cornflakes on both sides. Press firmly with the palm of your hand: the breading should adhere, not just settle. Transfer (set aside) to a baking sheet, without overlapping the pieces.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly on the surface.

Place the tenders in the pan, leaving about two centimeters between each one. Work in two or three batches. An overcrowded pan loses heat and the breading will become soggy instead of crisp. Let them rest for about four minutes without touching them.

Turn the tender over when it easily separates from the meat. Reduce the heat to medium and continue cooking until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F), about 10 minutes. If the breading is browning too quickly, reduce the heat to a lower setting. The juices should run clear when pierced with a knife.
Place on a rack, never on absorbent paper laid flat: the steam would soften the underside.

Wipe the pan clean and return it to low heat. Add the buffalo sauce, honey, butter, and garlic salt. Stir until the sauce is smooth and coats the back of a spoon, about 2 minutes. Alternatively, you can heat it in a bowl in the microwave for 1 minute.
Spoon the sauce over the tenders just before serving, or present the sauce on the side to keep the crust clean.

title: Tangzhong soft burger buns
intro: Everything hinges on the tangzhong (a porridge of flour and liquid cooked and then cooled): it soaks the dough with water and keeps the loaves soft for two days.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty and then covered, it radiates a gentle, enveloping heat: the bottom develops a crisp crust while the crumb remains moist. Without a coating, the dough balls release easily when they're ready—that's your signal to turn them over.
steps: Whisk the flour and almond milk for the tangzhong together in a saucepan. Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until you have a thick cream that leaves a trail when the whisk is lifted. Remove from the heat and let cool completely.
Combine the flours, whey protein, peanut powder, gluten, and yeast in a bowl. Add the egg, almond milk, water, stevia, and cold tangzhong. Knead for 5 minutes.
Add the salt. Knead for another 5 minutes.

Incorporate the softened butter in three stages, waiting for it to be fully incorporated before adding more. Allow 10 minutes: the dough should become smooth, elastic, and pull away from the sides of the bowl.
Cover. Let rise for about 1 hour 45 minutes, until the volume has almost doubled.
Deflate the dough (press the gas out with the palm of your hand), divide into 10 equal pieces. Shape them into balls, stretching the surface well, then flatten them slightly.
Leave to rise for one hour covered, until the dough balls are puffed up and soft to the touch.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Mix the egg yolk and almond milk, brush the dough balls with the mixture, and sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired. Place them in the pan without crowding them, and cover. Flip them as soon as they release easily and the bottoms are golden brown, then continue cooking covered. The total cooking time should be about ten minutes.
Once out, spread a knob of butter on each loaf and cover with a cloth for 20 minutes: the retained steam will finish softening the crust.

title: Stir-fried chicken, rice and green beans
intro: It all comes down to the browning of the chicken: a really hot pan, and don't touch anything for the first few minutes.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold pieces are added: the meat sears instead of releasing its juices. Wait until it releases easily from the surface before turning it. If it resists, the crust hasn't formed.
steps: Finely chop the onion. Cut the chicken fillet into even pieces, season with salt, pepper, and spices.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the oil: it should simmer gently, never smoke.

Add the onion to the hot pan, stir for 1 minute, then push it to the sides and arrange the chicken on top. Let it brown undisturbed over medium-high heat for about 8 minutes total, only turning the pieces once they begin to separate easily.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice in the microwave for 3 minutes, covered.

Deglaze the pan with the soy sauce (pour the liquid onto the hot bottom to loosen the browned bits). Add the green beans, cut into pieces, and stir for 3 minutes over medium heat, until they are hot and coated.
Arrange the rice on a plate, then pour the chicken and its garnish over it. Serve immediately.

title: Pan-fried flourless banana bread
intro: A cake held together only by banana, egg and peanut puree: everything depends on the ripeness of the fruit and the hot pan that sears the batter on first contact.
titane: Preheat the pan empty before pouring in the batter. The hot base immediately forms a golden crust, and the pan then goes directly into the oven without transferring: a single utensil from mixing to unmolding.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a bowl. Add the peanut butter and mix until smooth, without any pieces of fruit.
Incorporate the eggs one by one, then the sugar. Whisk vigorously to lighten the mixture.
Add the baking soda, keeping well below half a teaspoon if you're unsure: beyond that, its taste will overpower everything else. Mix briefly.
Reserve a handful of chocolate chips and fold the rest into the batter with a spatula.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter: it should simmer without smoking.
Pour the batter all at once into the hot pan, level the surface and sprinkle with the remaining chocolate chips.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 50 minutes. The top should be thoroughly golden brown and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let it cool for 10 minutes in the pan before unmolding, allowing the crumb to firm up.

title: Grated carrots with toasted spices
intro: Everything hinges on the first few seconds: the mustard seeds must burst in the hot oil before the carrots arrive, otherwise the spices remain raw and powdery.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil or butter. The temperature rises quickly: the seeds pop immediately, the carrots brown without releasing their water, and they retain their crispness. Once the carrots are in the pan, don't touch them. They will stick, then release on their own when the side in contact with the pan is seared. This is the signal to toss them (stir with a quick flick of the wrist, without using a spatula).
steps: Grate the carrots using the large holes of a grater, or slice them into thin strips with a vegetable peeler. Set them aside on a cloth: a dry surface allows them to sear better.
Heat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour in the oil, then immediately add the cumin, ground coriander, mustard seeds, and ginger. Wait 2 minutes: the seeds should burst and the aroma should become rich and almost nutty. Do not let them turn black.

Add the carrots, spread them in a single layer, and increase the heat to medium-high. Wait without stirring until they detach from the bottom on their own, then sauté them for 3 to 4 minutes until they soften but still have some resistance to the bite.
Remove from heat, add the sugar, lemon juice and fresh coriander. Mix well. Adjust the seasoning with salt.
Serve immediately, or transfer to a cold dish to stop the cooking process and let it rest for a few hours in the refrigerator: the spices will settle and the dish will become more pronounced.

title: Oatmeal porridge with milk, red berries and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the milk-oat ratio and stirring: it's this that releases the starch and gives the creamy texture, without added cream.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan. Preheated empty for two minutes, it distributes heat evenly across its entire surface: no hot spots in the center, so no oats sticking while the rest remains liquid. With 350 ml of milk, the volume is far less than that which would require a tall container. The metal spatula works perfectly, and the porridge goes directly from the pan to the bowl.
steps: Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. It should be hot above the palm of your hand, never smoking.
Pour in the milk, then the oat flakes. Stir immediately with a spatula.
Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring regularly and scraping the bottom. The oats should be tender and the mixture should coat the spatula (leaving a film that holds for a few seconds).
Remove from heat and transfer directly into a bowl.
Stir in the honey and cinnamon. Mix briefly so as not to break the texture.
Roughly chop the Brazil nuts. Scatter them on top along with the pomegranate seeds, blueberries and raspberries.
Place the pistachio butter in two dots, then sprinkle with dark chocolate shavings or chunks. Serve immediately: the porridge thickens quickly as it cools.

title: Gluten-free pan pie crust
intro: Without an oven and without gluten, everything depends on patience: the dough only comes off when the crust is formed, and it is this that holds the filling.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly to the edges: the base of the batter sears like a pancake and browns without needing an oven. A flick of the wrist cooks the second side, exactly as the oven's dome would.
steps: Combine the water, oil, gluten-free mix, and salt in a bowl. Mix with a spatula until you have a smooth, pliable dough without lumps. Stir in the seeds, if using.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. It must be thoroughly hot before adding the batter.
Place the dough in the center and spread it with oiled fingertips or the back of a spoon, bringing it up two centimeters on the edges.
Cover, reduce heat to low-medium and cook for 10 to 12 minutes. Do not intervene: the dough will release itself from the pan when the crust is set.
Flip with a flick of the wrist, cover again and continue for 8 to 10 minutes, until the second side is golden brown and firm under the spatula.
Remove from heat and let the pie base cool slightly in the pan. It will firm up as it cools.
Top directly in the pan: spread a layer of fresh cheese, then sprinkle with grated or shaved smoked tomme cheese. Serve warm, cut into slices.

title: Rustic zucchini and Beaufort cheese tart
intro: It all depends on the moisture of the courgette: if it releases its water in the pan before reaching the pastry, the base remains clean.

ing.note: a green one and a yellow one
plus a little bit for training

titane: The pan gets two uses. First, over medium-high heat, sear the onion and zucchini: let them brown without touching them; they'll release from the bottom on their own once a crust has formed. Then, wiped clean and filled, it goes straight into the oven. No baking sheet, no mold, no transfer.
steps: Work together flour, butter, egg and water in a bowl until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous ball. Add a pinch of flour if the dough sticks to your fingers.
Cover and refrigerate while preparing the filling.
Finely chop the onion. Slice the courgettes into thin rounds using a mandoline: being uniform, they will all cook at the same rate.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. A drop of water should roll in it like a ball without evaporating immediately.

Pour in the grapeseed oil, then add the onion, zucchini, salt, and thyme. Let it cook without stirring until the vegetables pull away from the bottom of the pan. Then stir regularly for 12 minutes, until they are very soft. A spoonful of water is all you need to loosen any sticking.
Remove the filling (transfer it out of the pan) to a dish and let it cool slightly.
Grate the Beaufort cheese.
Preheat the oven to 190°C, conventional heat.
Roll out the dough (spread it out with a rolling pin) into a disc of about 26 cm, the size of the bottom of the pan.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper, place the pastry disc in it and prick the base with a fork.
Spread the crème fraîche, leaving a 3 cm border of bare pastry around the edge.
Spread two-thirds of the cheese, then the vegetables, then the rest of the cheese. Add pepper.
Fold the edge of the pastry over the filling, in irregular folds.
Place the pan in the bottom of the oven for 35 minutes. Finish for 3 to 4 minutes at the top of the oven if you want a more browned top.
Take out the pan, sprinkle with fresh thyme and serve directly from it.

title: Breaded chicken au gratin with tomato and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the fillet: if it's even, it cooks in one go without the breading burning before the center.
ing: Grape seed oil, in a spray bottle
titane: The preheated titanium pan, empty, does the work of an oven and an air fryer combined. Direct contact builds the crust through the Maillard reaction (browning of proteins and sugars under dry heat), then the lid traps enough steam to melt the cheese without softening the breadcrumbs. All in one pan from start to finish.
steps: Slide the net between two sheets of parchment paper. Flatten it with a rolling pin using firm pressure, until it is 1 cm thick along its entire length. Then blot it with absorbent paper: a dry surface provides better adhesion.
Coat in the English style (flour, dip in beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs). Tap to remove excess flour, then press the panko with the palm of your hand to make it adhere.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Spray the oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the fillet on top and leave it untouched. After about 4 minutes, it will release on its own: that's the signal. Turn it over and brown the second side for another 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice half the tomato into rounds and dice the other half. Mix the diced tomato with the salad, salt, and vinegar.
Reduce the heat to low. Arrange the tomato slices on top of the chicken, cover with grated cheese, and put on the lid. Let it cook for 3 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve immediately, directly from the pan, with the salad on the side.

title: Caramelized bread bites with dark chocolate
intro: It all depends on the state of the bread: slightly stale, it keeps its edges and caramelizes instead of collapsing.

ing.note: or 3 tablespoons of grapeseed oil if

titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the bread. The dry, direct heat of the titanium pan attacks the coconut sugar in points of contact: the edges crack, the centers remain soft. A baking sheet would produce a uniform, flat color. Here, irregularity is the goal.
steps: Mix the coconut sugar and cinnamon in a large bowl. Add the bread cubes, pour over the melted vegan butter, and toss by hand until each side is coated. Allow 5 minutes for the bread to absorb the fat.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It must be thoroughly hot before first contact.

Pour the cubes into the pan in a single layer. Let them brown undisturbed, then toss them in the pan with a quick, sharp movement to turn them over. Don't crush them with a fork; this will dull the crispy edges. Increase the heat to medium-high towards the end. Cook for 8 minutes. The pieces are ready when they easily release from the bottom of the pan, are golden brown, and sizzle.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack. Let cool for 10 minutes: the residual heat from the metal would continue cooking and burn the sugar.
Dip each bite halfway into the melted dark chocolate. Place them on a sheet of baking paper, chocolate side up.
Sprinkle with a little fleur de sel while the chocolate is still soft. Serve within the hour, while the bread is still crisp.

title: Psyllium seed bread
intro: Without flour or yeast, this bread holds together solely through psyllium and chia seeds: everything depends on the resting time, which transforms a mush into a workable dough.
ing: tablespoon of neutral oil for the pan

ing.note: a loaf of bread approximately 20 cm long

titane: The titanium pan replaces the bread tin. It goes from the worktop to the oven without temperature limits, and its bare steel, without coating, releases the bread in one piece once the edges are retracted.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C, fan-assisted.
Weigh the seeds, psyllium, salt, and bicarbonate, then combine them in a large bowl. Mix thoroughly to distribute the psyllium evenly; if it remains in clumps, it will gel into lumps.
Crack the eggs directly onto the seeds. Work with a spatula until the mixture is homogeneous and sandy.
Pour in the water all at once. Mix vigorously for one minute: the dough should become heavy and sticky.
Let it rest for 15 minutes at room temperature. The seeds will absorb the liquid, the mass will firm up and detach from the sides of the bowl.

Lightly oil the titanium pan or line it with baking paper (covering the bottom and sides). Pour in the batter and press it down with the back of a damp spoon to form a compact loaf, without any air pockets.
Bake for 60 minutes. The bread is cooked when the crust is golden, pulls away from the edges, and sounds hollow when touched.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. When hot, the crumb remains moist and crumbles easily.

title: Pan-fried protein dulce de leche
intro: A dense cream with a milky taste, obtained without added sugar: everything depends on evaporation, therefore on the cooking surface.
titane: In a pan, the liquid spreads over a wide diameter: the water in the milk evaporates faster than in a saucepan, and the cream sets in eight minutes instead of ten. The even heating of the uncoated titanium eliminates the need for any fat—nothing sticks as long as the whisk remains in motion.
steps: Pour the cornstarch into the still-cold pan, add the condensed milk and whisk until completely dissolved. No lumps should remain before turning on the heat.
Place over medium heat. Whisk continuously, paying particular attention to the edges. After approximately 8 minutes, the cream will thicken and coat the whisk: remove from heat.
Remove from the pan immediately and spread out in a thin layer onto a baking sheet or wide dish. Cover with cling film, pressing it directly onto the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Allow to cool completely, either 2 hours in the refrigerator, or 30 to 40 minutes in the freezer.
Scrape the cold cream into a bowl and whisk it vigorously: it loosens up and becomes smooth again.
Incorporate the whey in two stages, whisking until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture. Refrigerate.

title: Carob marble cake for dogs
intro: A cake without added sugar or cocoa, where all the sweetness comes from very ripe bananas: it is their ripeness that determines the result.
ing: Pure peanut butter, without salt or sugar
titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe without needing to be transferred. Simply butter the inside, pour in the two batters alternately, and bake. No pan to wash, and the cake will unmold cleanly once it's lukewarm, directly onto a wire rack.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Lightly butter the titanium pan, base and sides.
Mash the bananas with a fork until you get a coarse puree. The black filaments will dissolve during cooking, so there's no need to hunt for them.

Combine the blended oats, flour, psyllium husk, yeast, peanut butter, plant-based milk, and oil in a bowl. Mix until the dough is smooth. It should be thick but still pourable: the psyllium husk will firm it up after two or three minutes of resting.
Divide the dough into two equal portions in two bowls.
Incorporate the carob into one of the two. You get a brown color and a taste close to chocolate, without the theobromine in cocoa, which is toxic to dogs.
Pour the two batters alternately into the center of the pan, a light spoonful, then a brown spoonful, without stirring. The circles will spread on their own and create a marbled effect.
Bake for 30 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out dry.
Let it cool in the pan for about ten minutes, then unmold onto a wire rack and let it cool completely.
Loosen the plant-based yogurt with the carob, then spread it evenly over the top of the cake using a spatula. Serve a small slice; the rest will keep for three days in the refrigerator.

title: Lentil steak
intro: It all comes down to how the device is handled: dry enough to be shaped by hand, flexible enough to withstand a brisk grip.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: this is what gives delicate steaks a crisp crust. Preheat it empty, then don't touch the patties. They will release on their own once the crust has formed; as long as they resist, they are not ready to be turned.
steps: Peel the carrot, onion, and potato, and cut them into large pieces. Combine them in a saucepan with the rinsed lentils, and cover with water. The volume is greater than what you would cook in a pan, so keep this step in the saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for at least 30 minutes, until a knife blade pierces the carrot easily. The liquid should be almost completely absorbed.
Drain if any broth remains, then mash with a fork or potato masher. Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly: a smooth purée without any large lumps.

Stir in the soy sauce, smoked paprika, herbs, salt, and pepper. Add the cornstarch in two batches and work by hand until you have a soft dough that holds together in a ball without sticking to your fingers.
Divide into eight portions. Shape into even discs 1.5 cm thick, smoothing the edges with the palm of your hand. The thinner they are, the more even the grip will be.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water that is dropped on it should bead up and evaporate immediately.

Pour the grapeseed oil into the pan, tilt it to coat the steaks evenly, and place them in the pan without crowding them. Let them cook until they release easily from the pan when lifted with a spatula: the top will then be golden brown. Flip them over and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve immediately, either as is with a herb salad, or slipped into a burger bun.

title: Raw brownie with dates and okara
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the date paste: if it is smooth, the brownie holds together without baking or binding.
titane: The chocolate coating melts directly in the titanium pan, without a double boiler. The conductivity of the bare metal is sufficient over very low heat: place the pan on top, break up the chocolate, and stir continuously with a spatula. As soon as the mixture is liquid and glossy, remove from the heat. Titanium doesn't retain hot spots, so nothing will stick as long as the spatula is rotating.
steps: Cover the pitted dates with hot water and let them soak for 10 minutes. Drain them.
Blend the dates alone with 5 tablespoons of water until you obtain a perfectly smooth paste. Do this step first, without anything else: the paste will act as a binder for everything else.
Add the cocoa, okara, and almond butter. Blend again until the mixture is smooth and compact. If using almond flour, omit the almond butter.
Pour the mixture into a small square mold lined with baking paper. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon to remove air pockets, to a thickness of about 2 cm.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. The dough should cut cleanly with a knife.
Place the titanium pan over very low heat. Break the dark chocolate into it and stir continuously with a spatula for about 3 minutes, until it is liquid and glossy.
Coat the still-cold brownie with the melted chocolate, spreading it with a spatula, and sprinkle with fleur de sel. Chill for 20 minutes, then cut into squares.

title: Giant pan-fried cookie
intro: A single cookie, cooked under a lid over low heat: it's all about the patience of the bottom browning while the center remains soft.
titane: The covered pan works like a small oven. Direct contact with the titanium base creates a golden crust, while the steam trapped under the lid cooks the top without drying it out. Preheat the pan empty for 2 minutes over low heat: a pan heated too high will burn the sugar before the center sets.
steps: Mix together the melted butter, yogurt, sugar and salt until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture (base mixture).
Add the flour, baking powder, and chocolate chips. Mix briefly, just enough to form a soft dough. Overworking it will make the cookie dense.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes over low heat, then coat it (cover the surface with a light film) with a veil of grapeseed oil, using a brush or absorbent paper.
Shape the dough into a single ball, flatten it slightly between your palms and place it in the center of the hot pan.
Cover. Cook for 8 minutes over low heat without touching the cookie: it should detach itself from the bottom and have firm edges.
Reduce the heat to very low for the last 4 minutes, until the center sets without the bottom browning too much. Remove from the heat when the center is still slightly wobbly.
Turn off the heat and let it rest for 2 minutes in the pan off the heat: the residual heat will finish the center. Transfer to a plate.

title: Breaded chicken tacos with cheese sauce
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: a nice hot pan, a drizzle of oil, and above all, the patience to leave it alone.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an air fryer, and better. Preheated empty for two to three minutes, then oiled at the last minute, it heats up high enough to trigger the Maillard reaction (the browning that creates a crust and flavor) on the panko bread. It then handles the vegetables, the sauce, the pancake, and the final grilling: a quick wipe with a paper towel between each step is all it takes; there's no need to wash it.
steps: Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then drizzle in a little oil. Season the eggplant and zucchini slices with salt and spices, and arrange them in a single layer. Leave them alone; they will release easily once browned. Turn them over and continue cooking until tender, then remove from the skillet and set aside. This should take about 8 minutes.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold broth, pour it into the pan, and bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly. As soon as the sauce coats the back of a spoon, add the mozzarella and let it melt. Remove from the heat and stir in the cream cheese. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Wipe the pan clean again. Season the chicken with salt and spices, dip it in the beaten egg, then press it into the panko breadcrumbs so they adhere completely. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the oil, and place the chicken over high heat. Do not move it: it will release itself once a crust has formed, after about 4 minutes. Turn it over, brown the other side, and finish cooking through. Remove from the pan.

Mix the flour and cream cheese until you have a smooth dough. Roll it out thinly between two sheets of parchment paper. Wipe the pan clean, lightly oil it, and cook the pancake over medium heat for 1 minute per side, until it releases easily from the pan.

Spread a spoonful of sauce on the tortilla, arrange the vegetables, then the sliced chicken. Fold it like a wallet. Return the taco to the lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat, cooking for 2 minutes per side, pressing it down with a spatula, until golden brown and sealed.

title: Gluten-free seeded bread
intro: A bread without flour or yeast, whose structure relies entirely on psyllium and chia: the water must be really boiling when mixing, otherwise the dough will not set.
titane: The pan acts as a mold. You shape the bread directly in it, then bake it as is: titanium can withstand any oven temperature. The base of the bread cooks in direct contact with the hot metal, resulting in a bottom crust that is significantly drier and crispier than with a traditional mold. A drizzle of oil before shaping is all it takes to ensure easy release.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop the oilseeds with a knife: keep some pieces visible, they give structure to the crumb.
In a bowl, dry-mix the oat flakes, almond flour, psyllium, chia seeds, chopped nuts, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, and salt. Distribute the psyllium evenly; it should not clump.
Pour the olive oil, then pour the boiling water all at once over the mixture.
Mix with a spatula immediately. In a few seconds, the mixture will thicken and hold its shape. Stop as soon as it is homogeneous.

Lightly oil the bottom of the titanium pan. Place the dough in the pan and shape it by hand into a compact disc, the size of the pan's base, about 4 to 5 cm thick. Press down firmly: any gaps will create breaks when you cut it.
For a more pronounced bottom crust, place the pan on medium heat 3 minutes before putting it in the oven, until you hear the bottom sizzle.
Cover and bake for 60 minutes at 180°C. The bread is cooked when the crust easily pulls away from the bottom with a spatula and the top sounds hollow.
Remove from the baking dish and place on a wire rack to cool completely, at least two hours. When still warm, the crumb will remain sticky and difficult to slice.

title: Bowls of roasted potatoes, taco beef and Mexican-style corn
intro: It all comes down to two distinct colors, that of the beef and that of the potatoes, obtained in the same pan without ever stirring too soon.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when you add 1.7 kg of cold meat: this prevents the beef from releasing its juices and boiling. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, oil it, then let it do its work. The meat will stick at first, then release itself: that's the signal. The same principle applies to potatoes, which you sear in the same pan before putting them directly into the oven, without transferring them to a baking sheet.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It is ready when a drop of water dances in it before evaporating.

Pour the oil over the beef until it reaches a high smoke point. Crumble the beef into an even layer, sprinkle with taco seasoning, and let it sear without touching it. The meat will resist, then begin to pull away from the sides of the pan: only then should you break it up with a spatula and finish cooking.
Add the green chilies and enchilada sauce. Stir over medium heat until the liquid coats the meat without pooling at the bottom. Stir in the cheddar cheese off the heat.
Remove the beef (transfer it from the pan) to a plate. Wipe the pan with paper towels.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes, as even as possible.
Plunge the cubes into a saucepan of boiling salted water and cook for 5 minutes. They should remain firm in the center.
Drain thoroughly, let air dry for 2 minutes, then season with garlic salt, smoked paprika, onion powder, and olive oil. Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Heat the pan over high heat, add the potatoes in a single layer, and let them cook for 2 to 3 minutes without stirring: the sides in contact with the potatoes should release easily and turn golden brown. Transfer the pan to the oven and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are crispy on the outside and tender on the inside.
Meanwhile, combine the corn, cotija, red onion, cilantro, yogurt, mayonnaise, lime juice, and tajine. Taste it: the mixture should be distinctly acidic.
Whisk together the mayonnaise, chipotle paste, lime juice, garlic salt, and pepper. Thin with a tablespoon of water if the sauce is too thick to whisk.

Remove the skillet from the oven. Spread the hot beef over the potatoes, top with Mexican-style corn, sprinkle with red onion and cilantro, then drizzle with chipotle sauce. Serve directly from the skillet or divide among bowls.

title: Chocolate, peanut and almond bars
intro: It all comes down to the cold: a well-set base, a peanut caramel that's set all the way through, and only then the chocolate.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without preheating. The metal's conductivity distributes the heat evenly, preventing hot spots: the chocolate remains smooth, without any lumps or sticking to the bottom. The pan then becomes the dipping bath, eliminating the need for a double boiler and the associated washing up.
steps: Mix together the almond flour, coconut milk and maple syrup until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous paste.
Transfer to a rectangular baking tin lined with baking paper. Press down using the back of a spoon, pressing down towards the corners for an even thickness.
Place in the freezer for 45 minutes, until the base hardens.
Mix together the peanut butter, agave syrup, and melted coconut oil. The mixture should be smooth and glossy.
Pour this vegetable caramel over the set base and smooth with a spatula.
Return to the freezer overnight, or for a minimum of 8 hours.
Remove from the mold and cut into bars with a smooth-bladed knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each cut. Return the bars to the refrigerator while you melt the chocolate.

Chop the dark chocolate and place it in the cold titanium pan. Heat over very low heat, without preheating: this is melting, not searing. Stir with a spatula for about 3 minutes. The chocolate is ready when it coats the back of a spoon in a smooth, even film.

Remove from heat, dip each bar in the chocolate, turning it over with a fork, let it drain for a few seconds over the pan, then place on a wire rack. Transfer to a cold plate and return to the freezer for 15 minutes to set the coating.

title: Stuffed eggplants with lentils
intro: It all comes down to cooking the eggplant: it must completely collapse before being stuffed, otherwise the stuffing remains on top instead of melting into it.
titane: The pan goes through four stages of cooking without ever being washed: first, the whole eggplants go in the oven, then the onion is seared, the stuffing simmers, and finally it goes back in the oven. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the onion, and wait until it releases itself from the bottom before stirring. This is when the base browns without sticking.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Prick the whole eggplants all over with a fork: the steam must be able to escape.
Brush them with olive oil, place them in the pan and bake for 30 minutes. The skin should wrinkle and the flesh should yield to the touch.
Take out the pan, remove the eggplants (transfer them to a board) and let them cool slightly.
Place the pan back on medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes empty.
Pour in the grapeseed oil and add the chopped onion. Let it brown without stirring; it will detach from the bottom of the pan on its own after 4 to 5 minutes. Then stir until it becomes translucent.
Add the tomato paste, cumin, coriander, paprika, chili pepper and salt. Stir for 1 minute to toast the spices.
Pour in the lentils and water. Scrape the bottom to collect the juices.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes over low heat, until the lentils are tender and the stuffing has thickened. It should no longer release any liquid.
Split the eggplants lengthwise without cutting them in half. Lightly crush the flesh with the back of a spoon to create a hollow.
Put them back in the pan, on top of the stuffing, and fill them generously, packing it down.
Bake for 25 minutes at 200°C. The edges should brown and the filling should form a dry crust.
Serve with rice and yogurt, directly from the pan.

title: Flourless chocolate-almond fondant cake
intro: Without flour, everything relies on whipped egg whites: they are what give the height and texture, the rest is just chocolate and almond.

ing.note: including a walnut for the pan

titane: The pan becomes the baking dish. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then generously butter the bottom and sides: butter adheres to a hot surface and forms an even film. Pour the batter into the pan and bake as is. The mixture will come out in a single container, and the cake will release easily from the sides once it has cooled slightly.
steps: Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Reserve the egg whites in a perfectly dry bowl.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form, adding a pinch of salt. They should hold their shape on the whisk without falling off.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until white (the mixture will lighten and thicken).
Incorporate the almond flour. You will get a compact dough, that's normal.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a double boiler over low heat. Smooth with a spatula off the heat.
Pour this lukewarm mixture over the almond paste and work until homogeneous.

Fold in the egg whites in three stages, using a spoon, lifting the mixture from the bottom up. The first third loosens the batter, the next two lighten it. Don't strive for perfection: a trace of egg white is better than a deflated mixture.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then butter the bottom and sides.
Pour the batter, smooth the surface.

Bake the pan at 180°C (350°F) for about 40 minutes. If you don't have an oven: cover the pan and cook over very low heat. The center should no longer jiggle; a knife inserted into the center should come out moist but not liquid. Check after 40 minutes; a smaller pan will result in a thicker cake, which will take longer to cook.
Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes. The cake will easily pull away from the sides. Turn it out onto a wire rack.

title: Hasselback potatoes, cream of white beans with lime
intro: Everything hinges on the first side: the incised strips must touch the hot metal long enough to form a crust before the oven takes over.

ing.note: 1 tbsp (high smoke point, reserved for the

titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, pour in the grapeseed oil, and place the potatoes scored side down. Do not touch them: they will release on their own once the crust has formed. The same pan can then be used in the oven, without transferring or using an additional dish.
steps: In a bowl, combine the smoked paprika, parsley, grated garlic, and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, and mix until you obtain a smooth paste.
Place each potato between two wooden sticks and make incisions every 3 mm: the blades stop on the wood, the slices remain attached at the base.
Brush the potatoes, forcing the marinade slightly between the slices. Salt the surface.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the potatoes cut-side down. Increase the heat to high and let them sear for 5 minutes, without moving the pan. They will release easily once a crust has formed.
Place the pan in the oven at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes. A knife tip should pierce easily and the strips should fan out.

Meanwhile, blend the white beans with the plant-based yogurt, lime juice, and zest. Season with salt and pepper, and blend again until smooth. If the sauce is too thick, thin it with a tablespoon of cold water.
Remove the potatoes from the pan and place them on plates, add a large spoonful of sauce next to them, a turn of the pepper mill and a few parsley leaves.

title: Rustic onion and Comté cheese tart
intro: It all comes down to the onions: they need a full twenty-five minutes to lose their water and turn golden brown, otherwise the tart remains bland and soggy.
titane: One pan from start to finish. It caramelizes the onions over high heat without them sticking, then goes in the oven with the tart inside. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil: the surface will then be hot enough for the onions to easily detach from the bottom when you stir.
steps: Combine the flour, butter, egg, and cold water in the bowl of a food processor or a mixing bowl. Knead until a smooth ball forms. If it's sticky, add a tablespoon of flour; if it won't come together, add a teaspoon of water.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Slice the onions finely and evenly.
