Heat the titanium pan empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour in the grapeseed oil, add the onions, salt, balsamic vinegar, and brown sugar. Let them brown without stirring; wait until they pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own. Continue cooking over medium-high heat for 25 minutes, until they are soft and brown. Add a tablespoon of water if they are browning too quickly.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F), conventional setting. Remove the onions (transfer them to a dish) and let the pan cool slightly.
Roll out the dough (spread it out with a rolling pin) into a disc of 24 to 26 cm, the diameter of the bottom of the pan, on a sheet of baking paper.
Spread the mustard in the center, leaving a 4 cm border. Distribute two-thirds of the Comté cheese over the mustard, then the onions, then the remaining Comté.
Fold the edge of the pastry over the filling, in successive folds. Slide the whole thing, including the paper, into the pan.
Bake in the bottom of the oven for 35 minutes, until the bottom is cooked and the edges are golden brown.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme leaves, season with pepper and serve warm, straight from the pan.

title: Naans stuffed with mozzarella, garlic butter and parsley
intro: A yogurt dough without resting, a mozzarella heart sealed neatly: it all comes down to a pan hot enough to make the bread puff up before the cheese escapes.

ing.note: (It can withstand intense fire without burning)

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: the naan behaves like it would on the wall of a tandoor, bubbling and developing a golden crust without sticking. Don't move it while it's still adhering. As soon as it releases on its own and begins to puff up, flip it over with a flick of the wrist, without pressing down, so as not to burst the pocket of melted cheese.
steps: Combine the flour, yogurt, and garlic salt in a large bowl. Mix by hand until the mixture comes together, with no traces of dry flour remaining.
Knead for 3 to 4 minutes on the work surface, until you obtain a smooth and supple dough that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Divide into 10 equal portions. Shape them into balls and cover with a cloth.
Roll out each piece of dough very thinly, into a regular disc.
Place approximately 55g of mozzarella in the centre. Bring the edges towards the middle and pinch firmly to enclose the cheese.
Turn the ball of sealant over and spread it out again, gently, until you have a disc of about 18 cm. Work without pressing too hard on the edges to avoid leaks.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, until it is lightly smoking. Brush it with a light coating of clarified butter.
Place a naan in the pan. Let it cook without touching it: it should detach on its own and form blisters.
Flip it over with a quick flick of the wrist. Continue cooking until golden brown on the second side. Repeat for the remaining naans, adding a little clarified butter to the pan between each one.
Remove from heat, brush with the remaining clarified butter, sprinkle with chopped garlic and parsley.
To store: allow to cool slightly, wrap individually in aluminum foil or a freezer bag, and freeze for up to 3 months.

title: Seared chicken, mushrooms and creamy pasta
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: a nice hot pan, spaced-out cubes, and above all, no impatience before turning them over.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature even when cold meat is added. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the fat, then place the diced chicken on top and leave it alone. It will stick at first, which is normal: a crust will form and it will release on its own once it sets. Add the mushrooms and spinach to the same pan, without washing them, to collect the juices.
steps: Cut the chicken breast into even 2cm cubes. Season them with garlic salt and black pepper, mix by hand to distribute well.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the clarified butter or oil: the fat should simmer gently and coat the bottom without smoking.

Place the chicken cubes in a single layer, without packing them too tightly. Work in two batches if necessary. Let them sear for 4 to 5 minutes without touching them, until they release easily and show an even golden-brown color.
Turn the cubes over, continue for 2 minutes, then remove from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the mushrooms to the still-hot pan and let them release their water and brown for 3 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Meanwhile, heat the pasta with cream of mushroom sauce in the microwave according to the package instructions.
Pour the pasta into the pan, add the chicken and its juices, mix off the heat to coat the cubes with sauce without boiling it.
Sprinkle with red chili flakes when serving, if you want some spice.

title: Sweet potato granola with honey
intro: It's all about moisture: a very cold puree and a firmly packed mixture result in pieces that are crunchy instead of soggy.
titane: The titanium pan acts as both a mold and a baking sheet. You press the mixture into it, put it in the oven, break the pieces into the pan, coat them with honey, and put it back in the oven. No transfer, an even thickness, and the rapid conductivity of titanium dries the edges without burning them.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, pierce it in several places, and bake it whole at 200°C (180°C for fan-assisted cooking) for 45 to 60 minutes. The flesh should yield easily to the tip of a knife. This method is best done in the oven; a pan does not heat a whole vegetable evenly.

Split the sweet potato lengthwise, scoop out the flesh, and mash it into a smooth puree. Let it cool completely, ideally overnight in the refrigerator: the colder and denser it is, the crunchier the granola will be. Weigh out 260g.
Mix the cold puree with the oat flakes, melted butter, 40g of honey, collagen, vanilla, and salt. Work for 5 minutes until no traces of puree remain.

Lightly oil the titanium pan with grapeseed oil. Press the mixture firmly into the pan, to a thickness of 1 to 1.5 cm, packing it down to the edges with the back of a spoon. This pressure determines the crispness.
Place the pan in the oven at 180°C for 20 to 25 minutes. The surface should be set and lightly browned.
Take out the pan and break the still-hot plate into irregular pieces, directly into it.
Drizzle with the remaining 20g of honey, mix gently, then spread again in a thin layer. Pinch a few pieces between your fingers to form denser clusters.
Return to the oven at 180°C for 15 to 25 minutes, turning the pieces every 5 to 10 minutes. Stop when the color is a deep brown.

Remove from the cooking container and place on a wire rack or cold plate. Allow to cool completely, preferably in the refrigerator. The crispness develops during this cooling process, not in the oven.
Serve with raw milk, plain yogurt or cottage cheese.

title: Cashew and chocolate pan cookies
intro: It all comes down to cooking with the lid on: the base caramelizes while the steam trapped under the lid keeps the center soft.

ing.note: ointment (taken out in advance, soft to the touch)

titane: Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the batter. The titanium surface heats up quickly and distributes heat from the bottom; the lid reflects gentle heat back onto the top. It's like an oven, without the oven. Then, don't touch it: a cookie placed on a hot surface will stick until a crust forms, then it will release on its own. If you try to lift it with a spatula, you'll tear it off.
steps: Cream the butter with the two sugars and the salt (work the mixture until it whitens slightly and becomes smooth). Allow two good minutes, using a spatula or a mixer.
Add the egg. Mix until the mixture becomes homogeneous again, without trying to aerate it.
Mix the flour and baking soda together, then add them all at once. Stop mixing as soon as the dough is smooth: beyond that point, the gluten will develop and the cookie will become elastic.
Pulse the cashews in a food processor. You want irregular pieces, not a powder. Stir them into the dough.
Add the chocolate chips and mix by hand.
Shape into 7 to 8 even balls, about 60g each.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. This step is optional, but the cold firms the butter and limits spreading: the cookies remain thick.
Preheat the pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Do not add any fat, the dough contains enough. Place two or three balls of dough in the pan, well spaced apart, and cover.

Reduce heat to low to medium. Cook for 13 to 14 minutes without moving the cookies. They are ready when the edges are golden brown, the center is still soft, and they easily release from the bottom of the pan.
Turn off the heat and let them rest in the pan for a few minutes. They will firm up as they cool. Bake the next batch in a pan that has been briefly cooled and then reheated.

title: Pan-roasted cherry tomato pasta
intro: Everything hinges on the first ten minutes: tomatoes that are left untouched, bursting on their own and releasing a juice concentrated enough to serve as a sauce.
titane: The preheated titanium pan, empty, replaces the oven. The heat rises quickly and intensely: the tomato skins tighten and burst, and the juice concentrates instead of evaporating slowly. The lid then takes over, softening the flesh without drying it out. The released juices are enough to loosen anything stuck to the bottom.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the olive oil; it should ripple immediately.

Place the whole cherry tomatoes in the pan, leaving them unwashed to remove any residual moisture if you've just rinsed them, then add the herbs and salt. Let them roast for 10 minutes without moving them. They will detach from the bottom of the pan on their own when the skin is set; that's the signal, not before.
Cover and continue cooking for 5 minutes over medium heat. The tomatoes will soften and release their juices.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water, according to the package directions. Reserve a ladleful of the cooking water before draining.

Remove from the heat and mash the tomatoes with a fork directly in the pan. The juice will loosen the caramelized bits left from cooking. Stir in the vegan cheese: the sauce will thicken and lighten in color.
Add the drained pasta and chopped basil. Mix. If the sauce becomes too thick, thin it with a little pasta water, one spoonful at a time.

title: Chicken rolls with garlic and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: cubes seared without being stirred, which color brightly before being bound with the cold sauce.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding the oil. The chicken placed on top will stick for a few seconds, then release on its own once a crust has formed: this is the moment, and not before, when it's time to stir it. The same skillet can then be used in the oven to brown the rolls and to re-toast them after freezing.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, mayonnaise, and lemon juice with a third of the garlic salt, onion powder, paprika, and pepper until smooth. Chill until ready to serve.
Cut the chicken into 2cm cubes. Season them with the chopped garlic and the remaining spices. Mix by hand to coat them well.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in 2 tablespoons of grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, without smoking.

Place the chicken in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Leave it undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes: it will release easily once a crust has formed. Then stir and finish cooking for 3 minutes, until the pieces are firm and browned.

Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside in a large bowl. While still warm, add the mozzarella, the reserved sauce, and the parsley. Mix well: the cheese should just melt and bind everything together.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Spread the filling on the bottom third of each tortilla, fold over the sides, then roll tightly.

Place the rolls seam-side down on a baking sheet, brush them with the remaining oil, and bake for 15 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. One-pan variation: Sear the rolls for 2 minutes per side in the titanium pan, then bake for 8 minutes.
For storage: allow to cool completely, wrap each roll in foil or a freezer bag, and freeze for up to 3 months.

To reheat: wrap the frozen roll in a damp paper towel, microwave for 3 to 4 minutes, then toast for 1 minute per side in a hot, dry titanium pan. The paper towel prevents the tortilla from drying out, and the pan crisps it up.

title: Beef crunchwraps with a grilled cheddar cheese shell
intro: It all comes down to the shell: a layer of melted and then grilled cheddar that seals the fold and replaces the crispness of the tostada.
ing: 0% fat grated cheddar for the stuffing
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat, allowing you to perform three cooking steps in the same pan: browning the beef, sealing the fold, and then grilling the cheese shell. The cheese bubbles, dries, forms a lacy pattern, and releases itself when it's ready. Never try to loosen it with a spatula: if it resists, it's not cooked.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. A drop of water should bead on it without evaporating immediately.
Mix the ground beef with the taco seasoning, then place it in the hot pan. Let it brown without stirring for 2 minutes, then crumble with a spatula and continue until almost no pink remains.
Add the green chilies, enchilada sauce, and 112g of cheddar cheese. Mix off the heat until combined, then transfer to a serving dish.

Lay a large tortilla flat. Spread about 180g of filling in the center, top with a spoonful of nacho sauce, add the tostada if you're eating it the same day, then the yogurt, tomatoes, and lettuce. Cover with a small tortilla and fan out the edges of the large one, pinching each fold against the previous one. Repeat for all ten.

Wipe the pan clean, add a drizzle of high-smoking oil or butter, and place the crunchwraps seam-side down over medium heat. Do not touch them: they will separate on their own once sealed, in about 2 minutes.

In the same pan, spread about 55g of cheddar cheese into a disc slightly larger than the crunchwrap. Let it simmer until the edges dry and brown, then place the crunchwrap on top, smooth side down, and wait for the crust to loosen on its own, about 5 minutes. Flip and grill the other side in the same way.
For meal prep: let cool completely on a wire rack, wrap individually, and freeze. Omit the tostada, which softens when reheated.

title: Spelt flakes and banana, cooked in a covered pan
intro: What matters here is the gentleness of the fire: if it's too hot, the bottom burns before the center catches.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing it. Titanium cast iron heats up slowly and then maintains a stable temperature; when covered, it traps steam and diffuses a gentle, enveloping heat, just like an oven at 180°C (350°F). The top remains moist, and the edges release easily.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork until smooth. Add the plant-based milk, oats, yeast, cinnamon, and protein powder. Mix well, then let it sit for 5 minutes: the oats will absorb some of the liquid and the mixture (the raw mixture) will thicken.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. The surface should shimmer when a drop of water is added, without smoking. Then brush with clarified butter or grapeseed oil.
Pour the mixture and spread it with a spatula motion to the edges, in an even thickness.
Scatter raspberries and chocolate chips over the top, barely pressing them in.

Cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes: the center should be set, and the edges should pull away from the sides. Uncover for 2 minutes at the end of cooking to dry and brown the surface.
Let it cool for 5 minutes off the heat before cutting. Serve directly from the pan, with the yogurt on the side.

title: Bowl of salted yogurt, candied eggplant and tofu crumble
intro: It all comes down to two cooking steps in the same pan: the eggplant coloring before becoming caramelized, the tofu drying until crispy.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat the oven empty, place the eggplant on it dry (without oil) and leave it alone: it will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. Oil is only added afterward to finish cooking. The same principle applies to tofu, which develops a crumbly texture without being baked.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. The heat must be evenly distributed before any contact with the food.

Place the eggplant cubes in a single layer on a dry surface. Leave them undisturbed for 3 minutes. When they begin to separate and turn golden brown, add half the oil and continue cooking for another 3 minutes, turning regularly.
Add the cherry tomatoes, tomato paste, cumin, lemon juice, coriander, and salt. Stir, cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 8 minutes. The sauce should reduce until it coats the cubes.
Transfer to a bowl (out of the pan). Wipe the pan with paper towels, without washing it.
Mix the crumbled tofu with the soy sauce, paprika, a little salt and the remaining oil.
Return the pan to high heat. Spread the tofu in a thin layer and let it brown for 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 to 3 minutes. It should dry and crisp, not sweat.
Meanwhile, season the yogurt with the dill, salt, and lemon juice. Taste it: the base should be quite salty, as this is what holds the bowl together.
Spread the yogurt in the bottom of a bowl, making a well in the center with a spoon. Place the stewed eggplant in the center, then top with the tofu crumble. Serve with bread.

title: Asparagus sticks wrapped in rice paper, white sesame
intro: It all comes down to the hydration of the rice paper: too wet it sticks, not wet enough it remains opaque and never cracks.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly: the rice paper puffs up and browns like it's air-fried, without oil. Preheat the pan empty, then oil it, and leave it alone. The stick will release on its own when one side is cooked—that's the only sign that it's safe to flip. Forcing it beforehand will tear the coating.
steps: Break the asparagus by hand: the hard base will break off on its own at the right place. Discard the ends.
In a large shallow bowl, whisk together the plant-based milk, baking soda, cornstarch, salt, and pepper until completely dissolved.
Dip a sheet of rice paper into the mixture on both sides, without letting it sit. It should be coated, not soaked.
Lay it flat on a board and let it relax for a minute, until it becomes flexible and manageable.
Cut the sheet in half.
Wrap an asparagus spear in the first half, at an angle, then repeat with the second half to double the wrap. Tighten without crushing the stem.
Roll each stick in the white sesame seeds spread on a plate. The still-damp mixture acts as glue.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without oil.
Pour in the grapeseed oil and swirl it around to coat the entire bottom.
Place the sticks loosely in a single layer. Let them cook for 4 minutes without touching them: wait until they detach themselves from the pan.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist and continue for 4 minutes on the other side, rolling them a quarter turn if the sides remain pale.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process as soon as the outer layer is uniformly crisp and the sesame seeds are golden. Serve immediately: the crispness will not last.

title: Pan-fried buckwheat, pistachio and coconut granola
intro: A roasted granola without an oven, where everything depends on the patience of the low heat and the regularity of the mixing.
titane: The titanium pan toasts like an oven floor: dry, diffused, and consistent heat. You control it by sight and sound. When the flakes stop sticking and move as a single unit under the spatula, the toasting process is underway. If they resist, lower the heat rather than forcing it.
steps: Combine the oats, pistachios, coconut, maple syrup, and almond butter in a bowl. Pour in the aquafaba. Mix until each oat is coated: the liquid will bind the mixture and form the crunchy clumps.
Heat the empty pan over low-medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the clarified butter and spread it evenly. It should simmer without smoking.
Spread the mixture in a thin, uneven layer. The raised areas brown faster and create contrast.
Cover and roast for 15 minutes over low heat. Stir every 3 minutes with a spatula, bringing the edges towards the center.
Halfway through cooking, turn the whole thing over in large shovelfuls to expose the pale sides. The pieces should detach easily, without sticking.
Stop cooking when the color is golden and the smell is distinctly toasted. Transfer (remove from the pan) to a cold plate in a thin layer: the granola will harden as it cools.

title: Blueberry, oat and peanut bars
intro: It all comes down to compaction: a well-compressed base holds up when cut, a soft base crumbles.

ing.note: melted butter with the whey removed

titane: The titanium pan does all three functions. It cooks the blueberries, holds the finished dish, and then goes straight into the oven. Its even heat sets the base while the center remains soft and gooey, and since nothing changes containers, there's no need to worry about unmolding it in between. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the liquid.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

In a bowl, combine the rolled oats, almond flour, peanut butter, agave syrup, and fleur de sel. Mix by hand or with a spatula until the mixture is homogeneous and holds together when pressed between your fingers. This should take about 5 minutes.
Taste it. Adjust the salt or agave now; nothing can be fixed after cooking.
Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the blueberries and water.
Let it simmer (cook gently until the fruit softens) for about 6 minutes over medium heat, stirring regularly. The coulis is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the sauce from the cooking container and place it in a bowl. Wipe the still-warm pan with a paper towel.
Coat the bottom of the pan with a thin layer of clarified butter. Spread half of the oat mixture over the bottom and press down firmly with the back of a spoon, right up to the edges.
Spread the blueberry coulis in an even layer, without going quite to the edge.
Cover with the remaining mixture. Smooth it out, then press it down again.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 10 minutes. The surface should be lightly browned and firm to the touch.
Allow to cool completely in the pan before slicing. This is essential for a clean slice.

title: Red lentil dahl with coconut milk
intro: It all comes down to the order of operations: the onion is first colored, then the curry is awakened in the fat, and only after that the liquids.

ing.note: to be adjusted between 1 and 2 teaspoons

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding any oil. Titanium cookware heats up quickly: the onion will stick nicely, and the spices will release their aromas in the hot fat. Then, everything is done in the same pan, right up to plating.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. The surface must be thoroughly hot before proceeding.
Meanwhile, finely slice the onion (cut it into thin, even strips).
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan, then add the onion. Do not stir it: wait until it pulls away from the bottom of the pan on its own. This is the sign that it has browned.
Add the herb salt and curry to the onion. Mix for 30 seconds, allowing the spices to absorb the fat and release their aromas.
Pour the red lentils, water, tomato pulp and coconut milk into the same pan. Stir to loosen the browned bits from the bottom.

Simmer for about ten minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally. The lentils should be tender and the sauce thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Add a splash of water if it thickens too quickly.
Chop the coriander and scatter it over the dahl when serving.

title: Baked churros with caramel milk sauce
intro: Without a deep fryer, everything depends on the drying of the dough in the pan and on the direct contact with the pan, which gives the crispy grooves.
ing: Dulce de leche flavored protein powder
titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe: shape the churros directly on it, then bake the pan as is. No baking sheet or parchment paper required. The heat from the base heats the edges while the internal steam keeps the center soft.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Combine the water, oil and salt in a small saucepan, and heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer.

Remove from heat and pour in the three flours all at once. Stir firmly with a spatula until you obtain a panade (a dense, homogeneous dough that pulls away from the sides of the pan). Return to low heat for 30 seconds to dry it out.
Transfer the mixture from the cooking utensil to a bowl. Let it cool for two minutes, then stir in the egg and 20g of fromage blanc.
Add the egg whites in three parts. The mixture will resist at first, then it will loosen up: work until you have a smooth and shiny dough that is supple but holds its shape.
Lightly oil the titanium pan and warm it. Fill a piping bag fitted with a fluted nozzle, then pipe 10 cm sticks directly onto the pan, spaced two fingers apart.
Bake the pan for 15 minutes at 180°C. The churros are ready when the ridges are golden brown and the sticks easily detach from the bottom.
Meanwhile, whisk the 150g of cottage cheese with the protein powder, then thin with almond milk until you have a coating sauce (that holds on the back of a spoon).
Serve the churros hot, straight from the pan, with the sauce on the side.

title: Crispy Korean-style chicken, broth rice
intro: It's all about the crust: a nice hot pan, short batches, and pieces left alone until they detach on their own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat, giving the starch-coated chicken the dry crust you usually get with an air fryer. Place the pieces in the pan and leave them alone. As long as they stick, the crust will form; as soon as they release easily, it's done. Use the same pan for the sauce: the juices left at the bottom give it its depth.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the diced chicken, soy sauce, garlic salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and eggs. Mix until each piece is evenly coated.
Pour the cornstarch into an airtight container. Add the chicken, draining off any excess marinade, seal, and shake. Each cube should come out matte and powdery, without any clumps of cornstarch.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the pieces flat, spaced apart, without ever covering the entire surface. Work in three or four batches. Let them sear for about 8 minutes, without stirring.
Turn them over as soon as the pieces separate on their own. Continue for 6 minutes, rolling them on their sides, until they are a uniform golden color.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack or plate, in a single layer to maintain crispness. Repeat with the next batch.

In the same pan, over medium heat, add the soy sauce, gochujang, brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, and ginger. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon (it should coat the back of the spoon with a film that doesn't drip).
Return all the chicken to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats each piece. Serve immediately.
Divide the hot rice among the bowls, place the chicken on top, and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion.

title: Silken tofu tortillas
intro: Two ingredients make the whole dough: what matters here is the thickness of the dough and the heat of the pan, nothing else.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop
crunchy seasonal vegetables and yogurt sauce

titane: Preheat the pan empty, without any oil or butter. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly to the edge: the tortilla will sear in seconds and release easily. Wait until it releases before flipping, otherwise the tortilla will tear.
steps: Mash the silken tofu with a fork in a bowl until smooth. Add the flour, salt, and baking powder. Mix roughly so the flour absorbs the moisture.
Knead by hand for 5 minutes on a lightly floured work surface. The dough should become firm, supple, and smooth, without sticking to your fingers. If it remains wet, add the flour by spoonfuls.
Let it rest for 10 minutes under a cloth. The gluten relaxes, the dough then flattens out without springing back on itself.
Divide into 4 equal portions. Roll each one out (spread into a regular disc) as thinly as possible, 2 mm maximum.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without any fat: this is dry cooking (no fat in the pan, the heat alone works the dough).

Place a tortilla on the plate. Do not touch it. After 45 seconds to 1 minute, it will detach on its own and show golden spots. Flip it over and continue for 30 to 45 seconds. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
Stack the cooked tortillas in a clean tea towel and fold it closed. The trapped steam will keep them soft until serving.
Top with crunchy vegetables and yogurt sauce, fold, serve immediately.

title: Sautéed apples, toasted oats and coconut yogurt
intro: It all comes down to how the slices hold together: a nice hot pan, no movement during cooking, and the apple caramelizes without falling apart.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding any oil or butter. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and retains its heat: the slices brown on the surface instead of releasing their moisture and sinking. You can then mix them with the flakes without them sticking.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes: it should be hot, never smoking. A drop of water should bead up and slide off.
Pour in the coconut oil, maple syrup and cinnamon. Mix for a few seconds, until the mixture becomes smooth and fragrant.
Arrange the apple slices flat in the pan. Cover and cook for 5 minutes without touching them. They are ready when they easily pull away from the bottom and give way under the tip of a knife.
Remove from heat. Add the oats and salt, and stir for 30 seconds to coat them in the caramelized syrup. The residual heat will toast them.
Meanwhile, whisk the coconut yogurt with the protein powder until smooth. Transfer the apples and oats to the top, then finish with the peanut butter.

title: Gluten-free pan-fried baguette
intro: Gluten-free, it all comes down to psyllium: it replaces the gluten network and retains moisture during cooking.
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from stovetop to oven without transferring. You start the baguette covered on the stovetop to begin the crust formation and allow the dough to rise gently, then you transfer the pan directly to the oven, lid off, to finish browning. One pan, one even crust all around.
steps: Pour the water over the psyllium fiber, whisk briefly, and let it sit. Wait until you obtain a thick, translucent gel that clings to the spoon: that's the signal to continue.
In a bowl, combine the gluten-free premix, baking powder, and salt. Mix dry to distribute the yeast, then add the psyllium gel all at once.
Knead by hand for 5 minutes. The dough should become smooth, supple, slightly sticky without sticking strongly to the fingers.
Shape an elongated sausage, calibrated on the bottom of the pan: it must fit there without touching the sides, which would hinder it when rising.
Make diagonal cuts lengthwise across the surface with the tip of a sharp knife. Count four to five clean, shallow cuts.
Oil the titanium pan, place the baguette in it, and cover. Cook over low-medium heat for about twenty minutes: the base will color and the dough will tighten.

Remove the lid, place the pan in the oven at 200°C (390°F) and continue cooking for approximately 25 minutes, until a golden-brown crust forms and it sounds crisp when pressed with a fingernail. Transfer the bread to a wire rack and let it cool completely before slicing: the crumb will finish developing its structure as it cools.

title: Creamy chicken, pasta and mozzarella in a single pan
intro: It all comes down to two things: searing the chicken before adding the liquids, and using a limited amount of liquid so that the pasta cooks without drowning the dish.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the meat is added: the chicken and onion brown instead of releasing their juices. Then, the total liquid level (broth, water, and cream combined) remains below 450 ml. This is the threshold that allows the pasta to cook evenly, absorb the released starch, and the sauce to thicken on its own without boiling over.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Wait for the first wisps of smoke, then pour in the grapeseed oil or clarified butter. These fats withstand high temperatures without burning.

Season the chicken cubes with spices and salt. Place them in a single layer with the onion. Do not stir: the meat will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. Cook for 5 minutes, turning halfway through.

Reduce the heat to medium. Pour in the stock and water, scraping the bottom of the pan with a spatula to loosen any browned bits, then add the cream. Add the uncooked pasta directly to the pan and stir.
Cover and simmer for about 12 minutes, stirring every 3 or 4 minutes to prevent sticking. The liquid should gradually reduce and thicken.
Slice the zucchini into thin strips. Add it when the pasta is still slightly firm to the bite, cover again and continue for 5 minutes.
Scatter the mozzarella pieces on top, cover, and turn off the heat. Let it melt for 2 minutes, then stir one last time off the heat. Adjust the salt and serve immediately.

title: Buffalo chicken burritos with protein sauce
intro: It all comes down to two textures: shredded chicken still moist with sauce, and a tortilla cooked quickly enough to be crispy without drying out.
titane: The titanium pan seamlessly transitions between searing and simmering without changing pans: the chicken browns over medium-high heat, then finishes covered over low heat in thirty-five minutes, compared to nearly three hours in a slow cooker. At the end of the cooking process, the same pan, preheated empty, gives the burritos a golden crust that the convection heat of an air fryer simply cannot replicate.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, without smoking.
Place the chicken pieces in the pan with the 150g of onions from the first list. Leave it undisturbed for three minutes: the meat will release itself from the pan once it's seared. Turn it over.
Add the garlic salt, ranch seasoning, pepper, and 120g of buffalo sauce. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 35 minutes. The chicken should be fork-tender.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, buffalo sauce, honey, milk, garlic salt, onion powder, and pepper in a blender until smooth and pourable. Set aside.
Remove the chicken (take it out of the pan and place it on a board) and shred it with two forks, into long strands rather than crumbs.

Remove the pan from the heat and return the chicken to it. Mix in the protein sauce, the remaining 150g of onions, the mozzarella, and the chives. The residual heat will be enough to bind everything together.
Spread a portion of rice on each tortilla, then a generous ladleful of buffalo chicken. Leave three centimeters of space on the sides.
Fold in the sides, then roll tightly, pushing the filling towards you with each turn. You'll get 10 burritos.
To store: wrap each burrito in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag. Keeps for up to 3 months in the freezer.

To serve: Defrost the burrito in the microwave, wrapped in a damp paper towel. Preheat the titanium pan empty, then sear for 3 minutes per side, without oil. The tortilla will release easily when golden brown.

title: Feta in filo pastry, honey and sesame
intro: It all comes down to two stages of cooking: low and covered to melt the feta, high and uncovered to crisp the filo.
ing: square of baking paper the size of the bottom of the pan
titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. The filo pastry, placed on its parchment paper, receives the direct heat of the metal and dries from below, while the lid radiates a gentle, enveloping heat that softens the cheese. When you remove the lid, the titanium surface heats up again in seconds: it's your grill. Stay by the pan for that last minute.
steps: Place a sheet of filo pastry flat on the square of baking paper. Brush it with olive oil, right up to the edges.
Cover with the second sheet, offset by a quarter turn, and brush it in turn.
Drain the feta, dry it with paper towels and place it in the center. Fold the sides over each other to form a sealed packet, seam underneath.
Oil the top of the package and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Lightly press the seeds into the package to make them stick.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour a drizzle of olive oil into the bottom.
Place the package, along with its baking paper, directly into the pan. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 12 minutes. The filo should brown without burning and easily release from the pan.
Remove the lid, increase the heat to high and cook for 1 to 2 minutes to finish browning. The top should sound hollow when touched.
Remove from the pan immediately onto a plate, drizzle with a little honey and serve immediately, with a rocket salad if you want to cut through the fat.

title: Turkey rice, vegetables and white sauce
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the turkey crust flavors the juices, the rice absorbs them, and the cold sauce arrives last to cut the heat.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: Preheat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water thrown into it should bead up and slide off without evaporating immediately: the surface is at temperature. The turkey will brown in a few minutes without sticking, and you can then cook vegetables and rice in the same pan, without ever washing it.
steps: Place the empty pan over high heat and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Check the heat by the water droplet.
Cut the turkey into 3cm cubes. Add salt, spices, oregano and chopped garlic, mix by hand.

Pour a drizzle of high-smoke-point fat into the pan. Arrange the pieces in a single layer, without moving them. After 4 to 6 minutes, they will separate easily: this is the signal to turn them over. Remove from the heat and transfer to a plate.
While the mixture is searing, finely chop the yellow onion, slice the pepper into strips and the courgette into half-moons.
In the still-hot pan, sauté half the onion with the pepper for 5 minutes over medium-high heat. Return the turkey to the pan, stir, then remove everything from the pan.
Throw the rest of the onion and zucchini into the pan, add the raw rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it in hot fat until the grains become translucent at the edges.
Pour in the water, add salt, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Let it simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until the water is fully absorbed and the cheese is tender. Do not open during cooking.
Meanwhile, whisk together the fromage blanc, mustard, olive oil, stevia, salt, and a pinch of spice. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
Place the turkey and vegetables back on top of the rice, cover and reheat for 3 minutes over low heat.
Finely chop the red onion and tomato, and distribute them raw on top. Drizzle with sauce just before serving.

title: Pasta with seared beef and chipotle sauce
intro: It all comes down to the beef crust: a really hot pan, space between the pieces, and you don't touch it.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the meat is added: this is what creates the Maillard reaction (browning that enhances the flavor) instead of a grayish glaze. The same pan can then be used for the direct transfer to low heat for assembly, without any additional washing up or transfers.
steps: Cut the beef into even 3cm pieces. Season with garlic salt and black pepper, mix by hand.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently and spread without smoking.
Place the beef in a single, loose layer. Work in two batches if necessary. Do not stir: the meat will release from the bottom on its own once the crust has formed.
Turn the pieces over and brown the second side. Remove from the heat, add a drizzle of oil if the pan is dry, and roll the meat in the cooking juices.
Blend together the cottage cheese, milk, parmesan cheese, garlic, chipotle peppers, garlic salt and pepper until perfectly smooth. Set aside.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water in a saucepan for one minute less than the indicated time. Drain, reserving a ladleful of the cooking water.
Return the pan to low heat. Add the pasta and sauce to the beef, and stir for 2 to 3 minutes to heat through. Thin with pasta water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Sprinkle with chopped chives.
Divide into 10 portions in airtight containers. Let cool uncovered before sealing.
Store in the freezer for up to 3 months. To reheat, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a damp paper towel and microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through.

title: Naan stuffed with cheese and green chili
intro: A leavened dough, made with cottage cheese, which rises in the pan and keeps its melted cheese center: it all depends on the temperature of the cooking surface.
titane: Heat the dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the oil or butter: titanium dioxide heats up quickly and retains heat well, which is what creates the mottled crust. Once the naan is in the pan, don't touch it. It will stick at first, then release itself once the crust has formed. This is the signal to flip it, and the only way to avoid tearing the dough over the filling.
steps: Combine the flour, cottage cheese, yeast, and salt in a bowl. Knead by hand until you obtain a soft, smooth dough that no longer sticks to your fingers. Divide it into two portions and roll each out into a disc about 12 cm in diameter.
Finely chop the green chili. Mix it with the two cheeses and almond milk until you have a smooth filling that holds its shape on a spoon.

Place half of the mixture in the center of each disc. Bring the edges towards the center, pinch to seal, and fold the seam downwards. Flatten with the palm of your hand, then with a rolling pin, without forcing, to create two even discs.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the fat: it should simmer gently, never smoke.

Place a naan in the pan. Leave it for 3 minutes without touching it. As soon as it releases easily, flip it and cook for another 3 minutes: the second side should be browned and the cheese should be melting in the center. Transfer it to a wire rack to keep it crispy, then cook the second naan.

title: Blueberry pancakes, without eggs or butter
intro: It all comes down to two things: the vinegar, which makes the dough rise when it comes into contact with the yeast, and patience in front of the pan.
titane: Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for two to three minutes. Titanium heats up quickly and distributes heat evenly without hot spots: the first side browns evenly. Only then add the fat in a very thin layer, and immediately pour in the batter.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, and sugar in a bowl. Pour in the plant-based milk and vinegar. Mix briefly until you have a thick batter. A few lumps should remain: this is a sign that you haven't overworked the batter.
Add the blueberries and gently fold them in with a spatula, so as not to crush them.
Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the oil or clarified butter and spread it thinly with a paper towel.

Pour a small ladleful of batter into the center. Leave it undisturbed for about 3 minutes. The pancake is ready to be flipped when it easily lifts from the surface and the edges have lost their shine.
Turn over and continue for 2 minutes, until the second side is golden and the heart closes under the finger.
Repeat this process with the remaining batter, one pancake at a time. A pan full of batter loses heat, and the pancakes will turn white instead of brown. Serve with maple syrup.

title: Chicken rolls with queso
intro: It all comes down to the color of the chicken: a real crust on the surface, otherwise the filling releases water and makes the tortilla soggy.

ing.note: pressed cheese studded with chili peppers

titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding the oil. The raw chicken will initially stick, then release on its own once a crust has formed: this is the signal to flip. The same skillet then goes in the oven to brown the rolls, without transferring them.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, enchilada sauce, milk, salsa, and taco seasoning until perfectly smooth and grain-free. Refrigerate.
Cut the chicken into 2cm cubes. Mix them with the taco seasoning, garlic salt and pepper, then let it sit for 5 minutes.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the oil: it should ripple on the surface.

Sear the chicken in a single layer, or in two batches if necessary. Leave it undisturbed for 4 minutes. Turn it over when the pieces begin to separate easily, then continue cooking for another 4 minutes until cooked through. Remove from the pan (transfer to a cold dish to stop the cooking process).
Remove from heat and mix the chicken with the mozzarella, pepper jack, green chilies, pico de gallo, and cilantro. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of queso sauce to bind.
Fill each tortilla to the bottom third, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Arrange the rolls in the pan, seam down, and bake for 15 minutes: the cheese should be melted and the surface just golden.
Serve with the remaining queso sauce, cooled slightly.

title: Ground beef, potatoes and cheddar in a single skillet
intro: It all comes down to the first minute: a really hot pan, meat left alone, and the crust forms on its own.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for two to three minutes before adding any oil or butter. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold meat is added: this is what allows the crust to form, rather than relying on cooking liquid. Place the beef in the pan, then leave it alone. It will stick at first, then release on its own once browned. This moment is your timer. The rest of the recipe, including the vegetables, can be prepared in the same pan.
steps: Cut the potatoes and courgette into two centimeter cubes, finely chop the onion. Set aside separately.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the clarified butter: it should ripple without smoking.

Place the beef in a single mass. Leave it undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes, until it loosens from the metal. Then break it up with a spatula, continue cooking for 3 minutes, and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate.

Without cleaning the pan, add the onion, potatoes, and zucchini. Season, stir to loosen any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cover and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring three or four times. The potatoes should be tender when pierced with a knife and golden brown in places.
Meanwhile, whisk together the cream cheese, mayonnaise, ketchup, and maple syrup in a bowl. Taste and adjust the seasoning with pepper.
Return the meat to the vegetables and mix. Distribute the cheddar cheese evenly, cover, and turn off the heat. Two minutes is all it takes: the cheese melts without sticking to the bottom.
Spoon the sauce over the dish when serving, directly in the pan.

title: Pizza turnovers with yogurt dough
intro: A dough without leavening, two ingredients, and the whole success lies in the thickness at which you roll it out: thin, otherwise the turnover remains soft in the center.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold batter is placed on it. This allows the bottom to sear immediately upon contact and form a dry, golden crust, without the need for an air fryer and without the filling having time to make the base soggy. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then grease it: the fat should never heat up on its own in a cold pan.
steps: Combine the flour, 520g of yogurt, garlic salt, and Italian herbs in a bowl. Work the mixture by hand until it is smooth and no dry flour remains at the bottom.
Knead for 3 minutes on a lightly floured surface, until you obtain a smooth and supple dough.
Divide into 10 equal portions. Roll them into balls and cover them with a cloth.
Roll out each ball very thinly. Aim for the edge before the dough tears: this is what gives it its crispness.
Fill one half of each disc: tomato sauce first, leaving a 2 cm border, then turkey pepperoni, then mozzarella.
Fold the pastry over the filling. Pinch the edges firmly, then mark them with a fork to lock the seal.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the grapeseed oil or clarified butter, tilt to distribute.

Place the pastries loosely on the baking sheet. Do not touch them again: they will detach on their own once the baking sheet is set. Then turn them over and brown the other side. Allow approximately ten minutes in total.
Meanwhile, whisk together the 225g of Greek yogurt with the ranch dressing and skimmed milk. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon without running.
For storage: allow to cool completely, wrap each pastry in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag, and freeze for up to one month.
When ready to serve a frozen turnover, wrap it in a damp paper towel and microwave it on a plate for 4 minutes. The moisture prevents the pastry from drying out.
Finish it for 3 minutes in the hot titanium pan, medium-high heat, one side then the other, until it is crispy again.

title: Sweet potato patties with psyllium
intro: Without flour, it's the psyllium that holds everything together: let it rest for five minutes, otherwise the dough won't take shape.
ing: a small pinch of baking soda
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding the fat. The patties will sear on contact, develop a crust, then finish cooking covered over low heat: the center will steam from the sweet potato itself. No oven baking required.
steps: Mash the sweet potato flesh with a fork in a bowl. Crack the eggs into the bowl and mix until you have a smooth mixture.
Add salt, add the bicarbonate, mix again.
Sprinkle the psyllium over the mixture, stir, then let it rest for 5 minutes. The mixture should thicken and hold its shape: when it detaches from the spoon in a soft block, it is ready.
Incorporate three-quarters of the seeds and the spices if you are using them.
Moisten your hands and shape into 8 flattened discs about 2 cm thick. Avoid tall balls, which would remain raw in the center. Sprinkle the remaining seeds on top, pressing lightly.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the clarified butter. It should ripple without smoking.

Place the patties loosely in the pan. Let them cook for 4 to 5 minutes without touching them: they will detach themselves from the bottom once a crust has formed. Cover and continue cooking for 7 minutes over low heat.
Flip each patty with a flick of the wrist, cover again and cook for 8 minutes over low heat. The outside will be golden, the inside melting.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to stop the cooking process. Let cool slightly. The crust will remain dry underneath.

title: Oat and banana pancakes
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas, the only sugar in the batter, and on patience when turning.
titane: Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, two to three minutes before adding any oil or butter. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and evenly: the batter will brown uniformly without sticking. Don't touch anything until the pancake releases itself from the pan.
steps: Peel the bananas and roughly chop them. Blend them with the oat flakes and liquid until you obtain a smooth paste with no visible lumps.
Place the empty pan over medium heat. Let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the fat. Tilt the pan so that it covers the entire bottom, then remove the excess with a paper towel.
Drop small ladles of batter onto the pan, leaving space between them. Let it cook for 3 minutes without touching it: bubbles should break the surface and the edges should flatten.
Flip the pancake over with a quick flick of the wrist as soon as it releases from the pan. Cook for another 2 minutes, until it reaches an even golden color.
Remove the food from the pan and place it on a wire rack rather than a plate to avoid the steam softening it. Wipe the pan clean between batches.

title: Flatbread with red lentils
intro: A flourless bread that stands upright thanks to psyllium and is cooked entirely in a pan: it's all about patience, you only turn it over once.
titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty and then oiled, it sears the bottom into a golden crust while the lid reflects the heat back into the center of the dough. No sticking, no drying out: the steam remains trapped under the lid and cooks the crumb.
steps: Cover the lentils generously with cold water and let them soak for a maximum of 2 hours. Beyond that, they will fall apart and the dough will become sticky.
Drain them thoroughly, then shake the colander to remove any water trapped between the grains.
Blend the lentils with the coconut milk, olive oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder and herbs. Blend until you have a smooth paste with no visible grains.
Incorporate the psyllium and baking powder, mix vigorously, then let it sit for 5 minutes: the dough thickens and becomes manageable.
Shape a thick pancake by hand, the diameter of your pan, as even as possible so that the center cooks at the same time as the edges.
Sprinkle the top with sesame seeds and press them lightly so they adhere.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly by tilting the pan over the entire surface.

Place the galette on the griddle, cover, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Leave it for 18 minutes without touching it: the bread is ready to be turned over when the bottom easily detaches from the metal.
Turn over with a flick of the wrist, cover and continue for 17 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out dry.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a wire rack to cool for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Fennel, nectarine and grilled salmon salad
intro: It all comes down to two contrasts: raw vegetables cut to the thickness of a leaf, and a truly crispy salmon skin.

ing.note: mini, or half of a large one

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when the cold salmon fillet is placed on it. Preheat the pan empty, oil it, place the salmon skin-side down, and then leave it alone. It will stick until a crust forms, and will release itself when it's ready. If you pull it off before then, you'll leave the skin in the pan.
steps: Trim the fennel, keeping the fronds. Thinly slice the bulb and cucumber using a mandoline. Cut the nectarines into slightly thicker slices with a knife.

Combine everything in a salad bowl. Pour in the olive oil, vinegar, and honey; season with salt and pepper. Mix gently by hand, without crushing. Refrigerate while the fish cooks: the vegetables will soften slightly.
Dry the salmon skin with absorbent paper. Salt it.
Heat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should ripple, not smoke.

Place the salmon skin-side down. Leave it undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes. When it begins to flake easily, reduce the heat to medium and continue cooking for another 3 to 4 minutes, depending on the thickness, until it reaches your desired doneness. Transfer to a cutting board.
Cut the avocado in half, remove the pit and skin, and slice.
Divide the salad between two plates. Add the avocado, then the salmon in large pieces, skin included. Sprinkle with dill, fennel fronds, and a pinch of chili salt.

title: Coconut butter popcorn
intro: It all comes down to the starting temperature: a pan that's already hot makes the grains burst together, a warm pan cooks them before they swell.
titane: The titanium's metallic mass heats up quickly and retains that temperature when the cold grains arrive. The result: a more even burst, fewer grains left at the bottom, and no overheating. Always shake by the handle, never with a spoon, to stir the grains without scraping the bottom.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water that is dropped on it should hiss and evaporate immediately.
Pour in the coconut oil. It melts in a few seconds and should coat the bottom without smoking.
Add the corn kernels in a single layer, without overlapping them. Maintain medium heat.
Cover. As soon as the first popping starts, shake the pan by the handle, with small wrist movements, about every ten seconds. Allow 5 minutes.
Turn off the fire when the popping stops more than two to three seconds apart. Don't wait for complete silence: the bottom would burn.
Remove the pan from the heat, take off the lid, and sprinkle the salt and sugar directly onto the still-hot grains. Stir by tossing the pan. The seasoning adheres better to hot grains.
Transfer (out of the pan) to a rectangular dish in a thin layer, allowing time for the steam to escape and the popcorn to remain crunchy.

title: Broccoli curry with peanuts, tempeh crumble
intro: The key is the second cooking stage: the crumbled tempeh must crisp up dry in the still-hot curry pan.
ing: The juice of half a lime
titane: The titanium pan heats up incredibly high without flinching. It allows you to sear crumbled tempeh over high heat, without added fat, and achieve a golden crumble where an air fryer would normally be needed. One pan is all you need, from stir-frying vegetables to toppings.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then pour in the grapeseed oil.
Add the spring onion, ginger and curry paste. Fry for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
While this stock is infusing, cut the broccoli into small florets and quarter the mushrooms.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the vegetables and let them sear without stirring; they will detach from the bottom of the pan on their own once browned. Then sauté for a total of 7 to 8 minutes, until the broccoli is tender when pierced with a knife.
In a bowl, mix the peanut butter with 200 ml of water until you get a smooth sauce.
Pour the sauce over the vegetables, reduce heat to medium and stir for 2 minutes to coat.
Season: salt, lime juice, a pinch of sugar. Taste and adjust the acidity.
Remove the curry from the pan and place it in a dish. Cover and wipe the pan with paper towels.
Crumble the tempeh or tofu into a bowl by hand, in irregular pieces.
Add the oil, cumin, salt and soy sauce. Mix well so that each crumb is coated.

Return the pan to high heat, without any oil. Pour the crumble in an even layer, without overloading. Let it set without stirring until it releases easily, then brown for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally. It should be dry and crispy.
Serve the curry with the rice, and scatter the crumble on top at the last moment.

title: Sardine, chickpea and buckwheat patties
intro: It's all about patience: a pancake flipped too soon leaves its crust in the pan.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the oil. The heat will rise quickly and spread evenly without creating a cold spot, forming a continuous crust under the pancake. It will release easily when ready; as long as it resists, it's not cooked.
steps: Roughly mash the chickpeas with a fork in a bowl: a few whole pieces give some bite.

Add the sardines with their tomato sauce, the buckwheat flakes, the egg, salt, and paprika. Mix until you have a smooth paste that holds its shape in the palm of your hand. If it's too sticky, let it rest for 5 minutes: the flakes will absorb the moisture.
Shape into 4 even patties, about 2 cm thick. Smooth the edges with the palm of your hand to prevent them from crumbling during cooking.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly, without smoking.
Place the pancakes on the baking sheet, spacing them apart. Do not move them. Cook for 4 minutes, then test: the pancake that slides easily under the spatula is ready to be flipped.
Turn over and brown the second side for 4 minutes. Transfer (out of the pan) to a wire rack rather than a plate, to keep it crispy.

title: Warm potato salad and tofu schnitzel
intro: It all comes down to two things: seasoned potatoes that are still warm, absorbing the broth, and breading that is left alone until it comes off on its own.
ing: clarified butter or vegetable fat with a high smoke point
titane: The same pan is used for sautéing onions, deglazing, and searing. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before each addition of fat: the surface heats up evenly, the oil film remains thin, and the breadcrumbs adhere and then release on their own. Wipe the pan clean between uses; the sweet juices from the broth would otherwise burn under the breadcrumbs.
steps: Cook the whole, unpeeled potatoes in a saucepan of salted water. Cook for about 20 minutes from the time the water boils, then reduce to a simmer. They are ready when a knife inserted into them meets no resistance.
Drain. Peel them while still warm, protecting your fingers with a tea towel, and slice them into thin rounds. Set aside in a salad bowl.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It should be hot all over.
Add the clarified butter, then the chopped onion. Sweat it for 8 minutes over medium heat, until it is translucent and lightly browned at the edges.
Deglaze (dissolve the caramelized juices with liquid) with the vegetable stock, scraping the bottom. Let it reduce for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Pour this hot mixture over the potatoes. Add the vinegar, agave, mustard, salt, and pepper. Gently mix with a spatula and let it rest: the salad will season itself as it cools.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, water, spice mix, and a pinch of salt until you have a smooth paste with the consistency of heavy cream. Pour the breadcrumbs into a second plate.
Pat the tofu slices dry with paper towels. Dip them in the batter, let the excess drip off, then press them into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper. Preheat it again empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the oil: it should ripple and smoke very lightly.
Place the breaded slices on the plate. Do not touch them. After about 4 minutes, the crust will detach itself from the bottom: then turn them over and continue for 4 minutes on the other side.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a wire rack, not paper towels, to maintain its crispness. Serve with potato salad, chopped parsley, and a lemon wedge.

title: Zucchini caviar with tahini
intro: It all comes down to the charré: a side well blackened in the pan gives the courgette the smoky taste that we usually look for in braised eggplant.

ing.note: cut in half lengthwise and notched

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: it sears the zucchini like a griddle while the lid tenderizes them throughout. Don't move them. As long as they stick, the caramelization isn't complete. When they release easily, they're ready to be flipped.
steps: Cut the courgettes in half lengthwise. Make diagonal cuts in the flesh side, without cutting through the skin: the grooves increase the contact surface and allow water to evaporate.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil; it should ripple without smoking.
Place the zucchini cut-side down in the pan. Cover, or press them down with a weight (a small saucepan works well). Leave them undisturbed for 8 minutes. They will detach from the metal on their own.
Turn them over with a flick of the wrist. Continue for 2 minutes, until the flesh is clinging to the bones and tender to the touch.
Remove the still-warm courgettes from the pan and place them in a blender. Add the tahini, lemon juice, and salt.

Blend until smooth and homogeneous. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and lemon juice. Serve warm, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator: the preparation will keep for 4 to 5 days.

title: Accordion potatoes
intro: It all comes down to the regularity of the cuts: the thinner and straighter they are, the more the slices open up and crisp up in the oven.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The base of the potatoes will develop a crust over high heat, then the pan goes directly into the oven: a single piece of equipment, no transfer, no lost crust during the change of dish.
steps: Wash and dry the potatoes without peeling them. Place a chopstick on each side of each potato: the blade will stop on the chopsticks and never penetrate the tuber.
Make notches across the width every centimeter, up to the contact of the chopsticks.
Turn the potato over, rotate it a quarter turn and repeat the cuts. The two sets of crisscrossing cuts create the accordion-like opening.
Mix together the olive oil, salt, pepper, smoked paprika and dried herbs.
Brush on the marinade, paying particular attention to the areas between the blades. Gently separate them with your finger to allow the marinade to penetrate.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should simmer without smoking.
Place the potatoes cut-side up. Sear (brown quickly in the hot pan) for 5 minutes without touching them. They will release easily when the base is golden.
Place the pan in the oven at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes. The gills will open, the tips will brown, and the flesh will flake easily with a knife. Transfer to a warm plate and serve immediately.

title: Coconut, grape and pistachio frozen yogurt
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the layer: if it's even, it breaks cleanly and melts uniformly in the mouth.
titane: The pan acts as a mold, not a heat source. Its bare, smooth, uncoated metal doesn't retain frost: the frozen disc releases with a single, sharp movement, whereas a non-stick or plastic base requires force. A single container, from mixing to unmolding.
steps: Roughly chop the pistachios with a knife just before starting. Reserve a third for finishing.
In a bowl, mix the coconut yogurt and maple syrup until smooth. Stir in the raisins and two-thirds of the pistachios, mixing gently.
Pour into the cold, dry titanium pan. Spread with a spatula into an even layer of about 1 cm. Unevenness is the only real possible flaw here.
Melt the dark chocolate in a double boiler, let it cool for a minute, then drizzle it over the surface in thin streams. Chocolate that is too hot will cause the yogurt to sink.
Scatter the reserved pistachios and fleur de sel over the top.
Place the pan in the freezer, flat, for a minimum of 4 hours. The surface should be firm and distinctly cold to the touch.

Remove the pan from the refrigerator and let it cool for 1 minute on the work surface, or warm the bottom for a few seconds in the palm of your hand. Flip it over quickly: the disc will detach easily from the metal. Slice or break into irregular pieces and serve immediately.

title: Savory French toast with parmesan, mushrooms and a soft-boiled egg
intro: The bread should absorb the liquid without falling apart: a stale loaf with a tight crumb holds up well to soaking and gives a clean crust in the pan.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: the mushrooms sear instead of boiling in their own juices, and the bread develops a crisp crust. In both cases, don't touch anything until the food releases itself from the pan—that's the sign the crust has formed. Use only one pan for both, and alternate between them.
steps: Cut the bread slices to the desired size, without exceeding two centimeters in thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together the 2 eggs, milk, and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the bread in the machine and turn it over two or three times. It should be soaked throughout but still be pliable.
Clean the mushrooms, then slice them evenly.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Then add a knob of clarified butter.

Add the mushrooms in a single layer, sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Let them sit until they separate on their own, then stir and continue cooking. Cook for a total of 8 minutes. Don't overcrowd the pan: two batches are better than one large pile that releases its juices. Transfer to a plate.
Bring a small saucepan of water to a boil — less than 500 ml is enough. Add the eggs and cook for 6 minutes 30 seconds.
Transfer them immediately to a bowl of ice water, then peel them gently.

Wipe the pan clean, return it to medium-high heat, and add the second knob of clarified butter. Place the soaked slices in the pan and reduce the heat to medium. Let them brown undisturbed until they release easily from the pan, then turn them over and brown the other side. Approximately 7 minutes total.
Briefly warm the mushrooms in the pan. Arrange the French toast, mushrooms, arugula, and halved soft-boiled egg on a plate. Sprinkle with chives and Parmesan shavings, and season with pepper.

title: Fruit pastes with collagen and sweet potato
intro: It all comes down to the gelatin: it must swell when cold and then melt without ever boiling, otherwise the texture remains soft.
titane: The covered titanium pan replaces the oven. Empty, it heats up in two minutes and distributes heat evenly; with the lid on, the trapped steam cooks the sweet potato thoroughly without drying it out. Once the flesh is scooped out, the same pan, now cooled, is used to combine the orange juice and gelatin. A single utensil, from raw tuber to set mass.
steps: Prick the whole sweet potato all over with a fork. Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes: the heat should be felt by holding the palm of your hand above the bottom.

Brush the bottom of the pan with clarified butter. Place the sweet potato on top, cover, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 55 minutes, turning it every 15 minutes. It's ready when a knife inserted into the flesh meets no resistance.
Split it open, take out 200g of flesh and mash it with a fork or blend it until you have a smooth puree, without fibers.
Incorporate the collagen peptides, honey, vanilla, and salt into this puree. Mix until the mixture is perfectly smooth, without any lumps of powder.

Wipe the pan clean and let it cool completely. Pour in the cold orange juice, sprinkle the gelatin evenly over the surface and let it bloom (swell in a cold liquid before dissolving) for 10 minutes, off the heat.
Place the pan over low heat. Stir for 3 to 4 minutes until the liquid becomes clear and no lumps remain on the spoon. Never let it simmer: above 60°C, the gelatin loses its gelling power.
Pour this hot liquid over the sweet potato mixture and whisk immediately, without waiting. The mixture should remain fluid and smooth.
Transfer the mixture from the baking pan to a square baking pan lined with parchment paper. Smooth the surface. Refrigerate until firm, or freeze for 35 to 45 minutes.
Remove from the mold using the paper and cut into 16 squares. Each square provides approximately 2.5 g of collagen peptides. Store them in the refrigerator in an airtight container.

title: Chocolate and peanut bars
intro: Three layers, no oven baking: everything depends on the firmness of the packing and on the casting being conducted at a low temperature.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. It heats up quickly and retains heat: place it over low heat, let the coconut oil melt, then turn off the heat. For chocolate, go even further—remove the pan as soon as the first shards begin to soften. The thermal mass (the heat stored in the metal) finishes melting on its own, without lumps or signs of overheating.
steps: In a bowl, combine the oats, peanut butter, syrup, and salt. Mix with a spoon until no flakes remain dry.

Line a square dish with baking paper. Pour in the mixture and press it down firmly with the back of a spoon, all the way to the corners. The surface should be flat and compact: this is what will hold the cut.
Melt the coconut oil in the titanium pan over low heat for 2 minutes. Remove from heat, add the melted peanut butter and syrup, and stir until smooth and without separation.
Spread the still-warm caramel evenly over the base. Tilt the dish to spread it; do not smooth it with a spatula.
Place in the freezer for 30 minutes. The caramel should be set, matte, and firm to the touch.

Wipe the pan clean. Over very low heat, add the chopped chocolate and peanut butter. As soon as the first pieces begin to melt, remove from the heat and stir continuously: the mixture will finish melting and become glossy.
Pour the chocolate over the set caramel, spread with an offset spatula, and sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Refrigerate for 2 hours. Remove from mold using the paper, then cut with a knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: White chocolate and strawberry mousse
intro: A light mousse that holds together thanks to the whipped egg whites, not the cream: everything depends on the temperature of the chocolate when you incorporate the fromage blanc.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan and double boiler. Melted chocolate, heated milk, dissolved gelatin: a single surface, low heat, and the thermal mass remains low enough that you immediately feel any excess heat. Stir continuously; white chocolate burns before it colors.
steps: Rehydrate the gelatin in a little cold water. Roughly chop the white chocolate.
Place the pan over very low heat. Melt the chocolate, stirring continuously with a spatula, until smooth and glossy. Transfer it to a bowl and set aside.
In the same pan, warm the almond milk. Off the heat, dissolve the drained gelatin in it, then pour over the chocolate. Whisk until smooth and lump-free.
Allow to cool to room temperature. Pour the mixture back into the cold pan, add the cream cheese and strawberry powder, and whisk until perfectly smooth.

Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form in a separate bowl. Whisk in one-third of the egg whites to loosen the base, then gently fold in the remaining whites with a spatula, lifting from underneath. Stop as soon as the color is uniform.
Divide into seven jars. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until the surface is firm to the touch.

title: Flourless chocolate rice cake
intro: A flourless cake whose appeal lies entirely in the contrast of textures: a golden and crispy base, a heart that remains creamy thanks to the rice.

ing.note: (It can withstand higher heat without burning)

titane: The pan serves as both a mold and a heat source. The hot butter at the bottom sears the batter on contact, creating a golden crust, while the lid maintains a humid atmosphere above. The cake is ready when it pulls away from the sides on its own: at this point, the base is set and releases effortlessly from the pan.
steps: Melt the clarified butter over low heat in the titanium pan for 3 minutes. Remove two-thirds of it and place it in a bowl, leaving the rest to coat the bottom of the pan. Keep the pan on very low heat.
In a bowl, roughly mash the cooked rice with a fork to separate the grains. Add the eggs, applesauce, and reserved butter. Mix until well combined.
Incorporate the sugar, vanilla and baking soda. Work for only a few seconds; the dough should remain pliable.
Add the chocolate chips and mix with a spatula, without overmixing.
Pour the mixture into the hot, greased pan. Smooth the surface with a spatula, pushing the batter to the edges.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes: the base should brown without smoking. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Transfer the covered pan to the oven for 20 minutes. The cake is cooked when it is firm in the center and pulls away easily from the sides.
Take out, let it cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn it over onto a plate: the golden side will be on top.

title: Pan-fried date and almond puree cookies
intro: A dough without added sugar or gluten, bound only by date and egg: everything depends on the gentleness of the fire and the patience before removing the cookies.
ing: a large tablespoon of almond puree
large tablespoon of gluten-free flour mix
titane: The titanium pan, preheated empty and then covered, recreates the enveloping heat of an oven while giving the bottom direct contact with the metal, resulting in a golden and crispy crust. The key is simple: as long as a cookie sticks, it's not ready. As soon as it releases easily under the spatula, the caramelization is complete.
steps: Microwave the dates for 10 to 15 seconds, until they soften.
Mash them with a fork until you get a coarse paste, without large pieces of skin.
Add the almond puree and work the mixture until smooth.
Incorporate the egg and mix thoroughly to homogenize the mixture.
Add the gluten-free flour and mix just enough to absorb it. The dough remains soft, almost runny.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then brush it with a light coating of clarified butter.
Place small mounds of dough in the warm pan, well spaced apart: they will spread slightly in the heat.
Distribute the chocolate chips over each mound, barely pressing them in.
Cover and cook for 12 minutes over very low heat. Only lift the lid once, halfway through cooking, to check the color underneath.
Remove the lid and continue cooking for 2 minutes to firm up the tops. Remove the cookies when they release easily, then transfer them to a wire rack.

title: Bowls of seared potatoes, beef tacos
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the potatoes: a short dip in water, then searing in a single layer, without touching it.
titane: The frying pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it develops a dry and even crust on the potato cubes in fifteen minutes. It then goes on to cook the meat, and then to assemble the dish: a single utensil, from start to finish.
steps: Cut the potatoes into one-centimeter cubes, as uniform as possible. Uniformity is key to cooking.
Plunge them into a saucepan of boiling water for 5 minutes over high heat. The tip of a knife should slide in easily for the first millimeter; the center should remain firm.
Drain thoroughly, then let it air dry for 2 minutes. A damp surface will not adhere.
