Mix the cubes with the garlic salt, smoked paprika and onion powder.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple on the surface.

Place the potatoes in a single layer. Leave them undisturbed for 5 minutes. Turn them over when they begin to separate on their own, then continue cooking over medium heat for a total of 15 minutes, until a golden crust forms.
Remove the potatoes from the pan and set aside in a dish.
In the still-hot pan, sear the ground beef, breaking it up with a spatula, over medium heat. Let it brown before stirring.
Add the taco seasoning and enchilada sauce. Cover and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the meat without releasing any water.
Return the potatoes to the pan. Sprinkle with cheddar cheese, jalapeños, tomatoes, and red onion. Cover and remove from heat for 2 minutes; the residual heat will melt the cheese.
Divide into 10 containers. Top with nacho sauce when serving, if using.

title: One-pot pasta with seared beef, green pepper, and two cheeses
intro: It's all about the order: a proper crust on the beef first, then the pasta in the same pan, which retains the juices from the searing.
ing: Rump steak or other lean cut of beef
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and intensely: three minutes of cooking without oil is enough to create a surface capable of searing a rump steak in four minutes. The same pan then handles simmering pasta and melting cheese without anything sticking, right up until serving time.
steps: Thinly slice the shallots, bell pepper, and mushrooms into even strips. Mince the garlic. Remove the beef from the refrigerator, pat it dry with paper towels, and season with salt and pepper.
Place the empty pan over high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should be smoking slightly.

Place the steak in the pan and leave it undisturbed. Cook for approximately 4 minutes; it will release easily once a crust has formed. Flip the steak over, cook for another minute, then transfer it to a warm plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the vegetables and garlic to the still-hot pan, stir for 5 minutes to color them and loosen the beef juices.

Add the uncooked pasta, pour in enough stock to cover, and cover. Cook for 12 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring two or three times: the pasta should be tender and the liquid almost completely absorbed.
Meanwhile, whisk together the cottage cheese, mustard, honey and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Slice the rested steak into thin strips, across the grain.
Distribute the cheddar, mozzarella and beef strips over the pasta. Cover and cook over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheeses melt and the meat is heated through.
Remove from heat and stir in the cream cheese sauce. Mix well and serve in the pan.

title: Soft banana, coconut and chocolate cakes
intro: Without flour, these little cakes are held together only by the eggs and the banana: everything depends on a gentle and covered cooking, which replaces the oven.

ing.note: (It can withstand higher heat without burning)

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: the patties brown as if in a hot pan. The lid does the rest, trapping the steam and cooking the center without drying out the edges.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a bowl until you obtain a smooth puree without any lumps.
Add the eggs and mix until smooth.
Pour in the almond flour, coconut flour and sugar.
Mix until a thick paste forms that clings to the spoon.
Stir in the chocolate chips, roughly chopped if they are large.
Heat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush with clarified butter: it should simmer without smoking.

Drop small mounds of dough, well spaced apart, flatten them slightly, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 minutes: the surface will set, the edges will brown, and the pastry will release easily from the pan. Do not touch it before then.
Flip each patty with a flick of the wrist, cover again, and continue cooking for 4 minutes. Both sides should be golden brown and the patty puffed up. Transfer to a wire rack.

title: Pan-fried mashed potato salad
intro: A warm salad that hinges on one single point: the potato crust must be formed before they meet the sauce.

ing.note: plus the salt from the cooking water

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and intensely, enough to replace the oven for this recipe. The ridges created by mashing the potatoes absorb the heat directly and brown in minutes, while the center remains soft and creamy. There's only one rule: don't touch the potatoes while they're still sticking. They'll release on their own when the crust is ready. If you force them before then, you'll leave the crust in the pan.
steps: Place the whole, unpeeled potatoes in a large pot of boiling salted water. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, depending on their size: a knife should pierce them easily. Drain and let them cool for five minutes, allowing the steam to escape.
Place the potatoes on a board. Mash them one by one with the bottom of a glass or bowl, without mashing them completely. You're looking for an irregular, textured patty.
Sprinkle with smoked paprika, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.

Arrange the potatoes in a single layer, without crowding them. Do this in two batches if necessary. Let them brown for 7 to 8 minutes without touching them, until they release easily from the pan and the edges are golden. Turn them over and repeat on the other side.
Meanwhile, whisk together the plant-based yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, and dried dill in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the cucumber into half-moons, add it to the sauce along with the chopped onion and fresh herbs.
Remove the potatoes from the pan to stop the cooking process and stir them into the mixture while still hot. Mix with a spoon and serve immediately: the hot-cold contrast only lasts a few minutes.

title: Greek salad with marinated chicken and roasted chickpeas
intro: It's all about contrast: dry and crispy chickpeas, crispy seared chicken, and cold raw vegetables.
ing: High smoke point olive oil, or clarified butter
High smoke point olive oil for searing
titane: The pan handles both cooking processes without ever going through the sink. It goes in the oven to roast the chickpeas, returns to the stovetop, is wiped with a paper towel, and then receives the chicken. The juices left by the spices flavor the searing, and the rapid rise in temperature creates the crust.
steps: Combine the chicken strips, yogurt, oil, lemon juice, honey, paprika, and thyme in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper, and mix well by hand. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Preheat the oven to 210°C, conventional heat.
Rinse the chickpeas under cold water, then dry them thoroughly in a tea towel. Rub them between your palms to loosen the skins and remove them: this is what makes them crispy.
Pour them into the titanium pan with the fat, paprika, thyme and a pinch of salt. Stir to coat them with an even film.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven for 17 minutes, until the chickpeas are golden brown and sound dry when you shake the pan.
Meanwhile, cut the cherry tomatoes in half, slice the cucumber into half-moons, and crumble the feta by hand.
Whisk together the oil, lemon, vinegar and honey. Season with salt and pepper, taste: the vinaigrette should remain bold.
Remove the pan from the oven, transfer the chickpeas to a dish and let them cool in the open air, never covered.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper. Place it over high heat and let it heat up empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the fat.

Place the chicken strips loosely in the pan, in two batches if necessary. Reduce the heat to medium and leave them undisturbed: the meat will release itself once a crust has formed, after about 4 minutes. Turn them over and continue cooking for another 3 minutes, until cooked through.

To serve: arrange the chickpeas on the base, then the cucumber and tomatoes, the still-warm chicken strips, the feta cheese, and the olives. Drizzle with vinaigrette and sprinkle with chopped mint at the last minute.

title: Blonde lentils, roasted figs and grilled halloumi
intro: It all comes down to two crusts: the fig crust, which caramelizes on the flesh side, and the halloumi crust, which only forms if you don't touch anything.
titane: The same pan is used for both cooking methods without washing in between: first, the candied figs, covered (cooked gently in their own juices until soft), then the halloumi, seared quickly. In both cases, the rule is the same: never force it off. Once the crust has set, the food will release easily. Forcing it will tear off the golden surface and ruin the meltingly tender center.
steps: Place the lentils in a saucepan, cover with cold water (no salt added), and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes: they should be tender but not falling apart. Starting with cold water ensures even cooking from the center to the edges.
Meanwhile, cut the figs into quarters. Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add a drizzle of olive oil.

Place the wedges flesh-side down in the pan, season with salt, and let them brown undisturbed. When they begin to separate easily, cover, reduce the heat to low, and let them confit for 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Rinse the halloumi under cold water to remove the brine, dry it thoroughly, and cut it into cubes.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, preheat it again empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add a drizzle of olive oil. Sear the cubes for 3 to 4 minutes on one side, without moving them. As soon as they release easily, turn them over and cook for another 2 minutes.
Drain the lentils, rinse them in cold water to stop the cooking, and let them drain.
In a bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons of olive oil, the vinegar and honey until the mixture thickens slightly.

To serve: place mesclun salad on the bottom, then lentils, figs, still-warm halloumi, slivered almonds, and hand-torn basil. Season with salt and pepper, and drizzle with vinaigrette at the last minute.

title: Scrambled tofu wraps for the week
intro: It's all about patience: tofu that is left to stick before being stirred takes on a grilled taste that crumbling alone will never give.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when the cold mass of tofu is added. Preheat it empty, pour in the oil, then spread the tofu in an even layer and forget about it. It will stick at first, then release itself from the bottom once the surface is toasted. This spontaneous release is what allows you to stir, not the clock.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, tear the tofu by hand into irregular pieces about the size of a hazelnut. The jagged edges grill better than neat cubes.
Pour the oil into the hot pan, then spread the tofu in a single layer. Don't touch it until it resists the spatula.
As soon as it detaches on its own, stir it once and let it regain its color.
In a bowl, whisk together the cream, plant-based drink and all the flavorings: malted yeast, turmeric, garlic, pepper, kala namak.
Pour this mixture over the tofu. Let it reduce for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the yellow color is uniform and the liquid no longer coats the bottom.
Remove from heat and, if desired, stir in the vegan cheese and chopped chives. Transfer to a cold dish to stop the cooking process.
Let cool slightly, fill the galettes one by one, roll them up tightly and wrap them individually.
Keep refrigerated for up to three days. Toast the wrap in a dry pan for 2 minutes before eating: the wrap will regain its crispness.

title: Honey BBQ Chicken Burritos
intro: It all comes down to the chicken crust: it's what replaces the four hours in the slow cooker and gives the sauce its depth.
titane: One pan, two uses. First, sear the chicken at high temperature, empty and then with clarified butter, to develop its color. Then, once the burritos are rolled, use the same still-hot pan to crisp them on both sides. Don't wash it in between: the residual juices do the work for you.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the clarified butter: it should simmer without smoking.
Season the chicken pieces with garlic salt, pepper, and onion powder. Place them in the hot pan in a single layer, without overlapping.
Don't touch anything. The chicken will stick, then release on its own once a crust has formed. Turn it over and continue cooking until it's cooked through, 18 minutes total.
Remove the chicken (transfer it out of the pan) and drain off the released juices.
Shred the flesh with two forks (separate it into strands, along the direction of the fibers).
Return the shredded chicken to the pan over low heat. Add the barbecue sauce, honey, red onion, and green onion. Stir for 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the chicken evenly.
Fill each tortilla with rice, mozzarella cheese, and then barbecue chicken. Fold in the sides and roll tightly. You'll have 10 burritos.
Drizzle with reduced-fat barbecue sauce when serving, or reserve it separately for freezing.
For crispiness: put the burrito back in the still hot pan, high heat, 2 minutes per side until the tortilla is golden brown.

title: Ramen with leek and mushroom broth
intro: It all comes down to the colouring of the vegetables before the liquid arrives: it is this that gives the broth its depth, not the simmering time.

ing.note: beautiful specimen, white and soft green

titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the vegetables are added: the leek and mushrooms brown instead of releasing their water. The broth then develops in the same pan, uncovered, and reduces without a lid.
steps: Halve the leek lengthwise, rinse it between the leaves, then slice it thinly. Cut the mushrooms into thick slices.
Place the titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple on the surface without smoking.

Add the leek and mushrooms all at once. Don't touch anything for 2 minutes. The vegetables will separate on their own once they've browned: stir then and continue cooking for up to 5 minutes in total over high heat.

Season with salt, herbs, and curry powder. Stir for 30 seconds to release the spices, then add the water and coconut milk. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer uncovered for 12 minutes: the broth will reduce slightly and become more fragrant.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in a pot of boiling water according to the package directions. Drain them and transfer them to bowls.
Cut the tofu rosso into cubes or thick slices.
Pour the hot broth and vegetables over the noodles. Arrange the tofu on top and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

title: Peanut butter protein pancakes
intro: A thick pancake is due to an undermixed batter: lumps are a sign that the gluten hasn't worked.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then add the oil. The heat will rise steadily, creating an even golden crust, and the pancake will release easily from the pan. Wait until it releases before flipping: a flick of the wrist is all it takes, no need to use a spatula.
steps: Combine all the dry ingredients in a bowl: the three flours, vanilla protein, dried peanuts, yeast, salt, and stevia. Whisk dry to distribute the yeast.
In a separate bowl, whisk the peanut butter with the egg until smooth. Gradually whisk in the almond milk in two additions.
Pour half the liquid over the dry ingredients. Mix briefly with a spatula. Add the rest and stop as soon as the flour is absorbed: the dough should remain thick and uneven. Lumps are desirable.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of grapeseed oil and wipe off the excess with paper towels.

Pour a small ladleful of batter onto each pancake, without spreading it. Let it cook for about 1 minute without touching it. When bubbles burst on the surface and the pancake slides freely, flip it over.
Cook for another minute: the surface should be golden brown and firm to the touch. Remove from the oven (transfer to a plate) and continue baking.

title: Rustic zucchini and Beaufort cheese tart
intro: It all comes down to how the courgettes are cooked: if they are seared quickly and thoroughly, they retain their shape instead of making the pastry soggy.

ing.note: a green one and a yellow one
plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The oil will begin to shimmer, the vegetables will slide in, and the surface will sear them instead of letting them sweat. Don't stir immediately: the slices will stick, then release on their own once a crust has formed. This step is what gives the filling a tender, lightly browned texture, without any water at the bottom.
steps: Combine flour, butter, egg, and water in a bowl. Knead until you obtain a smooth, homogeneous ball, adding a pinch of flour if the dough sticks to your fingers. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Finely chop the onion. Slice the courgettes into thin rounds, using a knife or a mandoline.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil, which withstands high temperatures better than olive oil. Wait until it ripples.
Add the onion, courgettes, a pinch of salt and the thyme. Leave in place without touching: the vegetables should stick and then detach on their own.

Reduce the heat to medium-high and continue cooking for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is soft and lightly browned. If it starts to stick, add a tablespoon of water. Remove from the pan and transfer to a cold dish to stop the cooking process. Season with pepper.
Grate the Beaufort cheese.
Preheat the oven to 190°C, conventional heat and not fan-assisted.
Roll out the dough (spread it out with a rolling pin) on a sheet of baking paper, into a disc of about 30 cm.
Slide everything onto a baking sheet and prick the bottom with a fork.
Spread the crème fraîche, leaving 3 cm of bare pastry all around.
Spread two-thirds of the cheese, then the courgette-onion mixture, then the remaining cheese.
Fold the edges of the pastry over the filling, overlapping them with successive folds.
Bake in the lower part of the oven for 35 minutes. If the top is not brown enough, move the tray to the top of the oven for 3 to 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme when you take it out and serve warm.

title: Pumpkin, potato and Comté cheese patties
intro: It all comes down to the water: the more water you remove from the grated vegetables, the crispier the crust will be.
titane: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil or butter. The temperature will rise quickly and evenly: the galette will form a crust on contact. Then, leave it alone. It will release from the pan on its own when it's ready; that's your only signal to flip it.
steps: Peel the squash and potatoes. Grate them using the large holes of a grater into a bowl. The butternut squash is firm: hold it firmly and work with a firm pressure.
Gather the grated cheese in a clean tea towel. Twist and squeeze over the sink until no more cheese comes out. This step determines the texture.
Finely chop the parsley and chives.
In a bowl, mix together the drained grated cheese, eggs, flour, cornstarch, Comté cheese, and herbs. Season with salt and pepper. The mixture should hold together when you squeeze it in your hand.
Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour a layer of grapeseed oil or clarified butter. A few seconds is enough: the fat should coat the bottom and ripple slightly.
Form patties of about 60g each, flatten them to 1cm thick and place them in the pan without crowding them. Three or four at a time, no more.
Let it cook without touching it for about 4 minutes. When the galette detaches itself from the bottom, turn it over and brown the other side for 4 minutes.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a plate lined with paper towels. Prepare another batch, reheating the pan for 2 to 3 minutes if it has cooled down.
Mix together in a bowl the cottage cheese, salt, pepper, chives, a dash of lemon juice and the zest.
Serve the patties hot, with the sauce on the side.

title: Buffalo chicken rolls with cheese
intro: It all comes down to the color of the chicken: quickly seared and dry cubes, not steamed, otherwise the filling releases water and makes the tortilla soggy.

ing.note: (which can withstand high heat without burning)

titane: Empty pan, medium heat, two to three minutes. The titanium rises quickly and easily: the chicken cubes brown before they have a chance to release their juices. The same pan then receives the mixture off the heat and goes into the oven with the rolls. One single container, from start to finish.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, buffalo sauce, cream cheese, ranch seasoning, and pepper until smooth. If it's too thick to spread, thin it out with a tablespoon of water, and another if needed.
Cut the chicken into small, even cubes, about one centimeter in size. Season them with garlic salt and pepper, and mix by hand.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes. Add a drizzle of grapeseed oil or clarified butter.

Place the cubes in a single layer, without packing them down. Don't touch them. When they start to lift from the bottom, turn them over and continue cooking until they are nicely browned and cooked through. Do this in two batches if the pan is full.
Turn off the heat. Pour the creamy sauce over the still-warm chicken, add the mozzarella and chives, and stir in the pan. The cheese should melt from the residual heat, not from the flame.
Distribute the filling evenly over the ten tortillas, one-tenth per tortilla, in an off-center roll. Fold in the sides, then roll tightly, seam underneath.

Preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F). Arrange the rolls in the titanium pan, seam side down, or on a baking sheet. Spray with oil. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the surface is golden brown and crispy.

For storage: allow to cool completely, wrap each roll in aluminum foil, and freeze for up to three months. To reheat, cover with a damp paper towel, microwave for three to four minutes, then briefly in a very hot titanium pan to restore crispness.

title: Banana and oat pancakes
intro: A blended banana batter, without added sugar, whose success depends entirely on the temperature of the pan and patience before turning.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. As a result, the edges dry, the bottom browns, and nothing sticks. There's just one condition: don't touch the pancake until it releases easily from the spatula.
steps: Blend the banana, eggs, oats, whey protein, plant-based milk, and vanilla for about 3 minutes. The batter should be smooth, fluid, and free of oat lumps.
Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It is ready when a drop of water beads on the surface instead of evaporating immediately.
Pour the grease and spread it over the entire surface with absorbent paper.
Pour a small ladleful of batter per pancake, two at most, into the pan. Let it cook for 2 minutes without touching it: the edges will dry out, and bubbles will burst on the surface.
Slide the spatula over the pancake: if it releases easily, flip it over with a quick, firm motion. Otherwise, wait another 20 seconds.
Continue cooking for 2 minutes on the other side, until golden brown and firm to the touch. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining batches.

title: Chili cheese sauce emulsified with hard-boiled egg
intro: A mayonnaise made with hard-boiled egg, therefore more stable and less fatty, which is then thinned with a cheddar mixture bound with cornstarch: everything depends on the complete cooling of this mixture before mixing.
titane: The titanium pan, heated empty for two to three minutes, reaches a uniform temperature across its entire surface. Pour in the stock-cornstarch mixture: it thickens continuously, without any hot spots in the center, and therefore without lumps. A microwave is no longer necessary.
steps: Dissolve the cornflour in the cold stock (or almond milk) until completely dissolved. Set aside.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It should be hot but not smoking.
Pour in the liquid mixture and whisk continuously for 2 minutes. The mixture will thicken and coat the whisk.
Remove from heat. Add the cheddar and stir until completely melted. Stir in the cream cheese, finely chopped green chili, and salt.
Transfer (out of the cooking container) onto a metal tray in a thin layer. Place in the freezer for 15 minutes, until completely cooled.
Blend the hard-boiled eggs with the mustard and vinegar. Drizzle in the olive oil while the blender is running until you reach a smooth, creamy texture.
Combine the cold mixture and the emulsified base. Briefly blend or whisk until you obtain a smooth sauce. Adjust the salt.

title: Creamy mushroom sauce
intro: It all comes down to the water from the mushrooms: you have to let it come out, then let it go away, before adding cream.
titane: The pan, heated empty, heats up quickly and retains its heat when you add the onion: it browns with just one spoonful of oil, not three. After that, nothing changes. The mushrooms sweat in the same pan, the sauce simmers on top, and the sauce thickens on top. All done with one pan from start to finish.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple on the surface.
Meanwhile, finely slice the mushrooms. Chop the onion.
Place the onion and garlic in the hot pan. Don't touch anything. The onion will detach itself from the bottom when it's golden brown.
Add the mushrooms, cover and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat. They will release their water and lose two-thirds of their volume.
Season with salt, pepper, dried herbs and drizzle with soy sauce.
Moisten (add liquid during cooking) with the stock. Reduce to low-medium heat and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Pour the coconut milk over low heat, but it should not be boiling.
Dissolve the cornstarch in a tablespoon of cold water, stir it in, and cook for 2 minutes. The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.

title: Tablet of dates, peanuts and dark chocolate
intro: Everything hinges on the first layer: the dates must be firmly bonded together, otherwise the tablet will crumble when unmolded.
titane: The pan serves three purposes: a rigid base for crushing dates with a rolling pin, a container for melting chocolate over very low heat without a double boiler or oil, and finally, a mold that can be chilled as is. The titanium distributes heat evenly: the chocolate cools down without sticking, provided it is removed from the heat as soon as it is shiny.
steps: Remove the pits from the dates. Split them lengthwise and open them flat.
Line the bottom of the cold pan, off the heat, with baking paper. Bring the paper up slightly on the sides.
Arrange the opened dates in an even layer, edge to edge, without any gaps.
Roll over the date with firm pressure. The dates should fuse together (merge into a single continuous layer) and form a smooth base of approximately 5 mm.
Spread the peanut butter evenly over the top, right to the edges. Distribute the peanuts evenly and press them in lightly with your fingertips.

Remove the parchment paper from the pan and set it aside on a plate. Wipe the pan clean, break the chocolate into it, and place over very low heat. Stir continuously for about 3 minutes: turn off the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy; it will finish melting in the residual heat.
Return the parchment paper to the pan and coat (cover with a thin, even layer) with chocolate. Tilt the pan to spread it to the edges.
Leave to set in the refrigerator overnight, pan included, until completely set.
Remove from the mold by pulling on the paper, turn over onto a board and break into irregular pieces.

title: Peanut praline Easter eggs
intro: It's all about the contrast: a dense, still-icy core, a chocolate shell that sets in seconds on contact.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its mass heats up quickly, so use very low heat and short bursts of action: place the pan on the heat for thirty seconds, remove it, stir off the heat, and then place it back on the heat. The chocolate melts by thermal inertia, never exceeding the point where it would grain. The smooth, uncoated surface is non-stick, and you can easily scrape everything off with a spatula.
steps: In a bowl, combine the almond flour, peanut butter, and maple syrup. Work with a spatula, then by hand, until you have a smooth, sticky dough that holds together in a ball without crumbling.
Take portions of approximately 40g and shape them into eggs between your palms. Smooth the surface with your fingertips.
Arrange them on a baking sheet or plate lined with baking paper, without them touching each other.
Place the tray in the freezer for 10 minutes. The cold firms the center and accelerates the setting of the shell.

Meanwhile, place the chocolate and coconut oil in the titanium pan over very low heat. Cook for 5 minutes, removing the pan from the heat every 30 seconds and stirring. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Remove the pan from the heat and take the eggs out of the freezer. Roll them one by one in the chocolate using two forks, then let them drain for a few seconds over the pan.
Place them back on baking paper and immediately sprinkle with fleur de sel: the chocolate sets quickly on contact with the frozen center, you have five seconds per egg.
Keep refrigerated until serving. Remove them 10 minutes before serving; the texture will soften.

title: Chickpea curry with coconut milk and peanuts
intro: Everything hinges on the moment the spices meet the hot base: that's when the curry gains its depth, even before the liquid arrives.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding any oil or butter. The heat rises quickly and remains steady: the onion sweats without sticking, the spices toast on contact with the pan, and the juices deglaze with a simple flick of the spatula as soon as the water is added. The entire dish, including the saucepan, is prepared in this single pan.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat. Let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes: it should be hot but not smoking.
Pour in the oil, then the chopped onion. Sauté it for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. It will become translucent and detach easily from the bottom: that's the signal.
Add the curry powder, garam masala, herbs, salt and pepper, then the tomato purée. Stir for 1 minute over low heat. The spices should smell toasted, not burnt.
Stir in the peanut butter, add the water and deglaze (scrape the browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan with a spatula, stirring as you do so). The sauce will thicken on its own.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the carrots into thin rounds, then slide them into the sauce.
Cover and continue for 5 to 6 minutes, until the tip of a knife pierces the carrots without resistance.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the chickpeas and spinach. Mix.
Heat gently for 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts and is coated in sauce. Adjust the salt and serve.

title: Tofu balls in dumpling wraps
intro: It all comes down to the crust: the tofu balls must brown without moving, otherwise the dumpling sheet will have nothing to stick to.
titane: Sear the meatballs dry, then steam them under a lid in the same pan. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the fat, place the meatballs in the pan, and leave them undisturbed. When a crust has formed, they will release themselves from the bottom of the pan—that's the signal to move on to the next step. Add water afterward to deglaze the pan without disturbing the flavors.
steps: Crumble the tofu by hand into a bowl. Add the spring onion, grated carrot, flour or cornstarch, salt, and soy sauce. Mix until you have a homogeneous mixture that holds together between your fingers.
Shape into 12 even balls, about the size of a large walnut. Press them down firmly.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Pour in the oil. Arrange the balls, spacing them apart. Let them brown without touching them: they will detach themselves from the bottom when the crust has set. Turn them over to brown the other sides.
Press a dumpling sheet onto the top of each ball, pressing it against the sides.
Pour the water around the balls, not on top of them.
Cover immediately and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, until all the water has evaporated. The leaves will become translucent, while the underside will remain crispy.
While steaming, mix in the sweet soy sauce, vinegar, and chili flakes.
Remove from the pan and serve hot, with the sauce on the side.

title: Sweet potato and dark chocolate cookies
intro: Sweet potato puree replaces some of the sugar and eggs here: it provides the softness, provided it is roasted whole so that its water evaporates instead of being diluted in the batter.

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: With the lid closed and the heat low, the titanium pan radiates a gentle, enveloping warmth comparable to that of an oven, with the added benefit of direct contact that beautifully browns the bottom. Do not touch the cookies during the first bake. When the bottom is set, it will easily detach from the base—that's the signal to flip. Before this point, the dough is still too soft and will tear.
steps: Prick the sweet potato with a fork and roast it whole in the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 45 to 60 minutes. The flesh should be completely tender when pierced with the tip of a knife. This long cooking time is best done in the oven; a frying pan is not suitable for a whole vegetable.
Split the sweet potato lengthwise, scoop out 260g of flesh and mash or blend it until smooth. Let it cool slightly.

Combine the mashed potatoes, melted butter, almond butter, honey, vanilla, and salt in a large bowl. Mix well, then add the baking soda, baking powder, rolled oats, oat flour, and chocolate. Mix until a smooth dough forms.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight if possible. The cold hydrates the oats and tightens the dough: the cookies spread less and hold their shape better during baking.
Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Shape into flattened discs about 1.5 cm thick, calibrated to fit spaced apart at the bottom of the pan.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat, then brush it with a light coating of grapeseed oil. Wipe off the excess with a paper towel.
Place the cookies loosely in the pan, cover, and cook over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes. Do not touch them. The bottoms are ready when they easily pull away from the base and are golden brown.
Flip them over with a spatula, cover and continue for 5 to 7 minutes. They should be firm in the center and golden brown on both sides.
Remove them from the pan and place them on a wire rack. Sprinkle with a little sea salt and let them cool completely: the texture will set as it cools.

title: Potato and soy burritos with lime sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the potatoes: seared covered, they retain their crispness even after freezing and reheating.
ing: The juice of half a lime
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two minutes and instantly transfers that heat to the potato wedges. You get oven roasting without turning on the oven. And since the protein sauce then simmers in the same pan, it absorbs the juices left from the searing.
steps: Cover the soy protein with boiling water in a bowl. Let it soak for 10 minutes, then squeeze it between your hands to remove the excess water.
Cut the potatoes into small wedges, skin and all. Dry them in a tea towel.
Mix them with paprika, crushed pepper and a drizzle of grapeseed oil.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in a spoonful of oil and wait until it ripples.

Arrange the wedges in a single layer. Let them brown for 4 minutes without touching them; they will detach easily once a crust has formed. Turn them over, reduce the heat to medium, cover, and continue cooking for 14 minutes, stirring twice. Season with salt at the end of cooking. Transfer to a serving dish.
Return the pan to medium heat with the remaining oil. Sauté the sliced onion for 4 minutes, until translucent.
Add the herbs de Provence, ground pepper, and drained soy protein. Mix for 1 minute to allow them to absorb the juices.
Pour in the tomato sauce. Simmer for 10 minutes over medium-low heat, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon without running. Adjust the seasoning with salt.
For the cold sauce: whisk together the vegan skyr, ketchup, chili oil, and citrus juice. Taste and adjust the acidity.
Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds per side in the wiped pan: they will roll up without cracking.
Fill each tortilla with a ladleful of the soy mixture, a handful of potatoes and a drizzle of cold sauce. Leave 3 cm free around the edges.
Fold the sides towards the center, then roll firmly from bottom to top.
For storage: wrap each burrito in baking paper, then freeze. Reheat for 8 minutes in a covered pan over low heat, turning halfway through.

title: BBQ Chicken Quesadillas
intro: It's all about patience: neither the chicken nor the tortillas should be moved before they have come loose on their own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then oil it, and let it come into contact with the oil. The chicken and the tortilla will release easily once a crust has formed: that's the signal to flip, not before.
steps: Season the chicken breasts on both sides with garlic salt, pepper and onion powder. Massage to make it adhere.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple on the surface.

Sear the chicken without touching it until it's nicely browned, turn it over, and then continue cooking until it's cooked through. This should take about 12 minutes in total. The center should no longer be pink.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside on a cutting board. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then shred it (separate the meat into strands with a fork) or cut it into pieces.
Mix the chicken with the 120g of barbecue sauce, the honey, the red onion and the green onion. Taste and adjust the pepper.
Spread the filling over one half of each tortilla, cover with mozzarella, then fold into a half-moon shape.

Return the pan to medium heat. Place the quesadillas in the pan one at a time, without pressing them down. Let them separate on their own, then flip and brown the other side. Approximately 8 minutes for two quesadillas.
Cut into portions and serve with the lightened barbecue sauce on the side.

title: Textured tofu from freezing, pan-fried
intro: The cold does all the work here: the ice crystals hollow out the block of tofu, which becomes fibrous, spongy, and absorbs the marinade like a sponge.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The rapid and even heat distribution allows the tofu to form a crust in just a few minutes, without ever sticking. Once the pieces are in the pan, leave them alone: they will release on their own when the crust is ready.
steps: Freeze the entire block of tofu, either in its packaging or in an airtight container. Allow at least one night, ideally 24 hours.
Defrost it slowly in the refrigerator overnight. Alternatively, let it come to room temperature, or microwave it in 2-minute intervals.
Press the tofu for 1 hour under a weight (a plate weighted with a pan of water is sufficient), placed on a clean cloth. It will release the water left by the melting crystals and develop air pockets.
Cut it into cubes or slices about a centimeter thick.
Mix together the soy sauce, vinegar, and agave syrup. Immerse the tofu and let it marinate for 30 minutes, turning the pieces halfway through.
Drain the tofu on a rack. Reserve the marinade.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without oil.
Pour the grapeseed oil over the pan, then place the pieces in a loose layer. Let them cook without moving them for 4 to 5 minutes: they will release themselves when the top is golden brown.
Turn over, brown the second side for 4 to 5 minutes. Transfer to a warm plate and serve.

title: Breaded chicken burger, lacquered soy sauce
intro: It all comes down to the breading: it must be dry and golden before it comes into contact with the sauce, otherwise the panko absorbs it and collapses.

ing.note: one third of a whole egg
g, just enough to veil the flesh

ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter

ing.note: g, or the tip of a knife

titane: Heat the empty skillet over medium-high heat for two to three minutes, then pour in the fat. The breading will set instantly and form a crust that adheres. Don't touch anything while the chicken is still coated; it will release itself once one side is cooked. Then wipe the skillet clean and add the glaze; the cooking liquid will do the work for you.
steps: Bread the chicken using the English method (flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs): coat it in flour, dip it in the egg, press it into the panko. The coating should be even, without any bare patches.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the fat: it should simmer gently, never smoke.

Place the chicken in the pan and let it sit undisturbed for 5 minutes. Turn it over when it releases easily and continue for another 3 minutes. The breading should be golden brown and make a squeaking sound when you pinch it.
Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack. Wipe the pan with paper towels.
Medium heat. Pour in the water, soy sauce, stevia, then the cornstarch dissolved in a drop of cold water. Bring to a simmer for 3 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken to the pan, turn it twice in the sauce to glaze it (coat it with a shiny layer). One minute, no more.
Mix ketchup and mayonnaise, spread on both sides of the bread. Place the chicken on top, cover with cucumber slices, and close the sandwich.

title: Crispy tofu wrap
intro: It all comes down to the starch and patience: the crust forms on its own, provided you don't touch the pancake.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly. You can therefore sear the patty directly on it, without an oven or air fryer: the surface dries and crisps while the inside remains soft, in half the time.
steps: Crumble the tofu between your fingers into a bowl. Add the curry, soy sauce, neutral oil, cornstarch, and salt.
Work the mixture by hand until you obtain a homogeneous and sticky mass, without dry lumps. The starch should have disappeared visually.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly.
Place the mixture in the center and press it firmly with the back of a spatula to form a thin, even pancake. Press firmly: that's where the cohesion comes from.
Place over medium-high heat and cook for 7 minutes without touching it. The pancake is ready when it easily pulls away from the bottom of the pan.
Flip with a flick of the wrist and continue for 6 minutes, until the second side is golden and crispy.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking, garnish according to your taste and roll up like a wrap.

title: Fudge brownie, cooked in a pan
intro: It all comes down to the control of the fire: a long, gentle cooking under cover to keep the center half-cooked, then a brief burst uncovered to crust the top.
titane: The titanium pan replicates the grilling effect. After cooking covered, turn up the heat for two minutes uncovered: the surface will develop a crust while the inside remains soft and moist, without the oven. Always preheat the pan empty before adding the batter; otherwise, the bottom will stick and the underside will cook faster than the rest.
steps: Over low heat, melt the chocolate directly in the pan, stirring constantly. Remove from the heat as soon as it is smooth, then stir in the peanut butter.
With the mixture off the heat, loosen it (soften it with a liquid or a more pliable ingredient) with the cream cheese. Work until the mixture is perfectly smooth.
Add the eggs one at a time, then the dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, whey protein, powdered peanut butter, and stevia. Mix just until the batter is smooth. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Wipe the pan clean, then place it back on medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. When it starts to smoke slightly, brush it with grapeseed oil.
Pour the batter, smooth it over the entire surface, and cover.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 minutes covered. Do not try to loosen the dough: it will detach itself from the sides of the pan once it has set.

Remove the lid, turn up the heat, and cook for 2 minutes, no more. The surface will quickly form a crust on the titanium pan; the center should remain soft. Let it cool slightly in the pan before unmolding and slicing.

title: Five-layer Tex-Mex burritos, freezer ready
intro: Ten burritos built in a single session, with beef seared without fat and a pan finish that rivals the crispiness of an air oven.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and can withstand high heat: the 4% fat beef sticks at first, then releases itself once a crust has formed. Don't stir beforehand. The same rule applies at the end, for browning the burritos: place them in the pan, count them, and flip them when the surface starts to lift on its own.
steps: Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. A drop of water should sizzle and run.

Pour the ground beef into the pan, sprinkle with taco seasoning, and do not add any oil. Spread it in an even layer and let it set. The meat will stick at first: this is normal, it will separate on its own once the crust has formed.
After 4 to 5 minutes, start breaking up the meat with a spatula. Continue for another 5 minutes, until you have short, golden-brown pieces. The total cooking time should be 10 minutes.

Reduce the heat to low. Add the enchilada sauce and green chilies, then scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze (dissolve the caramelized bits with liquid). Let it cook for 2 minutes, until the mixture has reduced slightly. Remove from the pan and let it cool slightly.
Blend the yogurt, chipotle, adobo, lime juice, garlic salt, onion powder, and pepper in a blender until smooth and homogeneous. Refrigerate.

Layer the ingredients on each large tortilla, starting with the following in the center: meat, rice, refried beans, shredded cheddar cheese, and cheese sauce, then top with a dollop of Greek yogurt. Place a small tortilla on top of the filling; it absorbs moisture and prevents the burrito from getting soggy in the freezer.
Fold both sides inwards, then roll tightly starting from the nearest edge. Fold underneath.
Wrap each burrito in aluminum foil or a freezer bag. They will keep for 3 months.
To reheat: remove the foil, wrap the still-frozen burrito in a damp paper towel, and microwave for 4 to 5 minutes. Check that the center is hot.

Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Place the burrito in the skillet, either dry or with a drizzle of high-smoke oil. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, without moving it. It will release easily when ready. Serve with chipotle sauce.

title: Pan-fried potatoes with a white herb sauce
intro: It all comes down to two things: pieces of the same size and a pan that you let do the work on its own.
titane: The lid transforms the titanium pan into a heat chamber: hot air circulates around the pieces while the bottom sears them (browning them deeply on direct contact). You get a crisper crust than in the oven, provided you don't stir anything while the potatoes are still sticking. They release themselves once the top is cooked.
steps: Wash the potatoes and cut them into thick wedges, all the same size. A sharp knife prevents crushed edges, which burn before the rest.
Combine them in a bowl. Pour in the oil, then the paprika, herbes de Provence, salt, pepper, and cornstarch. Mix by hand until each piece has a dry, even coating.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Test: a drop of water should roll into a ball on the surface without evaporating immediately.
Place the wedges in a single layer, without packing them tightly. Cover. Leave for 10 minutes without intervening: the side in contact should color and detach on its own.

Turn over with a flick of the wrist, cover, and continue cooking for 15 minutes over medium heat, stirring only three or four times. The potatoes are ready when a knife tip pierces them easily and the outside still sounds crisp.
Meanwhile, whisk together the yogurt, vinegar, herbed salt, garlic powder, and pepper. Stir in the chives at the last minute to preserve their color.
Remove from heat and serve immediately, with the sauce on the side.

title: Gluten-free quiche with potato crust, leek and tofu
intro: It all comes down to the crust: well-dried potatoes, packed tightly, left alone until they detach themselves from the metal.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the pie dish. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, oil it, then shape the crust directly in it: it browns on contact with the metal without sticking. Pour the filling over it and finish covered or in the oven, without changing pans.
steps: Cook the potatoes in boiling salted water in a saucepan until a knife pierces them easily. Drain and let them air dry for 5 minutes: residual moisture is the enemy of a good crust.
Roughly mash them with a fork. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the olive oil and spread it evenly.
Spread the crushed potatoes over the entire surface. Press down with a spatula to obtain an even thickness, slightly up the sides.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Leave for 12 minutes without touching. The crust is ready when it easily detaches from the metal: shake the pan, it should slide off in one piece.

Meanwhile, whisk the plant-based milk with the cornstarch, then stir in the egg alternative and smoked paprika. Crumble the tofu and add it along with the sliced leek. Season to taste. This is the base (the liquid mixture that will thicken during cooking).
Pour the mixture over the crust and smooth the surface.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes over low heat. Or, for a more even set, place the pan in the oven at 180°C (350°F). The center should feel firm to the touch.
Let it rest for 5 minutes off the heat before cutting.

title: Rice brownie with two types of chocolate
intro: Cooked and blended rice replaces flour: it is what gives the dense and melting center, provided that it is blended long enough so that no grains remain.

ing.note: two mixed varieties (dark and milk, by

titane: Preheat the empty skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing it. The rapid heat of the titanium coating sears the surface of the batter on contact, forming the thin crust of the brownie. The lid does the rest: it reflects the heat back onto the top, replicating the effect of an oven, without a pan or parchment paper.
steps: Mix the cooked rice with the eggs, sugar and hazelnut powder. Continue until you obtain a smooth paste, with no visible grains under the spatula.
Melt the 170g of chocolate in a bain-marie or in the microwave, in short bursts, stirring between each.
Pour the melted chocolate over the rice dough and mix until the color is uniform.
Preheat the empty pan over low-medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush the bottom and sides with a thin layer of clarified butter or grapeseed oil.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and spread it with a spatula to an even thickness.
Distribute the chocolate pieces over the surface, without pressing them in.
Cover and cook for 18 minutes over low heat. The brownie is ready when a matte crust has formed on top and the edges begin to shrink.
Remove from the heat and let it cool slightly in the pan before unmolding. The inside remains soft and moist, but it holds its shape better once it has cooled.

title: Noodles with seared beef and chili crisp sauce
intro: It all comes down to the beef crust: the chili crisp oil that coats the meat is enough to sear it, provided the pan is already scorching hot.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold meat is added: the crust forms immediately, without any added fat. Do not touch the pieces while they are still sticking. When they release easily, the side is done. The same pan can then be used to coat the pasta, off the heat, without washing it.
steps: Cut the beef into pieces of a uniform size, about 3 cm. Uniformity is key to cooking.
Mix the meat with the garlic salt, pepper and 15g of chili crisp oil. Each piece should be coated: this is the only fat used for searing.
Blend the cottage cheese, 25g of chili crisp oil, garlic, garlic salt and skimmed milk until smooth and spreadable. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta according to the package directions, about 10 minutes. Drain, reserving a glass of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat.

Sear the beef in a single layer, in two or three batches depending on the size of the pan. Allow 8 minutes total. Turn only when the pieces easily pull away from the pan and have a golden crust. Remove from the pan and set aside, covered.
Remove from heat, add the drained pasta to the still-hot pan, stir until completely coated. Thin with a little pasta water if the sauce thickens.
Arrange the beef on a plate, and sprinkle with finely chopped green onions.

title: Soufflé pancake with Comté cheese and mushrooms
intro: Everything hinges on the hot pan: the appliance must hear the metal before even entering the oven, otherwise it rises softly and falls back down.

ing.note: (It can withstand high temperatures) or oil

titane: Bare titanium has no temperature limitations: the pan preheats empty, goes in the oven at 210°C, and gives the pancake caramelized edges through direct contact. Once the pancake is served, it can be used to cook the mushrooms without washing. A single utensil, from the first egg to the plate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 210°C (conventional setting). Leave the pan aside, empty.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Grease it with clarified butter or grapeseed oil, then slide it into the hot oven.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Gradually add the flour while whisking continuously until you obtain a smooth mixture. Stir in the grated Comté cheese.

Remove the hot pan with a thick oven mitt: the handle gets just as hot as the rest of the pan. Pour in the mixture all at once and immediately place it in the middle of the oven for 22 minutes. Do not open the door before the 15th minute, or the soufflé will collapse.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic. Clean the mushrooms with a dry cloth and slice them.
Remove the pancake from the pan and place it on a board, or serve it immediately. Rinse the pan, dry it, and return it to medium-high heat with the olive oil and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Do not touch anything for 7 to 8 minutes: they will detach themselves from the titanium once they have released and evaporated their water.
Spread the mushrooms over the pancake, sprinkle with chives and serve in the pan immediately.

title: Pan-fried almond-maple cookies
intro: Two ingredients, no oven: it all comes down to the gentleness of the fire and patience under a lid.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty, then kept on low heat and covered, it diffuses an even heat that cooks the cookies from below without burning them. No fat, no parchment paper: when the dough is cooked, it releases itself from the metal. As long as a cookie resists the spatula, it's not ready.
steps: Mix the almond flour and maple syrup with a fork until you obtain a smooth, sticky dough with no dry lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Shape ten equal-sized balls between your palms. If the dough is too sticky, lightly dampen your hands.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. The base should be warm and even, never smoking.
Place the balls in the dry pan, spacing them apart, then flatten them with a fork to form discs about 1 cm thick.
Cover and cook for 12 to 14 minutes over low heat, without turning. The edges will firm up, and the bottom will turn golden.
Check if they are cooked by sliding a spatula under a biscuit: if it comes away easily, remove them all and let them cool on a wire rack. They will finish hardening as they cool.

intro:
# Chocolate and Silken Tofu Cake

```markdown
---
title: "Chocolate and Silken Tofu Cake"
servings: 8
prep_time_min: 60
cook_time_min: 35
theme_candidates:

- pan-fried pastries

- chef's daily life
needs_review: true
---

Silken tofu replaces eggs and butter: it provides moisture and binds the mixture, provided it is blended long enough to remove all lumps.

ing.note: grape seeds), plus a little for the pan

titane: The titanium pan goes from countertop to oven without temperature limitations. It becomes the baking pan: you mix, you pour, you bake, all in the same container. No batter transfer, no coating that degrades under dry heat, and clean release if the base has been oiled.
steps: Preheat the oven to the temperature indicated on the preparation package, usually 180°C.
Mix the dry ingredients, 350g of silken tofu and the oil. Continue mixing until the paste is perfectly smooth: the tofu should disappear, with no visible grains on the sides of the bowl.
Lightly oil the bottom and sides of the titanium pan. Pour the batter into it and smooth the surface with a spatula.
Bake the pan uncovered, without a lid, for about 35 minutes. The cake is cooked when the top is firm and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove the pan from the oven and let it cool completely, including the pan. A cake that is still warm will cause the glaze to run.
Blend the remaining 50g of silken tofu with the melted dark chocolate until you obtain a smooth and glossy cream.
Remove the cooled cake from the mold, then spread the icing on top with an offset spatula.

title: Minced chicken steaks, sun-dried tomatoes and parmesan
intro: A minced poultry steak remains tender on one condition: mince two different pieces yourself, the fillet for firmness, the thigh for fat.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The temperature rises quickly: the surface of the steak sears immediately and forms a crust that seals in the juices. Then, don't touch it. The steak will stick, then release on its own once it's browned. It's this spontaneous release that tells you to flip it, not the clock.
steps: Cut both meats into large cubes, then chop them with a knife or meat grinder. Aim for a coarse mince texture, not a purée: the pieces should still be visible.
Grate the onion over the salad bowl to collect the juice. Dice the tomato petals into very small cubes.
Combine the meat, onion, tomatoes, parmesan, parsley and egg white. Season with salt and pepper, and mix by hand until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Divide into 5 equal parts. Shape each part in a pastry ring, pressing lightly, to obtain a uniform thickness of about 2 cm.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the oil and wait until it spreads into a thin film.
Place the steaks loosely on the grill. Reduce the heat to medium and cook undisturbed until they begin to separate from the bone. Turn them over once and cook until tender, about 10 minutes total.
Remove from the pan and place on a rack or plate and let rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Pan-fried red lentil bread
intro: Gluten-free and oven-free: it's all about soaking the lentils and using a lid that retains moisture while the crust forms.

ing.note: soaked for a minimum of 4 hours

titane: The titanium pan, preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, maintains a high and consistent temperature. Covered, it acts like a small dome: the heat envelops the dough balls, the base browns, and the interior cooks with its own moisture. Add the oil after preheating, never before.
steps: Cover the lentils generously with cold water and let them soak for 4 hours, or overnight. Drain and rinse them.
Blend the lentils with 150ml of water, olive oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder and herbs. Push until you have a perfectly smooth paste, with no grains remaining under the spatula.
Incorporate the psyllium and baking powder. Mix thoroughly: the dough thickens in one minute and pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then shape into 6 balls. Flatten them slightly, to about 2 cm: they will cook more evenly under the lid.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly.

Place the dough balls spaced apart, reduce the heat to low-medium, and cover. Do not touch them while they are still sticking: they will detach on their own when the crust has set, after about 12 minutes.
Turn over, cover again and continue for 12 to 13 minutes. The loaves are golden brown and firm; a knife inserted into the center should come out dry.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto a rack and let cool for 10 minutes before cutting, allowing the crumb to stabilize.

title: Potato and sweet potato gratin with beef
intro: It all comes down to searing the beef: a good crust at the start, and the subsequent simmering has flavor instead of water.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The pan heats up quickly and intensely: the ground meat browns instead of boiling. Then it simmers, covered, and is placed directly under the broiler to melt the cheese. One pan, three cooking stages, no transferring required.
steps: Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the fat: it should spread out without smoking immediately.

Season the mince with salt and spices, spread it in the pan in an even layer. Don't touch it. It will release on its own when a crust has formed: then turn it over in large pieces, then remove it from the pan and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Sauté the onion and pepper in the pan juices until translucent. Scrape the bottom of the pan to loosen any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and let them brown for 4 to 5 minutes without stirring too much. Then add the sweet potato, which is more delicate.
Moisten with hot stock, being careful not to drown the vegetables. Cover, simmer over low heat for 20 minutes. A knife tip should pierce a stock cube easily.

Return the meat to the pan, stir, and adjust the salt. Distribute the mozzarella evenly. Cover for 5 minutes to melt it, or place the pan under a hot broiler for 3 to 4 minutes for a golden, uneven surface.

title: Sweet potato breaded mozzarella sticks
intro: The key to success lies in the core temperature: a very cold mozzarella melts at the precise moment when the sweet potato crust finishes browning.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop

titane: Titanium heats up in two to three minutes and releases that heat instantly: a crust forms as quickly as when deep-frying, with just a trickle of oil instead of a deep bath. Don't touch anything while the stick is still attached. When the crust has set, it will detach easily under the spatula. That's the only reliable indicator.
steps: Wash the sweet potatoes, pierce them with a fork and cook them whole, skin included, until a knife pierces them without resistance, about 55 minutes.
Split them open, scoop out the flesh with a spoon, mash it finely, and let it cool completely. Refrigerating overnight results in a much firmer paste; at least 30 minutes. Then weigh out 350g.
Cut the block of mozzarella into 12 even sticks and place them in the freezer while preparing the dough, about thirty minutes.

In a large bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, cheddar cheese, flour, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika. Mix until you have a firm dough that no longer sticks to your fingers. Add a spoonful of flour if it's still too soft.
Divide the dough into 12 equal parts.

On a floured surface, flatten each portion into an oval. Place a mozzarella stick in the center, fold the dough around it, and pinch the edges to seal. Roll under the palm of your hand to smooth: no cracks should remain, or the cheese will escape during baking.
Arrange the sticks on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and place them in the freezer for 15 minutes, until they are firm to the touch.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and tilt the pan to spread it evenly over the surface.

Place the sticks on the griddle, leaving a finger's width between each one. Cook in two batches rather than one. Reduce the heat to medium and let them sear without moving them: they will release from the metal on their own once a crust has formed. Then turn them over, one side at a time, for about 12 minutes in total.
Reduce heat to low and cover for 2 to 3 minutes if the center is not yet soft. The steam will finish melting without causing further browning.
Remove (transfer from the pan to stop the cooking) onto a wire rack, let rest for a minute and serve hot.

title: Pan-fried chia pita
intro: Everything depends on the settling of the gel: if it's too runny, the pita will tear when turned over.
titane: The pan, heated to a high temperature even when empty, sears the chia gel on contact, forming a golden crust where a cold base would have stuck. Wait for the disc to release on its own: it's the disc that gives the signal, not the timer.
steps: Combine the chia seeds, hot water, and herbed salt in a bowl. Whisk for about 20 seconds to prevent the seeds from clumping at the bottom.
Let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature. The mixture should gel (thicken by absorbing water) until it forms a soft and homogeneous mass that clings to the spoon without running.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly over the surface with a paper towel. The oil should ripple, not smoke.
Place half of the gel in the center and spread it into an even disc about 5 mm thick. Cover, reduce the heat to medium-low and leave for 10 minutes without touching it.
Check: the pita should release easily when you shake the pan, with a golden brown bottom. Flip it over with a quick, firm motion, cover, and cook for another 10 minutes.
Remove from the pan and set aside, then repeat with the remaining gel. Open each pita pocket with a knife along the edge, following the length.

title: French toast burger, caramelized banana
intro: It all comes down to the crust: a loaf of bread that is well soaked but not drowned, placed in a pan that is already hot, browning on one side only before it is touched.
ing: Whey protein, dulce de leche flavor
titane: Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for two to three minutes, then grease it. The bread placed on top will stick at first, that's normal. Wait: when a crust forms, it will release on its own. The same principle applies to the bananas, which then cook in the juices of the French toast.
steps: Beat the egg with half the almond milk, the cinnamon and the salt.
Dip each side of the two bread halves into the mixture. Let them soak for a few seconds, no more: the crumb must remain firm.
Heat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the fat. It should simmer gently without smoking.
Place the rolls cut-side down. Let them brown for 5 minutes without moving them. Turn them over when they release easily, then brown the other side. Transfer them to a wire rack and set aside.
Whisk the cottage cheese with the whey and peanut powder.
Thin with the remaining almond milk, poured little by little, until you reach a coating cream consistency.
Slice the banana into thick rounds, about 1 cm.
Return the still-hot pan to the heat, arrange the slices flat. Let them caramelize for 5 minutes, without moving them, then turn them over once.
Hull the strawberries and cut them in half.
Cover the base of the French toast with a layer of cream, arrange the bananas, and close with the top.
Serve the strawberries on the side, with the remaining cream in a bowl for dipping the burger.

title: Rustic mushroom and Comté cheese tart
intro: It all comes down to the mushrooms: they must be coloured and soft before touching the pastry, otherwise their water will make the base soggy.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the mushrooms are added in large quantities. As a result, they sear instead of boiling in their own juices. Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, then pour in the oil. A drop of water thrown onto it should sizzle and slide off.
steps: Combine the flour, diced butter, egg, salt, and water in a bowl. Work the mixture until a smooth ball forms, but do not overwork it once it is homogeneous.
Wrap the ball in film and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Clean the mushrooms, remove the earthy end of the stem, slice them into even strips.
Place the empty pan over high heat. Wait 2 to 3 minutes, until it is thoroughly hot.

Pour in the oil, then add the mushrooms all at once along with a pinch of salt. Don't touch them: wait until they start to detach from the bottom of the pan, a sign that they've browned. Stir and continue cooking until all the water has evaporated and the mushrooms are soft, about 10 minutes. Season with pepper, then transfer to another container to stop the cooking process.
Preheat the oven to 190°C in static mode, bottom and top heating.
Roll out the dough (spread it out with a rolling pin) directly onto a sheet of baking paper, into a disc of about 30 cm. Slide it with its paper onto the baking tray.
Spread the mustard in the centre, leaving a 3-4 cm border.
Grate the Comté cheese. Spread two-thirds of it over the mustard.
Cover with the mushrooms, then with the remaining Comté cheese.
Fold the pastry edge over the filling, forming regular folds all around.
Place in the bottom of the oven for 30 to 35 minutes: the base should be cooked and the folds golden brown.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme leaves when you take it out of the oven, let it cool for 5 minutes before cutting.

title: Textured soy köfte
intro: It all comes down to seasoning the soybeans during rehydration: if they cook in plain water, no amount of added spice will make up for the blandness.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the köfte arrive. The result: a dry, golden crust with just a drizzle of oil, whereas the classic recipe calls for deep-frying. Don't touch anything until the köfte sticks. When it releases easily from the spatula, the crust is ready.
steps: Combine the soy protein, water, salt, and soy sauce in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Simmer uncovered until all the liquid is absorbed, stirring occasionally. The soybeans should be soft, never soggy.
Place the soybeans in the blender bowl along with the cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, tomato paste, and onion. Pulse only 3 to 4 times: the texture remains coarse, which is what gives it a bite.
Transfer the mixture from its cooking container to a bowl. Stir in the flour and parsley, working until you obtain a dough that holds its shape between your fingers.
Shape the köfte into elongated shapes, all of the same size. Irregularity will be affected during cooking.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Pour the oil, then place the köfte on top, leaving space between them. Do not move them. They are ready to be turned over when they detach easily.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist, continue until golden color on all sides.
Serve hot, with tzatziki.

title: Rice and chocolate brownie, cooked in a pan
intro: Cooked rice takes the place of flour: it absorbs the cocoa butter and gives a dense, moist, gluten-free crumb, provided it is cooked very gently and covered.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty and then kept on very low heat under a lid, it distributes heat evenly without hot spots, cooking the cake from the bottom and with the trapped steam. The indicator is visual: when the edge shrinks and detaches itself from the pan, the center is cooked.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and almond flour until the mixture is smooth and homogeneous.
Melt the chocolate in a double boiler or in the microwave in 20-second intervals. Let it cool for a minute before using.
Pour the melted chocolate over the egg mixture, stir, then fold in the cooked rice. Use a spatula to gently mix until the grains are completely coated.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush the bottom with clarified butter or oil.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan, smooth the surface, and sprinkle with crushed hazelnuts.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 20 to 25 minutes. The brownie is ready when the center no longer jiggles and the edge pulls away from the sides.
Let it cool in the pan before unmolding and cutting into slices. When warm, the cut is mushy; when cold, it's clean.

title: Crispy chicken in double breading
intro: A frying crust obtained with two tablespoons of oil: it's all about the hot pan and patience before turning.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for two to three minutes before adding the oil. The metal heats up quickly and evenly: the breading seals on contact and doesn't stick. Then, don't touch anything. The chicken will release itself from the bottom once the crust has formed; if you force it before then, you'll leave the breading in the pan.
steps: Cut the thigh into even pieces about the size of a generous bite. Add salt.

Prepare two mixing bowls. In the first, combine the 40g of flour and the spices. In the second, mix the remaining 20g of flour with cold water until you obtain a smooth batter with the consistency of heavy cream.

Coat each piece in the seasoned flour, then in the batter, then back in the seasoned flour. Press the coating between your fingers to make it adhere and let it rest for five minutes: it will stick better during cooking.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for two to three minutes.
Pour in the grapeseed oil and tilt the pan to spread it evenly over the bottom.
Place the pieces without overlapping them. Let them set for five minutes without touching them.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist as soon as they detach on their own and the surface is golden. Allow five more minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium, cover, and cook for five minutes. The steam will finish cooking the center while the crust retains its shape. Uncover for thirty seconds before removing from the pan to allow excess moisture to escape.

title: Creamy polenta with Comté cheese, sautéed mushrooms and a soft-boiled egg
intro: It all comes down to two textures: truly golden mushrooms, never boiled in their water, and a polenta soft enough to coat the back of the spoon.

ing.note: divided between cooking the eggs and cooking

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding the oil. The rapid temperature rise of the titanium sears the surface of the mushrooms on contact: the water evaporates instead of accumulating. Once in place, do not touch them. They adhere, then detach on their own once a crust has formed. That's the signal, not the clock.
steps: Mince the garlic. Slice the brown mushrooms into thick strips, tear the oyster mushrooms by hand into large pieces.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently and run across the bottom.

Add the mushrooms and garlic all at once, season with salt, and reduce the heat to medium-high. Let them cook for 8 to 10 minutes. Stir only once, when they pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own and the edges are amber-colored.
Remove the mushrooms from the pan and place them in a bowl, cover, and keep warm.

Bring a small saucepan of water, less than 500 ml, to a boil. Add the eggs and cook for exactly 6 minutes 30 seconds. Cool them under cold running water, then peel them (remove the shell) carefully: the yolk will remain runny.
Empty the saucepan, pour in 650 to 700 ml of water along with the stock cube. Bring to a simmer.

Pour the polenta in a steady stream (using one hand to avoid lumps) while whisking. Reduce the heat to medium-low and whisk for 3 to 5 minutes. If the mixture thickens, thin it with a little stock, water, or milk.
Remove from heat and stir in the grated Comté cheese. Mix until the polenta is smooth and coats the back of a spoon.
Divide the mixture between two bowls. Top with the mushrooms, halved eggs, and thyme leaves. Season with pepper and adjust the salt to taste.

title: Tomato and courgette crumble with Comté cheese
intro: Everything hinges on searing the vegetables before baking: without it, the savory crumble turns into a soggy mush.

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for two to three minutes over medium-high heat. The vegetables will brown instead of releasing their water. Since the pan is oven-safe, you can bake, garnish, and brown the vegetables all in the same pan: no transferring, no gratin dish to wash.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), conventional setting.
Cut the tomatoes and courgette into even, bite-sized pieces.

Pour the oil into the hot pan. Add the vegetables, crushed garlic, salt, and thyme. Increase the heat and sear for 5 minutes without stirring: the pieces will pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own when they are browned.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 10 minutes. The vegetables will finish releasing their water while you prepare the crumble.
Grate the Comté cheese.

In a bowl, combine the flour, flaked almonds, softened butter, a pinch of salt, and the Comté cheese. Rub the mixture between your palms until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Stop mixing: overworking the dough will make it lose its crispness.
Take out the pan and spread the crumble over the vegetables, without packing it down.
Return to the oven for 30 minutes, until the surface is thoroughly golden.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme and serve in the pan, after resting for 5 minutes.

title: Crispy iced tacos, protein cookie cream
intro: It all comes down to two textures: a really dry tortilla shell, and ice cream firm enough to stay inside without running.
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for two to three minutes over medium heat, then oil it. The batter, very thin and with little oil, will immediately set and form a crust: it will release itself from the surface. As long as it sticks, it's not ready—don't try to loosen it with a spatula, or you'll tear it.
