steps: In a bowl, dissolve the protein powder in the condensed milk. Whisk until no lumps remain.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Gently fold them into the mixture in three stages, using a spatula and lifting the mixture from the bottom up (this helps retain trapped air).
Pour into a rectangular metal dish, preferably with thin walls: the cold will penetrate faster. Freeze for at least 2 hours, until completely frozen.
Meanwhile, combine the flour and cottage cheese. Work by hand until you obtain a smooth dough that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Divide it into two portions. Roll each out into a very thin disc between two sheets of baking paper.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the oil: it should ripple, not smoke.
Place one disc on the baking sheet. Let it cook undisturbed. As soon as it releases easily, flip it over and brown the other side. Repeat for the second disc.
While still soft and warm, fold the tortillas into aluminum molds to set the taco shape.
Bake at 150°C for 10 to 12 minutes, until the shells are dry and brittle. Let cool in the molds.
Fill each shell with 60g of ice cream scooped with a spoon. Serve immediately.

title: Lightened-up mayonnaise with caramelized onions
intro: A cold sauce that maintains its texture with little oil: it is the onion compote, slowly caramelized, that provides the apparent fat and depth.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat: the onions brown without sticking, and the creamy compote detaches with a single pass of the spatula. No need to scrape.
steps: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil, then add the sliced and salted onions.
Let it caramelize over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The strips will take on a deep golden color and detach easily from the bottom.
Pour the light cream directly over the onions. Continue cooking over low heat for 5 minutes, until the mixture coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the pan and spread the compote onto a cold plate. Place in the freezer for 10 minutes: it must be thoroughly chilled before proceeding.

Blend the hard-boiled eggs with the mustard and vinegar. Then, with the blender running, slowly drizzle in the 50g of oil to emulsify the mixture (incorporate the fat until thickened). The texture will become creamy and glossy.
Add the cooled compote and blend for another 30 seconds until smooth. Taste before adding more salt: the onions are already seasoned.

title: Egg-free coconut kayak
intro: A coconut spread that gets its texture from silken tofu and a little starch: it's all about thickening, which needs to be monitored with a spatula.
titane: The volume remains under 500 ml: the titanium pan replaces the saucepan and works flat, therefore faster. The heat is distributed evenly without hot spots, preventing cornstarch lumps. Start with a cold pan, without any oil or butter, and continuously scrape the bottom with a flexible spatula—the smooth surface ensures thorough scraping, nothing sticks.
steps: Pour the coconut cream and sugar into the cold pan. Heat over medium heat, stirring, for about 5 minutes, until the sugar is completely dissolved: the mixture should no longer squeak under the spatula.
Meanwhile, blend the silken tofu with the cornstarch and salt until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream, without any lumps.
Pour this mixture into the pan, over the coconut-sugar base. Mix with a spatula until everything is homogeneous.

Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring regularly and scraping the bottom of the pan. The mixture is ready when it has the consistency of thick jam and a spatula leaves a clean trail on the bottom of the pan.
Remove from heat and transfer to a clean container, then cover and let cool. The texture will thicken further as it cools. It will keep for 10 days in the refrigerator.

title: Creamy curry with pea protein and cashew nuts
intro: It all comes down to the aromatic base: onion, garlic and ginger must color thoroughly before the liquids are added, otherwise the sauce remains flat.

ing.note: or grapeseed oil for a seizure
failing that, the same quantity of ground curry

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty, then let the aromatic toppings sit undisturbed: they will detach on their own once a crust has formed. Next, deglaze (dissolve the browned bits stuck to the bottom with liquid) with tomato and coconut milk, blend with an immersion blender in the same pan, and you won't need to use a second utensil.
steps: Cover the pea protein with very hot water and let it soak for 10 minutes, until completely absorbed. Drain, then squeeze between your hands to remove any remaining water: waterlogged protein will dilute the sauce.
Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any fat.

Add the margarine, then the aromatic garnish in a single layer. Leave for 5 minutes without stirring: the pieces will separate on their own when golden brown. Then stir briefly; the onion should be translucent.
Stir in the curry and tomato paste, season with salt and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes over medium heat, until the spices release their aroma and the paste darkens slightly.
Pour in the tomato sauce, coconut milk and cashews. Scrape the bottom to loosen any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Blend with an immersion blender directly in the pan until smooth, about 2 minutes. The cashews should have completely dissolved in the sauce.
Add the drained pea protein, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 8 minutes. The sauce should coat the back of the pan (enough to form a thin, firm layer).
Serve with basmati rice or naan bread. Finish with a drizzle of coconut milk, cashew pieces, and chopped coriander.

title: Roasted carrots with za'atar, hummus and pistachios
intro: It all comes down to the cut side of the carrots: a thorough caramelization obtained dry, then a lid to finish the center without drying anything out.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The titanium surface heats up evenly and sears the cut side of the carrots in just a few minutes. The lid then takes over: the steam released by the vegetables cooks the inside while the browned side remains intact. No oven is needed.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the carrots and halve them lengthwise. Keep the thickness consistent from one half to the other: this ensures even cooking.

Pour the olive oil into the hot pan. Arrange the carrots cut-side down, add the honey and za'atar, and season with salt. Let them sear for 5 minutes without moving them. They will release easily when caramelized.
Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 17 minutes, turning once halfway through. A knife should pierce the carrots easily. Add a few minutes if your carrots are thick.
While cooking, roughly chop the pistachios and finely chop the parsley and mint.

Spread the hummus in a thick layer on a serving plate, make a slight indentation in it with the back of a spoon. Place the still-warm carrots on top, sprinkle with pistachios and herbs, and season with pepper.

title: Dark chocolate squares with dried fruit
intro: It all comes down to heat: the chocolate must soften, never melt.
titane: The titanium pan is a great alternative to a conventional oven. Over very low heat, it distributes even heat from the bottom, without any hot spots: the chocolate softens from below while the surface remains matte. You can see the process in real time, something an oven simply can't do.
steps: Break the tablet into squares. Arrange them flat in the cold pan, off the heat, without overlapping them.
Roughly chop the dried fruit. Distribute it over the squares, pressing lightly.
Place the pan over very low heat. Count 5 minutes. The chocolate is ready when the edges are shiny and yield to the touch: the edges of the squares should still be visible.
Remove from heat. Press each square with your fingertips to embed the dried fruit and slightly widen the disc. Add a pinch of fleur de sel if using.
Transfer the mixture from the pan to a sheet of parchment paper using a thin spatula. Let it set for 20 minutes in the refrigerator, then store at room temperature in an airtight container.

title: Chocolate date balls
intro: Everything hinges on the texture of the date paste: compact, smooth, never grainy.
titane: One pan for both heatings. Boiling water softens the dates off the high heat, then, with the pan wiped dry, melts the chocolate over very low heat. The titanium melts quickly: keep it on the lowest setting, stir continuously, and stop as soon as the surface becomes shiny, well before it starts to simmer.
steps: Place the pan over low heat, pour in the boiling water and add the dates. Turn off the heat and let them soften for 5 minutes.
Remove the dates from the pan (to stop the heat) using a slotted spoon. Reserve two tablespoons of the soaking water.
Mash the dates with a fork until you obtain a compact, caramel-like paste. If it remains grainy, incorporate the soaking water in small amounts.
Shape into balls the size of a walnut. Place them on a sheet of baking paper.
Wipe the pan clean. Return it to very low heat, add the chopped chocolate and coconut oil. Stir continuously for 3 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Remove from heat, roll the balls one by one in the chocolate directly in the pan, then place them back on the paper.
Sprinkle with grated coconut while the coating is still soft.
Place in the freezer for 10 minutes, until the chocolate sets.

title: Oat tiramisu, vegan skyr cream
intro: It all comes down to cooking covered over low heat: the base must remain soft in the center, just golden underneath, otherwise the coffee won't penetrate.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding any oil or butter. With the lid on, the heat circulates and cooks the cake like an oven, while allowing the surface in contact with the pan to brown (Maillard reaction, the browning that contributes to the flavor). To flip, wait until the cake moves on its own when you shake the pan. If it resists, leave it for another minute.
steps: Blend the banana, plant-based milk, oats, and chia seeds in a blender until smooth, with no oat lumps. Let it rest for 5 minutes: the chia seeds will thicken the mixture.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the fat and spread it with a brush or paper towel. It should simmer gently, never smoke.
Pour the mixture into the pan, smooth the surface, and cover. Reduce the heat to low and cook for about fifteen minutes.
Shake the pan: as soon as the disc slides off in one piece, flip it over with a flick of the wrist. Continue cooking, covered, for 5 minutes. The center should feel firm to the touch.
Meanwhile, whisk the plant-based skyr with the light brown sugar until it is smooth and glossy.
Remove the cake from the pan and place it on a wire rack to cool completely. If it's still warm, it will tear.
Place the disc in a dish. Soak it with espresso coffee in several stages, allowing the liquid to soak in between each soaking.
Cover with the skyr cream, smooth with a spatula. Cover with cling film and refrigerate overnight.
When ready to serve, sprinkle with cocoa using a fine sieve.

title: Pots of dulce de leche cream, pan-fried apples
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the milk: if it's too hot, the cream loses its velvety texture and the protein solidifies into grains.
ing: whey protein dulce de leche flavor
titane: The pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. It warms the almond milk without any hot spots or sticking, then, rinsed and preheated empty, it caramelizes the apple cubes on the surface while the center remains soft. A single utensil for both operations.
steps: Soak the gelatin sheets in a bowl of very cold water. Let them soften while you heat the milk.
Pour the almond milk and cream into the pan. Heat over medium heat, stirring regularly. Stop as soon as the surface begins to simmer slightly: the mixture should never boil.
Remove from heat. Squeeze the gelatin between your fingers (press to remove the soaking water) and stir it in. Add the whey protein and mix until completely dissolved and lump-free.
Divide into six small pots.
Allow to return to room temperature, then place in the refrigerator for 2 hours, until completely set.
Cut the apples into small, even cubes.
Rinse and dry the pan. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat: a few drops of water should dance on the surface before evaporating.
Pour in the fat, add the apple cubes, and let them cook for 10 minutes without stirring. They will stick at first, then detach on their own once a golden crust has formed. Stir only at this point.
Arrange the still-warm apples on top of the set creams. Serve immediately.

title: Protein oat cream with cocoa and biscuit pieces
intro: It all comes down to consistency: stop cooking as soon as the cream forms a ribbon, otherwise it will solidify into a paste when cold.

ing.note: a small spoonful, or about 5 g

titane: Starting from a cold pan, without oil or preheating: the liquid and flour go into the pan together, preventing the oats from sticking. The large surface area of the titanium pan allows for rapid evaporation and thickens the mixture in minutes, whereas a narrow pan requires more patience.
steps: Pour the almond milk into the still cold pan, sprinkle the oat flour over it and whisk to dissolve any lumps before heating.
Place over medium heat. Whisk continuously for 4 to 5 minutes. The mixture will simmer, thicken, then coat the whisk and fall back in a thick ribbon: this is the time to stop.
Remove from heat and gradually whisk in the whey protein. Stir vigorously until the mixture is perfectly smooth again. Adding it over heat would cause the protein to coagulate and become grainy.
Remove from the cooking utensil and place in a ramekin. Cover with cling film, pressing it directly onto the surface to prevent the skin from forming.
Leave to set in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Thirty minutes in the freezer will do if you're short on time.
When ready to serve, arrange the banana slices, sprinkle with chocolate chips and place the spread in a quenelle shape in the center.

title: Almond, peanut and chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the product: compact enough to hold its shape without cooking, yet flexible enough to remain melt-in-your-mouth.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, the heat is evenly distributed without hot spots: the chocolate melts evenly, without sticking to the bottom. Stir continuously, then pour directly from the pan to coat the bars with an even layer.
steps: Combine the almond flour, peanut butter, and maple syrup in a bowl. Work with a spatula until you obtain a homogeneous, soft, and slightly sticky mass, similar to raw cookie dough.
Stir in the chocolate chips. Mix briefly to distribute them without crushing them.
Divide the mixture into small molds. Press down and smooth the surface with the back of a spoon: the more even the layer, the cleaner the cut will be.

Break the dark chocolate into pieces in the cold titanium pan. Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly. Remove from the heat as soon as the chocolate is melted and glossy, before it heats up further.
Pour the chocolate over the bars, spread in a thin layer and sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours, until the bars are firm to the touch. Unmold when cold.

title: Crispy panko chicken, vegetable pilaf rice
intro: It all comes down to the order of cooking: the rice first, then the chicken, in the same pan, so that the breading finds a surface that is already hot and dry.

ing.note: g, plus a small reserve for breading
small beaten, you will only use a third
g, plus a little head start

titane: The titanium rises quickly and strongly. Place the breaded pieces on the pan, then don't touch them: as long as the crust adheres, it's not set. It will detach on its own when golden brown. For the rice, add the broth in small ladles rather than all at once—the base remains hot enough for each addition to evaporate, coating the grains until they become translucent on the surface.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. The heat must be evenly distributed before any contact with the food.
Pour in half the oil. Add the diced onion, carrot, and peppers. Stir for 4 minutes, until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the uncooked rice, stir for one minute to coat it. Season with salt and pepper.
Moisten with a first ladleful of broth. Stir until absorbed, then repeat. Allow approximately 18 minutes in total: the rice should be tender and the bottom of the pan dry.
Remove from the pan and place in a bowl. Cover and wipe the pan with paper towels, without washing it.
Cut the chicken into large pieces and salt them. Coat them in flour, pat them dry, then dip them in beaten egg, and finally press them into the panko breadcrumbs to make them stick.

Return the pan to medium-high heat with the remaining oil. Place the pieces in the pan, spacing them apart. Let them sit for 4 to 5 minutes without touching them; they will release easily once a crust has formed. Turn them over and continue cooking for another 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix ketchup, soy sauce and maple syrup in a bowl. Keep the mayonnaise separate.
Arrange the rice, place the sliced chicken on top, coat with sweet and sour sauce and add a dash of mayonnaise.

title: Soba salad, stir-fried vegetables and tempeh
intro: It all comes down to the searing: the vegetables must color quickly, without releasing their water, to remain crisp under the cold sauce.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two or three minutes when empty. This instantly available heat sears zucchini, carrots, and tempeh before they even begin to sweat. The result: golden edges, a firm center, and no puddles at the bottom of the pan.
steps: Finely slice the courgette, carrot and tempeh. Aim for pieces of the same thickness: this is essential for even searing.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour the oil into the pan, then spread the vegetables and tempeh in a single layer. Don't touch anything: the pieces will stick at first, then release on their own once browned. Cook for a total of 8 minutes, turning once or twice.
Add salt, sprinkle with curry powder, mix one last time and remove from the pan to stop the cooking process.
Meanwhile, cook the soba noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water, according to the package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water to firm them up.
In a bowl, whisk together the lime juice, soy sauce, syrup, water, gochujang, and chopped mint.
Add the noodles and the warm topping, mix to coat, and serve immediately.

title: Chicken and sweet potato nuggets
intro: It all comes down to the moisture content of the sweet potato: roasted whole, it dries out enough to bind the stuffing without making it soggy.

ing.note: or 1 heaped teaspoon of garlic paste

titane: Seared over high heat to create a crust, then the pan goes straight into the oven. The preparation never changes containers, so the nuggets don't lose their shape and the crust from searing remains intact.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Place the whole sweet potato on a baking sheet and roast for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife inserted into the flesh meets no resistance. Let it cool slightly, then scoop out 200g (7 oz) of the flesh and mash it finely with a fork.

Combine the warm mashed potatoes, ground chicken, Parmesan cheese, flour, fresh garlic, salt, garlic and onion powder, and paprika in a bowl. Mix by hand until smooth and free of lumps. Let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes: the flour will absorb the moisture and the mixture will hold its shape better.
Lightly dampen or oil your palms. Shape into nuggets about 4 cm long, flattened to 1.5 cm thick. Transfer them (set them aside off the work surface) to a plate.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It's ready when a drop of water beads up and rolls off the surface. Then pour in the grapeseed oil, which withstands this temperature better than olive oil.
Place the nuggets loosely on the grill, in two batches if necessary. Do not touch them for 3 to 4 minutes: they will detach from the metal on their own once a crust has formed.

Flip them over with a flick of the wrist and let the second side brown for 2 minutes. Place the pan in a 200°C oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74°C. Remove from the oven and let rest for 3 minutes before serving.

title: Crispy pan-fried fries, double flour coating
intro: It all comes down to two things: perfectly dry fries before coating, and a pan hot enough for the crust to form on contact, not from steam.

ing.note: 1 g of garlic powder, 1 g of ground black pepper

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: direct contact with the metal replaces the forced air of an air fryer and creates a crispier crust. Cover for the first twelve minutes to keep the inside soft, then finish cooking uncovered over high heat. Never force the fry off: a fry that resists will continue to form a crust.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick, even sticks. Evenness matters more than thinness: identical sections cook at the same rate.
Rinse the sticks in cold water to remove surface starch. Drain, then dry them thoroughly with a cloth. Any residual moisture will cause steam to form instead of a crust.
Divide the flour between two bowls, 56g in each. Add half the salt and spices to each bowl.
Pour the 78g of water into one of the two bowls and whisk until you obtain a smooth paste, with the consistency of liquid cream.
Dip the fries in the batter, let the excess drip off, then roll them in the dry flour from the second bowl. Tap to remove the excess: a thin coating is enough.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without oil.
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan and swirl it to spread a continuous film. Grapeseeds withstand high temperatures without smoking.

Arrange the fries in a single layer, without overlapping them. Work in two batches if necessary: each fry must touch the metal. Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 12 minutes without touching.
Lift the lid: the fries should detach easily. Turn them over with a flick of the wrist, cover again and continue for 8 minutes.

Remove the lid, increase the heat to high, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring regularly, until all sides are golden brown and crispy. Immediately transfer to a wire rack, never to paper towels, which will soften the crust. Season with salt.

title: Light pan-fried msemen
intro: It all comes down to the hydration of the dough and the heat of the pan: a supple dough and a surface that is already hot give a clean flaky texture with very little fat.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly. The msemen forms its crust in seconds, without sticking, whereas a warm surface would have dried it out before browning. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat: a drop of water should sizzle and slide off, not evaporate immediately.
steps: Mix the flour, semolina, and salt in a bowl. Gradually add the water, working the mixture by hand until you obtain a soft, slightly sticky dough. Stop mixing as soon as the texture is right, even if some water remains.
Knead for 5 minutes, until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into 4 pieces of dough. Lightly oil the work surface and your hands, then roll out each piece of dough into a very thin, almost translucent disc.
Brush the surface with a thin layer of fat. Fold the left and right edges towards the center to form a rectangle, then fold the top and bottom to form a square. Let it rest while the pan heats up.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Then apply a thin layer of oil and wipe off the excess with absorbent paper.
Gently flatten a square with your fingertips to widen it, then place it in the pan. Do not touch it: it will detach on its own when the first side is cooked, after about a minute.
Turn over and let the other side brown for 1 minute. The grill marks should be distinct, golden, not uniform. Transfer to a wire rack to keep them crispy, and repeat with the remaining three.

title: Large protein pancake with apples and cinnamon
intro: One pancake for the whole pan, cooked under a lid: what matters here is patience over low-medium heat, the only guarantee of a set center and a golden base.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before greasing. Titanium heats up evenly: the batter cooks from the bottom while the steam trapped under the lid cooks the top. Never flip the pan. The telltale sign is simple: when the bottom easily releases from the pan, it's cooked.
steps: Combine the pancake mix, egg, and skimmed milk in a large bowl. Mix for 5 minutes until you have a thick batter without any dry lumps. It should fall heavily from the spatula.
Stir in the cinnamon. Let it rest while the pan preheats.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then brush with clarified butter: it should simmer gently without smoking.
Pour the batter into the center and spread it evenly over the entire surface with the back of a spatula. Work quickly, the batter is already starting to set.
Distribute the diced apples evenly over the surface, then add the granola if you are using it. Press them in only slightly; they should remain visible.

Cover and reduce heat to low-medium. Cook for 15 minutes. Only lift the lid at the end: the center should no longer be liquid and the bottom should easily pull away when you slide a spatula under the edge.
Meanwhile, mix the icing sugar with the milk until you obtain a smooth icing that flows in a ribbon.
Slide the pancake onto a board, let it cool for 2 minutes, cut into slices and top with icing.

title: Sweet potato, date and oat cookies
intro: It all depends on the moisture content of the puree: if it's too runny, the dough collapses in the pan; if it's well drained and dense, it holds its shape on its own.

ing.note: mashed into a smooth puree (about 1 large potato)

titane: A bare skillet replaces a baking sheet. Preheated empty and then covered, it provides direct, even heat that browns the edges while the steam trapped under the lid keeps the center soft. The indicator is more tactile than visual: as long as the cookie sticks, it's not ready. When it releases easily under the spatula, flip it over.
steps: Prick the whole sweet potato with a fork. Bake at 200°C (390°F) for 1 hour, or until a knife inserted into the flesh meets no resistance. Let it cool slightly, then scoop out 200g of the flesh and mash it into a smooth purée.

Combine the mashed potatoes, dates, honey, rolled oats, vanilla, and fleur de sel in a bowl. Mix until you have a compact dough that holds its shape in a ball in your hand. If it's still sticky, let it rest for 10 minutes: the oats will absorb the remaining moisture.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Brush it with a film of oil.
Form balls the size of a large walnut. Place them in a single layer, without packing them tightly, and flatten them with a fork to about 1 cm thick.
Cover and cook for 7 minutes. Test: the cookie should easily release from the pan. Turn over, cover again, and continue cooking for another 7 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden.

Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a wire rack. Repeat this process for subsequent batches, reducing the cooking time by one minute if the pan has become too hot. Allow to cool completely; the texture only sets when cold.

title: Vanilla rice pudding
intro: It's all about the texture: the rice must remain creamy, never dry, which requires attention rather than time.
titane: The pan offers a wide, shallow surface: the milk heats up faster and more evenly than in a saucepan, but it also evaporates more quickly. Preheat the pan empty for 1 to 2 minutes before adding the milk, then stir every 5 to 8 minutes, scraping the bottom well. A liter of liquid is manageable in this pan as long as you keep the heat low and judge the cooking by texture, not by timing.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat. The heat should be felt a few centimeters above the bottom.
Pour in the milk. Heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer around the edges, without ever letting it come to a full boil.
Add the sugar and vanilla. Mix until completely dissolved.
Sprinkle the rice evenly over the surface. Let it become translucent at the edges for a minute in the hot milk.

Reduce the heat to low. Cook for 35 minutes, stirring every 5 to 8 minutes and scraping the bottom of the pan with a flexible spatula. The rice is ready when it has absorbed most of the milk and coats the spatula.
Remove from heat and place in individual bowls. Allow to cool slightly before serving: the texture will firm up as it cools.

title: Bowl of eggplant, roasted chickpeas and spinach patties
intro: It's all about patience: the eggplant and chickpeas only turn over once they have detached themselves from the bottom, that's what gives them their color.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains heat, allowing you to sear eggplant and chickpeas directly on the stovetop rather than in the oven. This ensures even tenderness throughout, more vibrant color, and a single pan for everything from the first vegetable to the last. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should dance in it before evaporating.
Meanwhile, cut the eggplant into even 2 cm cubes. Regularity matters more than exact size.
Drain the chickpeas, rinse them in cold water and remove their skins (rub them between two cloths, the skins will come off). Dry them well.
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan. Add the eggplant and chickpeas, thyme, and a pinch of salt. Spread them in a single layer: if they overlap, the vegetables will sweat instead of browning.

Cook undisturbed until the cubes pull away from the bottom of the pan. Then reduce the heat to medium and stir regularly for a total of 20 minutes, until the eggplant is tender and the chickpeas are golden brown and crispy.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a dish and keep warm.
Cut the cherry tomatoes in half, crumble the feta by hand into uneven pieces. Set aside.

In the still-hot pan, add a drizzle of oil if the bottom is dry and place the spinach patties in. Cook for about 4 to 5 minutes, turning them only once, until they release easily and are golden brown.

Assemble the bowls: eggplant and chickpeas at the base, spinach discs on top, tomatoes and feta cheese distributed on top. Season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with hand-chopped mint and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Vegan ricotta made with soy milk
intro: It all comes down to the hand that presses: too firm, you get a dry cheese; barely pressed, you keep the creaminess.
titane: The titanium pan spreads the liter of milk over a wide surface: the temperature rises quickly and evenly, without any hot spots at the bottom. Curdling therefore begins immediately, everywhere at once, as soon as the vinegar is added. Heating and curdling take place in the same pan; no additional saucepan is needed.
steps: Pour the soy milk into the titanium pan. Heat over high heat until small simmers appear across the entire surface, then turn off the heat.

Remove from heat and pour in the rice vinegar all at once. Give it a couple of stirs, no more. Let it rest for 15 minutes: the milk will curdle and white lumps will separate from the whey, which will remain pale yellow and translucent.
Line a colander with a thin cloth. Transfer the clumps to the skimmer, then pour in the rest.
Gather the corners of the cloth and squeeze with your fingertips to remove excess liquid. Stop as soon as the flow slows down: the cheese should remain soft, not compact.
Transfer to another container in a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Season with lemon juice and salt just before serving. Taste and adjust as needed.

title: Chicken tikka masala burritos
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the chicken simmers, shreds on the spot, and the burritos get their crust before going into the freezer.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and withstands high heat without a coating. It replaces the slow cooker: covered, 45 minutes is enough where four used to be necessary. It then serves as a work surface for shredding, and later as a grill for toasting tortillas. No transferring, no microwave, no air fryer.
steps: Combine the chicken, onion, ginger, garlic, salt, garam masala, ground coriander, cumin, brown sugar and crushed tomatoes in the cold pan.
Mix with a spatula while cold, until the spices coat each piece. Working with cold spices prevents them from burning on direct contact with the metal.
Bring to a simmer over high heat. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes. The chicken is ready when it is fork-tender.
Tilt the pan and ladle out the excess cooking juices. The sauce should coat the burrito, not flood it: a burrito that's too wet won't toast properly.
Shred the chicken directly in the pan, using two forks pulled in opposite directions (separate the fibers from the flesh).
Remove from heat and stir in the Greek yogurt and fresh coriander. Mix well. The yogurt should never boil, or it will curdle.
Place a portion of rice on each tortilla, then a portion of chicken. Leave a 3 cm margin on the edges.
Fold in the sides, then roll tightly starting from the edge closest to you.
Wrap each burrito in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag. They will keep for three months.

To serve: defrost the burrito, heat an empty skillet over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, add a drizzle of clarified butter, and place the burrito seam-side down. Do not touch it. It will release easily once a crust has formed; allow 2 minutes per side.

title: Marinated chicken, pan-fried apricots and feta
intro: Everything happens in the same pan, without washing it between the two cookings: the apricots leave their caramelized sugar there, the chicken comes to collect it.
ing: A few sprigs of fresh thyme
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat: a drop of water should sizzle immediately. This rapid temperature increase allows the apricots to brown and then the chicken to sear without any intermediate cleaning. In both cases, don't touch anything while the pieces are sticking: they will release on their own once a crust has formed.
steps: Cut the chicken into large, even pieces. In a bowl, combine them with the oil, lemon juice, spices, tomato sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix to coat, then refrigerate until ready to slice.
Pit the apricots and cut them into quarters. Halve the cherry tomatoes, slice the sundried tomatoes, and finely chop the spring onions.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Drizzle with olive oil, place the apricot wedges cut-side down, and add the honey. Leave for 5 minutes without stirring: they should be soft and golden, and easily separate from the skins.
Remove the apricots from the pan and set them aside on a plate. Do not wash the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium, add a drizzle of olive oil if the bottom is dry. Place the chicken, drained of its marinade, in a single layer. Let it brown without disturbing it, turning it over when the pieces easily separate from the skin, and continue cooking until fully cooked, about 10 minutes depending on their size.

Arrange the cherry tomatoes, onions, sun-dried tomatoes, apricots, and still-warm chicken on plates. Crumble the feta cheese over the top, sprinkle with fresh thyme, adjust the seasoning, and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Red curry and peanut ramen
intro: A sauce that can be prepared in ten minutes, frozen in portions, and in which the noodles cook directly: everything depends on the consistency of the coconut milk, which should never boil vigorously.
ing: a thumb-sized piece of fresh ginger
titane: Preheat the pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, before adding any oil. The titanium heats up quickly: you sauté the aromatics, simmer the sauce, and cook the noodles all in the same pan, without ever changing utensils or washing anything in between.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 2 minutes, until they become translucent and fragrant. They should not color.
Add the curry paste and peanut butter. Mix to coat the aromatics and awaken the spices on contact with the fat, for about thirty seconds.
Moisten with coconut milk then with stock. Scrape the bottom with a spatula to dissolve the juices (the caramelized deposits stuck to the pan, which carry the flavor).
Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.
For storage: allow to cool, divide into portions in ice cube trays or small containers, freeze.

When ready to serve, melt the sauce over low heat directly in the pan. As soon as it begins to simmer, add the uncooked noodles and continue cooking, separating them with tongs. They will soften and absorb the sauce in 3 to 4 minutes.

title: Rustic leek and Comté cheese tart
intro: It all comes down to the leeks: they need to caramelize before melting, otherwise the filling releases water and makes the pastry soggy.
titane: Preheat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter. The leeks will initially stick, brown, and then release on their own: that's the signal. The same pan then goes directly into the oven with the tart inside, without transferring it or using an additional baking sheet.
steps: Combine flour, butter, egg, water, and fleur de sel in a bowl. Knead until you obtain a smooth ball, free of butter lumps. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Finely slice the white parts of the leeks. Wash them, then dry them well: residual water prevents colouring.
Heat the titanium pan empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the oil, add the crushed garlic and the leeks. Mix once, then leave them in place. They should stick to the bottom for a few moments before freeing themselves.

Add the balsamic vinegar. Reduce the heat to medium-high and continue cooking for about ten minutes, until the leeks are very soft. If they start to stick, add a spoonful of water to loosen the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Grate the Comté cheese. Remove the leeks (transfer them to a dish) and let them cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 195°C (385°F), conventional setting. Fan-assisted cooking dries out the edges of the pastry before the base cooks.
Roll out the dough into a 26-28 cm disc on a sheet of baking paper, the same diameter as the pan.
Slide the pastry and parchment paper into the cooled pan. Prick the base with the tip of a knife. Spread the mustard, leaving a 2-3 cm border all around.
Distribute two-thirds of the Comté cheese, then the leeks, then the remaining cheese.
Fold the pastry edge over the filling in irregular folds.
Place the pan in the bottom of the oven for 30 to 35 minutes, until it is a nice golden color. Move it to the top of the oven for 3 minutes if the surface remains pale.
Remove the pan using an oven mitt. Scatter the thyme leaves over the top and serve in the cooking dish.

title: Breakfast sandwiches for the week
intro: Ten sandwiches, one pan: it all comes down to the crust of the pancakes and the gentle cooking of the eggs, which must remain soft after freezing and reheating.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the fat: this allows the patties to sear at a high temperature without sticking. Once the meat is removed from the skillet and set aside, simply wipe the bottom with paper towels, without washing. The eggs are then cooked in the same pan, covered, over low heat. One skillet, two opposing cooking methods.
steps: Mix the beef and turkey together with your fingertips, without overworking the mixture. Season with garlic salt, onion powder, Italian herbs, and pepper.
Divide into 10 portions of approximately 115g each. Flatten each into a thin pancake, slightly wider than the muffin: it will shrink during cooking.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of grapeseed oil.
Grasp the patties without moving them. Wait until they release from the pan on their own before flipping them, then finish cooking them thoroughly. Work in batches rather than overloading the pan.
Remove the pancakes and keep them warm. Wipe the pan with paper towels to remove any burnt bits, which would make the eggs bitter.
Beat the eggs with the garlic salt and pepper. Stir in the onions and peppers.

Re-oil the pan, reduce the heat to low, and pour in the eggs. Cover and let set for 10 to 12 minutes, until the center is firm. Turn out onto a board and cut into squares the size of muffins. Variation: Finish under the broiler for 2 minutes; the pan is fine.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the sriracha, lemon juice and garlic salt.
Assemble each sandwich: muffin base, sauce, egg square, patty, cheese slice, topping. The residual heat is enough to melt the cheese.

Allow to cool completely to room temperature before wrapping—otherwise the steam will make the muffin soggy. Wrap individually in parchment paper, then place in a freezer bag. They will keep for up to one month.
To reheat: remove the sandwich from the paper, place a damp paper towel on top and microwave for 4 to 5 minutes.

title: Chocolate cake in a pot, cooked in a water bath
intro: Without an oven, the steam from a bain-marie (gentle cooking in a container placed in simmering water) produces a moist crumb that dry heat cannot produce.
titane: The pan's wide, flat surface holds several pots side by side without them slipping, and its even heat distribution eliminates hot spots under the bottoms: all the pots cook at the same rate. One centimeter of water is all that's needed.
steps: Beat the egg in a bowl until it is frothy.
Add the sugar, cocoa, flour, yogurt and oil. Finish with the yeast.
Mix until you obtain a smooth, lump-free batter. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Incorporate the chocolate chips with a short, quick motion, so as not to melt them into the mixture.
Pour the dough into one or two heatproof pots, filling them two-thirds full: the dough will rise.
Pour 1 cm of water into the pan. Place the pots flat on the bottom. Place the lids on top without screwing them on, to avoid any pressure buildup.
Cover the pan and cook for 20 minutes over medium heat, with the water just simmering. Check the water level halfway through cooking and top up with hot water if necessary.
The cakes are ready when they have risen and the surface is firm to the touch. Remove the pots with tongs and let them rest for 10 minutes off the heat.

title: Chocolate chip cookies with a brownie center
intro: It's all about the cooking: lid closed, moderate heat, and take the cookies out when the center is still wobbly.

ing.note: g, replaceable by the same quantity of starch

titane: The pan acts as both a saucepan and an oven. Melt the chocolate in it over low heat, wipe it clean, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then bake with the lid on: the very hot base forms a thin, crispy crust while the steam trapped by the lid keeps the center gooey. Three or four cookies per batch, no more, otherwise the temperature drops and the crust won't form.
steps: Chop the chocolate and cut the butter into cubes. Place them in a cold pan and heat over low-medium heat, stirring with a spatula, for about 5 minutes. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy. Transfer to a bowl.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla until the mixture lightens slightly.
Pour the still-warm melted chocolate over the sweetened eggs. Whisk until smooth.
Add the flour, cocoa and baking powder all at once. Mix with a spatula, without overmixing: you are looking for a thick and supple batter, similar to a brownie batter.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat: a hand held a few centimeters from the bottom should feel a distinct heat.
Grease the bottom with a very thin film of clarified butter or grapeseed oil, spread with a brush or paper.
Place 3 to 4 portions of dough using an ice cream scoop. Space them two fingers apart: the dough doesn't spread much.

Cover. Cook over low-medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes. Do not touch the cookies while they are still sticking; they will release on their own when the bottom is set. The center should remain soft when pressed with a finger.

Lift them with a thin spatula and place them on a wire rack. Sprinkle each one with a pinch of fleur de sel while they cool slightly. Repeat with the remaining batter, allowing the pan to reheat between batches.

title: Chocolate, peanut and almond bars
intro: It all comes down to the cold: a night in the freezer gives a clean cut and a vegetable caramel that holds under the chocolate.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly: it doesn't stick despite the lack of a coating. The pan then becomes the dipping bath. A single surface for melting and coating, nothing else to wash. Turn off the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth; it heats up quickly.
steps: Mix together the almond flour, 100g of peanut butter and maple syrup until you obtain a smooth paste that holds together between your fingers.
Pour into a rectangular baking tin lined with baking paper. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon: a compact base will not crumble when cut.
Place in the freezer for 20 minutes, while preparing the rest.
Work the 200g of peanut butter with the agave syrup and melted coconut oil. The mixture should be smooth and glossy.
Spread this caramel evenly over the chilled base. Sprinkle with crushed peanuts and press them in lightly.
Return to the freezer overnight, or at least 8 hours. The whole thing should be completely firm.
Remove from the mold and cut into bars with a smooth-bladed knife, which has been rinsed under hot water and dried between each cut. Return them to the refrigerator while you melt the chocolate.
Chop the dark chocolate and place it in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously for about 3 minutes, until smooth. Remove from the heat immediately.

Dip each bar in the chocolate, directly in the pan, turning it over with two forks to coat it completely. Drain briefly, then transfer (out of the pan) to a sheet of parchment paper. The chocolate will set in a few minutes upon contact with the frozen bar.

title: Burger and fries, one pan
intro: It all comes down to the order of cooking: the fries first, then the steak, in the same pan and in the fragrant fat they leave behind.

ing.note: cut into sticks with the skin

ing: Homemade burger buns with smoked paprika
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the oil. The titanium coating heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold sticks are added: this is what creates the crust without an oven. The same principle applies to the steak, which is placed on the still-hot skillet and left undisturbed until it releases itself.
steps: Cut the potatoes into even sticks, skin included. Dry them in a cloth: surface moisture delays coloring.
Mix the sticks with the oil, half the paprika and a pinch of salt. Each side should be coated with fat.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. The oil released by the potatoes will then be sufficient.

Pour the sticks into a single layer, cover, and reduce the heat to medium. Cook for 18 minutes, stirring every 4 to 5 minutes. The lid cooks the inside, while leaving the lid on dries and browns the outside.
Remove the fries from the pan to stop the cooking process and place them on a warm plate. Add salt at this point.

Turn up the heat. Season the steak with salt and the remaining paprika, place it in the pan, and leave it undisturbed. It will release easily after 3 to 4 minutes: that's the signal to flip it. Continue cooking for another 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat.
Top the steak with cheese, turn off the heat, and cover for 1 minute. The residual heat will do the work without drying out the meat.
Spread the sauce on both inner sides of the bread.
Stack the cheese steak, tomato, and salad. Close and serve immediately with fries.

title: Teriyaki chicken and fried rice, ten servings
intro: It all comes down to two things: rice cooked the day before and very cold, and a pan hot enough to brown the chicken before it releases its water.
ing: cornstarch dissolved in 3 tablespoons of cold water
titane: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil. The diced chicken should sizzle the moment it touches the metal and remain still until it releases itself: this is the sign that a crust has formed. Use the same pan for the sauce reduction, scrambled eggs, and fried rice, without transferring the ingredients. Each step incorporates the juices from the previous one.
steps: Mix the diced chicken with the garlic salt, pepper, and chili oil. Set aside while you prepare the rest.
Whisk together all the ingredients for the yum yum sauce until smooth. Refrigerate.
In a large bowl, fluff the cold rice with your hands, then mix it with the soy sauce and sesame oil until evenly colored. Set aside.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the grapeseed oil and wait until it ripples.

Place the chicken in a single layer, without packing it down. Work in two batches if necessary. Do not stir while the pieces are still sticking. As soon as they separate on their own, turn them over and continue cooking until browned on all sides, about 10 minutes total.

Reduce the heat to medium. Pour the soy sauce, honey, brown sugar, vinegar, garlic, and ginger directly over the chicken. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a spatula to dissolve the browned bits (deglaze: loosen the caramelized deposits with liquid). Let it reduce for 6 minutes.
Stir in the diluted cornflour, pour it in a thin stream and mix for 1 to 2 minutes: the sauce should coat the chicken and become shiny.
Push the chicken to one side of the pan. Crack the eggs into the empty space and scramble them with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes, until set but still soft.
Add the frozen vegetables, then the seasoned rice. Increase the heat to high and stir-fry for 5 minutes, stirring regularly, until everything is hot and evenly distributed.
Transfer to 10 airtight containers. Let cool uncovered before sealing.
In the freezer, for up to 3 months. To serve: add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a damp paper towel and microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through.

title: Quesadillas with shredded chicken, chipotle and honey
intro: It's all about the balance between the smokiness of the chipotle and the honey: the sauce must coat the chicken without making it soggy, otherwise the tortilla will never be crispy.
titane: One pan for everything. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, oil it, sear the chicken, then cover and simmer: the titanium handles the heat without flinching and maintains even heat distribution over low heat. At the end, the same pan transforms back into a griddle to give the quesadillas a crisp, well-defined crust.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour in half the oil. Place the chicken breasts, seasoned with garlic salt and pepper, in the pan. Sear for 3 minutes per side, without moving them.
Add the chipotles, lime juice, and honey. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. The chicken should be cooked through and the liquid significantly reduced.
Meanwhile, blend all the sauce ingredients together until smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Refrigerate.
Remove from heat and drain off any excess cooking liquid by tilting the pan. Reserve two tablespoons of the liquid.
Shred the chicken directly in the pan, using two forks (pull the meat in the opposite direction to separate it into strands).
Stir in the chipotle sauce, grated mozzarella, and chives. Mix until the filling is well combined and holds its shape on a spoon.
Spread the filling over one half of each tortilla, fold over the other half and press lightly with the palm of your hand.

Wipe the pan clean, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour in the remaining oil. Brown the quesadillas for 3 minutes per side over medium-high heat. Only flip them when they release easily from the bottom of the pan.
Remove from the pan and place on a rack and let cool for 2 minutes before cutting: the cheese stabilizes and the filling doesn't escape.

title: pan-smoked baba ganoush
intro: It all comes down to the skin: it must darken completely to flavor the flesh, then disappear entirely from the plate.

ing.note: whole, studded in a few places at the
g, to be adjusted between 60 and 100 g depending on the bitterness

titane: Bare titanium withstands direct and prolonged contact with skin, causing it to char, where a coating would fail. Preheat the oven empty, place whole eggplants on it, and roll them with a flick of the wrist every two or three minutes. The charring remains even, without any concentrated burn spots.
steps: Heat the empty titanium pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle and evaporate immediately.

Place the whole eggplants in a hot, dry pan (without any oil or butter). Cook for about 20 minutes, turning them regularly. The skin will blister and blacken all over, and the flesh will soften when pressed.
Remove the eggplants from the pan and set aside, cover them, and let them rest for an hour. The trapped steam will loosen the skin.
Remove all the blackened skin, leaving no trace. Keep only the tender flesh.
Mash this flesh with a fork. No blender: we want chunks, not a smooth cream.
Stir in the tahini, garlic, lime juice, salt, and smoked paprika. Mix, taste, and adjust the acidity.
Spread the mixture by making a groove on the back of the spoon. Pour the olive oil into the groove, sprinkle with sumac.

title: Steamed bao buns
intro: It's all about restraint: two short shoots and a lid that's left alone at the end.
titane: The titanium pan becomes a warming oven. Add 2 cm of water, place a low rack (or three crushed balls of aluminum foil as a support), and put the lid on top: the water simmers in a few minutes and the heat is evenly distributed without any hot spots. The pan's width allows the loaves to be spaced apart, so they rise without touching each other.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, and salt in a mixing bowl. Pour in the lukewarm water and oil. Mix, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes: the dough should become smooth, supple, and no longer stick to your fingers.
Cover with a damp cloth. Let rise for 1 hour 30 minutes, no more. Beyond that, the crumb will loosen and the bao will collapse during baking.
Degas (press the dough with the palm of your hand to expel large bubbles). Work it for 30 seconds to homogenize.
Divide the dough into two portions. Roll each into a 1 cm oval, lightly oil half of the surface, fold in half without sealing. Place each roll on a square of baking paper.

Let it rise a second time, covered, until it reaches one and a half times the original volume. Allow 30 to 40 minutes depending on the room temperature. Don't aim for it to double in size: the steam will finish the job.

Pour 2 cm of water into the titanium pan, place the rack or aluminum supports inside. Bring to a simmer, place the breads on their paper, and cover. Cook for 18 minutes over medium heat. Monitor the water level occasionally—the pan heats up quickly—and add more hot water if needed.
Turn off the heat and wait 5 minutes with the lid closed. The sudden blast of cold air would cause the loaves to collapse.

title: Sweet potato balls stuffed with jalapeño
intro: It all comes down to the moisture content of the puree: when well cooled, it requires less flour and gives a light dough that browns instead of collapsing.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the ghee. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without creating hot spots: the crust forms cleanly on contact, the center remains soft, and the dough doesn't stick. Once the dumplings are in the pan, don't touch them. They will release on their own when the crust has set.
steps: Roast the whole sweet potato in the oven at 200°C for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife pierces the flesh without resistance.
Take 350g of flesh. Blend or mash until you obtain a smooth puree.
Chill the purée in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, preferably overnight. This will reduce its moisture content and make the pastry lighter.
Incorporate the flour by handfuls, along with the salt, until you obtain a soft and barely sticky dough. Stop as soon as the texture holds together: too much flour will make it heavy.
Leave the dough to rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to 2 hours if it remains difficult to handle.
Mix together the cream cheese, jalapeños, spring onions and Parmesan cheese.
Divide the dough into 8 portions. Flatten each one in the palm of your hand, place a spoonful of filling in the center, close by sealing the edges well, then roll into a ball.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the ghee and wait for it to simmer gently, without smoking.
Place the meatballs in the pan, leaving space between them. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat. Turn them over when they release easily and the surface is golden brown.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto absorbent paper for a few seconds, then serve hot.

title: Seared chicken fillet, finished under a lid
intro: It all comes down to two things: a pan that is really hot before the first contact, and a final stage of cooking off the heat that lets the heat do its work.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly: a crust forms within the first minute, without the base losing temperature when the meat is added. Its mass then retains enough heat to finish cooking the meat through off the heat, without drying it out.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Check: a few drops of water should slide onto the surface and evaporate immediately.
Meanwhile, season the fillet with salt and pepper on both sides.
Pour the fat into the hot pan just before cooking. It should ripple slightly without smoking.
Place the fillet in the pan and let it sear for 3 minutes without touching, moving, or pressing it.
Turn it over when it detaches itself from the bottom. If it resists, the crust has not formed: wait.
Cover the pan.
Remove it from the heat and let the chicken finish cooking for 5 minutes covered, using only the heat of the pan. The flesh will remain pearly (opaque and shiny, without dry fibers).
Remove the fillet from the pan and place it on a plate. Collect the concentrated juices at the bottom: this is enough to coat the meat or to make a sauce.

title: Protein-enriched hazelnut-cocoa spread
intro: It all comes down to the roasting of the hazelnuts: it's what gives the depth, the cocoa just follows.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. It heats up quickly and evenly across the entire surface, so hazelnuts roast in seven minutes without burning the edges. Preheat it empty and dry, stirring continuously.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat. Let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes: a drop of water should dance on it before evaporating.

Pour the hazelnuts into a single layer, without any oil. Toast them for 7 minutes (dry-roast them to develop their aromas), stirring continuously. The skins will brown and crack, and the toasted flavor will become pronounced.

Remove the hazelnuts from the pan (to stop the cooking process) and place them on a cold plate. Let them cool for 3 minutes, then rub them between your palms or in a tea towel to remove most of the skins.
Blend the hazelnuts alone until they go from a sandy texture to an oily paste. This should take 3 to 4 minutes, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed.
Add the almond milk, honey, cocoa, vanilla, and whey protein. Blend again until smooth and homogeneous. If the batter remains too thick, thin it with 10 ml of almond milk at a time.
Transfer to a clean jar. The paste thickens when chilled: take it out 10 minutes before spreading. It will keep for one week in the refrigerator.

title: Chickpea and psyllium rolls
intro: Without flour, these little loaves hold together entirely on the psyllium: it is the psyllium that fixes the water in the dough and prevents the chickpeas from crumbling when cut.
titane: Covered pan, medium-low heat: the lid reflects the heat back onto the tops of the balls, causing them to puff up, while direct contact with the titanium builds the crust. Never turn them over until the cooked side easily releases from the bottom. If it resists, they're not ready, and the still-sticky dough will tear.
steps: Drain the chickpeas and discard the liquid from the can. Rinse them quickly, then dry them with a cloth.
Blend the chickpeas with the eggs, psyllium, yeast, salt, and vanilla. Stop when the dough is smooth and quite sticky: it should cling to your finger without running.
Let it rest for 5 minutes. The psyllium will swell and the paste will firm up.
Shape the dough into balls by hand, moistening them if necessary, about the size of a small brioche. Keep them all the same size for even baking.
Sprinkle the top with a light dusting of sugar.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter or oil, and wait until it simmers.
Place the balls well spaced apart, cover, and reduce the heat to low-medium. Cook for about 15 minutes, until the bottom is golden brown and easily releases from the pan.
Turn over, cover again, and continue for 15 minutes. The loaves will be puffed up and browned on both sides.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool completely before cutting. They will still be moist in the center when hot.

title: Pan-fried lasagna with beef and vegetables
intro: It all comes down to the initial browning of the beef: it's what gives depth to a short sauce in which the pasta will cook directly.
titane: The pan heats up quickly and intensely: the ground meat develops a crisp crust before it even releases its moisture. Once this base is in place, nothing leaves the pan—vegetables, sauce, pasta, finishing touches. Just keep an eye on the liquid level: a pan evaporates faster than a tall saucepan, so add two tablespoons of hot water if the sauce thickens too quickly.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should bead on it without sizzling violently.

Pour the oil over the beef, then crumble it into a single layer. Leave it undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes: the meat will flake away from the surface on its own once a crust has formed. Turn it over in large pieces.
Add the onion, carrot, eggplant and garlic. Reduce the heat to medium and let it sweat for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and let it simmer for 1 minute (cook until it darkens and loses its acidity). Moisten with the tomato sauce and 50 ml of stock. Season with spices and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes over low heat. The sauce should remain thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, never runny.

Break the lasagna sheets into irregular pieces and press them into the sauce. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes over low heat, stirring gently two or three times to prevent sticking. They should yield easily to the tip of a knife.
Meanwhile, dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining 50 ml of stock. Microwave in 30-second intervals, whisking between each interval, until you obtain a thick cream.
Remove from the microwave and whisk together the fromage blanc and mozzarella. Thin with almond milk until you reach a smooth béchamel consistency. Season with salt.
Coat the pasta with this sauce, sprinkle with Parmesan and oregano. Cover, turn off the heat, and let it sit for 1 minute: the cheese will melt in the residual steam.

title: Mashed eggplant with tahini, caramelized tofu
intro: It all comes down to two textures: a melting, almost liquid eggplant flesh, and tofu seared quite strongly to retain some crunch under the glaze.
titane: The crumbled tofu doesn't need to be stirred. Preheat the pan empty, add the oil, place the crumbs in, and leave them alone: a crust will form on its own, and the tofu will release itself once it's set. That's the signal to flip. The final caramelization with soy sauce and agave benefits from the rapid temperature increase: the syrup adheres without turning bitter.
steps: Pierce the entire eggplant with a fork, all over its surface. The steam must be able to escape.
Bake at 200°C (oven or air fryer) for 20 to 25 minutes. The eggplant is ready when it softens and a fork pierces it easily.
Split it in half lengthwise. Mash the flesh with a fork, without pureeing it.
Add the tahini, lemon juice, and salt. Mash again until you have a smooth paste. Taste and adjust the acidity.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle and run. Then pour in the oil.
Crumble the tofu directly into the hot pan over medium-high heat. Spread it in a single layer.
Don't touch anything. Wait for the crumbs to detach themselves from the surface, then turn them over all at once.
Add the tomato paste, soy sauce, agave and a pinch of salt.
Sauté for 5 minutes. The tofu takes on a golden hue and a sticky surface.
Place the tofu on top of the crushed eggplant. Sprinkle with chopped coriander, and serve with bread on the side.

title: Potato skin chips
intro: The peelings become crispy provided they are given time to adhere and then detach themselves from the metal: do not touch them during searing.
ing: Skins of 8 to 10 large organic potatoes
titane: The preheated pan, when empty, heats up quickly and maintains its temperature when the skins are added. This intense heat dries the surface in minutes, whereas an oven would require slow dehydration. The skins stick at first, then detach on their own as soon as a crust has formed: this is the signal to turn them over, not before.
steps: Dry the skins thoroughly with a cloth. Any residual moisture will delay crisping.
In a bowl, mix the skins with the oil, garlic powder, herbs, paprika, salt and pepper. Work by hand so that each skin is coated.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle immediately.
Arrange the hides in a single layer, flesh side down against the metal, without overlapping them. Do this in several batches if necessary.
Let them set without touching or stirring for 5 to 6 minutes. The skins will stick together, then detach on their own: wait until this moment to turn them over with a flick of the wrist.
Continue for 4 to 5 minutes on the second side, until golden colour and edges curled.
If some skins remain soft, reduce the heat to low for 2 minutes to dry them without burning. Transfer them to a wire rack, never to paper towels: the steam will soften the crispness.

title: Waffle sandwiches, chicken patty and egg white
intro: Ten breakfasts prepared at once, in a single pan: everything depends on the color of the pancakes, which must be a deep golden brown before they go into the cold.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when the cold patties are added: this is what gives them a golden crust instead of soggy, gray meat. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then oil it. Once the patties are removed from the pan and set aside, wipe the bottom clean and cook the eggs over low heat in the same pan.
steps: Mix the ground chicken with the garlic salt, onion powder, chili flakes, pepper, smoked paprika, and maple syrup. Work it in just enough to distribute the spices.
Weigh out 85g portions, roll them into balls, then flatten them into regular patties of about 1cm. The uniformity of thickness determines the cooking time.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, without smoking.

Place the pancakes loosely on the pan. Do not touch them again. Let them cook for 4 minutes, turn them over when they easily detach from the bottom, then cook for another 4 minutes on the other side over medium heat.
Place the patties on a plate and cover them with aluminum foil.
Wipe the pan clean and place the egg molds in it. Mix the egg whites and chives, then divide the mixture among the molds. Cover and cook over low heat for 6 minutes, until the center is firm.
Assemble each sandwich: a waffle, a chicken patty, a slice of cheese, an egg white disc, a second waffle. The cheese should touch the still-warm meat to begin melting.
Wrap each sandwich in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag. Storage: 3 months in the freezer.
To reheat, wrap the frozen sandwich in a damp paper towel, place it on a plate and microwave it for 3 to 4 minutes.

title: Birria crunchwraps
intro: It all comes down to the crust: the crust of the steak before simmering, then the crust of the folded seam downwards, which keeps the pastry closed and gives it its crispness.
titane: The titanium pan, preheated empty, handles a 1.1 kg piece of meat perfectly, something a slow cooker could never achieve. It then handles everything without changing pans: sauce, covered simmering, shredding in the juices, and finally sealing the crunch wraps. All done in one pan from start to finish.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should ripple on the surface.
Sauté the onions and garlic for 5 minutes over medium heat, until translucent and fragrant.
Add the deseeded chilies, tomatoes, broth, enchilada sauce, and all the spices. Bring to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 10 minutes, allowing the chilies to rehydrate.
Transfer the contents of the pan to the blender. Blend until smooth, with no skin bits remaining. Set aside.

Wipe the pan clean, then return it to high heat with a little oil. Sear the steak on all sides for about 6 minutes total. Do not move it until it releases easily from the pan: this is the sign that the crust has formed.
Pour the sauce over the meat, cover and simmer over low heat for 40 minutes. A fork should pierce the meat easily.
Shred the meat (separate the fibers) using two forks, directly in the pan, and mix it with the sauce. Add the chopped coriander.

Assemble each crunchwrap: a large tortilla, shredded meat in the center, cheese, a spoonful of Greek yogurt, lettuce, diced tomatoes, then a small tortilla on top. Fold the edges of the large tortilla in even pleats towards the center.
Place the crunchwrap seam-side down in the hot pan for 2 minutes, until it seals. Flip and brown the other side for 2 minutes.
For meal prep: let cool completely, wrap in aluminum foil or a freezer bag, for up to 3 months. Omit the crispy tostada; it doesn't survive freezing.
Reheating: 4 to 5 minutes in the microwave, then 2 to 3 minutes per side in the hot titanium pan to restore the crispiness.

title: Almond-peanut bars with chocolate-coconut glaze
intro: It all comes down to the packing: a well-compacted base cuts cleanly and does not crumble under the icing.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: the chocolate melts over very low heat without sticking, the coconut milk is stirred in off the heat, and you pour directly from the pan. A single utensil to melt, blend, and glaze.
steps: In a rectangular dish, combine the almond flour, peanut butter, and maple syrup. Mix with a spoon until you obtain a smooth, pliable, and slightly sticky dough.
Add the chocolate chips. Mix again, gently, to distribute them without crushing them.
Press the dough firmly into the bottom of the dish with the back of a spoon. Work from the center outwards until you have a flat, dense surface. This compression is what holds the bar together.

Melt the chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly. This should take 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, pour in the coconut milk, and mix off the heat until smooth and glossy.
Pour the still-warm glaze over the pressed base. Tilt the dish to spread it to the corners.
Refrigerate until the icing is firm to the touch and no longer marks, about 2 hours.
Remove from mold and cut (into regular portions) into small bars, using a blade that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped between each cut.
Serve with fleur de sel, added at the last moment so that it still crunches between the teeth.

title: Sweet potato pizza with beef
intro: It all comes down to two distinct cooking methods: a sweet potato roasted long enough for its flesh to become dense and sweet, and beef seared hot enough to color without drying out.
titane: The pan never leaves the worktop: it roasts sweet potatoes in the oven, sears beef on the stovetop, holds the pizza base, and then returns to brown. Always preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the ghee: this preheating time prevents the meat from sticking and gives it a nice color.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Prick the whole sweet potato all over with a fork and place it in the titanium pan. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a knife inserted into the flesh meets no resistance and the skin begins to caramelize.
Remove the pan from the heat and transfer the sweet potato to a plate. Place the pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until a light smoke begins to rise.
Add the ghee, then the minced beef in a single layer. Season with salt. Do not touch anything for 3 to 4 minutes: the meat will stick at first, then detach on its own once a crust has formed.
Crumble the beef with a spatula and continue cooking for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned. Stop cooking while it's still pink in the center; it will finish cooking in the oven. Remove from the pan.
Cut the sweet potato in half, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and spread it directly in the pan to a thickness of 1 cm, pressing down to form a regular disc.
Distribute the beef, the sliced red onion, then the hand-torn mozzarella.
Bake the pan as is for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the edges of the disc are slightly crispy.
Drizzle with raw honey, sprinkle with chili flakes and serve in the pan.

title: Puffed quinoa bars
intro: It all comes down to the melting: chocolate that is melted too quickly loses its shine and turns grey when it cools.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. The chocolate starts cold, heats up with the metal, and you keep a close eye on it from beginning to end. No water buffer, so no respite: very low heat, spatula in constant motion. The quinoa is mixed in the same pan, off the heat.
steps: Break the chocolate into even pieces. Place them in the cold pan with the peanut butter.
Place over very low heat. Stir continuously from the first second, scraping the bottom of the pan. Allow 3 minutes: the chocolate should be melted, smooth and fluid, never smoking.
Remove from heat as soon as the mixture is homogeneous. Prolonged heat would cook the chocolate and make it grainy.
Pour the puffed quinoa into the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to coat each grain: the whole thing should be shiny and without any dry pockets.
Transfer to a rectangular mold. Press down evenly with a spatula to a depth of approximately 1.5 cm.
Leave to set in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Remove from the mold, then cut into squares with a smooth-bladed knife that has been rinsed under hot water and dried.

title: Crispy tofu in rice paper
intro: It all comes down to the coating: the rice paper, soaked in a spiced liquid and then pan-fried, dries into a thin and brittle shell.

ing.note: for basting and for the pan

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat on contact. No oven is needed: direct contact is enough to crisp the rice paper. Place the sticks on top, then leave them alone. When the surface is set, it will peel off easily. If it resists, it's too soon.
steps: Drain the tofu and dry it with a cloth. Cut it into 8 even sticks.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together the water, soy sauce, curry powder, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt. The mixture should remain liquid, barely cloudy.
Dip a sheet of rice paper in this liquid, as you would for a spring roll. A few seconds is enough: it should become pliable again without becoming sticky.
Cut the sheet in half and wrap each half-sheet tightly around a tofu stick. Repeat for all 8 sticks.
Lightly brush or spray each stick with grapeseed oil on all sides.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in a drizzle of oil: it should simmer without smoking.
Place the sticks loosely in the pan. Leave them undisturbed for 4 minutes. They will release easily once one side is cooked. Cook in two batches rather than overcrowding the pan.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist and continue on each side, about 8 minutes in total, until a regular golden color is achieved.
Reduce the heat to medium for the last 2 to 3 minutes, until the crispness is even and the rice paper doesn't burn. Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to prevent condensation.

title: Chicken tikka masala, smoothed cream cheese sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust: marinated chicken that browns nicely before going into the sauce, and the sauce that then absorbs everything the pan has retained.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature, allowing you to sear meat coated in dairy without it sticking. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, grease it, place the pieces inside, and then leave them alone: they will release on their own once a crust has formed. Next, combine the onion, tomatoes, cream, and blend everything in the same pan, without transferring anything.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts and thighs into 3 cm cubes. Mix them with the cream cheese, salt, and spices, then let them marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. The dairy acidifies the fibers and helps the flavors bind to the meat.
Place the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the fat: it should melt immediately without smoking.
Place the pieces in a single layer, without crowding them. Let them brown undisturbed. Turn them over only when they release easily and have a deep brown color. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped onion to the pan, then deglaze with a little stock (stirring up the browned bits stuck to the bottom). Stir until the bottom of the pan becomes clear again.
