Add the grated garlic and ginger, the concentrated tomato puree, then the pulp. Simmer uncovered over low heat for 10 minutes, until the sauce has reduced and darkened slightly.
Pour in the cream, then blend with an immersion blender directly in the pan until you obtain a smooth, coating texture. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the chicken and its juices to the sauce. Let it simmer gently for 10 minutes; the meat will finish cooking without drying out.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in salted water in a saucepan for about 15 minutes, and steam the courgette cut into half-rings or cook it in the same water at the end of cooking.
Arrange the rice and courgette, place the chicken pieces on top, and cover with sauce.

title: Quesadillas with seared ground beef and pickle sauce
intro: Everything hinges on the crust: a piece of meat spread out, motionless, which only comes off when it is ready.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold meat arrives. Spread the beef out, set a mental timer, and don't touch anything: a golden crust will form, and that's what releases the meat from the surface. The same logic applies to tortillas in the same wiped pan: don't move them, just wait for them to release.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then add the grapeseed oil or clarified butter: these fats withstand high temperatures without burning.
Fry the sliced onions in the hot fat until they are golden brown around the edges, 6 to 8 minutes. Remove them from the pan and set aside.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the ground beef and press it into an even layer across the bottom of the pan. Do not stir. Wait until the meat breaks down on its own: a brown crust will have formed.
Chop the meat directly in the pan, at the edge of a rigid spatula, into thin and irregular pieces.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in the reserved onions, garlic salt, pepper, smoked paprika, 115g of cheddar cheese, mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard. Mix until smooth and glossy, then remove from heat.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, chopped pickles, pickle juice, and pepper. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
Fill each tortilla with the filling and shredded cheddar cheese, then fold. This recipe makes 10 quesadillas.

Wipe the pan with paper towels and return it to medium heat. Brown the quesadillas on both sides, without moving them until they release easily. Remove them when the crust is crisp and the cheddar has melted. Serve with the sauce.

title: Goat's cheese cream, pan-roasted sweet potato and pistachios
intro: It all comes down to the first side: a sweet potato that colors before softening is nothing like a sweet potato that cooks in its own water.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in minutes and handles intense heat relentlessly. You get the caramelized crust of an oven roast, then cover to tenderize the center. One pan only, no oven to preheat.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Regularity matters more than exact size: uneven cubes won't end up together.

Pour the oil into the hot pan. Add the stock cubes, salt, and smoked paprika, then spread them out in a single layer. Don't overcrowd the pan: if the cubes overlap, they will release their water instead of browning. Do two batches if necessary.
Let it sear (brown over high heat, without stirring) until the cubes detach themselves from the bottom. As long as they stick, a crust has not formed.
Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. It's ready when a knife inserted into the center goes in easily. Transfer to a plate.
While cooking, finely chop the parsley and mint.
Blend the fresh goat cheese, yogurt, juice of half a lemon, half the herbs, salt and pepper, until smooth and homogeneous.

Spread the goat cheese cream on the back of a spoon in each plate. Place the still-warm sweet potato cubes on top, sprinkle with crushed pistachios and the remaining herbs. Season with pepper and salt, and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Chicken quesadillas with queso sauce
intro: It all comes down to two stages of cooking: a long, covered cooking that keeps the chicken moist, then a quick sear that gives the tortilla its crispy crust.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before oiling. Place the quesadilla in the pan and leave it untouched: no pressing with a spatula, no moving. The even heat of the titanium pan will do the work, and the quesadilla will release itself once the crust has formed. That's the signal, not a timer.
steps: In a bowl, combine the raw chicken with the taco seasoning, garlic salt, pepper, drained green chilies (reserve the juice), and lime juice. Massage to coat.

Place the chicken in a cold pan, pour over the chili juice, cover, and cook over low heat. Let it cook for about 60 minutes, stirring no more than two or three times. The chicken should be opaque throughout and tender when pierced with a fork.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, enchilada sauce, milk, salsa, and taco seasoning until smooth and grain-free.
Remove from heat and shred the chicken directly in the pan (separate the meat into strands using two forks). Let it cool slightly.
Incorporate the two mozzarella cheeses, pepper jack, queso sauce, pico de gallo, and cilantro. Mix until the filling is smooth and well combined.
Place a generous spoonful of filling on one half of each tortilla, then fold over. You will need 10 tortillas.
Empty and wipe the pan clean, return it to medium-high heat and preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Drizzle in a little oil and spread it evenly over the surface.
Place the quesadillas in pairs. Leave them untouched for 3 minutes: they will release on their own when the top is golden brown. Flip them over and cook for another 3 minutes.
Let cool on a wire rack, then wrap each quesadilla in aluminum foil.

title: Gluten-free walnut bread
intro: Gluten-free, it is the psyllium that holds the dough together: respect its gelling time, everything else depends on it.
titane: The titanium pan serves as the first cooking chamber. Covered and over moderate heat, it sears the base and forms a thick crust that the oven alone cannot produce. It then goes into the oven, uncovered, to cook the crumb thoroughly: you save on preheating time and get a crispier loaf.
steps: Pour the water over the psyllium in a bowl. Whisk for a few seconds, then let it gel (the psyllium absorbs the water and sets into a gel) for 5 minutes. The texture should become soft and elastic.
In a second container, combine the flour, yeast, bicarbonate of soda, and coarsely chopped walnuts. Mix together dry ingredients.
Incorporate the psyllium gel into the powders. Work first with a honing tool, then by hand.
Knead for 10 minutes, until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous ball that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Shape the dough into a round, slightly flattened loaf, the same diameter as your titanium pan. Lightly oil the pan with grapeseed oil.
Place the bread in the cold pan. Cover and cook over low to medium heat for 20 minutes. Do not attempt to turn it over until it releases itself from the bottom.
Flip it over with a flick of the wrist. Cover again and continue cooking for 15 minutes over the same heat, until the second side is golden brown.
Place the pan uncovered in the oven at 190°C for 20 minutes. The bread is cooked when the crust is amber and it sounds hollow when you tap (fingertip) on the bottom.
Remove from pan onto a wire rack and let cool completely before slicing: the crumb finishes structuring itself as it cools.

title: Chocolate protein ice cream with peanut swirl
intro: It's all about the texture: a well-hydrated base, a fairly long chilling period, and a marbling of melted peanut poured into the center of the pot rather than on the surface.
titane: The titanium pan serves only one purpose here: to melt the peanut butter chips with the coconut oil over very low heat. You watch the mixture change state, and you remove it from the heat as soon as it coats the spatula. The microwave heats in patches and solidifies the peanut butter into lumps; the pan allows you to stop the melting process with precision.
steps: Combine the protein shake, sweetener, cocoa, a pinch of salt, and xanthan gum in a tall container. Blend with an immersion blender until perfectly smooth, with no cocoa nibs remaining. The xanthan gum should be dispersed, not clumped.
Pour the base into the ice cream maker container. Close, place flat in the freezer, and leave for 16 hours. Overnight is not always enough: the base must be hard from edge to edge.
Run the outside of the pot under hot water for a full minute. The block should detach from the sides when you tilt the pot.
Place the container inside and start the reduced-fat ice cream program. At the end of the first cycle, the surface is often sandy: this is normal.
If the texture remains powdery, restart the cycle. You are looking for a homogeneous and glossy mass that holds its shape on the spoon.

Meanwhile, put the peanut butter chips, coconut oil, and a pinch of salt in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir constantly and lift the pan from the heat in short bursts: the mixture should melt, never simmer. Count to one minute. Remove from the pan as soon as it is smooth.
Using a butter knife, make a well in the center of the ice cream, all the way to the bottom of the container. Pour the still-warm melted mixture into it.
Start the incorporation cycle. The marbling should appear throughout the entire height, not just on the surface.
Sprinkle with chopped chocolate-peanut spread and serve immediately.

title: Beef rolls with cheddar shell
intro: It all comes down to the shell: cheddar melted until it bubbles, which detaches itself from the pan and encloses the filling in a golden crust.
titane: One pan for two contrasting uses. First, quickly sear beef over medium heat in a preheated, empty pan. Then, with the pan wiped clean and the heat reduced, slowly melt cheddar cheese. The rapid temperature rise of the titanium creates a smooth, even surface that releases easily, without sticking or needing to change pans.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.
Place the ground beef in the pan and let it brown without touching it. It will break apart on its own once a crust has formed; allow approximately 10 minutes in total, crumbling it gradually.
Season with garlic salt, onion powder and Italian seasoning. Mix.
Once the heat has evaporated, stir in the turkey pepperoni, minced garlic, tomato sauce, and parsley. Cook for another 2 minutes, until the sauce coats the meat.
Mix until you have a homogeneous stuffing, then remove from the pan and let it cool slightly.
Divide the filling into 10 portions. Fill each with mozzarella, seal, and roll into firm logs. Place them seam-side up.
Wipe the pan clean. Over low heat, spread the cheddar in an even layer and let it melt for 3 minutes, until it bubbles across the entire surface.
Place the rolls seam-side down on the melted cheddar. Do not move them: the shell will form and detach itself from the pan.
Flip it over with a quick movement and cook the other side until the cheese is golden and crispy.
Let cool on a wire rack, crispy side up.
Wrap each roll in aluminum foil or a sealed freezer bag. Store in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Pumpkin and carrot puree, soft-boiled egg and parmesan
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the puree: enough body to hold under the egg, enough flexibility to coat the spoon.
titane: One pan from start to finish. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it receives the vegetables and a little water, covered: the short steam softens them without drowning them. Rinsed, it then receives less than 300 ml of water for soft-boiled eggs. No steamer, no saucepan.
steps: Peel the squash, remove the seeds, and cut the flesh into 2 cm cubes. Peel the carrots and cut them into thin slices.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the clarified butter or grapeseed oil. The even heat distribution prevents the vegetables from sticking.

Add the squash and carrots, 2 to 3 tablespoons of water, and cover. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. The pieces should be very tender and easily mashed with a fork.
Remove the vegetables (transfer them from the pan) to the blender bowl. Rinse the pan.
Bring 250 ml of water to a boil in the pan, plunge in the eggs and cook for exactly 6 minutes 30 seconds.
Transfer them immediately to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking, then peel them (remove the shell) once they are cold.
Roughly chop the walnuts, finely chop the chives, and set aside.
Blend the vegetables with the olive oil, half the milk, salt, pepper, and smoked paprika until smooth. Gradually add the remaining milk until you reach the desired consistency.
Make parmesan shavings using a vegetable peeler.
Divide the purée between two bowls, place the halved eggs on top, then the walnuts, shavings and chives. Adjust the seasoning.

title: Buffalo chicken orzo
intro: It all comes down to two things: a good crust on the chicken, and a sauce added off the heat so that it doesn't curdle.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly: preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The chicken will stick at first, then release easily once a crust has formed—this is the only reliable indicator for turning it. The juices (caramelized deposits left at the bottom of the pan) then remain in place and flavor the orzo, which is cooking in the same pan.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, buffalo sauce, cream cheese, 14g of ranch and 4g of pepper until smooth and grain-free. Refrigerate.
Place the breasts between two sheets of cling film, flatten them with a rolling pin or on the bottom of a pan until they are an even thickness. A consistent thickness ensures even cooking.
Mix together garlic salt, ranch dressing, smoked paprika, onion powder, and pepper. Coat the chicken on all sides, leaving no bare areas.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the oil: it should ripple on the surface.
Place the chicken in the pan without packing it down, in batches if necessary. Do not touch it. Turn it over when it releases easily, then continue cooking until it is cooked through.
Remove from the pan and set aside. Let rest for 5 minutes, then slice or shred.
In the same pan, using the juices, sauté onions and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat, until translucent.

Add the dry orzo and broth. Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring regularly to loosen any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. The orzo should be tender and the liquid absorbed.
Stir in the mozzarella. Remove from the heat and let cool for 5 minutes, then add the buffalo sauce and mix. If added too hot, it will become grainy.
Divide into 10 portions, place the chicken on top, and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Chill quickly before sealing the containers and freezing.

title: Pan-fried sunflower seed bread
intro: Without flour or yeast, this bread owes its crumb to two things: a fairly fine seed powder and sufficient resting of the psyllium, which structures the dough in place of gluten.

ing.note: plus 1 heaping tablespoon for the topping

titane: A covered pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty, it sears the bottom of the galette and creates a crust in minutes; the lid then traps the steam and steams the dough (cooking in its own moisture, covered), causing it to puff up. A single, decisive flip halfway through cooking.
steps: Blend the 200g of sunflower seeds for 30 seconds, until you obtain a fine powder similar to flour. Stop as soon as the texture is homogeneous: beyond this point, the seeds release their oil and the powder compacts.
Add the eggs and salt. Mix until smooth.
Incorporate the psyllium. Work for about thirty seconds: the dough will thicken and become elastic, stretching without breaking. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Moisten your hands, then shape into a ball. Flatten it into a disc the same diameter as the bottom of your pan, about 3 cm thick.
Scatter whole sunflower seeds on top and press them lightly with the palm of your hand so they stick.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should ripple without smoking.

Place the galette on the pan, cover, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 minutes without touching it. The bread will easily detach from the bottom when it's cooked through: that's the signal.
Flip it over with a flick of the wrist. Cover again and continue for 10 minutes, until it is puffed up, golden brown on both sides and sounds hollow when tapped with the tip of your finger.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool for 15 minutes before slicing. If cut too hot, it will crumble.

title: Butternut squash pancakes with cheese and a fried egg
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the puree: well drained, it gives soft pancakes that hold their shape without collapsing.
ing: 400g of butternut squash, peeled and cut into

ing.note: plus a little bit for the service

ing: egg per person for the fried egg
titane: Preheat the pan empty, for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the pancakes brown all over, and the egg cooked afterward gets crisp edges in the same pan, without anything sticking.
steps: Steam the squash cubes for 20 minutes, until a knife tip pierces them without resistance.
Mash them with a fork, then let them cool uncovered to evaporate the moisture. You should end up with about 360g of purée.
Grate the cheese.
In a bowl, combine the lukewarm mashed potatoes, milk, eggs, flour, yeast, cheese and chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk until you obtain a smooth, lump-free batter. It should fall heavily from the spoon.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil or clarified butter.
Place 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake, spacing them apart. Do not touch them again.
Wait until the bottom releases easily from the pan, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook for another 2 minutes on the other side, gradually reducing the heat. Transfer to a warm plate and set aside.
Repeat with the remaining batter, in the same pan, adding a little more fat between each batch.
Turn up the heat, grease lightly, crack the eggs and let them set without moving them: the white should be set, the yolk still liquid.
Arrange the pancakes, place an egg on top, add chives and pepper.

title: Pan-fried cookie & cream waffles
intro: Without a waffle iron, everything depends on the heat of the pan: hot enough to crust the surface, stable enough for the center to finish setting.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold paste is applied. This thermal shock solidifies the underside into a golden crust: the disc then detaches easily, without the need for a spatula or any resistance. Preheat empty for 2 to 3 minutes, no less.
steps: Whisk the egg with the almond milk in a bowl. Add the flour, baking powder, stevia, and salt. Mix until the batter is smooth and lump-free.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly on the surface.

Spoon a ladleful of batter into the center and let it spread into a thick disc. Leave it undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes. When the edges start to lift and the disc slides easily, flip it over and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Repeat this process, disc by disc, to maintain control over the cooking time.
Meanwhile, smooth the cottage cheese with the whey using a whisk until you obtain a smooth cream with no traces of powder.
Coat (cover with an even layer) the still-warm discs with cream and serve immediately.

title: Crispy tofu glazed with gochujang
intro: It's all about patience: the tofu should only be turned over once the crust has formed, never before.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold pieces are added. The crust forms dry and even with very little fat. The same pan then reduces the glaze: the juices from the searing pass directly into the sauce, without transfer or the need for a second container.
steps: Press the tofu for 20 minutes between two cloths, under a weighted plate. Cut it into 2.5 cm cubes: the more sides, the more crust.
Mix the cornstarch and spices in a bowl.
Roll each cube in the mixture. Each side should be matte, without any wet areas.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, before adding any fat.

Pour the oil over the cubes, then arrange them in a single layer, leaving space between them. Let them sear without touching them. After 3 to 4 minutes, they will release easily: that's the signal. Turn them over and brown the other sides, for a total of 8 minutes.
Remove the tofu from the pan and place it in a bowl. Keep the pan on the heat, then reduce the heat to medium.
Pour in the soy sauce, gochujang, vinegar and agave syrup. Scrape the bottom to collect the juices.
Let it reduce for 2 minutes while stirring, until the sauce coats the spoon (leaves a clear trace when you run your finger along the back of the spoon).
Return the tofu to the pan, coat with a flick of the wrist, and cook for 1 minute. Serve immediately: the crust softens quickly.

title: Feta and pan-roasted figs
intro: Everything hinges on the first three minutes: a feta seared before the oven develops a golden crust that a simple dish-bake will never produce.
ing: dried thyme or 3 sprigs of fresh thyme
titane: The pan heats up empty for two to three minutes, allowing the titanium to reach a consistent temperature. This is what allows you to sear the block of feta and the figs over medium-high heat, then slide the pan directly into the middle of the oven. A single container goes from stovetop to oven, with no heat loss during the transfer.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F), conventional setting. Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut each fig into six wedges. Roughly chop the pistachios with a knife.
Pour the olive oil into the hot pan. Place the block of feta in the center, the figs around it, cut side down.

Sear (cook over high heat to brown the surface without cooking the center) for 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without stirring. The feta is ready when it pulls away from the bottom of the pan on its own and the base begins to brown.
Add salt, pour the honey over the feta, sprinkle with pistachios and thyme.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven for 15 minutes. The feta should be melted in the center and the figs softened, glistening with their juices.
Season with pepper when it comes out of the oven. Serve in the pan, with toasted country bread and a green salad with olive oil.

title: Chocolate-coconut cream with a hint of peanut
intro: Two ingredients, no real cooking: everything depends on the temperature of the milk, which must melt the chocolate without ever overheating it.
titane: The titanium pan heats the coconut milk quickly and evenly, without creating a hot spot at the bottom. This prevents the chocolate from grainy (separating into small, granular lumps) when you stir it in. Heating and mixing are done in the same container: you don't need to take anything else out.
steps: Pour the coconut milk into the cold pan. Heat gently, stirring, for about 3 minutes. Stop as soon as the surface begins to simmer: the milk should not boil.
Remove the pan from the heat. Break the chocolate into pieces and plunge them directly into the hot milk.
Wait one minute, then mix off the heat until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream, with no trace of unmelted chocolate.
Transfer (out of the cooking container) into four ramekins.
Place a small dollop of peanut butter on the surface of each and swirl it into a spiral with the tip of a knife or a stick.
Place in the refrigerator for a minimum of 4 hours. A full night gives a significantly firmer hold.

title: Hazelnut-cocoa balls
intro: It all comes down to roasting: a raw hazelnut gives a flat paste, a golden hazelnut gives aroma.
titane: Heat the pan empty for two minutes over medium heat before adding the hazelnuts. The heat is then already distributed across the entire surface: the nuts brown evenly instead of burning in the center. No oil is needed; titanium dioxide is enough.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Pour the hazelnuts into a single layer. Dry roast them for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring frequently. They should brown lightly and become fragrant. Stop as soon as the aroma intensifies.
Remove them immediately (transfer them from the pan) to a cold plate. Let them cool for 5 minutes; otherwise, the pan will continue to cook them.
Blend them into a fine powder using short pulses. If you continue, the powder will turn into a puree.
Add the maple syrup and cocoa. Mix until you get a sticky dough that holds its shape between your fingers.
Shape into 8 balls by hand, pressing firmly. Refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm up.

title: Oatmeal porridge with melted banana
intro: It all comes down to the cold start: the flakes swell in the water as the temperature rises, and the banana melts instead of browning.

ing.note: piece (half sliced into rounds for cooking)
cc, to be adjusted according to your taste

titane: The frying pan offers a much larger, flat surface than a saucepan: the porridge spreads in a thin layer, evaporation is even, and thickening occurs more quickly, without any sticking in the center. With just 200 ml of liquid, the process is straightforward—no adjustments needed. Cooking and plating are done in the same pan.
steps: With the pan still cold and off the heat, add the oats, slices of half a banana, cinnamon, vanilla, sugar, and salt. Pour in the water and stir to ensure no oats remain dry.

Turn on the heat to medium. Cook for 7 minutes, stirring frequently with a flexible spatula: the titanium pan heats up quickly and the heat covers the entire surface, so keep a close eye on it. The mixture is ready when it coats the spatula (leaving a layer that doesn't drip) and pulls away cleanly from the bottom.
Remove from heat. Stir in the milk, then the fromage frais, and work briskly for 30 seconds. The fromage frais should not cook: it's what gives it its creamy texture.
Pour directly into a bowl. Distribute the second half of the banana slices, the blueberries, the crushed pistachios and a dollop of spread.

title: Tomato sauce thickened with white beans
intro: A tomato sauce that gains body and structure without cream or flour thickening: everything depends on the fineness of the bean puree, which must disappear completely.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before pouring in the mixture. The heat rises quickly and spreads evenly from one side to the other: the sauce thickens without sticking, without needing an extra pan.
steps: Drain the white beans and rinse them in cold water. Blend them on their own until perfectly smooth. No lumps should remain: this is what makes the addition invisible in the mouth.
Place the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Test: a few drops of water should bead and roll on the surface.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour in the tomato sauce and bean purée. Stir with a spatula, bringing the mixture from the edge towards the center, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and simmering gently.
Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove from heat or use directly over pasta.

title: Peanut udon noodles, zucchini spaghetti, and crispy smoked tofu
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the sauce: thick enough to coat the udon, flexible enough not to stick to the courgette.
titane: One pan, two zones. Heated high and dry, it sears the garlic and ginger in seconds without sticking. The udon noodles then finish cooking over low heat on one side, while the tofu sticks brown on the other, placed there and left undisturbed: they release themselves once the crust is formed.
steps: Use a spiralizer to create long spaghetti-like strands. If you don't have a spiralizer, cut it into julienne strips (thin, even strips).
Mince the garlic and ginger.
If you are working with dried udon noodles, cook them in a pot of water according to the package instructions, then drain. Set aside.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in a drizzle of sesame oil, add the garlic and ginger, and stir until fragrant.
Reduce heat to medium-high. Add the soy sauce, peanut butter, and hot water. Stir until smooth.
Add the udon noodles and zucchini. Cook over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce should coat the noodles; add a little hot water if it becomes too thick.

Push everything to one side of the pan. Heat the remaining area over medium-high heat with a drizzle of sesame oil, place the tofu sticks in the pan, and leave them undisturbed. Cook for approximately 7 minutes, turning them only when they release easily.
Roughly chop the peanuts with a knife.
Divide the noodles and zucchini between two bowls. Place the sticks on top, sprinkle with peanuts and chopped parsley, and squeeze in half a lime just before serving.

title: Tahini yogurt, caramelized tomatoes and a soft-boiled egg
intro: It all comes down to the tomato juice: it must be reduced to a syrupy consistency, because it's what seasons the yogurt on the plate.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The even heat distribution of the titanium caramelizes the tomatoes directly on the stovetop, without going through the oven, and concentrates their juices in about ten minutes. Arrange them in a single layer: an overcrowded pan will steam, not caramelize.
steps: Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the olive oil. Add the halved cherry tomatoes, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt. Arrange them in a single layer, cut side down.
Let it cook undisturbed. The tomatoes will detach on their own once caramelized. Then stir occasionally, for a total of 10 minutes, until the juices become syrupy.
Remove (transfer from the pan) the tomatoes into a bowl with all the cooking juices.
Meanwhile, place the eggs in a saucepan of simmering water. Allow 6 minutes 30 seconds for a runny yolk.
Transfer them immediately to a bowl of ice water, then peel them (remove the shell).
Mix the yogurt with the tahini, a pinch of salt, a dash of lemon juice and the zest of half a lemon.
Spread the yogurt in the bottom of two bowls. Place the tomatoes, the halved egg, and drizzle with the cooking juices.
Season with pepper, sprinkle with sesame seeds and chopped mint. Serve immediately.

title: Pan-fried glazed tofu popcorn
intro: It all comes down to the crust: tofu torn by hand, seared without being touched, then glazed in the same pan.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two to three minutes when empty, which is enough to crisp the tofu without using an oven or air fryer. Once the pieces are set aside, the glaze reduces in the same pan, incorporating the juices from the searing. A single utensil, from start to finish.
steps: Drain the block of tofu and press it briefly between two sheets of paper towel. Tear it by hand into walnut-sized pieces. The irregular edges will hold the sauce much better than if cut with a knife.
In a bowl, combine the cornstarch, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the tofu and gently stir until each piece is coated with the powder.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should dance on it before evaporating.
Pour the oil over the tofu, then arrange the pieces in a single layer. Leave space between them; if they touch, they will steam. Cook in two batches if necessary.
Don't touch anything. Allow about ten minutes in total: the tofu will release itself once the crust is formed. Then turn the pieces over, one side at a time, to brown them on all sides.
Remove (transfer from the pan) the tofu to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. In the still-hot pan, pour in the water, soy sauce, maple syrup, ketchup, brown sugar, then add the margarine. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a spatula to dissolve any browned bits.
Let it reduce for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon and is glossy.
Return the tofu to the pan and stir for 1 minute, no more: just enough time for the coating to set, before the crust gets soggy.
Divide into two portions. For meal prep, let it cool uncovered before closing the containers, otherwise the steam will make everything soggy.

title: Potatoes with garlic cream, quick vegan bolognese
intro: Everything hinges on the first cooking: wedges placed in a single layer, covered, and left alone until they detach on their own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat under the lid: it replaces the oven for crisping potatoes while keeping the center tender. It then sears textured protein and reduces the sauce. One pan, three cooking methods, no oven required.
steps: Cover the textured protein with boiling water, let it soak for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze between your hands to remove excess water.
Cut the potatoes into even wedges, without peeling them. Evenness ensures even cooking.
Coat them with smoked paprika, herbs, salt, pepper and oil.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a fat with a high smoke point (grapeseed or clarified butter). It should simmer, never smoke.

Arrange the wedges in a single layer, cover, and reduce the heat to medium. Cook for about 20 minutes, turning only when they easily pull away from the bottom of the pan. The crust should be golden brown on the outside and tender inside.
Meanwhile, whisk the plant-based cream with the nutritional yeast, garlic, salt, pepper and plant-based cheese if you are using it.
Remove the potatoes from the pan, reduce the heat to low, and return them briefly with the garlic cream until coated. Set aside.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper, preheat it empty, add a drizzle of oil. Sear the textured protein over high heat without stirring: it will brown and release from the pan on its own.
Deglaze (dissolve the juices from the bottom with a liquid) with soy sauce, pour in the tomato sauce, simmer for 10 minutes over medium heat until the sauce coats the spoon.
Divide the potatoes and Bolognese sauce between the containers, allowing them to cool uncovered before closing.

title: Turkey, courgette and mushroom risotto
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the turkey browns first, then the rice benefits from the juices left at the bottom.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. This thorough preheating does two things: it allows the turkey to caramelize and then release itself from the pan, and it keeps the surface smooth enough so the rice doesn't stick during the 20 minutes of cooking. Never change pans.
steps: Finely chop the onion. Dice the zucchini and quarter the mushrooms. Keep the broth warm nearby.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil or clarified butter.

Place the turkey in the pan, season with salt, and leave it alone. It will release easily once a crust has formed: this is the signal to turn it over. Finish cooking over medium-high heat, then remove it from the pan and keep it covered.
Reduce the heat to medium. Sauté the onion, then the zucchini and mushrooms, until they release their juices and become soft. The turkey juices will loosen up in the process.

Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, until it becomes translucent around the edges. Add a ladleful of hot broth and let it absorb before adding the next. Cook for approximately 18 minutes, stirring regularly, until the rice is creamy but still slightly firm to the bite.
Cut the turkey into pieces. Mix it into the rice along with the Parmesan, mustard, and cream cheese. Stir well to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with mozzarella, cover and leave off the heat for 5 minutes. Serve in the pan.

title: Pan-fried buffalo chicken turnovers
intro: It all comes down to two cooking steps in the same pan: a chicken seared and then finished covered, and a yogurt pastry spread thin enough to brown before the filling gets too hot.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes, then add a high-smoke-point fat. The rapid heat-up of the titanium pan eliminates the need for hours in a slow cooker: the chicken is seared and then cooked, covered, in 25 minutes. For the turnovers, don't move them for the first few minutes. The lack of a coating results in a crisp, dry crust, and the pastry will release easily when it's ready. That's the only indicator you need to follow.
steps: Season the chicken breasts with garlic salt, smoked paprika, ranch spices and pepper.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Add a drizzle of high smoke point oil and sear the chicken without touching it. Turn it over when it releases easily.
Add the onion and salsa, cover and cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes depending on the thickness, until fully cooked through.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, buffalo sauce, milk, garlic salt, pepper and onion powder until smooth.

Remove the pan from the heat and shred the chicken (separating the meat into strands using two forks) directly into the warm pan. Stir in the protein-enriched buffalo sauce, the remaining 120g of buffalo sauce, half the mozzarella cheese, and the chives. Transfer to a separate container and let cool slightly.
Mix the flour, yogurt, garlic salt and Italian herbs by hand until you get a crumbly mixture.
Knead for 5 minutes, until the dough becomes smooth and supple. Divide it into 10 equal portions and shape them into balls.
Roll out each ball very thinly into an oval. A thick dough would remain raw in the center.
Fill one half of each oval with shredded chicken and the remaining mozzarella, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold over and pinch firmly to seal.

Clean the pan, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add a drizzle of oil or butter. Cook the turnovers over medium heat, seam-side up, without moving them. Turn them over when they release easily and brown the other side. Allow approximately 10 minutes total per batch.

title: Beetroot, date and almond balls
intro: The beetroot provides moisture and color, the date provides sugar: the key is to cook it covered, which dries the surface without drying out the center.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty and then lightly greased, it diffuses a gentle heat that the lid reflects back onto the tops of the balls: the surface develops a thin, praline-flavored crust while the inside remains soft. The indicator is simple: the balls release easily when they are ready to be turned over.
steps: Cover the dates with hot water and let them soak for 10 minutes. Drain them, then gently squeeze them between your fingers.
Cut the beetroot into large pieces and put it in the blender bowl. Add the dates.
Pulse until you obtain a coarse puree, with no residual liquid at the bottom of the bowl.
Add the almond flour and mix again until you have a smooth dough that holds its shape when pressed with your finger. If it's too sticky, let it rest in the refrigerator for 5 minutes.
Shape into balls the size of a walnut. Roll them in the flaked almonds or sprinkle them on top, pressing them in to make them stick.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with a film of clarified butter or grapeseed oil, then reduce the heat to low.
Place the balls well spaced apart, without overcrowding the pan. Cover and cook for 7 to 8 minutes.
Gently turn them over when they detach on their own, using a flexible spatula. Cover again and continue for 7 minutes.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool slightly. The texture will set as it cools.

title: Polenta au gratin with beef Bolognese sauce
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the meat first browns without being touched, then the polenta takes its place on the same wiped-off juices, and the gratin is done under a lid.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter

ing.note: Dried oregano, smoked paprika, sweet chili

titane: Leave the beef still for the first few minutes on a preheated pan: it will release easily once a crust has formed, and it's this caramelization that gives the sauce its depth of flavor. Then, wipe the pan with paper towels before adding the polenta—the starch will stick to any remaining juices. Finally, use the same pan as a gratin dish, with the lid on and the heat on low.
steps: Dice the onion and carrot into small, even pieces. Mince the garlic. Pick the basil leaves.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the fat: it should simmer and remain clear, without smoking.

Place the beef in a single layer, then add the vegetables and garlic on top. Leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes. When the meat starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan, stir and cook for another 3 minutes.

Add the chopped tomatoes, 200ml of water and the stock. Season and add the spices. Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon without releasing any liquid.
Add the chopped basil off the heat, then transfer the Bolognese sauce to a shallow dish.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Gradually whisk in the polenta, 250 ml of water, a pinch of salt, and any leftover stock. Stir over low heat, then add the remaining water in two or three additions, waiting for it to be absorbed each time. Cook for 10 minutes: the polenta should be creamy and fall slowly from the spoon.
Smooth the polenta in the pan, top with Bolognese sauce, and sprinkle with mozzarella.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 5 minutes, until the cheese melts and stretches. Serve in the pan.

title: Raw brownie with chickpeas and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to two things: a base that is blended long enough to lose all traces of grain, and chocolate that is melted off the heat, never heated directly.

ing.note: rehydrated for 10 minutes in hot water

titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for ganache (chocolate melted in a hot liquid). Its rapid and even heat distribution allows you to bring the coconut milk to a simmer without any hot spots, then remove the pan from the heat: the residual heat in the metal is enough to melt the chocolate. No lumps, no burnt chocolate at the bottom.
steps: Drain the dates. Blend them with the chickpeas and cocoa for 5 minutes, scraping down the sides halfway through. The paste should be thick, smooth, with no noticeable lumps on the tongue.
Transfer the mixture to a rectangular dish. Spread it to a thickness of approximately 2 cm, press down with a spatula, and smooth the surface.
Pour the coconut milk into the titanium pan. Heat gently until it just begins to simmer, without ever letting it boil.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the chopped dark chocolate. Wait 1 minute, then stir from the center outwards until the mixture is glossy and perfectly smooth.
Pour the still-warm ganache over the chickpea base. Tilt the dish to spread it in an even layer.
Refrigerate overnight. It's set when the ganache is firm to the touch. Cut into squares with a knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between cuts.

title: 'Three no-oven snacks: almond, peanut, chocolate'
intro: Three preparations that fit on a single tray and a little bit of cold: what matters here is the texture, therefore respecting the setting times.
titane: For almond cookies, a covered titanium pan can replace the oven for a small batch. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, add a drizzle of high-smoke oil, place the cookies in the pan, and cover. Don't touch them: they will release on their own when the bottom is set. That's the only sign you need to wait for.
steps: Work the almond flour with the maple syrup until you obtain a soft and homogeneous paste that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Take even portions, roll them into balls, then flatten them slightly with the back of a fork.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of high smoke point oil.

Place the biscuits in the pan, cover, and cook over low to medium heat for about ten minutes. When they release easily and the bottoms are golden brown, turn them over and cook the other side. Transfer them to a wire rack to cool.
For the bars, combine the rolled oats, peanut butter, maple syrup, and salt. Press this mixture into the bottom of a baking pan lined with parchment paper.
Melt the coconut oil, then stir it into the melted peanut butter and maple syrup. The caramel should remain runny.
Pour it onto the base, smooth it out, and place in the freezer for one hour, until it is firm to the touch.

Melt the dark chocolate, mix it with the peanut butter and salt. Spread over the cold surface, let it set for two minutes, then cut into bars with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry.
Keep the bars in the freezer: they will keep for several months and are best eaten when barely at room temperature.
For the cups, mix together the almond flour, peanut butter and maple syrup, then add the chocolate chips without crushing them.
Press the dough into molds or a small mold, packing the edges down well.
Melt the chocolate, loosen it with coconut milk until you get a smooth ganache, and cover.
Refrigerate for one hour, until the topping has set.

title: Oat and applesauce pie crust
intro: Two ingredients, no fat: everything hinges on the slow drying of the dough, which must lose its moisture without browning.
titane: The covered pan works like an oven: the heat circulates under the lid and envelops the dough, but you maintain control over the browning of the bottom at all times. The end signal isn't the timer, it's the edges pulling away from the sides on their own. As long as they're sticking, the dough still contains too much water.
steps: Combine the oats and applesauce in a bowl. Mix with a spatula until well combined, with no dry flakes remaining. Let it rest for 5 minutes: the oats will absorb the liquid and the dough will firm up.

Pour the mixture into the still-cold titanium pan. Press it down with the back of a spoon over the entire surface, then push it up a 2 cm border against the side. Even out the thickness of the base; the more even it is, the better the cooking will be.
Place over low heat and cover. Let it dry (evaporate the moisture over low heat) for 18 minutes. The surface will no longer be sticky and the edges will begin to shrink.
Remove the lid. Continue cooking for 4 minutes over low heat to firm up the base. Gently lift one edge with a spatula: it should come away easily.
Turn off the heat and let it cool completely in the pan before unmolding. It is during this time that the dough sets properly.

title: Chocolate and cashew fudge
intro: It all comes down to how the chocolate melts: if it's too hot, it cuts through the cashew cream, and if it's cold, the fudge releases oil.

ing.note: soaked for 30 minutes in hot water then rinsed

titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its conductivity distributes heat evenly without hot spots: the chocolate melts in three minutes over very low heat, with constant monitoring, and you can keep your hand on the whisk from start to finish. No need to preheat the pan; the chocolate goes into it cold or barely warm.
steps: Cover the cashews with hot water and let them soak for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse with clean water, and set aside.
Chop the chocolate into even pieces with a knife. The finer they are, the faster and more evenly it will melt.

Pour the chocolate into the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula or small whisk. Cook for 3 minutes: the chocolate should be perfectly smooth and fluid, never smoking. Remove from the heat at this point.
Place the drained cashews, plant-based milk, and agave syrup in the blender bowl. Pour the melted chocolate over the top.
Blend at full power until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream, with no grains remaining on the tongue. Scrape down the sides once or twice during the process.
Transfer to a baking pan lined with parchment paper, or into individual molds. Smooth the surface.
Leave to set in the refrigerator overnight. The fudge will unmold cleanly and remain firm, almost crunchy, when removed from the refrigerator.

title: Tomato tarte tatin with sheep's milk cheese
intro: It all comes down to the balsamic caramel: cooked enough to coat, yet soft enough for the tomatoes to sit on without slipping.
titane: The caramel rises over medium heat in the pan, the tomatoes are arranged on top, the batter is poured over everything, and the pan goes straight into the oven without being moved. When unmolding, the caramelized base came away easily: a quarter turn of the wrist was all it took.
steps: Combine flour, butter, egg, water and salt in a bowl. Knead until you obtain a smooth ball, without overworking.
Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes. The dough can be kept at this stage for up to 24 hours.
Cut the tomatoes into even slices of half a centimeter. Place them for a few minutes on absorbent paper to remove excess water.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Set the oven to 190°C (375°F), conventional setting.
Pour the olive oil into the hot pan, add the balsamic glaze, honey, and salt. Stir for 2 minutes: the caramel should become fluid and smooth. Remove from the heat.
Arrange the tomato slices on the caramel in a tight rosette. Cut more pieces to fill the gaps: the surface should be full.
Grate the sheep's milk cheese and spread it over the tomatoes.
Roll out the dough (spread it out with a rolling pin) into a disc that is 4 to 5 cm larger than the diameter of the pan.
Place the pastry on the filling, fold the edges towards the inside of the pan to seal, then prick the surface with a fork.
Place the pan in the oven as is, without a lid, in the middle of the oven. Bake for 37 minutes, until the pastry is thoroughly golden brown.
Remove the pan and let it cool for 3 minutes. Place a serving dish on top of the pan and flip it over in one swift motion: the tart will detach easily.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme leaves and serve warm.

title: Beetroot pancakes, savory or sweet version
intro: These gluten-free pancakes hold together solely through the strength of rice and chickpea flours: everything depends on the batter resting and a really hot pan.

ing.note: g, juice from the preserved sachet

titane: Titanium heats up faster than a conventional pan: the batter cooks instantly, a crust forms, and the pancake releases itself. As a result, very little oil is needed, there's no sticking, and the whole batch can be cooked in the same pan. The oven is only used to keep them warm.
steps: Combine the two flours, yeast, bicarbonate and salt in a bowl. Whisk to distribute the dry ingredients.
Drain the beetroot over a bowl and keep the juice from the sachet. Add the diced beetroot and this juice to the powders: the color will come from both the liquid and the flesh.
Pour in the plant-based milk, oil, and egg. Blend with a blender or immersion blender until you obtain a smooth, uniformly pink paste.
Place the bowl in the refrigerator for about ten minutes while you prepare the toppings. This resting time hydrates the flours and results in a less crumbly pancake.
Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It should be hot before adding the first drop of oil.
Pour in the grapeseed oil, wipe off the excess with paper, then pour a small ladleful of batter onto each pancake. Reduce the heat to low to medium.
Do not touch it. Wait until the surface bubbles have burst and the disc detaches itself from the pan, then turn it over and count 1 to 2 minutes on the other side.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a plate and keep in a warm oven while you cook the rest in the same pan.

title: Poached eggs, roasted sweet potato and lemon-flavored fromage blanc
intro: It all comes down to two textures: cubes of sweet potato that are truly caramelized, and an egg white that has just been set on a still-liquid yolk.

ing.note: skyr or ricotta are also suitable)

titane: The empty pan replaces the oven. The sweet potato cubes touch a surface that's already scorching hot, the sugars concentrate in a few minutes, then the lid finishes cooking them through. Wipe the pan, pour in 400 ml of water: the same utensil becomes a poaching basin. One wash is all it takes for the whole dish.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the olive oil.
Meanwhile, peel the sweet potato and cut it into one-centimeter cubes, as regular as possible: this ensures simultaneous cooking.
In a bowl, roll the cubes in the spices and salt until they are evenly coated.

Pour them into the hot pan in a single layer. Let them brown without touching them: the cubes will release on their own when the top is golden. Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and continue cooking for 20 minutes, stirring every 4 or 5 minutes.
Remove the cubes from the pan and place them on a plate, then cover them to keep them warm.
Whisk the fromage blanc with the lemon zest and juice, chives, salt and pepper. Keep chilled while poaching.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Pour in 400 ml of water and the vinegar, and heat over medium heat until simmering. Reduce the heat immediately: the titanium cast iron retains heat and the water would boil.
Crack each egg into an individual ramekin. Create a whirlpool in the water with a spoon, slide an egg into the center, and cook for 2 minutes. The white should be set, the yolk still soft.
Drain the egg on absorbent paper and repeat with the other three, one by one.

Spread the lemon-flavored fromage blanc on the bottom of the plates, add the sweet potato cubes, and place two eggs on each plate. Finish with fresh thyme, a drizzle of chili oil, and a grind of pepper.

title: Chocolate and banana fudge
intro: Just two ingredients: everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas and on melting the chocolate gently enough so that it remains smooth.

ing.note: approximately 200g of flesh, skin speckled with

titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without a double boiler. The coating distributes the heat evenly, preventing hot spots: nothing sticks or sears. The banana puree is added to the same pan, and you only need to transfer the mixture to another container once, to pour it into the mold.
steps: Peel the bananas and blend them until you obtain a perfectly smooth puree, without any strings or pieces. Set aside.

Place the titanium pan over very low heat and pour in the chocolate. Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the edges towards the center. Allow a few minutes: the chocolate should be melted, shiny and fluid, never smoking.
Remove the pan from the heat. Pour the banana puree over the chocolate and mix thoroughly until the mixture is smooth and glossy. It will thicken immediately: this is normal.
Pour into a 15cm square baking tin lined with baking paper. Smooth the surface with a spatula and tap the tin once on the work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Place in the refrigerator overnight, or at least 8 hours. The chilling process is what gives it the fudge texture: if it's not done properly, it will leave a soft consistency.
Remove from the mold by pulling on the paper, then cut into 2 cm cubes with a thin-bladed knife that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Coconut-chocolate ganache, peanut marbling
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the coconut milk: warm, never boiling, otherwise the emulsion separates and the ganache becomes grainy.
titane: The titanium pan heats coconut milk quickly and without hot spots, then becomes the working container: melt the chocolate off the heat, pipe the design, and let it set in the refrigerator. Its thinness dissipates heat rapidly, accelerating the setting process.
steps: Pour the coconut milk into the pan. Heat gently, stirring, for about 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as small bubbles appear around the edge: the milk should not boil.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the chopped chocolate all at once and let it melt for 30 seconds without touching it.

Mix in the center using small circles, then gradually widen to the edge. The mixture should bind into a smooth, glossy ganache, about 3 minutes. If it appears grainy, add a tablespoon of warm coconut milk and stir again from the center.
Smooth the surface. Drizzle the peanut butter in thin lines on top, then draw crosswise lines with the tip of a knife to marble (bring two materials into each other without mixing them).
Place the pan in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. The ganache is ready when it feels firm to the touch.

title: Three chocolate snacks in the blender, one pan
intro: Three oven-free recipes, the success of which depends on one single point: melting the chocolate gently in an empty, preheated pan, without ever rushing it.

ing.note: rehydrated for 10 minutes in hot water

titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan over low heat for two minutes, then turn off or reduce the heat to low before adding the chocolate. The metal mass distributes heat evenly, without any hot spots: the chocolate melts by thermal inertia, like in a double boiler, but without a saucepan or bowl. Wipe the pan with paper towels between each batch and prepare all three chocolates in the same pan.
steps: Blend the chickpeas, drained dates, and cocoa until you obtain a smooth, grain-free paste. Scrape down the sides of the bowl once during blending.
Spread this base to a thickness of 1.5 cm in a small dish or square mold lined with baking paper. Press down with a spatula, ensuring a flat surface.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, low heat, 2 minutes: it should be hot without smoking.
With the heat off and on low heat, melt the 150g of dark chocolate with the coconut milk, stirring with a flexible spatula. Cook for 3 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Pour the lukewarm ganache over the base, tilt the mold to even it out. Refrigerate until set, about 2 hours.
Wipe the pan clean, then preheat it again empty for 2 minutes over low heat. Melt the 200g of 70% chocolate in the pan for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Stir in the peanut butter, if using.
Remove from heat, pour the puffed quinoa into the pan and mix until completely coated, without crushing the grains.
Transfer to a lined mold, press down firmly with the back of a spoon. Chill for 1 hour, then cut into bars.
In a bowl or jar, mix the plant-based yogurt, chia seeds, and agave syrup. Let it soak for 10 minutes.
Spread a thin layer of peanut butter on top, then sprinkle with crushed peanuts.
Wipe the pan, preheat it empty for 2 minutes over low heat, melt the 50g of chocolate with the coconut oil until you obtain a smooth mixture.
Spread this chocolate evenly over the top of the porridge. Refrigerate overnight: the chocolate will form a shell that cracks when you spoon it on.

title: Beef quesadillas, chipotle sauce
intro: It all comes down to the beef crust: a single pan, nice and hot, and ten portions ready to spend the week in the freezer.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil: the steak will sear beautifully instead of releasing its juices. The same principle applies to tortillas, which brown without any added fat. A single pan for meat, vegetables, and assembly, with no intermediate washing required.
steps: Season the steak on both sides with garlic salt and black pepper. Let it come to room temperature while the pan heats up.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently and coat the bottom without smoking.
Place the steak on the grill and leave it untouched. Let it cook for approximately 10 minutes, turning it over only once. The steak will release easily from the grill once a crust has formed.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Cut the steak into small, even cubes, working against the grain.
Return the pan to medium-high heat. Sauté the onions and peppers for 5 minutes in the remaining juices, until softened and browned in places.
Mix together the mayonnaise, chipotle paste, lime juice, garlic salt and pepper until you have a smooth sauce.
Top each tortilla on one half: a drizzle of chipotle sauce, the diced beef, the sautéed vegetables, the mozzarella. Fold over.
Brown the quesadillas over medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes per side. They will release easily when the surface is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Allow to cool on a wire rack, then wrap individually in aluminum foil or in airtight freezer bags.

title: Mashed potatoes, beef and mushrooms au gratin
intro: It all comes down to the color of the beef: a clean sear, without stirring, then a short jus that binds everything together.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold meat is added: this is what creates the crust. It then proceeds to reduce the juices and then brown the meat, covered, without changing the pan or transferring it to the oven.
steps: Heat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Meanwhile, slice the potatoes into thick slices about 1 cm thick.

Add the slices to the pan with a little water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, adding a little more water if the bottom of the pan becomes dry. A knife tip should pierce the slices easily.
Drain, then transfer from the pan to a bowl. Mash with a fork, stir in the cream, and season with salt. Cover to keep warm.
Wipe the pan clean, then return it to medium-high heat with the fat. Finely chop the onion and quarter the mushrooms.

Arrange the beef in a single layer, add the onion and mushrooms. Don't stir: the meat will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. This should take 5 to 6 minutes. Then mix it in and season with the spices.
Moisten with the stock and let reduce uncovered for 4 minutes, until the juice coats the back of a spoon.

Set the topping aside. Spread the hot mashed potatoes in the bottom of the pan, distribute the beef and its juices on top, and cover with mozzarella. Cover and cook over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes: the cheese should melt and become stringy.
